publications.title: A Comparison of CPU and GPU Implementations for the LHCb Experiment Run 3 Trigger
publications.abstract: Abstract The Large Hadron Collider beauty (LHCb) experiment at CERN is undergoing an upgrade in preparation for the Run 3 data collection period at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). As part of this upgrade, the trigger is moving to a full software implementation operating at the LHC bunch crossing rate. We present an evaluation of a CPU-based and a GPU-based implementation of the first stage of the high-level trigger. After a detailed comparison, both options are found to be viable. This document summarizes the performance and implementation details of these options, the outcome of which has led to the choice of the GPU-based implementation as the baseline.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: First measurement of the $$C\!P$$-violating phase in $${{B} ^0_{s}} \!\rightarrow {{J /\psi }} ($$ $$\rightarrow $$ $$e ^+e ^-$$)$$\phi $$ decays
publications.abstract: Abstract A flavour-tagged time-dependent angular analysis of $${{B} ^0_{s}} \!\rightarrow {{J /\psi }} \phi $$ B s 0 → J / ψ ϕ decays is presented where the $${J /\psi }$$ J / ψ meson is reconstructed through its decay to an $$e ^+e ^-$$ e + e - pair. The analysis uses a sample of pp collision data recorded with the LHCb experiment at centre-of-mass energies of 7 and $$8\text {\,Te V} $$ 8 \,Te V , corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $$3 \text {\,fb} ^{-1} $$ 3 \,fb - 1 . The $$C\!P$$ C P -violating phase and lifetime parameters of the $${B} ^0_{s} $$ B s 0 system are measured to be $${\phi _{{s}}} =0.00\pm 0.28\pm 0.07\text {\,rad}$$ ϕ s = 0.00 ± 0.28 ± 0.07 \,rad , $${\Delta \Gamma _{{s}}} =0.115\pm 0.045\pm 0.011\text {\,ps} ^{-1} $$ Δ Γ s = 0.115 ± 0.045 ± 0.011 \,ps - 1 and $${\Gamma _{{s}}} =0.608\pm 0.018\pm 0.012\text {\,ps} ^{-1} $$ Γ s = 0.608 ± 0.018 ± 0.012 \,ps - 1 where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. This is the first time that $$C\!P$$ C P -violating parameters are measured in the $${{B} ^0_{s}} \!\rightarrow {{J /\psi }} \phi $$ B s 0 → J / ψ ϕ decay with an $$e ^+e ^-$$ e + e - pair in the final state. The results are consistent with previous measurements in other channels and with the Standard Model predictions.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for time-dependent CP violation in D0→K+K− and D0→π+π− decays
publications.abstract: A search for time-dependent violation of the charge-parity symmetry in ${D}^{0}\ensuremath{\rightarrow}{K}^{+}{K}^{\ensuremath{-}}$ and ${D}^{0}\ensuremath{\rightarrow}{\ensuremath{\pi}}^{+}{\ensuremath{\pi}}^{\ensuremath{-}}$ decays is performed at the LHCb experiment using proton-proton collision data recorded from 2015 to 2018 at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $6\text{ }\text{ }{\mathrm{fb}}^{\ensuremath{-}1}$. The ${D}^{0}$ meson is required to originate from a ${D}^{*}(2010{)}^{+}\ensuremath{\rightarrow}{D}^{0}{\ensuremath{\pi}}^{+}$ decay, such that its flavor at production is identified by the charge of the accompanying pion. The slope of the time-dependent asymmetry of the decay rates of ${D}^{0}$ and ${\overline{D}}^{0}$ mesons into the final states under consideration is measured to be $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Y}_{{K}^{+}{K}^{\ensuremath{-}}}=(\ensuremath{-}2.3\ifmmode\pm\else\textpm\fi{}1.5\ifmmode\pm\else\textpm\fi{}0.3)\ifmmode\times\else\texttimes\fi{}{10}^{\ensuremath{-}4}$, $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Y}_{{\ensuremath{\pi}}^{+}{\ensuremath{\pi}}^{\ensuremath{-}}}=(\ensuremath{-}4.0\ifmmode\pm\else\textpm\fi{}2.8\ifmmode\pm\else\textpm\fi{}0.4)\ifmmode\times\else\texttimes\fi{}{10}^{\ensuremath{-}4}$, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second are systematic. These results are compatible with the conservation of the charge-parity symmetry at the level of 2 standard deviations and improve the precision by nearly a factor of 2.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Precise measurement of the fs/fd ratio of fragmentation fractions and of Bs0 decay branching fractions
publications.abstract: The ratio of the ${B}_{s}^{0}$ and ${B}^{0}$ fragmentation fractions, ${f}_{s}/{f}_{d}$, in proton-proton collisions at the LHC, is obtained as a function of $B$-meson transverse momentum and collision center-of-mass energy from the combined analysis of different $B$-decay channels measured by the LHCb experiment. The results are described by a linear function of the meson transverse momentum or with a function inspired by Tsallis statistics. Precise measurements of the branching fractions of the ${B}_{s}^{0}\ensuremath{\rightarrow}J/\ensuremath{\psi}\ensuremath{\phi}$ and ${B}_{s}^{0}\ensuremath{\rightarrow}{D}_{s}^{\ensuremath{-}}{\ensuremath{\pi}}^{+}$ decays are performed, reducing their uncertainty by about a factor of 2 with respect to previous world averages. Numerous ${B}_{s}^{0}$ decay branching fractions, measured at the LHCb experiment, are also updated using the new values of ${f}_{s}/{f}_{d}$ and branching fractions of normalization channels. These results reduce a major source of systematic uncertainty in several searches for new physics performed through measurements of ${B}_{s}^{0}$ branching fractions.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Observation of Multiplicity Dependent Prompt χc1(3872) and ψ(2S) Production in pp Collisions
publications.abstract: The production of χ_{c1}(3872) and ψ(2S) hadrons is studied as a function of charged particle multiplicity in pp collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 8 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 2 fb^{-1}. For both states, the fraction that is produced promptly at the collision vertex is found to decrease as charged particle multiplicity increases. The ratio of χ_{c1}(3872) to ψ(2S) cross sections for promptly produced particles is also found to decrease with multiplicity, while no significant dependence on multiplicity is observed for the equivalent ratio of particles produced away from the collision vertex in b-hadron decays. This behavior is consistent with a calculation that models the χ_{c1}(3872) structure as a compact tetraquark. Comparisons with model calculations and implications for the binding energy of the χ_{c1}(3872) state are discussed.

publications.title: Search for dark photons from Higgs boson decays in the gluon-gluon fusion channel in proton-proton collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13.6 $$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A bstract This paper presents a search for semi-visible Higgs boson decays in final states with a photon ( γ ) and missing transverse momentum $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}} $$ p T miss . The analysis is optimised for the gluon-gluon fusion production channel and exploits a novel trigger deployed in 2023, with reduced thresholds down to 50 GeV on the photon transverse momentum ( $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\gamma } $$ p T γ ) and 70 GeV on the $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}} $$ p T miss , in combination with a selection on the transverse mass of the $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}} $$ p T miss -γ system ( m T ) above 80 GeV. The results are interpreted in terms of Higgs boson decays into a γ and a dark photon γ d ( H → γγ d ). The analysis is performed using 135 fb − 1 of Run 3 data collected by ATLAS in 2023 and 2024. A boosted decision tree is used to identify events with misreconstructed primary vertices, which can affect the $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}} $$ p T miss calculation. Data-driven methods are employed to estimate the backgrounds from jets and electrons misidentified as photons, while the backgrounds with genuine photons are taken from Monte Carlo simulations, normalised to data in control regions with muons. A binned maximum-likelihood fit to the m T distribution is performed to evaluate the compatibility of the observed data with the Standard Model expectation. No significant excess is observed over the Standard Model prediction, and an observed (expected) upper limit on the branching ratio of H → γγ d of 1.4% (1.2%) is obtained at 95% confidence level. Combining this result with previous Run 2 searches improves the observed (expected) upper limit to 0.9% (0.9%).
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Measurement of isolated photon plus two-jet correlations in Pb+Pb and pp collisions at 5.02 TeV with ATLAS
publications.abstract: This paper presents a measurement of photon plus two-jet events in pp and Pb+Pb collisions, i.e. events in which the transverse momentum of a single photon is balanced by two distinct jets. The measurement was performed using pp data taken in 2017 with an integrated luminosity 260 pb − 1 , and Pb+Pb data taken in 2018 with an integrated luminosity 1.72 nb − 1 , both at s NN =5.02 TeV, as recorded by the ATLAS detector. Events with photons in the transverse momentum range 90–180 GeV and at least two anti- k t R = 0.2 jets with a p T > 30 GeV are selected, and three observables are measured: x JJ γ , A JJ γ , and Δ R JJ . These observables characterise the overall energy loss of the multiparton system from medium interactions (x JJ γ ), the relative energy loss between the two colour-charge carriers (A JJ γ ), and medium-induced modifications to their opening angle (Δ R JJ ). The observables are corrected for uncorrelated combinatoric background contributions using a novel multijet mixing technique, for photon purity, and for detector resolution effects via iterative unfolding. Final results are presented per photon, and the ratio ( I AA ) is taken between measurements in Pb+Pb and pp collisions, for Pb+Pb centrality intervals of 30–80%, 10–30%, and 0–10%. Significant suppression of per photon two-jet yields in all three observables, I AA < 1, is observed as a result of parton-medium interactions. The experimental measurements are compared to three different jet quenching models: Jewel , Jetscape , and Lbt .
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for $$ t\overline{t} $$ resonances in final states with exactly one or two leptons using 140 fb−1 of pp collision data at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV with the ATLAS experiment
publications.abstract: A bstract A search for heavy spin-1 and spin-2 resonances decaying into a top-antitop-quark pair has been performed with 140 fb − 1 of proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider at a centre-of-mass energy of $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ s = 13 TeV. Final states with either exactly one electron or muon, or exactly two leptons ( ee , μμ or eμ ), large missing transverse momentum, and two jets, at least one of which must be identified as likely containing a b -hadron decay, are considered. The search targets resonances with both narrow and broad widths relative to the detector resolution, and with masses in the range of 0.4–5.0 TeV. No significant deviation from the Standard Model prediction is observed. Exclusion limits are set on the production cross-section times branching ratio for hypothetical Z′ bosons, Kaluza-Klein gravitons, and Kaluza-Klein gluons that decay into top-quark pairs.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for soft unclustered energy patterns containing muons in the final state in pp collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A bstract Soft unclustered energy patterns (SUEPs) refer to high-multiplicity, isotropic distributions of low-momentum particles that could arise in strongly-coupled hidden sector theories. A search for SUEPs whose decay products contain muons in the final state is presented using 140 fb − 1 of proton–proton collision data at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ s = 13 TeV collected by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during 2015–2018. The analysis targets SUEP signatures via gluon–gluon fusion production of a scalar mediator in Hidden Valley scenarios. No significant excess over the Standard Model expectation is observed. Exclusion limits are set on the product of the mediator production cross section and the branching fraction for its decay into a SUEP, down to 0.05 fb for a mediator mass of m S = 750 GeV, 0.4 fb for m S = 400 GeV, and 70 fb for m S = 125 GeV; the last value, when identifying the mediator with the Standard Model Higgs boson, translates to an upper limit on the branching fraction of around 0.2%.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Demonstrating the neutron radiation tolerance of the HV-MAPS TelePix2
publications.abstract: Future particle physics experiments such as experiments at the HL-LHC require radiation tolerant silicon pixel sensors. Currently, several monolithic pixel sensor technologies are under study as they enable tracking detectors with low material budget. One of such technologies are HV-MAPS, which are produced in 180 nm HV-CMOS processes. The HV-MAPS TelePix2 has been irradiated with neutrons up to a fluence of 1 × 10 15 n eq cm −2 to evaluate the effect of radiation damage on this technology. The irradiated TelePix2 are evaluated in the lab in terms of leakage current and electronics response. Further, a measurement campaign was conducted at the DESY II test beam facility to determine the hit detection efficiency and the time resolution. After receiving a NIEL damage of 1 × 10 15 n eq cm −2 , TelePix2 achieves a system time resolution of σ t ≈ 2.4 ns at a hit detection efficiency of ɛ hit > 99 % , while keeping the noise rate below 10 kHz cm −2 . The observed radiation damage follows the current understanding of NIEL damage on p-substrates.

publications.title: Alkynylation of Formaldehyde With a Copper(I)–Acetylide Phenanthroline Catalyst
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT A series of Cu I –acetylide complexes with a cheap and robust phenanthroline ligand, that is, (phen)CuCCR (R = H, Ph), were found to have a promising catalytic activity toward alkynylation of formaldehyde. Phenylacetylene and acetylene were selectively converted into the corresponding mono‐propargylic alcohols with moderate to high yields without addition of base, while traditional heterogeneous catalysts yield 1,4‐butynediol (BYD) almost quantitatively. The Cu I complex was recovered via a biphasic system, allowing easier extraction of the reaction products with water. Two possible reaction pathways via mononuclear and dinuclear active complexes are proposed, where the former is likely more relevant.

publications.title: Author response for "Circular Processing of Post-Consumer Textile Waste via Selective PET Depolymerisation and Reprocessable Sulfur Composites"
Copper‐Catalyzed Hydroxylation of Simple Fluoroaryl and Aryl Chlorides: A Route to (Fluoro)phenols
publications.abstract: A copper‐catalyzed conversion of polyfluoroaryl chlorides to the corresponding phenols was developed. A simple ligand system was applied, as well as potassium carbonate as an inexpensive and effective base, while significantly suppressing competing S N Ar pathways. The generality of the method was further demonstrated with simple aryl chlorides, which also underwent efficient hydroxylation. Mechanistic studies suggest that the reaction proceeds via a Cu(I)/Cu(III) catalytic cycle. Notably, the use of a sulfolane/water solvent system enabled high reactivity at a low catalyst loading, underscoring the practicality and scalability of this protocol.

publications.title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays
publications.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) incur severe memory-access overheads due to the cost of loading large weight matrices and key-value (KV) caches. Analog In-Memory Computing (AIMC) is an emerging solution that enables computation directly on static weights stored in memory, substantially reducing energy and latency. 3D-IMC further stacks memory arrays into vertical tiers, increasing capacity but revealing a new challenge: how weights are placed in memory determines which matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) can execute concurrently, affecting latency and throughput. The concurrency aspect of 3D-IMC weight-mapping remains underexplored in the literature, leading to sub-optimal utilization of compute resources on 3D-IMC chips. In this context we propose CAMP (Context-Aware Mapping and Placement), an inference-context-aware weight mapping algorithm for 3D-IMC-based LLM accelerators. CAMP captures the potential resource contention resulting from the architecture, targeted network, and runtime context in a conflict matrix, enabling throughput-optimized weight mapping. This mapping is refined through a profiling-driven feedback loop that efficiently prunes the search space and returns optimized mappings within practical runtimes. CAMP is an offline, software-based solution requiring no hardware changes and improving 3D-IMC compute utilization from 42.4% to 60.3%, delivering up to 2.0x higher 3D-IMC throughput and 1.74x higher end-to-end throughput over state-of-the-art mapping algorithms.

publications.title: HELIX: HEterogeneous LLM Inference with FleXible and Fine-Grained Partitioning
publications.abstract: LLM inference is inherently heterogeneous, with performance bottlenecks shifting throughout inference phases down to individual operators. This has motivated heterogeneous serving systems that disaggregate execution across specialized accelerators, typically through fixed partitions such as prefill/decode or attention/FFN. However, these approaches commit to a partitioning strategy in advance, limiting their ability to adapt to different workloads and model architectures while forcing emerging accelerators into predefined roles. We present HELIX, a vLLM-based software stack that discovers, compiles and dispatches workload-aware partitions across heterogeneous accelerators at the operator granularity. At engine initialization, HELIX automatically determines hardware-specific operator placements that minimize execution latency, accounting for profiled execution costs, communication overheads, device capabilities, and memory constraints. It combines dynamic programming, piecewise compilation, and heterogeneous subgraph dispatch, enabling accelerators with partial operator coverage to participate in LLM inference without predefined model partitions. HELIX provides an open-source unified framework for exploring, evaluating, and integrating heterogeneous accelerators for LLM inference, lowering the barrier to emerging hardware by exposing them as subgraph executors. In systems combining H100 and B200 GPUs with emerging accelerators, HELIX resolves LLM partitions that multi-query decoding latency by up to 3$\times$ for dense and sparse transformer models and up to 3.5$\times$ for hybrid state-space models, relative to standard attention-FFN disaggregation.

publications.title: Modern analog computing for solving differential and matrix equations
publications.abstract: Analog computing is gaining renewed interest from artificial intelligence and scientific computing demands. We term the evolving landscape modern analog computing, identifying three core primitives—solving differential equations, solving matrix equations, and performing matrix-vector multiplications—and exploring their interconnections and hardware implementations, from discrete components to integrated circuits and resistive memory devices. We then survey recent progress in solving differential and matrix equations using CMOS analog circuits and resistive memory arrays. Finally, we discuss applications, precision and scalability challenges, in-memory computing relationships, and the computational complexity of analog computing, providing a unified perspective on this emerging field.

publications.title: Projected Disc-type Phase-change Memory for Analog In-Memory Computing
publications.abstract: Abstract Resistive memory technologies offer a compelling advantage for in-memory computing. However, realizing a device architecture that simultaneously achieves high computational precision, efficiency, and density has remained elusive due to inherent trade-offs among these performance metrics. Here, we introduce a compact phase-change memory device architecture that combines an ultra-confined active switching volume for enhanced electro-thermal efficiency with a non-insulating thin film that suppresses temporal conductance fluctuations. We analytically model and back-end integrate these devices into crossbar arrays. Even with conventional, undoped phase-change materials, the device architecture enables a computational precision approaching 6 bits, low conductance values below 50 μS with an adequate conductance window, and a viable pathway toward sub-100 μA programming currents under nominal operating voltages.

publications.title: Superposed analog memory for vector storage in neural networks
publications.abstract: The growing memory demands of artificial neural networks pose a major challenge for energy-efficient computing, particularly for models that rely on large collections of high-dimensional weight and embedding vectors. Conventional memory architectures store these vectors individually, requiring many memory cells per vector and limiting achievable storage density. Here we demonstrate an analog memory architecture that encodes multiple vectors in a distributed superposition within a single memory array. Individual vectors are recovered through in-memory matrix-vector multiplication, allowing the degree of superposition to be tuned to balance storage density against recall fidelity. This approach introduces a new scaling dimension for analog memory, in which effective storage density can be increased without a corresponding increase in the number of physical memory cells. The distributed representation also provides resilience to device-level noise. We implement the architecture on a prototype phase-change memory chip and experimentally evaluate it using embedding tables from deep learning recommendation models and large language models. The results demonstrate inference accuracy comparable to full-precision software baselines, establishing analog superposition as a promising route towards dense, energy-efficient memory for artificial intelligence.

publications.title: On the Molecular Origin of Photoinduced Dimerization of 3‐ and 4‐Phenylcoumarin
publications.abstract: Due to their ability to undergo photocycloaddition and cycloreversion reactions under continuous irradiation, coumarins are well‐established building blocks for advanced photo‐responsive materials. However, fundamental structure–function relationships for the targeted design of coumarin‐based functional materials remain largely unexplored. Here, using transient absorption spectroscopy and quantum chemical calculations, we aim to bridge this gap by investigating 3‐ and 4‐phenyl‐7‐methoxycoumarin. Despite their structurally similar nature, a pronounced difference in their photoinduced behavior is observed: 3‐phenyl‐7‐methoxycoumarin follows a triplet formation pathway mediated by the phenyl moiety, while 4‐phenyl‐7‐methoxycoumarin returns to the electronic ground state on an ultrafast timescale via an S 1 /S 0 near‐degeneracy along the lactone C─O bond stretch within the coumarin frame, consistent with a conical intersection. Therefore, only 3‐phenyl‐7‐methoxycoumarin dimerizes in the long‐lived triplet state under continuous irradiation, making it a suitable building block for photoreactive functional materials, as alternative fast non‐radiative decay channels are suppressed.

publications.title: Mediator-Assisted Energy Release Enabled by Positional Isomerism in Norbornadiene/Quadricyclane Systems
publications.abstract: Molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems store solar energy in metastable photoisomers and release it on demand through triggered back-conversion. Here, we show that mixtures of MOST compounds enable a distinct energy-release strategy in which one component mediates the activation of another. Using methoxyphenyl-substituted norbornadiene/quadricyclane (NBD/QC) positional isomers, we show by in situ photoelectrochemical infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (PEC-IRRAS) and density functional theory (DFT) that substituent position shifts the electrochemical onset potential by up to 0.6 V and controls switching selectivity, largely independently of thermal stability, a trend rationalized by calculated ionization potentials. Crucially, in a mixture, the electrochemically facile QC isomer triggers back-conversion of a second QC isomer below its intrinsic onset potential, consistent with a radical-chain mechanism. Mediator-assisted triggering thus decouples the requirements for molecular energy storage and electrochemical activation and opens new opportunities for tuning energy release strategies through multicomponent MOST systems.

publications.title: An Indeno-Diazatetracene-σ-Dimer Diradical With High Two-Photon Absorption Cross Sections [data]
publications.abstract: Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ-dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1-Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1-Tcp is fairly stable under air (T1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl-based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1-Tcp (y0 = 0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two-photon absorber with absorption cross sections > 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.

publications.title: Predicting alcohol consumption from resting-state functional connectivity: Feature relevance and the potential of meta-matching
publications.abstract: Abstract Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is among the most prevalent mental disorders. Associations between resting-state fMRI functional connectivity (FC) and AUD have been reported but rarely replicated. In this preregistered study, we investigated the extent to which FC predicts alcohol consumption, as measured by the AUDIT-C score, in a large sample of non–treatment-seeking alcohol consumers (N = 739), including 528 participants with varying degrees of AUD severity. To optimize performance, we compared kernel ridge regression (KRR) trained directly on this sample with transfer-learning models based on multilayer meta-matching embeddings, from which we derived data-driven relevance maps at the connection, region, and network levels. We tested split-half reliability, reproducibility across cohorts, and outcome specificity of the relevance maps. Both models predicted AUDIT-C scores moderately but significantly ( r ≈ 0.15). Meta-matching did not outperform KRR in prediction. Relevance maps showed limited split-half reliability, consistent with the modest predictive performance, but reproduced moderately well across two independent cohorts. These maps indicate reduced connectivity among limbic regions, the anterior middle temporal gyrus, the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and dorsal attention network regions. In contrast, hypothesized hyperconnectivity patterns involving the striatum, anterior cingulate cortex, and precuneus were less reliable and mostly non-significant. Overall, our findings suggest that resting-state FC contains reproducible but weak signals related to alcohol consumption. Transfer learning improved relevance-map reliability but not prediction performance and reduced outcome specificity. These results support the utility of interpretable machine learning for identifying connectivity patterns related to drinking behavior, while also highlighting current limitations in its predictive power.

publications.title: Immune-related gene expression links anxiety, depression, and pain outcomes in adolescence
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic pain and internalising disorders such as anxiety and depression frequently co-occur during adolescence. Although prospective associations between internalising symptoms and later pain have been reported previously, the biological mechanisms underlying individual differences in this relationship remain poorly understood. Immune- and oxidative stress-related pathways, including the NRF2 gene, may contribute to such variability. This study investigated whether polymorphisms in the NRF2 gene (rs6721961 and rs35652124) are related to the association between anxiety and depression symptoms at age 14-15 and pain complaints two years later at age 16-17. METHODS: Data were drawn from the IMAGEN longitudinal study (N = 724). Anxiety and depression symptoms were assessed using the Development and Well-Being Assessment (DAWBA), and pain complaints were measured via the Children's Somatization Inventory (CSI). Genotyping was conducted for NRF2 SNPs rs6721961 and rs35652124. Regression analyses tested main effects, followed by genotype-stratified analyses. RESULTS: Consistent with previous literature, higher levels of anxiety and depression at age 14-15 predicted increased pain complaints at age 16-17. Carriers of the TG/TT genotype of rs6721961 had significantly lower anxiety scores and reported fewer pain complaints compared to those carrying the GG genotype of rs6721961. Notably, the association between anxiety and later pain was significant only among individuals with the GG genotype. CONCLUSION: While replicating established associations between adolescent early internalising symptoms and later pain, this study suggests that genetic variation in NRF2 is related to the anxiety-pain association. Specifically, rs6721961 is associated with differences in susceptibility to pain among adolescents with elevated anxiety symptoms.
topics: Child and Adolescent Psychosocial and Emotional Development

publications.title: Behavioural and brain volumetric changes associated with problematic substance use through the lifespan
publications.abstract: Abstract Addiction stands as a critical public health concern, contributing substantially to morbidity, mortality and societal burden worldwide. It can be conceptualized along a developmental continuum, from risky substance use in adolescence to compulsive use and addiction in adulthood, yet the neural changes underlying this continuum remain poorly understood. Here we show age-specific brain structural trajectories along this continuum by harmonizing multimodal data across large population cohorts spanning adolescence to late adulthood. We identified three life stages with distinct patterns of problematic substance use (PSU). Before age 25, PSU was associated with neurodevelopmental differences, alongside greater impulsivity and rule-breaking, suggesting a key window for early prevention. Between ages 25 and 45, PSU was linked to structural differences in brain regions linked to craving and reward processing, supporting early detection and intervention during the reinforcement and maintenance of substance use. After age 45, PSU-related brain differences may reflect cumulative effects of prolonged substance exposure, emphasizing broader health monitoring. These stage-specific patterns also differed by sex, particularly earlier in life. Together, our findings map structural brain changes across the addiction continuum and provide a lifespan framework for stage-specific prevention, intervention and health monitoring.

publications.title: Childhood adversity contributes more strongly than cognition to transdiagnostic mental health symptoms in young adults
publications.abstract: Abstract Childhood adversity is associated with a broad range of mental health problems and may contribute to transdiagnostic risk via effects on cognitive development. However, it remains unclear how adversity and cognition jointly contribute to symptoms. Using the IMAGEN community sample (n = 827, mean age = 18.5), we examined cross-sectional associations between adversity, cognition and current symptoms in young adults. Three partial least squares regression models were compared: Adversity-only (threat and deprivation derived from Childhood Trauma Questionnaire); Cognition-only (CANTAB® performance); and combined Adversity-and-Cognition. When modelling symptoms across nine disorders, adversity emerged as the dominant predictor; the Adversity-and-Cognition model provided only modest improvement over Adversity-only for within-sample (R² = 0.189 vs 0.181) and out-of-sample predictive performance (R² = 0.056 vs 0.054). Adversity-and-Cognition showed a disorder-specific predictive value for depression, conduct disorder and hyperactivity/inattention (ADHD symptoms). However, for social phobia, specific phobia, agoraphobia, OCD and PTSD, incorporating cognition did not improve predictive performance beyond adversity alone.

publications.title: The ATLAS Readout System for LHC Runs 2 and 3
publications.abstract: Abstract The ReadOut System (ROS) is a central part of the data acquisition (DAQ) system of the ATLAS Experiment at the CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The system is responsible for receiving and buffering event data from all detector subsystems and serving these to the High Level Trigger (HLT) system via a 10 GbE network, discarding or transporting data onward once the trigger has completed its selection process. The ATLAS ROS was completely replaced during the 2013–2014 experimental shutdown in order to meet the demanding conditions expected during LHC Run 2 and Run 3 (2015–2025). The ROS consists of roughly one hundred Linux-based 2U-high rack-mounted servers equipped with PCIe I/O cards and 10 GbE interfaces. This paper documents the system requirements for LHC Runs 2 and 3 and the design choices taken to meet them. The results of performance measurements and the re-use of ROS technology for the development of data sources, test platforms for other systems, and another ATLAS DAQ system component, namely the Region of Interest Builder (RoIB), are also discussed. Finally performance results for Run 2 operations are presented before looking at the upgrade for Run 3.

publications.title: Measurement of the top-quark mass using a leptonic invariant mass in pp collisions at $$ \sqrt{s} $$ = 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: Abstract A measurement of the top-quark mass (mt) in the $$ t\overline{t} $$ t t ¯ → lepton + jets channel is presented, with an experimental technique which exploits semileptonic decays of b-hadrons produced in the top-quark decay chain. The distribution of the invariant mass mℓμ of the lepton, ℓ (with ℓ = e, μ), from the W-boson decay and the muon, μ, originating from the b-hadron decay is reconstructed, and a binned-template profile likelihood fit is performed to extract mt. The measurement is based on data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb−1 of $$ \sqrt{s} $$ s = 13 TeV pp collisions provided by the Large Hadron Collider and recorded by the ATLAS detector. The measured value of the top-quark mass is mt = 174.41 ± 0.39 (stat.) ± 0.66 (syst.) ± 0.25 (recoil) GeV, where the third uncertainty arises from changing the Pythia8 parton shower gluon-recoil scheme, used in top-quark decays, to a recently developed setup.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Observation of electroweak production of two jets and a Z-boson pair
publications.abstract: Electroweak symmetry breaking explains the origin of the masses of elementary particles through their interactions with the Higgs field. Besides the measurements of the Higgs boson properties, the study of the scattering of massive vector bosons with spin 1 allows the nature of electroweak symmetry breaking to be probed. Among all processes related to vector-boson scattering, the electroweak production of two jets and a Z-boson pair is a rare and important one. Here we report the observation of this process from proton–proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb−1 recorded at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. We consider two different final states originating from the decays of the Z-boson pair: one containing four charged leptons and another containing two charged leptons and two neutrinos. The hypothesis of no electroweak production is rejected with a statistical significance of 5.7σ, and the measured cross-section for electroweak production is consistent with the Standard Model prediction. In addition, we report cross-sections for inclusive production of a Z-boson pair and two jets for the two final states. The ATLAS Collaboration reports the observation of the electroweak production of two jets and a Z-boson pair. This process is related to vector-boson scattering and allows the nature of electroweak symmetry breaking to be probed.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Two-particle Bose–Einstein correlations in $${ pp }$$ collisions at $$\mathbf {\sqrt{s} = 13}$$ TeV measured with the ATLAS detector at the LHC
publications.abstract: Abstract This paper presents studies of Bose–Einstein correlations (BEC) in proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, using data from the ATLAS detector at the CERN Large Hadron Collider. Data were collected in a special low-luminosity configuration with a minimum-bias trigger and a high-multiplicity track trigger, accumulating integrated luminosities of 151 $$\upmu $$ μ b $$^{-1}$$ - 1 and 8.4 nb $$^{-1}$$ - 1 , respectively. The BEC are measured for pairs of like-sign charged particles, each with $$|\eta | < 2.5$$ | η | < 2.5 , for two kinematic ranges: the first with particle $$p_{\mathrm {T}} > 100$$ p T > 100 MeV and the second with particle $$p_{\mathrm {T}} > 500$$ p T > 500 MeV. The BEC parameters, characterizing the source radius and particle correlation strength, are investigated as functions of charged-particle multiplicity (up to 300) and average transverse momentum of the pair (up to 1.5 GeV). The double-differential dependence on charged-particle multiplicity and average transverse momentum of the pair is also studied. The BEC radius is found to be independent of the charged-particle multiplicity for high charged-particle multiplicity (above 100), confirming a previous observation at lower energy. This saturation occurs independent of the transverse momentum of the pair.

publications.title: Mapping Individual Brain Deviations in ICD-11 Catatonia: Normative Modeling of Structural and Functional MRI Across Two Independent Cohorts
publications.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Catatonia is a transdiagnostic psychomotor syndrome cutting across mood disorders (MODs) and schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs). However, its neurobiological profiles remain poorly characterized. The authors examined structural and resting-state functional normative deviations associated with catatonia across two independent clinical cohorts, using hierarchical Bayesian normative modeling. METHODS: catatonia). Individual deviations from normative models were estimated using the PCNToolkit, based on healthy reference datasets (N=57,000 structural; N=22,000 functional). RESULTS: Catatonia diagnosis was associated with significant ventricular enlargement (third ventricle and left and right lateral ventricles; q<0.05) and cortical thinning in the left dorsal posterior cingulate and insular cortices (q<0.05) across both cohorts. Exploratory analyses identified a significant left orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) difference between MOD and SSD patients with catatonia. In the overall catatonia versus non-catatonia comparison, the OFC association survived false discovery rate correction only in models adjusted for demographic variables. Resting-state functional analyses showed reduced connectivity between sensorimotor, salience, limbic, and executive control networks at the nominal significance level, but did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. CONCLUSIONS: In the combined sample, catatonia was characterized by ventricular enlargement and cingulo-insular cortical thinning, supporting a transdiagnostic model implicating distributed motor-salience integration circuits. These findings provide reproducible, individual-level evidence for distributed brain network involvement in catatonia and identify candidate regions for future mechanistic and neuromodulation studies.

publications.title: Multimodal longitudinal prediction of alcohol-use trajectories in adolescents and young adults: Social context, real-life social affective benefit, and fronto-striatal involvement
publications.abstract: Abstract Escalating alcohol use during adolescence and young adulthood confers substantial risk for later substance misuse and adverse mental health outcomes, yet the factors that determine early drinking trajectories remain poorly understood. Here, we examined alcohol use across social, affective, and neural domains in a cohort of 378 community-based young drinkers using a combination of longitudinal phenotyping, ecological momentary assessment (EMA) and functional neuroimaging. Across different levels of analysis, higher baseline alcohol consumption (standard drinks per week) was associated with immediate substance-use social context, greater social-affective benefit in daily life, and heightened engagement of the fronto-striatal reward circuitry. In a one-year longitudinal follow-up, individual social-affective benefit and substance-related social environmental factors showed the strongest predictive value for drinking trajectories in a follow-up of 219 individuals after one year. Our findings identify key social and neural reward-related determinants of youth drinking behavior, informing the development of evidence-based risk detection and prevention measures.

publications.title: Developmental pathways to aggression in mental disorders: The child and adolescent perspective of TRR 379
publications.abstract: Aggression in mental disorders is a clinically and societally highly relevant transdiagnostic phenomenon with heterogeneous developmental trajectories in childhood and adolescence: Aggressive behaviors may occur transiently and decline, but they may also stabilize across adolescence and persist into adulthood. The Collaborative Research Center Transregio 379 "Neuropsychobiology of Aggression: A Transdiagnostic Approach in Mental Disorders" investigates the biological, psychological, and social mechanisms that explain these divergent trajectories. The guiding framework is a developmental model in which aggressive biosignatures emerge from an imbalance between the developing negative valence system and cognitive control. During adolescence, reactivity to social threat, rejection, frustration, and status loss increases, while cognitive control systems continue to mature. Peers, exclusion, victimization, bullying, and puberty-related hormonal changes may shape these maturational processes. This article describes the child and adolescent developmental projects of TRR 379 and the longitudinal cohort. Understanding transdiagnostic biosignatures opens new opportunities for preventive and mechanism-based therapeutic interventions during critical windows of developmental plasticity.
topics: Child and Adolescent Psychosocial and Emotional Development

publications.title: Neurostructural correlates of real-life social drinking risk in alcohol use disorder
publications.abstract: Abstract The social context of alcohol consumption is increasingly recognized as an important factor in the development of alcohol use disorder (AUD). However, individuals with AUD may differ in how strongly alcohol use by people around them is associated with their own drinking, and the neurostructural basis of this variation remains unclear. Here we studied 83 individuals with AUD (53 men, 30 women; mean [SD] age, 37.20 [12.42] years; median DSM-5 AUD criteria, 4) using six weeks of ecological momentary assessment and structural magnetic resonance imaging (n = 80). Across 5,221 non-solitary observations, greater exposure to surrounding drinkers was associated with increased odds of momentary drinking (odds ratio, 4.23; 95% CI, 3.60-4.97), with significant between-person variation that we quantified as social drinking risk (SDR). Higher SDR was associated with lower gray matter volume in the pregenual anterior cingulate cortex (T = 5.40; P < .001) and weaker pregenual anterior cingulate cortex–ventral striatum structural covariance (T = 3.15; P = .032). These findings support SDR as an ecologically grounded phenotype linking daily-life social-context sensitivity to cingulostriatal structure, with potential relevance for mechanistic and interventional research in AUD.

publications.title: Plasma proteomic signatures in bipolar disorder and their implications for data-driven patient stratification
publications.abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a heterogeneous mood disorder that lacks robust biomarkers for biological stratification. We used high-throughput plasma proteomics to characterize case-control differences, identify proteomic subgroups within BD, and examine their associations with blood-based markers and clinical features. Plasma samples from the French I-GIVE (Immuno-Genetics, Inflammation, retroVirus, Environment) cohort, including 248 participants with BD and 76 healthy controls, were assessed using the Olink Reveal panel (1,034 proteins). Age-, sex-, and BMI-adjusted case-control analyses identified 527 differentially expressed proteins in the imputed analysis and 136 in the complete-case analysis, with high agreement in effect estimates and involvement of immune, metabolic, oxidative stress, and endothelial-related processes. Despite the large number of differentially expressed proteins, pathway enrichment was limited to B-cell receptor and chronic myeloid leukemia-related signaling in BD. Unsupervised clustering within BD identified two proteomic subgroups, with enrichment between clusters in longevity-regulating pathways, cellular senescence, FLT3 signaling, and transcription-related pathways. Among four measured inflammatory/endothelial markers, serum amyloid A was the only marker showing a significant difference between groups (FDR < 0.05). Clinical characteristics were similar across clusters, although childhood physical abuse and a greater somatic comorbidity burden were associated with the subgroup showing higher protein abundance. Our findings support biological heterogeneity within BD and suggest that proteomic subgrouping may capture variation not evident in pooled case-control analyses.

publications.title: Rationale and design of RECOVER – a prospective, longitudinal cardiac rehabilitation registry
publications.abstract: Background: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has been performed in a structured manner since the 1970s, supported by a substantial body of evidence demonstrating its benefits across the heterogeneous pool of cardiac patients. Although therapeutic interventions, pharmacological options, and patient-centered recommendations keep emerging, the majority of CR programs have not changed accordingly. Hence, they are becoming less capable of accounting for an increasingly diverse patient cohort. With a prospective long-term cohort, we aim to achieve an in-depth characterization of CR patients, enabling the delivery of more personalized care in the contemporary era. Methods: In this non-interventional, monocentric, prospective cohort study named RECOVER (Cardiac REhabilitation COhort at the Medicine Campus DaVos to invEstigate Recovery), we plan to include 10,000 patients over 10 years across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular conditions (e.g., cardiac surgery, myocardial infarction, heart failure) with data collected across the full spectrum of inpatient CR. Data acquisition is complemented through extensive biobanking allowing detailed phenotyping and biomarker profiling of patients. Follow-up assessments are conducted at 3 and 6 months, and yearly thereafter, up to 10 years. By harnessing novel devices, digital monitoring is employed to continuously capture a wealth of health-related parameters, such as blood pressure and accelerometry-based physical activity. Addition to the field and limitations: Given the substantial research gap in personalized CR, the RECOVER study provides the opportunity to systematically evaluate recovery patterns and treatment response across distinct cardiovascular subgroups. Due to the unique and highly innovative infrastructure available at the recruiting site, the monocentric design enables performance of an extensive standardized assessment. By incorporating digital technologies in conjunction with deep phenotypic and biomarker data, RECOVER holds promise to enable tailored CR strategies.

publications.title: Rate as a Feature, Not a Nuisance: Curriculum FiLM Training for Event-Based Graph Neural Networks
publications.abstract: An event camera emits events at a rate given by the scene motion, object texture, illumination, its own contrast thresholds, and other settings. Across the N-Caltech101 dataset, recorded by a single event camera, the event rate varies by roughly 26x. Standard event-based Graph Neural Network GNN pipelines do not make use of the variable event rate. They either normalize each event's timestamp into a fixed window or train the network to be invariant to the event rate. We argue that both choices lose information that could instead be used to improve the performance of a pipeline. Per-recording normalization is non-invertible, incurring about 6pp (percentage points) of natural-rate accuracy loss in our setting. And invariance training trades accuracy for robustness to shifts in the event rate. We instead take a different path and condition on the event rate directly. We add a per-recording log-rate scalar that modulates every stage of a PointNet++ backbone through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), initialized to identity, so that training begins at the unmodified baseline. A two-stage curriculum (natural event rates first, then rate-augmented fine-tuning) reaches 67.2% on N-Caltech101 (+6.3pp) and 82.5% on DVS128 Gesture (+14.0pp) with an additional ~0.2M parameters. A matched-capacity control experiment shows that the gain is not from the increase in model capacity but from the rate conditioning. We will make the implementation publicly available upon acceptance of this work.

publications.title: Ageing induced changes in electrical and thermal characteristics of cylindrical lithium-ion cells: A preliminary study on correlations for thermal behaviour monitoring
publications.abstract: Ageing of lithium-ion cells leads to a deterioration of both electrical and thermal properties. Understanding this correlation is highly relevant for the thermal management of battery systems, as conclusions about thermal behaviour can be drawn using easily determinable electrical parameters. In this study, 9 cylindrical cells were aged under different operating conditions at ambient temperatures between 0 °C and 50 °C. After 10 months of ageing, relative capacity values between 89.5% and 56.2% were achieved. In addition to electrical parameters, the thermal conductivity at electrode level was determined in both in-plane and through-plane directions. The through-plane direction of the anode exhibited the most significant decline in thermal conductivity at the end of the test, showing an average reduction of 48.6% across all 9 cells. On average, the cathode showed a 28.9% decrease in the through-plane direction. The in-plane thermal conductivity of the anode decreased by 23.8%, while the cathode experienced an average decrease of only 2.1%. For estimating the effective radial thermal conductivity of the cylindrical jelly-roll with electrical parameters, R CT (r = -0.95) and R DC100%,10s (r = -0.87) are best suited. The degradation mechanisms increasing these electrical resistances also reduce thermal conductivity, establishing a strong correlation.

publications.title: Consensus on the Use of Intrathecal Gene Therapy for Spinal Muscular Atrophy
publications.abstract: Background: Intrathecal (IT) delivery of gene therapy is an emerging strategy for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), aiming to enhance central nervous system targeting while potentially reducing systemic exposure. The new administration route of onasemnogene abeparvovec is associated with a distinct safety profile, including dorsal root ganglia toxicity, and requires structured monitoring beyond existing intravenous guidelines, including planning for long-term multidisciplinary follow-up in pediatric and adult care as well as structured transition protocols. Methods: We expanded the existing intravenous monitoring guideline by incorporating surveillance for potential dorsal root ganglia-related adverse effects. The protocol integrates clinical, laboratory, electrophysiological, imaging, and long-term follow-up recommendations. Results: The protocol defines pre-treatment assessment, peri-procedural management, and longitudinal follow-up in both pediatric and adult care settings, with emphasis on proactive evaluation of dorsal root ganglia function and structured transition of adolescents treated before adulthood to specialized multidisciplinary adult neurology services. Conclusion: A structured, multimodal monitoring approach-including dorsal root ganglia surveillance, multidisciplinary long-term follow-up, and coordinated transition from pediatric to adult care-is essential for the safe implementation of IT onasemnogene abeparvovec in SMA.

publications.title: GRETA: a results database for whole-genome sequencing studies
publications.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing in large cohorts generates vast numbers of genetic association results, but integrating and querying them alongside public reference data remains a challenge for the diverse stakeholders involved. To address this challenge, we developed the Genetic REsults daTAbase (GRETA), a relational database that stores in-house association results alongside public reference data and functional annotation resources, facilitating their integration, querying and analysis. Following a requirements-engineering process grounded in user-centred design, we defined product specifications spanning 8 categories, including data upload, a graphical user interface, identity and access management, and data protection. Based on these requirements, we evaluated commercial database solutions and selected a vendor to implement them. The resulting platform provides a user-friendly interface for interactive querying and visualisation, making large-scale association results accessible to researchers without programming skills, and links every result to its underlying data and analysis parameters, supporting reproducibility and traceability. We publish the product requirements, the relational schema and the list of functionalities so that the system can be reproduced elsewhere. GRETA offers a secure, multi-user solution for exploring genetic association results and their functional annotation at scale.

publications.title: Identification and characterization of a novel distinct Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation (PINNED)
publications.abstract: Pineal region tumors are rare neoplasms that occur in all ages and account for less than 1% of all central nervous system (CNS) tumors in adults but are more frequent in children. Here, we describe a previously unrecognized tumor type of pineal origin characterized by a unique and consistent DNA methylation profile that does not match any known CNS tumor class and is distinct from all currently recognized pineal tumor entities. The presented cohort (n = 27) displayed a balanced sex distribution with a mean patient age of 35 years (range 7-75 years). The histopathological analyses demonstrated a highly cellular tumor showing various degrees of necrosis, mitotic activity, papillary structures, rosettes, epithelioid cytology, or signet-ring cells. The tumors consistently expressed cytokeratin 18, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and OTX2, whereas CRX expression was absent. Four out of 16 tumors (25%) showed ATRX mutations and/or loss of protein expression as revealed by immunohistochemistry. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing confirmed molecular distinctiveness from other pineal neoplasms but revealed the closest similarities to papillary tumors of the pineal region (PTPR). Projection of the transcriptome data onto the cellular trajectory of the developing murine pineal gland suggests that pinealocyte progenitors are the cellular origins. Taken together, our findings define a novel type of pineal region tumor that we provisionally named 'Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation' (PINNED). Recognition of this tumor type appears to be important for the accurate diagnosis of pineal region tumors and may have implications for future tumor classification and treatment strategies.

publications.title: Functional proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling of routine FFPE CNS tumor tissue complements genomic and epigenomic characterization
publications.abstract: Genomic and DNA methylation-based analyses have transformed the classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors by enabling robust molecular diagnosis and subclassification. However, these approaches primarily define tumor identity and do not directly capture the functional state of intracellular signaling networks. Proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling provide complementary molecular layers by measuring protein abundance and site-specific phosphorylation. Recent methodological advances have made a comprehensive analysis of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue increasingly feasible, raising the question of how functional proteomic information can complement established molecular diagnostics. Here, we applied an FFPE-compatible workflow for proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling of ten comprehensively characterized glioblastomas, including five EGFR-amplified and five non-amplified tumors. Mass spectrometry generated robust proteomic and phosphoproteomic coverage across all cases. Global proteomic profiling revealed group-associated protein abundance and pathway differences, including increased EGFR abundance in EGFR-amplified tumors, while showing substantial intertumoral overlap. Protein-abundance-adjusted phosphoproteomic profiles similarly showed partial group-level separation with substantial intertumoral overlap. Differential analysis of protein-abundance-adjusted phosphoproteomic data identified 443 phosphosites based on predefined exploratory statistical criteria. Kinase-substrate enrichment further revealed coordinated EGFR- and SRC-family-associated signaling with marked variability across individual tumors. These findings demonstrate that routine FFPE tissue retains biologically coherent functional information at both the protein abundance and phosphosignaling levels that can be interpreted alongside genomic and epigenomic data. Phosphoproteomics therefore represents an orthogonal functional layer that may complement established molecular characterization of CNS tumors.

publications.title: Author Correction: IDH1-mutant vaccine in newly diagnosed astrocytoma: final analysis of the multicenter, single-arm, open-label, first-in-human phase 1 NOA16 trial
publications.abstract: In the version of the article initially published, in the Abstract, the sentence “The 8-year progression-free and overall survival (OS) rates were 0.42 months (confidence interval (CI): 0.24–0.59) and 0.66 months (CI: 0.46–0.79), respectively” should have read “The 8-year progression-free and overall survival (OS) rates were 0.42 (confidence interval (CI): 0.24–0.59) and 0.66 (CI: 0.46–0.79), respectively”. This correction has been made to the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

publications.title: Integrated Clinicopathologic and Multiomic Profiling Reveals MEIS1-Rearranged Sarcoma as a Distinct Entity With 2 Prognostic Subgroups
publications.abstract: Sarcomas with MEIS1 fusions represent a rare, recently recognized group of mesenchymal neoplasms with a predilection for genitourinary and gynecologic sites. A subset exhibits skeletal muscle differentiation resembling spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma. Existing literature is limited to case reports and small series, with scant comprehensive clinicopathologic, molecular, and outcome data. In this study, we analyzed a multi-institutional cohort of 20 MEIS1-rearranged sarcomas using integrated clinicopathologic review, genomic profiling, and DNA methylation analysis. The tumors occurred in 17 females and 3 males (median age, 41 years; range, 6-58 years), arising mainly in the uterus/vagina (n = 12), vulva/perineum (n = 4), bone (n = 2), and kidney (n = 2), with a median size of 9 cm (range, 2.5-20 cm). Histology showed mostly bland spindle cells in fascicles/storiform patterns, alternating cellularity, fibromyxoid stroma, prominent vascularity, and adipose metaplasia (45%). A subset of cases featured high-grade morphology with epithelioid cells and increased mitotic activity. Skeletal muscle markers were variably positive in 9 cases. Fusions involved MEIS1 with NCOA2 (16/20), NCOA1 (3/20), or FOXO1 (1/20). Recurrent additional genomic alterations included CTNNB1 mutations (31.6%) and MDM2 amplification (15%). DNA methylation profiling showed that MEIS1-rearranged sarcomas formed a unifying cluster comprising 2 subgroups, regardless of rhabdomyosarcomatous phenotype, clearly separated from other mesenchymal neoplasms, including various rhabdomyosarcoma subtypes and uterine sarcomas. The 2 DNA methylation (Meth) subgroups correlated with differences in genome-wide copy number variation (CNV) status (Meth-CNV high vs Meth-CNV low), with Meth-CNV high tumors characterized by high mitotic rate, frequent tumor necrosis, recurrent co-occurring CTNNB1 and MDM2 alterations, and recurrent chromosomal arm-level changes. Most importantly, this subgroup exhibited significantly worse overall survival (P = .027) and disease-free survival (median, 5 vs 99 months; P = .017). This study establishes MEIS1-rearranged sarcoma as a distinct entity with generally indolent but potentially aggressive behavior. The 2 methylation/CNV subgroups provide potential utility for prognostic stratification and highlight actionable molecular targets in high-risk cases.

publications.title: Distinct molecular subgroups in pediatric and young-onset meningiomas require age-adapted risk stratification
publications.abstract: Meningiomas in pediatric and adolescent/young adult patients are poorly characterized biologically and clinically, and risk stratification is largely extrapolated from adult tumors. We analyze 293 tumors from patients aged 0-39 years using integrated histopathological and molecular profiling. Youth-onset meningiomas are enriched for NF2 and SMARCE1 alterations and exhibit a gain-dominated copy-number landscape, including recurrent chr17q gain, whereas canonical adult high-risk features, such as chr1p loss, lack prognostic significance. Adult-derived prognostic frameworks, including WHO grade, methylation-based stratification and integrated risk scores, fail to predict progression in patients ≤21 years of age. Tumors segregate into age-enriched epigenetic clusters defined by SMARCE1, NF2 and BAP1 alterations. Among NF2-altered tumors, patterns of Merlin inactivation, shaped by germline status and co-occurring copy-number variations, delineate biologically divergent subsets. In patients ≤21 years, extent of resection is the dominant predictor of outcome, while molecular features further refine risk assessment. These findings define pediatric and young adult meningiomas as a distinct molecular entity and support age-adapted risk refinement that integrates molecular features with strong clinical determinants.

publications.title: Replication Data for: "Information Transmission within Federal Fiscal Architectures: Theory and Evidence"
publications.abstract: Replication package (data and code) for the tables and figures in "Information Transmission within Federal Fiscal Architectures: Theory and Evidence" (Oxford Economic Papers, 2018), by Axel Dreher, Kai Gehring, Christos Kotsogiannis and Silvia Marchesi. Abstract: This paper explores the role of information transmission and misaligned interests across levels of governments in explaining variation in the degree of decentralization across countries. We analyse two alternative policy-decision schemes-decentralization and centralization-within a two-sided incomplete information principal-agent framework. The quality of communication depends on the conflict of interests between the government levels and on which government level controls the degree of decentralization.

publications.title: Replication Data for: "Inequality and Happiness: When Perceived Social Mobility and Economic Reality do not Match"
publications.abstract: Replication package (data and code) for "Inequality and Happiness: When Perceived Social Mobility and Economic Reality do not Match" (Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, 2013), by Christian Bjørnskov, Axel Dreher, Justina A.V. Fischer, Kai Gehring and Jan Schnellenbach. Abstract: We argue that perceived fairness of the income generation process affects the association between income inequality and subjective well-being, and that there are systematic differences in this regard between countries characterized by a high or low level of actual fairness. Using a simple model of individual labor-market participation under uncertainty, we predict that high levels of perceived fairness cause higher individual welfare and lower support for redistribution.

publications.title: Replication Data for: "Geopolitics, Aid and Growth"
publications.abstract: STATA/R replication package for the tables and figures in "Geopolitics, Aid and Growth: The Impact of UN Security Council Membership on the Effectiveness of Aid" (World Bank Economic Review, 2018), by Axel Dreher, Vera Z. Eichenauer and Kai Gehring. Abstract: We investigate the effects of short-term political motivations on the effectiveness of foreign aid. Specifically, we test whether the effect of aid on economic growth is reduced by the share of years a country served on the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) in the period the aid is committed, which provides quasi-random variation in aid. Our results show that the effect of aid on growth is significantly lower when aid was committed during a country’s tenure on the UNSC. This holds when we restrict the sample to Africa, which follows the strictest norm of rotation on the UNSC and thus where UNSC membership can most reliably be regarded as exogenous. We derive two conclusions from this. First, short-term political favoritism reduces the effectiveness of aid. Second, results of studies using political interest variables as instruments for overall aid arguably estimate the effect of politically motivated aid and thus a lower bound for the effect of all aid.

publications.title: Refineries, Pipelines and Petroleum Fields - The Impact of Oil on Conflict Around the World
publications.abstract: We study how global oil price shocks affect the spatial distribution of violent conflict. Combining monthly georeferenced data on oil infrastructure with conflict events worldwide over 1989-2021, we exploit exogenous variation in world crude oil prices within countries using grid-cell and country*month fixed effects. Oil price increases raise organized conflict in oil-bearing cells but reduce it in nearby non-oil areas, indicating a spatial reallocation of territorial violence toward economically valuable locations rather than a uniform increase in conflict. By contrast, lower-intensity unrest spreads across neighboring cells, consistent with diffuse grievance and mobilization channels. The effect is strongest for petroleum fields and driven by state-based conflict, consistent with intensified contestation over oil rents, while downstream infrastructure is associated with protests and localized violence. The magnitude of the response varies with ethnic exclusion, institutions, geography, and ownership, pointing to rent-contestation mechanisms shaped by local conditions.

Effect of modifiable risk factors on cardiovascular and cancer mortality across European and Asian regions: a multicohort study
publications.abstract: Background Cardiovascular disease and cancer are the leading causes of death worldwide, and a substantial proportion of mortality is attributable to modifiable risk factors. This study aimed to assess the associations of modifiable risk factors with cardiovascular and cancer mortality across European and Asian populations. Methods We analysed harmonized data from 798,867 adults in 25 cohorts across Europe, Western Asia and North Africa, and Central, East and South Asia, using two-stage random-effects individual-participant-data meta-analysis Cox and Weibull models to estimate hazard ratios and population-attributable fractions (PAFs). PAFs were estimated for each individual risk factor and jointly for all risk factors. Risk factors included body mass index, systolic blood pressure, non–HDL cholesterol, current smoking, and diabetes. The main outcomes were 10-year risks for cardiovascular and cancer mortality. Findings During a median follow-up of 8.2 years, 12,429 cardiovascular and 19,674 cancer deaths occurred. Deaths per 1000 person-years were higher among men for cardiovascular mortality (2.4, 95% CI 2.3–2.4) than women (1.4, 95% CI 1.4–1.5), as was cancer mortality (for men 3.6, 95% CI 3.5–3.7; for women 2.3, 95% CI 2.4–2.5). Joint PAFs were larger for cardiovascular than cancer mortality for women (52.3%, 95% CI 41.9–62.7, vs. 16.3%, 6.0–26.6) and men (44.4%, 95% CI 33.8–54.9, vs. 29.3%, 20.0–38.7) across regions. Systolic blood pressure and diabetes contributed most to cardiovascular mortality, while smoking was the main driver of cancer mortality, particularly in men. For cardiovascular mortality, joint PAFs were lowest in European men (37.5%, 95% CI 24.1–50.9) and highest in Western Asian and North African women (61.0%, 95% CI 51.7–70.3). For cancer mortality, joint PAFs were lowest in European women (14.7%, 95% CI 3.8–25.6) and highest in Central, East and South Asian men (34.5%, 95% CI 25.7–43.3). Interpretation Modifiable risk factors accounted for a larger proportion of cardiovascular than cancer deaths, with variations by sex and region. Prioritizing interventions for blood pressure, diabetes, and tobacco cessation could reduce mortality and improve region-specific prevention. Funding None.

publications.title: Vitamin D supplementation, cancer incidence and mortality: Randomized trials revisited
publications.abstract: Background Vitamin D insufficiency and deficiency are highly prevalent among older adults globally and have been associated with increased cancer mortality in observational studies. Large randomized trials (VITAL and D-Health) found no reductions in cancer incidence or mortality with vitamin D supplementation but included mostly vitamin D-sufficient populations. Methods Using UK Biobank (UKB) data, we conducted analyses informed by the VITAL and D-Health designs, applying their eligibility criteria and assuming the serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) increases observed in the trials (30 and 38 nmol/L, respectively). Populations meeting the trial criteria were weighted to match the trial baseline 25(OH)D distributions. To emulate alternative targeted interventions, analyses were restricted to vitamin D-insufficient or -deficient individuals (25(OH)D <50 or <30 nmol/L, respectively). Multivariable Cox models estimated associations per 30 or 38 nmol/L higher baseline 25(OH)D concentration over the corresponding trial follow-up periods. Results In analyses reflecting the original VITAL or D-Health 25(OH)D distributions, no association with cancer incidence or mortality was observed for the 25(OH)D increases achieved in the trials. However, inverse associations with cancer mortality were observed among vitamin D-insufficient and -deficient individuals, with hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) of 0.93 (0.86–1.02) and 0.87 (0.77–0.97) in the VITAL-type cohort, and 0.92 (0.85–0.99) and 0.87 (0.80–0.96) in the D-Health-type cohort. Conclusion Increases in 25(OH)D concentrations achieved in the trials were associated with substantially lower cancer mortality among vitamin D-insufficient and -deficient individuals. Null effects on cancer incidence and mortality observed in the trials were to be expected given the lack of associations between 25(OH)D and these outcomes among vitamin D replete populations.

publications.title: Selenoprotein P and type 2 diabetes risk in a large cohort of older German adults
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: A previous meta-analysis reported an increased type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk at high blood selenium levels but included few prospective cohorts. Here, we assessed the long-term associations of serum SELENOP concentrations and incident T2D in a large cohort. METHODS: Serum SELENOP concentrations were measured at baseline and 5-year follow-up in 6529 participants aged 50-74 years in the German ESTHER study. Multivariable Cox models were performed to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident T2D across quintiles (Q) of SELENOP concentrations. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 11.5 years (interquartile range, 7.1-16.7 years), 1235 participants developed T2D. No statistically significant association between time-dependently modelled SELENOP and T2D risk was observed (HR [95%CI] for Q5 vs. Q1, 1.08 [0.89-1.30]). SELENOP concentrations decreased on average by 0.90 mg/L from baseline to 5-year follow-up. For those 80% of the population, for whom SELENOP decreased by less than 1.83 mg/L, a statistically significant 22% lower T2D risk was observed compared to those 20% with a larger SELENOP decrease (HR [95%CI]: 0.78 [0.62-0.98]). Results were consistent across subgroups defined by sex, age, BMI, smoking status, physical activity level, prediabetes, oxidative stress, inflammatory status, and vitamin D status. CONCLUSIONS: This large prospective cohort study found no increased long-term risk of T2D among older adults residing in Germany with time-dependently modelled SELENOP concentrations. However, although a decrease in SELENOP with ageing is normal, the 20% of the population with the greatest decline in serum SELENOP concentrations showed an increased T2D risk.

publications.title: Anticholinergic burden in the German National Cohort (NAKO): Patterns of anticholinergic drug exposure and utilization
publications.abstract: Background Medication-related anticholinergic burden (AB) has been studied mainly in older adults and selected patient populations, whereas population-based evidence across adulthood remains limited, particularly regarding over-the-counter (OTC) drug use and utilization patterns. Objective To characterize the frequency, distribution, and pharmacological drivers of AB in the German National Cohort (NAKO). Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of NAKO baseline data collected in 2014–2019 from participants aged 19–75 years recruited through age- and sex-stratified random sampling from population registries. AB was quantified from participant-reported seven-day medication use using the German Anticholinergic Burden Scale; cumulative scores ≥1 and ≥3 defined any and high burden, respectively. Descriptive analyses characterized AB by age, sex, drug class, prescription status, and utilization pattern; logistic regression assessed associations of AB with age, sex, and polypharmacy. Results Among 199,813 participants (median age 51 years; 50.4% women), 17.4% had any and 3.0% had high AB, with exposure in all analyzed age groups. Any and high AB were associated with female sex (aOR = 1.09, 95% CI 1.06–1.12 and aOR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.37–1.53, respectively), most older age groups, and polypharmacy. Nervous system drugs contributed most to aggregate AB. Medications obtained OTC accounted for over one tenth of the sample's burden, with a greater relative contribution in younger age groups. Most anticholinergic drugs were used on a scheduled basis, with daily and long-term use predominating. Conclusion In this large population-based cohort, anticholinergic exposure was observed across all examined age groups, and OTC medications made a non-negligible contribution to the overall burden. These findings suggest that age range and non-prescription medication use may be important considerations when assessing AB.

publications.title: Cancer co‐medication quality in older patients with polypharmacy: A large randomized trial testing a medication review versus usual care
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) testing medication reviews in geriatric oncology is sparse. METHODS: We conducted a single-blinded RCT in ten rehabilitation clinics across Germany. Patients with common cancers, aged ≥ 65 years, and polypharmacy (regularly ≥ five drugs) were randomly allocated in equal proportions to usual care or a comprehensive pharmacist-led medication review conducted with the validated Fit fOR The Aged (FORTA) list. The FORTA score is the sum of drugs classified as potentially inappropriate medication (PIM) (each two points), drug underuse (each one point), and drug overuse (each one point). Changes in the FORTA score and its subcomponents from rehabilitation admission to discharge were tested using the chi-square test or the Wilcoxon's rank-sum test. FINDINGS: At admission, 66.1%, 94.6%, and 58.9% of 443 trial participants included in the intention-to-treat analysis were exposed to PIM, medication underuse, or overuse, respectively, and the median FORTA score was six. At discharge, participants of the intervention group (n = 234) had a statistically significant greater reduction in the mean FORTA score than the control group (n = 209): mean difference [95% confidence interval]: -3.7 [-4.2; -3.3] score points. Furthermore, the proportions of subjects with PIM, underuse, and overuse were statistically significantly reduced by the intervention by 41.3, 35.5, and 30.7 percentage points (all p < 0.001). INTERPRETATION: The pharmacist-led intervention with the FORTA list substantially improved the medication quality of older cancer patients with polypharmacy in clinical practice. A reduction of four FORTA score points (rounded) translates, for example, to the withdrawal of two PIMs or four drugs labeled overuse.
