publications.title: Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026): On Behalf of the Joint European Society of Cardiology (ESC)/American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA)/World Heart Federation (WHF) Task Force for the Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction
publications.abstract: The Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (UDMI) updates the classification to better reflect underlying pathophysiology, align with clinical evaluation of patients, and incorporate objective diagnostic criteria. This classification recognizes that myocardial infarction occurs in three clinical settings. First, myocardial infarction can arise spontaneously due to an acute coronary pathology (primary myocardial infarction). While most presentations are due to atherothrombosis, alternative coronary pathologies can be identified using coronary imaging and functional testing. Second, myocardial infarction may result from another acute condition causing oxygen supply–demand imbalance (secondary myocardial infarction). Here, objective criteria are proposed to guide the use of cardiac and invasive or non-invasive coronary imaging, promoting consistent diagnosis and informing treatment. Third, myocardial infarction may occur as a complication of percutaneous or surgical cardiac procedures (procedure-related myocardial infarction). The diagnosis of procedure-related myocardial infarction does not rely on cardiac biomarker thresholds and is comparable for percutaneous and surgical procedures. In each of these three settings, guidance is provided on the interpretation of symptoms and signs of myocardial ischemia, cardiac biomarkers, and imaging. Alignment of the classification of myocardial infarction with International Disease Classification (ICD)-11 codes, its distinction from myocardial injury, and implications for patients, public health, and research are discussed. It is anticipated that adoption of the classification in practice and research will ensure the diagnosis of myocardial infarction is meaningful for patients and clinicians with clear implications for care across healthcare settings.

publications.title: Revisiting Fischhoff et al. (1978)—How Safe is Safe Enough? A Psychometric Study of Attitudes Towards Technological Risks and Benefits
publications.abstract: Abstract Fischhoff et al. (1978) developed the psychometric paradigm of risk perception. The researchers asked 76 participants from Eugene, Oregon’s League of Women Voters and their spouses to rate their perceived risks and benefits of thirty activities or technologies. This participant sample is highly focused, as are the methods by prescribing the activities and technologies to be assessed along with the ways of assessing them. The results proffer patterns, and the authors interpret those patterns sensibly, with appropriate caution and without either overstating or understating significance. The data and analysis ultimately distil into the paper’s core thesis, representing a major advance at the time: the proposition that risk perception is broadly determined across two dimensions. First, a known-unknown axis and, second, the level of certainty of death if something goes wrong. Perceived benefit is added as a third dimension for predicting acceptability of activities and technologies.

publications.title: Equitable Risk Assessment and Risk Reduction Strategies: The Strategyfinder Method
publications.abstract: Significant progress has been made in improving equity in risk assessment and risk reduction, although major gaps remain. This paper offers one contribution for addressing a key aspect in improving equity-centred approaches in risk assessment and risk reduction: How to develop equitable risk assessment and risk reduction strategies and actions that are useful, useable, and likely to be used in practice. A specific methodological tool from operational research, Strategyfinder ™, is demonstrated for contributing to equitable risk assessment and risk reduction strategies. Strategyfinder is a browser-based software platform that helps groups collaboratively work online on systemic risk assessment to support equitable risk assessment and risk reduction. Key issues covered are choosing participants, those who do not participate, numbers of participants, and achieving equity among participants. A workshop with Strategyfinder is used to illustrate its use. This workshop involved eight participants sharing their views about the risks associated with trust and misinformation in a future pandemic, thereby illustrating the tool’s benefits and advantages. By centring equity in the selection and engagement of participants – especially those who are typically marginalized – Strategyfinder could enhance the relevance, usability, usefulness, and implementation of equitable risk assessment and risk reduction strategies. To seek improvements, further research should evaluate how inclusive and participatory Strategyfinder really is.

publications.title: End of humanity? Blow-by-blow account of what would happen if the Yellowstone supervolcano erupted now
Invisible Allies: Donkeys promote drought resilience in pastoralist communities but are excluded from policy
publications.abstract: Severe droughts in East Africa threaten pastoralist livelihoods, with donkeys providing vital but undervalued support in transporting water, food, and resources. This study examines policy and provision for working donkeys in Kenya and Ethiopia, countries severely affected by drought and heavily reliant on donkeys for community resilience. We narratively reviewed national and international documents relevant to donkey welfare, particularly during drought (n = 77), spanning animal health, agriculture, climate change, disaster risk management, and water. We found donkeys largely absent—only 17 policies referenced equids, mainly in economic rather than welfare terms. To explore ground realities, lived experience and barriers to successful provision of donkey welfare during drought, we conducted 41 semi-structured interviews with government officials, veterinarians, non-governmental organisation and pastoralist representatives. Stakeholders reported systemic exclusion of donkeys from veterinary curricula, health infrastructure, and drought relief efforts. Barriers to provision included the invisibility of their contributions, a lack of data on their economic value, and livestock models focused on production animals. Recommendations for future policy comprise the explicit inclusion of equids in policy definitions of livestock and corresponding inclusion in livestock and disaster risk management frameworks; ensuring eligibility for feed and veterinary support. Practical improvements could be made regarding welfare law enforcement, integrating donkeys into veterinary curricula, collecting data on their economic value and resilience contributions and prioritising drought preparedness initiatives. A One Health/Welfare approach linking human, animal, and environmental wellbeing, combined with coordinated and context-specific drought interventions, could strengthen community resilience, enhance animal welfare, and safeguard pastoralist livelihoods.

publications.title: Extreme heat and risk of pediatric emergency department visits: a time-stratified time-series analysis
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Children are vulnerable to heat, yet evidence on heat-related pediatric emergency department (ED) use in Germany remains limited. We quantified the acute short-term effects of extreme heat exposure on ED visits among children aged 0-18 years in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. METHODOLOGY: We assessed short-term effects of extreme heat on ED visits among children aged 0-18 years, including perinatal conditions in infants born at or after 22 weeks´ gestation, in Baden-Württemberg, Germany using 2.83 million records from (2014-2022). A time-stratified quasi-Poisson design with distributed lag non-linear model (lag 0-5 days) was applied, adjusting for air quality, spatiotemporal factors, and COVID-19 hospitalizations. RESULTS: Higher temperatures increased ED visits risk, strongest within 0-2 days. Cumulative relative risks increased by 4.2% (95% CI 3.7-4.8), 7.1% (6.1-8.1), and 9.6% (8.2-11.1) at the 95th, 99th, and 99.9th temperature percentiles, respectively. Heat-sensitive diagnoses included heat-related illnesses (+63%, 51-76), perinatal conditions (+57%, 26-92), and otitis media and externa (+25%, 16-33). Children < 5 years had higher ED visit rates share on hot days (RR 1.036, 1.02-1.05). CONCLUSION: Heat exposure increases pediatric ED use, highlighting the need of child-specific thresholds and targeted preparedness strategies. IMPACT: Extreme heat increases pediatric emergency visits, especially among infants and young children. By combining high resolution meteorological data with a large pediatric dataset and advanced time stratified modeling, the study provides detailed evidence on short-term effects of heat and identifies specific heat sensitive diagnoses. The study highlights rapid, lagged effects of heat and suggests pediatric specific temperature thresholds that may better capture risk than current heat warning thresholds. The findings support improving preparedness in pediatric emergency care and inform adaptations to heat warning-systems to better cater for child populations.

publications.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027
publications.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe), and the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database. In this publication we report on the status of InterPro (version 110.0), detailing new developments in the database, its associated web interface, and software. Notable updates include InterPro-N, a deep-learning method that increases sequence coverage of UniProtKB to over 90%; the transition from InterProScan 5 to the completely re-engineered InterProScan 6; the integration of structure-based domain classifications and predicted structures from AlphaFold; a redesigned protein viewer offering a concise summary view; and a new Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows AI assistants to query InterPro programmatically. Over the past two years, 9484 new InterPro entries have been created, bringing the total to 54 922. InterPro data, software and tools are freely available.

publications.title: A gut microbiome-kidney-heart axis predictive of future cardiovascular diseases
publications.abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) remain a major global health challenge. Early markers of disease initiation and progression are urgently needed. We, and others, have previously shown changes in the gut microbiome in association with metabolic and CVD. Here, we demonstrate that gut microbiome-related changes can be detected in association with subclinical variations in heart and kidney function. Markers related to gut microbial metabolism of aromatic amino acids, phenylalanine and tyrosine, associate with circulating pro-atrial natriuretic peptide and estimated glomerular filtration rate in a metabolically healthy European population. Observational and genetic evidence further identify microbiome-related metabolites as mediators of this gut microbiome-kidney axis, with their baseline levels associating with incident CVD in an external Canadian population. Altogether, our work suggests that the gut microbiome interacts with the cardiorenal axis and participates in an interorgan crosstalk affecting host physiology and risk of CVD.

publications.title: proGenomes4: providing 2 million accurately and consistently annotated high-quality prokaryotic genomes
publications.abstract: The pervasive availability of publicly available microbial genomes has opened many new avenues for microbiology research, yet it also demands robust quality control and consistent annotation pipelines to ensure meaningful biological insights. proGenomes4 (prokaryotic Genomes v4) addresses this challenge by providing a resource of nearly 2 million high-quality microbial genomes, a doubling in scale from previous versions, encompassing over 7 billion genes. Each genome underwent rigorous quality assessment and comprehensive functional annotation by applying multiple standardized annotation workflows, including the systematic identification of mobile genetic elements and biosynthetic gene clusters. proGenomes4 contains 32 887 species with ecological habitat metadata as well as precomputed pan-genomes. This substantially expanded resource provides the microbiology community with a foundation for large-scale comparative studies and is freely accessible via a newly developed command line interface and at https://progenomes.embl.de/.

publications.title: SMART v10: three decades of the protein domain annotation resource
publications.abstract: SMART (Simple Modular Architecture Research Tool, https://smart.embl.de) is a web-based platform for identifying and annotating protein domains and analyzing domain architectures. SMART version 10 features manually curated models for over 1300 protein domains. Approaching its 30th anniversary, SMART's user interface has been redesigned from the ground up, leveraging modern web technologies to enhance intuitiveness and usability. SMART's "Genomic" mode, which annotates proteins from completely sequenced genomes was synchronized with the current release of STRING, and now includes 12 035 species, compared to 5090 in the previous release. Protein and domain annotation pages have been updated with new information sources. Integration with eggNOG provides links to 17.5 million orthologous groups for over 53 million proteins. Additionally, synchronization with the interactive Pathways Explorer version 3 incorporates updated KEGG pathway and orthologous group data, enabling direct visualization on four distinct pathway overview maps.

publications.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2025
publications.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences into families. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and predict the presence of domains and significant sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for over 200 million sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mappings to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology (GO), Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) and the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database. In this publication, we report on the status of InterPro (version 101.0), detailing new developments in the database, associated web interface and software. Notable updates include the increased integration of structures predicted by AlphaFold and the enhanced description of protein families using artificial intelligence. Over the past two years, more than 5000 new InterPro entries have been created. The InterPro website now offers access to 85 000 protein families and domains from its member databases and serves as a long-term archive for retired databases. InterPro data, software and tools are freely available.

name: J. A. Aguilar–Saavedra
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Toponium effects on quantum steering and Bell nonlocality of top quarks
publications.abstract: We investigate quantum steering and Bell nonlocality in top-quark pair production at the LHC near threshold. The toponium contribution strengthens the spin-singlet component and substantially enhances the entanglement between the two quark spins. With current LHC data, quantum steering appears observable with a statistical significance around $10σ$. For Bell nonlocality, the statistical significance can also be high close to threshold, reaching about $9σ$, although the feasibility of such a measurement will depend crucially on the control of systematic uncertainties.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Momentum entanglement at colliders: The H → W W , Z Z case
publications.abstract: We address momentum entanglement in Higgs decays to weak boson pairs, H → W W , Z Z , by discretizing momentum space. The momenta of the two weak bosons are entangled, as well as the degrees of freedom in momentum and spin spaces. For H → Z Z in the four-lepton final state, we also estimate the statistical sensitivity of entanglement measures at the Large Hadron Collider and future upgrades. The discretization method introduced here is broadly applicable, offering a framework for studies of momentum entanglement at the energy frontier.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Time, quantum entanglement and particle decay
publications.abstract: We investigate the role of time ordering in entanglement experiments involving unstable particles, focusing on $\mu^+ \mu^-$ pairs produced in a maximally-entangled spin state. We analyse the correlations between measurements performed by two experimenters, Alice (who measures $\mu^-$ spin) and Bob (who measures $\mu^+$ decay products). Remarkably, the observed correlations persist irrespective of whether Bob's muon decays before or after Alice's spin measurement. We further discuss different interpretations of the same empirical results depending on the observer's reference frame. The findings reinforce the viewpoint that the Copenhagen interpretation of measurement is a mathematical tool rather than a literal account of physical reality.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Understanding Bell locality tests at colliders
publications.abstract: Abstract For decades, it has been known that generic local hidden-variable theories cannot be disproved by collider experiments involving decaying particles. However, if these theories satisfy a small set of mild assumptions, they become testable. In particular, this class of theories can be disproved using Bell-like inequalities for $$\mu ^+ \mu ^-$$ μ + μ - and $$\tau ^+ \tau ^-$$ τ + τ - pairs.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Measurements of Z -Boson Pair Entanglement in Decays of Higgs Bosons at the ATLAS Experiment
publications.abstract: Entanglement is a key property of quantum systems. In this Letter the first measurements of quantum entanglement between spins in pairs of Z bosons are reported, using proton-proton collision data from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at center-of-mass energies of 13 and 13.6 TeV, recorded with the ATLAS detector. Measurements of angular observables sensitive to ZZ^{*} spin-density-matrix elements in the H→ZZ^{*}→ℓ^{+}ℓ^{-}ℓ^{+}ℓ^{-} process yield coefficients C_{2,1,2,-1}=-0.71±0.45 and C_{2,2,2,-2}=0.08±0.44, consistent with their Standard Model predictions. A complementary hypothesis test using the full angular distribution, and relying on several Standard Model assumptions in the decays, provides substantially higher sensitivity to quantum correlations and disfavors the separable-state hypothesis at a significance of 4.7 standard deviations (expected 4.9σ) relative to the entangled Standard Model hypothesis. These results provide strong evidence of quantum entanglement between massive bosons (spin qutrits) at the electroweak scale.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

name: Jakob Nikolas Kather
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

publications.title: AI for detection of adverse events in the real world
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

publications.title: Artificial intelligence in oncology: from isolated task-specific tools toward integrated decision support systems
publications.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly becoming one of the most transformative forces in oncology, influencing how clinicians diagnose disease, make treatment decisions, conduct research, and generate real-world evidence. In the ‘AI in Oncology’ Special Issue of the ESMO Real World Data and Digital Oncology Journal, readers will find a comprehensive overview of this evolving landscape, beginning with perspective and review articles that provide a timely overview of how AI is reshaping the practice of oncology while simultaneously redefining the role of clinicians.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

publications.title: Extracellular matrix collagen remodeling predicts resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in mismatch repair-deficient endometrial cancer
publications.abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the therapeutic paradigm for mismatch repair-deficient endometrial cancer (MMRd EC). However, a considerable subset of patients fails to achieve durable clinical benefit. This pronounced interpatient variability underscores the urgent unmet need for mechanistic predictive biomarkers beyond MMRd status alone to guide clinical decision-making.Methods We performed a multiproteomic mass spectrometry analysis on tumor specimens from an advanced or recurrent MMRd EC cohort stratified into ICI responders (ICI-R) and non-responders (ICI-NR). Proteomic signatures were validated spatially and structurally using whole-section Masson’s Trichrome digital imaging and polarization-resolved second-harmonic generation microscopy. Machine learning algorithms were constructed to integrate extracellular matrix (ECM) structural metrics with immune parameters to build a multiparametric predictive model of ICI resistance.Results ECM remodeling emerged as the dominant proteomic program characterizing ICI resistance. Quantitative spatial imaging revealed that increased intratumoral collagen density and peripheral fiber disorganization were significantly associated with impaired CD8 + T-cell infiltration and immunotherapy failure. Integrating collagen structural metrics with immune parameters yielded a predictive score that showed promising discrimination between ICI-Rs and ICI-NRs in our cohort, providing a framework for future validation in independent cohorts.Conclusions Our findings implicate ECM remodeling as a key determinant of immune exclusion and ICI resistance in MMRd EC. These findings support developing collagen-based spatial biomarkers and stromal-targeted approaches, though the clinical utility of this predictive score requires further validation in larger, independent cohorts.

publications.title: Agentic AI Systems in Radiology: Design, Applications, Evaluation, and Challenges
publications.abstract: Building agents that perceive and act on their environment with a degree of autonomy has long been a focus of artificial intelligence research. This pursuit has become far more practical with the emergence of large language models (LLMs) capable of using natural language to integrate information, follow instructions, and perform forms of reasoning and planning across a wide range of tasks. With its multimodal data streams and orchestrated workflows spanning multiple systems, radiology is uniquely suited to benefit from agents that can adapt to context and automate complex, repetitive tasks. In radiology, LLMs and their multimodal variants have already demonstrated promising performance for individual tasks such as information extraction and report summarization. However, using LLMs in isolation underutilizes their potential to support complex, multistep workflows where decisions depend on evolving context from multiple information sources. Equipping LLMs with external tools and feedback mechanisms enables them to drive systems that exhibit a spectrum of autonomy, ranging from semiautomated workflows to more adaptive agents capable of managing complex processes. This review article examines the design of LLM-driven agentic systems, explores representative radiology applications, discusses evaluation frameworks, and outlines key challenges, including error cascades, tool-use effectiveness, and integration with health information technology infrastructure.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

publications.title: Class visualizations and activation atlases for computational pathology
publications.abstract: The clinical promise of computational pathology increasingly depends on foundation model-based pipelines, yet the morphological concepts encoded by these systems remain poorly understood. We address this gap with a concept-level visualization framework using class visualizations (CVs) and activation atlases (AAs) in a pathology foundation-model setting across colorectal tissue and multi-organ cancer tasks. Four pathologists annotate hematoxylin and eosin-stained image patches as well as generated visualizations, complemented by attribution- and similarity-based metrics. CVs retain class-associated morphology for distinct tissue classes, with reduced separability and higher annotator variability in morphologically overlapping cancer classes. AAs expose layer-dependent organization of encoded concepts, with coherent regions for coarse tissue and cancer groupings and increasing dispersion and overlap at finer label granularities. Together, these findings show that concept-level visualization makes representations learned by pathology foundation models inspectable across diagnostic difficulty levels, with feature separation decreasing and ambiguity increasing as morphological complexity and expert disagreement rise.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

publications.title: Endurance through adaptation: how agri-food policy resists reform in Austria, Germany, and Sweden
publications.abstract: How does the agri-food policy core (i.e., production and farmer orientation) persist despite sustained pressure for green transformation? Drawing on the concept of policy endurance – the preservation of the ‘policy core’ through incumbents’ strategies of ideational, institutional, and policy adaptation – we analyse agri-food policy dynamics in Austria, Germany, and Sweden. In each country, Green parties, the most likely challengers to the policy core, held government office for several years between 2014 and 2025, a period in which the European Green Deal and the Farm to Fork strategy generated pressure for change. Combining Manifesto Project data on party positions with qualitative analysis of policy documents, ministerial statements, and stakeholder assessments, we trace these three forms of strategic adaptation. We find that incumbent parties deploy such strategies to preserve the policy core. However, we challenge the argument that Green parties consistently act as challengers: in Sweden, the Greens actively endorsed the core-conforming National Food Strategy. These findings suggest that the incumbent-challenger distinction is more fluid than existing frameworks contend, that policy endurance can operate through rather than despite the absorption of reformist ideas, and that coalition politics shapes policy endurance in multiparty governments.

publications.title: Green Light for Change? Germany's Traffic Light Coalition and Energy Policy in Challenging Times
publications.abstract: The Traffic Light Coalition (Ampelkoalition) struggled to design new policies in the domain of energy policy. Heated debates, such as on the Buildings Energy Act (Gebäudeenergiegesetz), exposed difficulties in finding common ground among the political parties in the German Bundestag and among members of the coalition government. How did the parties enforce their positions on energy policy in the coalition agreement? To what extent did the coalition government adopt these energy policies from the coalition agreement? The Russian aggression against Ukraine aggravated the energy crisis and put further strain on the coalition government. How did this exogenous shock affect the adoption of the energy-specific elements of the coalition agreement and actual energy policy-making? While we would expect the crisis to serve as a catalyst for more ambitious and unified policy-making, this has not always been the case. Through content analysis of election manifestos, the coalition agreement, policy documents, and additional interview material, we review the energy policy-making process and its adoption by the former Traffic Light Coalition. The results provide us with important insights into developing resilient policy-making within uncommon coalitions in times of crisis.

publications.title: The persistence and predictability of policy tool use: Policy styles and the tools of government
publications.abstract: Abstract The relationship between “policy tools” and “policy styles” in literature is often implicit, resting on the assumption that governments’ characteristic ways of doing business shape their tool choices, without clarifying what a “style” is or how it connects to those choices. Resolving this ambiguity requires distinguishing two conceptions of policy style: a process-oriented one, describing how governments make decisions, and an output-oriented one, describing what kinds of instruments they characteristically deploy. Building on this distinction, the article introduces a three-level typology comprising a tool’s “genre,” “variation,” and “calibration” to specify at which level of abstraction a policy style exerts its influence on tool choice. Governance modes generate durable preferences primarily at the genre level – for broad categories such as regulation, public enterprises, or treasury-based instruments – rather than for specific design variations or finer calibrations. Making these linkages explicit advances understanding of policy continuity and improves prediction of future instrument choices.

publications.title: Rising health inequities require looking beyond health systems
Comparative Analysis of Intermediaries in Digital Governance
publications.abstract: Digital governance is defined by complexity, speed, and transnational reach – characteristics that challenge traditional regulatory approaches. In this evolving landscape, intermediaries have emerged as essential actors translating, shaping, and sometimes displacing formal authority. This special issue examines their role across key domains of digital governance, including platform regulation, digital sovereignty, financial oversight, and artificial intelligence (AI) auditing. Through comparative analysis, the contributions show how intermediaries – from AI tools to civil society coalitions – mediate not just implementation but the very terms of regulation. Together, they reveal how intermediation is transforming the architecture, accountability, and legitimacy of digital governance. This article synthesizes the contributions and advances a comparative perspective on how intermediaries reshape regulatory authority and accountability in digital governance.

publications.title: The 2026 report of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change: a decade of escalating health harms and a decisive moment for all
Interacting climatic, environmental, biologic and socio‐economic drivers of the global dengue expansion
publications.abstract: Dengue is the most rapidly expanding mosquito-borne viral disease worldwide. The worst year on record was 2024, with over 100 countries reporting 14.4 million cases and over 11,000 deaths. Since then, and up to August 2026, another 7.4 million cases and over 5000 deaths have been reported. The region of the Americas was impacted the most, followed by South-East Asia and the Western Pacific. Both the spread of dengue viruses (DENV) and their primary vectors, Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, are driven by several factors. Globalization has accelerated vector dispersal, particularly through international trade and transportation networks. The movement of desiccation-resistant eggs in used-vehicle tyres and the inadvertent transport of adult mosquitoes via trucks and passenger vehicles have enabled the establishment of vector populations in previously uncolonized regions. Human mobility and unplanned urbanization further contribute to dengue emergence by introducing DENV into susceptible populations where competent vectors circulate. Climate change has enhanced dengue transmission potential by altering temperature and rainfall patterns that influence mosquito survival, reproduction, biting behaviour and viral replication. Containing or even reversing this global dengue expansion will require a complementary set of interventions that rely on proven and novel control strategies, including sterile insect techniques, Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes, virus-resistant mosquito strains through CRISPR-Cas9 gene drive, vaccines, antiviral drug prophylaxis and urban interventions that eliminate Aedes habitats. Building climate-resilient urban environments through sustainable development to minimize the urban heat island effect and advancing climate-informed early warning systems are long-term strategies for effective dengue control.

publications.title: The 2026 Europe Cities Report of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change: cities at the forefront of climate change action
publications.abstract: Translations For the French and Spanish translations of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

publications.title: The hidden consequences of marine heatwaves: rising Vibrio risk in European coastal waters
publications.abstract: It is becoming alarmingly easy to grow accustomed to an unrelenting succession of broken climate records. June 2026 was the warmest June ever recorded in Western Europe, with mean temperatures reaching 3.06 °C above the 1991–2020 average and surpassing the previous record set only a year earlier.1 While prolonged terrestrial heatwaves dominate public attention, because of their immediate impacts on human health, they often overshadow equally profound changes occurring in the oceans. During the same month, the western Mediterranean Sea and adjacent Atlantic coastal waters experienced a record-breaking marine heatwave.

publications.title: Navigating global health futures under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
publications.abstract: The Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) provide valuable insights to understand how future socioeconomic changes could alter the magnitude and pattern of climate-related risks across sectors, which might facilitate or hinder adaptation and mitigation responses. Many sectors have created SSP narrative extensions to specify insights for their domains. In this Viewpoint, we created health narrative extensions for the SSPs, considering socioeconomic and demographic drivers and population health and health-system drivers. The projected health-relevant trajectories diverge substantially over the course of the 21st century. The SSP3 and SSP4 narratives detail changes that could contribute considerable risks to health, whereas the SSP1 and SSP5 narratives highlight the role of effective governance and adequate resourcing in reducing climate-sensitive population health outcomes and health-system drivers. Given that climate forcing is considered exogenous to these narrative extensions, SSP5's favourable health driver paths do not account for the potential adverse impacts of this high-emissions pathway. The narratives elaborate population health drivers that can improve the policy relevance of population health and health-system risk projections associated with climate change across a range of possible pathways, and link these drivers with relevant cross-sectoral issues (eg, water and energy). Further research is required to quantify key drivers of population health and health-system risks at global to local scales.

publications.title: Escape from replicative crisis and immortalization precedes complex genome evolution
publications.abstract: Shortening of telomeres restricts the proliferative capacity of human somatic cells by inducing replicative senescence and crisis. During cancerous transformation, premalignant cells must overcome these barriers and acquire replicative immortality. Single-cell DNA strand-specific genome sequencing of crisis cells revealed extreme genome instability characterized by complex chromosomal abnormalities. Unexpectedly, spontaneously emerging postcrisis clones showed relatively few and simple structural variants. However, with accumulating divisions following crisis escape, the genomes of immortal postcrisis clones evolve and amass genomic alterations, including tetraploidization events with subsequent losses and gains of individual chromosomes. Our data point towards a new model of tumorigenesis in which crisis acts as a strong selective barrier against cells with aberrant karyotypes, and in which high karyotypic complexity is acquired after immortalization and crisis escape.

publications.title: Circular DNA exposes a weakness in cancer cells
Comprehensive benchmarking of somatic mutation detection by the SMaHT Network
publications.abstract: Somatic mosaicism is increasingly recognized as a fundamental feature of human biology, yet the detection of somatic mutations remains challenging. The Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network conducted large-scale benchmarking experiments involving cell lines and donor tissues to evaluate sequencing technologies, experimental approaches, and computational methods for detecting different types of somatic mutations, generating community resources with >1,000× short-read and 100-400× long-read data for nine analyzed samples. We determined effective strategies for utilizing short- and long-read sequencing for mutation detection and demonstrated that using donor-specific and pangenome-inferred diploid assemblies improved calling, extending mutation catalogs to challenging genomic regions. We benchmarked six duplex technologies and showed that single-cell sequencing resolves cell-type-specific mutational patterns and heterogeneity. Our results indicate that bulk, single-cell, and duplex analyses are complementary and that leveraging all three provides comprehensive characterization of mosaicism within tissues. Together, these findings provide the scientific and clinical communities with a roadmap for accurate genome-wide somatic mutation analysis.

publications.title: Divergent medulloblastoma chromatin states disclose KDM2B as a selective dependency
publications.abstract: Medulloblastoma is a biologically heterogeneous childhood cerebellar tumor harboring frequent chromatin-modifying gene alterations. How these alterations promote transcriptional programs governing malignancy remains poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we evaluated chromatin states across medulloblastoma subgroups by multi-modal integration of histone modifications with mutational, DNA methylation and transcriptomic profiles. A bivalent/poised enhancer (EnhBiv) state was specifically enriched at the promoters of neurodevelopmental genes in Group 3/4 medulloblastoma. Integrative bioinformatics coupled with chromatin occupancy studies identified aberrant KDM2B binding at EnhBiv-enriched promoters. CRISPR-mediated knockout or acute protein degradation of KDM2B selectively suppressed the growth of medulloblastoma models in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, KDM2B promotes sequential recruitment of Polycomb repressive complexes (PRC1/PRC2) and EnhBiv chromatin, thereby repressing neuronal differentiation programs. Collectively, we provide foundational insights into an epigenetic basis of medulloblastoma, nominating KDM2B as a selective dependency in high-risk subgroups that warrants consideration as a candidate therapeutic target.

publications.title: Resource-efficient Strand-seq library preparation in microliter volumes: a one-pot-style adaptation for standard laboratory infrastructure
publications.abstract: Strand-seq is a single-cell sequencing method that preserves directionality of DNA template strands, enabling chromosome-length haplotyping, structural variant discovery, and sister chromatid exchange mapping. The conventional, microliter-scale protocol is reliable but consumable-intensive, requiring five bead-based DNA cleanups and individual per-cell processing across a 96-well plate. A nanoliter-scale, one-pot (OP) adaptation nearly eliminates bead cleanups and plastic consumables in sub-microliter volumes on bespoke nanoarrays, but requires an acoustic dispenser, custom array hardware, and humidity-controlled dispensing not widely available. Here we describe OP-style Strand-seq, a microliter-volume adaptation retaining the central efficiency principles of the one-pot method (pooled MNase digestion, cumulative reagent addition with minimal intermediate purification, and protease-based enzyme inactivation in place of most bead cleanups) while compatible with standard 96- or 384-well plates, liquid-handling robots, and manual pipetting. Relative to the conventional protocol, OP-style Strand-seq reduces tip consumption ∼60% and eliminates three of five cleanup steps, without specialized nanodispensing hardware. • Retains pooled MNase digestion and protease-based enzyme inactivation from the one-pot method, in microliter rather than nanoliter volumes. • Requires two bead-based cleanups instead of five, and no specialized nanoliter dispensing hardware. • Compatible with manual pipetting, liquid-handling robots, or acoustic dispensing in 384-well format, adoptable across diverse laboratory infrastructure.

publications.title: Three Decades of Socioeconomic Inequality in India's Breastfeeding Indicators, 1993–2021
publications.abstract: Although existing literature heavily focuses on the health outcomes of exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) in India, studies addressing socioeconomic inequalities across a broad spectrum of breastfeeding indicators remain scarce. We utilized five waves of National Family Health Survey data (1993-2021) to analyze temporal trends and socioeconomic inequalities, proxied by maternal education (no formal schooling, 1st-5th grade, 6th-8th grade, 9th-12th grade, and above 12th grade) and household wealth (poorest, poorer, middle, richer, and richest) across six World Health Organization-recommended indicators: ever breastfed, early initiation of breastfeeding (EIBF), exclusive breastfeeding for the first 2 days after birth, EBF, mixed milk feeding (MixMF), and continued breastfeeding. We estimated absolute and relative inequalities between the lowest and highest categories of each socioeconomic marker, followed by the computation of the Annual Absolute Change to assess progress over time (1993-2021). Between 1993 and 2021, absolute inequality in EIBF remained stagnant between the two extreme maternal education levels. EBF disparities shifted significantly; the initial advantage held by mothers with no formal schooling in 1993 narrowed as the gap closed, a trend mirrored across household wealth quintiles where the poorest maintained a higher, albeit diminishing, lead in EBF prevalence. EIBF increased at an equal annualized rate across both the lowest and highest education strata, and MixMF rose more sharply among the poorest households. Addressing these shifting socioeconomic disparities is critical for achieving equitable breastfeeding outcomes across all strata, especially given the recent (2024) reported decline in EBF prevalence nationally.

publications.title: Prevalence of Overweight and Obesity Among Children Younger Than 5 Years in India
publications.abstract: Importance: Evidence is lacking on long-term trends across Indian states and union territories (UTs) and on the attainability of the 2030 Global Nutrition Target (GNT) goals within these specific regions. Objectives: To estimate the trends in overweight and obesity among children younger than 5 years across 36 states and UTs in India between 2006 and 2024 and to assess the feasibility of achieving the GNT of restricting the overweight burden to 5% or less by 2030. Design, Setting, and Participants: For this cross-sectional study, microdata and aggregate data were used from the 4 most recent waves of the National Family Health Survey (repeated cross-sectional surveys conducted between January 1, 2006, and December 31, 2024). The analysis included individual-level samples of 41 306 children in 2006, 225 002 in 2016, and 201 687 in 2021, alongside aggregate estimates of overweight from the 2024 wave. Data were analyzed in January and updated in July 2026. Main Outcomes and Measures: Following World Health Organization definitions of overweight and obesity in children younger than 5 years (overweight is defined as weight for height >2 SDs above the World Health Organization median and obesity as >3 SDs), their prevalence and standardized annualized changes for 5 timeframes (2006-2016, 2016-2021, 2021-2024, 2006-2021, and 2006-2024) were computed. Additionally, the fractional logistic regression was used to model national and state-level overweight trajectories, forecasting probability of achieving the 5% or less 2030 GNT threshold. Results: The final sample included 467 995 children (241 645 [51.6%] male, 226 350 [48.4%] female) aged 0 to 59 months from NFHSs conducted between 2006 and 2021. Mean (SD) child age remained consistent from 2006 to 2021: 30.1 (17.1) months in 2006, 30.1 (17.0) months in 2016, and 29.9 (17.2) months in 2021. Between 2006 and 2021, the prevalence of overweight increased from 1.55% to 3.42%, whereas obesity prevalence increased from 0.50% to 1.30% before overweight prevalence decreased to 1.3% in 2024. Although India was projected to sustain the 2030 overweight target nationally, 9 states and UTs (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura) maintained a low to moderate probability of adherence. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cross-sectional study of Indian children younger than 5 years from 2006 to 2024, a historical overweight increase reversed in 2024. However, profound subnational disparities remained, suggesting that targeted regional interventions are needed to achieve the 2030 GNT.

publications.title: COVID-19 lockdown and coverage of maternal health and nutrition care in rural West Bengal, India: a single interrupted time-series analysis
publications.abstract: Abstract While COVID-19 lockdowns globally disrupted healthcare, the extent of changes in India’s maternal health and nutrition services coverage in rural settings requires further empirical investigation. Utilizing data from 57,371 pregnancies recorded between January 2012 and December 2023, by a health and demographic surveillance system in rural West Bengal, India, this study employed a single interrupted time-series analysis to examine changes in coverage of three key indicators following the COVID-19 lockdown (during March 25- May 31, 2020): receipt of ≥ 4 antenatal care visits (ANC), consumption of ≥ 100 iron-and-folic acid (IFA) tablets/ equivalent syrup, and institutional delivery. Of 57,371 pregnancies, 34.5% (95%CI: 34.1, 34.9%) accessed ≥ 4 ANC visits, 38.7% (95%CI: 38.3, 39.1%) consumed ≥ 100 IFA tablets/ equivalent syrup, and 87.3% (95%CI: 87.0, 87.5%) had institutional delivery. Between January 2012 and December 2023, relative to the pre-lockdown trend, a decreasing trend in the coverage of ≥ 4 ANC visits (β: -0.22, 95%CI: -0.31, -0.12, p < 0.001) and in the prevalence of institutional delivery (β: -0.17, 95%CI: -0.21, -0.13, p < 0.001) was observed. A downward trend in consumption of ≥ 100 IFA tablets/ equivalent syrup was observed (β: -0.58, 95%CI: -0.89, -0.27, p = 0.001) for a narrower time frame of January 2019 to December 2021.

publications.title: Author Correction: Obesity rise plateaus in developed nations and accelerates in developing nations
publications.abstract: In the version of the article initially published, María Elena Díaz-Sánchez, Patricia Varona-Pérez and Ramón Suárez-Medina (all affiliated with the National Institute of Hygiene, Epidemiology and Microbiology, Havana, Cuba) were inadvertently omitted from the list of NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC) members and have now been added in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

publications.title: Reducing early secondary school leaving: experimental evidence on information, tutoring, and incentives from Burkina Faso
publications.abstract: Despite major gains in primary school enrollment across low- and middle-income countries, secondary school completion remains low. We conducted a randomized controlled trial in Burkina Faso to evaluate the effectiveness of three interventions designed to reduce early secondary school leaving: (i) information on the economic and health returns to education, (ii) tailored tutoring, and (iii) conditional cash incentives. The cash intervention significantly increased school enrollment, any school attendance, and regular attendance, and reduced the total number of school days missed. Tutoring significantly increased school enrollment, while its effects on regular attendance and academic progression were imprecisely estimated. The information intervention generated limited evidence of impacts, with no statistically significant effects on the primary outcome or academic progression and only marginal evidence of an increase in any school attendance. Financial and academic support can help adolescents who left school early re-enroll, but larger studies are needed to identify which interventions most effectively sustain regular attendance.

name: Jens Antony
subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
topics: Advanced Physical and Chemical Molecular Interactions

publications.title: The first microsolvation step for furans: New experiments and benchmarking strategies
publications.abstract: The site-specific first microsolvation step of furan and some of its derivatives with methanol is explored to benchmark the ability of quantum-chemical methods to describe the structure, energetics, and vibrational spectrum at low temperature. Infrared and microwave spectra in supersonic jet expansions are used to quantify the docking preference and some relevant quantum states of the model complexes. Microwave spectroscopy strictly rules out in-plane docking of methanol as opposed to the top coordination of the aromatic ring. Contrasting comparison strategies, which emphasize either the experimental or the theoretical input, are explored. Within the harmonic approximation, only a few composite computational approaches are able to achieve a satisfactory performance. Deuteration experiments suggest that the harmonic treatment itself is largely justified for the zero-point energy, likely and by design due to the systematic cancellation of important anharmonic contributions between the docking variants. Therefore, discrepancies between experiment and theory for the isomer abundance are tentatively assigned to electronic structure deficiencies, but uncertainties remain on the nuclear dynamics side. Attempts to include anharmonic contributions indicate that for systems of this size, a uniform treatment of anharmonicity with systematically improved performance is not yet in sight.

publications.title: Far-IR and UV spectral signatures of controlled complexation and microhydration of the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon acenaphthene
publications.abstract: In this work we report on the experimental and theoretical investigations of the progressional complexation of the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) acenaphthene with itself and with water. In the interstellar medium, PAH complexes are an important link between molecular gas and solid state configurations of carbon, and in the form of grains they are postulated to serve as chemical catalysts. However, no direct detection of PAHs or their (microhydrated) complexes in interstellar space has been achieved as of yet. Therefore, we provide UV and far-infrared ion dip spectra of homogeneous PAH multimers and their hydrated clusters. The far-IR region of the IR spectrum is especially interesting since it contains the most spectral features that arise due to complexation or microhydration. We present microhydrated PAH complexes up to the third order, where we show that the water clusters are locked with little perturbation on the different PAH platforms. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations involving hydrogen bond interactions still seem challenging for predicting the far-IR frequency range, although applying anharmonic corrections leads to slight improvements.

publications.title: The furan microsolvation blind challenge for quantum chemical methods: First steps
publications.abstract: Herein we present the results of a blind challenge to quantum chemical methods in the calculation of dimerization preferences in the low temperature gas phase. The target of study was the first step of the microsolvation of furan, 2-methylfuran and 2,5-dimethylfuran with methanol. The dimers were investigated through IR spectroscopy of a supersonic jet expansion. From the measured bands, it was possible to identify a persistent hydrogen bonding OH-O motif in the predominant species. From the presence of another band, which can be attributed to an OH-π interaction, we were able to assert that the energy gap between the two types of dimers should be less than or close to 1 kJ/mol across the series. These values served as a first evaluation ruler for the 12 entries featured in the challenge. A tentative stricter evaluation of the challenge results is also carried out, combining theoretical and experimental results in order to define a smaller error bar. The process was carried out in a double-blind fashion, with both theory and experimental groups unaware of the results on the other side, with the exception of the 2,5-dimethylfuran system which was featured in an earlier publication.

publications.title: HYDROPHOBE Challenge: A Joint Experimental and Computational Study on the Host–Guest Binding of Hydrocarbons to Cucurbiturils, Allowing Explicit Evaluation of Guest Hydration Free-Energy Contributions
publications.abstract: The host–guest complexation of hydrocarbons (22 guest molecules) with cucurbit[7]uril was investigated in aqueous solution using the indicator displacement strategy. The binding constants (10 3 –10 9 M –1 ) increased with guest size, pointing to the hydrophobic effect and dispersion interactions as driving forces. The measured affinities provide unique benchmark data for the binding of neutral guest molecules. Consequently, a computational blind challenge, the HYDROPHOBE challenge, was conducted to allow a comparison with state-of-the-art computational methods for predicting host–guest affinity constants. In total, three quantum-chemical (QM) data sets and two explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (MD) submissions were received. When searching for sources of uncertainty in predicting the host–guest affinities, the experimentally known hydration energies of the investigated hydrocarbons were used to test the employed solvation models (explicit solvent for MD and COSMO-RS for QM). Good correlations were obtained for both solvation models, but a rather constant offset was observed for the COSMO data, by ca. +2 kcal mol –1, which was traced back to a required reference-state correction in the QM submissions (2.38 kcal mol –1 ). Introduction of the reference-state correction improved the predictive power of the QM methods, particularly for small hydrocarbons up to C5.

publications.title: Intramolecular London Dispersion Interaction Effects on Gas-Phase and Solid-State Structures of Diamondoid Dimers
publications.abstract: The covalent diamantyl (C 28 H 38 ) and oxadiamantyl (C 26 H 34 O 2 ) dimers are stabilized by London dispersion attractions between the dimer moieties. Their solid-state and gas-phase structures were studied using a multitechnique approach, including single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD), gas-phase electron diffraction (GED), a combined GED/microwave (MW) spectroscopy study, and quantum chemical calculations. The inclusion of medium-range electron correlation as well as the London dispersion energy in density functional theory is essential to reproduce the experimental geometries. The conformational dynamics computed for C 26 H 34 O 2 agree well with solution NMR data and help in the assignment of the gas-phase MW data to individual diastereomers. Both in the solid state and the gas phase the central C–C bond is of similar length for the diamantyl [XRD, 1.642(2) Å; GED, 1.630(5) Å] and the oxadiamantyl dimers [XRD, 1.643(1) Å; GED, 1.632(9) Å; GED+MW, 1.632(5) Å], despite the presence of two oxygen atoms. Out of a larger series of quantum chemical computations, the best match with the experimental reference data is achieved with the PBEh-3c, PBE0-D3, PBE0, B3PW91-D3, and M06-2X approaches. This is the first gas-phase confirmation that the markedly elongated C–C bond is an intrinsic feature of the molecule and that crystal packing effects have only a minor influence.

name: Jeroen Krijgsveld
topics: Retinoids in leukemia and cellular processes

publications.title: Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P
publications.abstract: Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics data remains an unmet challenge in the post-genomics era, discouraging researchers from pursuing integrative approaches to molecular biology research. Leveraging the power of translation profiling, we present RNA to Translation to Protein (R2T2P), a computational platform integrating genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translation and proteins, including a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. We applied R2T2P to investigate a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), where ectopic expression of the DUX4 retrogene in skeletal muscle triggers significant alterations in transcription and RNA metabolism. We uncovered hundreds of uncharacterized, highly overexpressed RNAs, including antisense and alternative transcripts, and quantified their contribution to translatome and proteome. Re-analysis of expression datasets from patient-derived myotubes and muscle biopsies validated this alternative transcriptome in FSHD patients, adding a reservoir of bona-fide novel molecular actors in a rare disease. Available at https://github.com/nfdata-omics/R2T2P/, R2T2P is a flexible and powerful workflow in modern integrative biology.

publications.title: Neuroendocrine Differentiation Mediates Escape from HER2-Targeted Therapy in Breast Cancer
publications.abstract: Neuroendocrine differentiation (NED) promotes lineage plasticity and therapy resistance in prostate and lung cancers. Here we identify NED as a route of treatment escape in breast cancer: neuroendocrine features emerged or increased in 22% of progressive cases, predominantly, but not exclusively, in HER2-positive subtype. Using patient-derived, epithelial/neuroendocrine organoid and xenograft models, we map the epigenetic and transcriptional divergence between epithelial and neuroendocrine states arising from a shared mutational background and define a breast cancer neuroendocrine signature. NED involves epigenetic silencing of EpCAM and amplified HER2, while NEUROD1 functions as a master transcriptional regulator of the neuroendocrine fate. NCAM-positive putative circulating tumor cells were detected in patients in whom EpCAM-based detection had failed. Neuroendocrine tumor cells exhibit an FGFR1 dependency associated with NCAM-FGFR1 interaction and mesenchymal FGFR1 splicing. Together, these findings establish NED as a mechanism of escape from HER2-targeted therapy in breast cancer, with implications for disease monitoring and intervention.

publications.title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning
publications.abstract: Proteins are the main drivers of cell function and disease, making proteomics a powerful technique for biomarker discovery and defining cell identity. While current technologies can profile thousands of proteins and reach single-cell sensitivity, limited throughput restricts applications such as robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts. To close this gap, we present a deep-learning (DL) approach for the direct analysis of mass spectrometric (MS) data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity. Specifically, we introduce the ProFormer, a transformer pipeline that classifies samples by tabular MS1-level features derived from peptide ions, eliminating the need for time-consuming data interpretation. The ProFormer outperforms traditional machine-learning and image-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs), demonstrating enhanced classification and generalization over 14 evaluated architectures. We further provide detailed insights into how the ProFormer dynamically aggregates MS1 data, while preserving signal contribution and enabling explainable AI at single-peptide resolution. Applied to diverse LC-MS data sets, the ProFormer accurately classified single-cell proteomes by cell type, cycle stage or differentiation trajectory, as well as patient disease status from plasma proteomes. Thereby, the ProFormer provides a versatile and rapid framework for the classification of proteomic data, with important implications for patient stratification, early detection and single-cell analysis.

publications.title: Oncogenic fusions induce an extensive cancer-restricted cryptic proteome in Ewing sarcoma
publications.abstract: Abstract How tumors generate a cryptic “dark” proteome absent from healthy tissues, and whether it can be reversibly activated, remains unclear. In Ewing sarcoma, all tumors are driven by EWSR1::ETS fusions, making it a tractable model to study dark proteome activation. Integrating matched transcriptomes, translatomes and proteomes from 48 patient tumors with long-read RNA sequencing, single-cell Ribo-seq, proteomics and immunopeptidomics in cell line models, we show that EWSR1::FLI1 acts as a reversible switch recurrently inducing hundreds of cancer-specific neoproteins. Many arise from canonical coding regions via intragenic transcription start sites, generating truncated or out-of-frame neoproteins. We uncover a fusion-dependent increase in ribosomal readthrough into poly(A) tails, generating a stable 80-amino-acid TRPM4 neoprotein that, despite lacking a stop codon, is the most abundant tumor-specific microprotein across patients. Proteomic, immunopeptidomic, and immunofluorescence analyses validate neoproteins as tumor-restricted antigens, revealing a therapeutically actionable cancer dark proteome controlled by one oncogenic fusion. Highlights Fusion proteins activate in- and out-of-frame neoproteins through intragenic transcription. Neoproteins exhibit distinct protein structures and localizations compared to their host genes. Mass spectrometry detects 911 cryptic proteins, including 29 EwS neoproteins, 15 HLA-I presented. TRPM4-dORF is a stop-less 80-aa neoprotein with abundant peptide evidence exclusively in EwS.

publications.title: Functional characterization of snoRNA-derived RNA (sdRNA) expression in healthy hematopoiesis and acute myeloid leukemia
publications.abstract: SnoRNAs are highly expressed in AML and have implications in leukemogenesis and leukemic maintenance. SnoRNAs can be further processed into snoRNA-derived RNAs (sdRNAs). The role of sdRNAs in AML and healthy hematopoiesis remains largely elusive. We characterized sdRNA and snoRNA levels in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), healthy WBCs, and 159 intensively treated AML patient samples at initial diagnosis. HSPCs, healthy WBCs, and AML blasts could be differentiated by their sdRNA expression pattern in a cell-type-specific manner. In AML, high sd3'-RNA/snoRNA-host gene ratios were associated with an inverse patient outcome. Particularly, in NPM1-mutated patients with favorable risk stratification and good initial therapy response, high sd3'-RNA ratios identified a subgroup with inferior outcome. High sd3'-RNA ratios were associated with altered oncogenic, inflammatory, and immune response signaling. Forced expression of single sdRNAs, such as sd3'-SNORD78, sd3'-SNORD76, and sd5'-SNORD93, enhanced clonogenic potential in AML and drove sdRNA-specific gene expression signatures in both AML and healthy HSPCs. Exemplarily, we propose and characterize NUDT21, an important regulator of alternative polyadenylation and oncogenic gene expression, as a downstream target of sd3'-SNORD78 in AML. Our data introduce sdRNAs as standalone regulatory effector molecules in healthy hematopoiesis and AML.

publications.title: Role of IL-17 cytokines in tubal fibrosis and infertility due to salpingitis
publications.abstract: This review systematically examines the etiology and pathophysiology mechanisms of infectious diseases affecting the female reproductive tract, with a specific focus on the intricate relationship between inflammatory lesions in the fallopian tubes and reproductive dysfunction. The interleukin-17 cytokine family, as pivotal inflammatory regulators, plays a central role in pathological processes of fallopian tube inflammatory responses, tissue fibrosis, and fertility impairment through a multi-faceted regulatory network. IL-17 C and IL-17 A, key members of the IL-17 family, are pivotal drivers of fibrosis. IL-17 A activates Th17 cells and T cells, promoting the release of inflammatory factors. Furthermore, IL-17 C boosts the expression of IL-17 A, establishing a positive feedback loop that amplifies both inflammatory and fibrotic responses. This exacerbates tissue damage, ultimately culminating in luminal obstruction and dysfunction that hinders gamete transport and fertilization. Although the precise pathogenic mechanisms of tubal inflammatory infertility are not fully elucidated, the detrimental impact of tubal inflammation on fertility is widely recognized. This is particularly relevant given the increasing trend of delayed childbearing. While perioperative interventions can partially mitigate infertility risk, persistent inflammatory stimulation remains the primary pathological factor driving infertility. By systematically investigating the epidemiological characteristics and pathogenesis of this condition, this study aims to enhance clinical treatment strategies.

publications.title: NLRP3 Inflammasome in Gynecologic Inflammatory Diseases: Mechanisms, Pathophysiology, and Therapeutic Strategies
publications.abstract: The NOD-like receptor family containing pyridine domain 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome serves as a pivotal mediator of innate immune responses and a central driver of inflammatory processes. Upon detection of pathogenic or danger-associated signals, it assembles into a multiprotein complex that activates caspase-1, thereby promoting the maturation and release of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-1β and inducing pyroptotic cell death. NLRP3 inflammasome activation is regulated by highly diverse yet tightly controlled mechanisms, and its dysregulation has been implicated in various pathological conditions. Inflammatory gynecologic disorders [such as endometritis, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), and endometriosis (EMS)] are typically characterized by chronicity, with persistent and recurrent symptoms that significantly compromise patients' quality of life. Although conventional anti-inflammatory drugs are widely used, their clinical efficacy is often limited. Emerging evidence has underscored the pivotal role of NLRP3 inflammasome in the pathogenesis of these conditions, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic target. This review summarized current knowledge on the mechanisms of NLRP3 inflammasome activation in gynecologic inflammatory diseases and explored possible therapeutic strategies targeting modulating NLRP3 inflammasome activation to alleviate disease progression.

publications.title: Threshold Effects of Nitrogen Fertilization Rates on Growth and Essential Oil Yield with Component Regulation in Cinnamomum camphora var. linaloolifera
publications.abstract: The determination of an optimal nitrogen (N) fertilization rate is critical for the sustainable large-scale cultivation of Cinnamomum camphora var. linaloolifera for essential oil production. Both suboptimal and excessive nitrogen inputs can adversely affect plant sustainable development and essential oil biosynthesis, underscoring the necessity of precise nutrient management. This study investigated the effects of five N application rates (0, 45, 90, 135, and 180 kg·hm−2) on vegetative growth, essential oil yield, and quality. Growth parameters, including plant height, basal diameter, specific leaf area (SLA), and essential oil yield and yield rate. Oil composition was characterized via gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The application of 90 kg·hm−2 N significantly enhanced plant height (74.31%), basal diameter (54.95%), SLA (20.91%), and biomass (181.8%) relative to the nitrogen-free control. Nitrogen uptake was concentrated in foliar tissues, accounting for 82.8% of total plant nitrogen accumulation. This fertilization rate also maximized essential oil yield (9.15 g·plant−1) and yield rate (2.44%), reflecting increases of 178.9% and 24.49%, respectively. Linalool was the predominant oil constituent (89.84–91.81%), with its highest concentration observed at the 90 kg·hm−2 treatment. At this rate, the relative abundance of oxygenated compounds increased by 0.97%, while hydrocarbon content decreased by 0.62%, indicating a qualitative improvement in oil composition. The findings reveal a threshold response to nitrogen input, wherein rates exceeding 90 kg·hm−2 did not confer further benefits and may reduce efficiency. Collectively, these results suggest that a nitrogen application rate of 90 kg·hm−2 optimally enhances vegetative growth, nitrogen assimilation, and both the quantitative and qualitative traits of essential oils in C. camphora var. linaloolifera.

publications.title: Strigolactones optimise plant water usage by modulating vessel formation
publications.abstract: Abstract Wood formation is crucial for plant growth, enabling water and nutrient transport through vessel elements, derived from cambium stem cells (CSCs). CSCs produce vascular cell types in a bidirectional manner, but their regulation and cell fate trajectories remain unclear. Here, using single-cell transcriptome analysis in Arabidopsis thaliana , we reveal that the strigolactone (SL) signalling pathway negatively regulates vessel element formation, impacting plant water usage. While SL signalling is generally active in differentiating vascular tissues, it is low in developing vessels and CSCs, where it modulates cell fate decisions and drought response. SL-dependent changes in vessel element formation directly affect transpiration rates via stomata, underscoring the importance of vascular tissue composition in water balance. Our findings demonstrate the role of structural alignment in water-transport tissues under unstable water conditions, offering insights for enhancing drought resistance in plants through long-term modulation of vascular development.
topics: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

publications.title: Modeling of Metal Fiber-Enhanced Ion Transport in Lithium-Ion Batteries
publications.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries employing a metal fiber fleece as a 3D current collector show an improved ion diffusivity in the electrolyte due to additional surface transport in the electrical double layer at the fiber surface. Since the metal fiber fleece is electrochemically inactive, the objective is to identify a fiber architecture where the enhanced diffusivity overcompensates for the inactive volume penalty. For optimization of the copper fiber architecture in a graphite half-cell, a reduced Poisson-Boltzmann model coupled with a surface diffusion mechanism is fitted against microfluidic channel experiments and integrated into a pseudo-two-dimensional (P2D) battery model. Full-cell reconstruction with a virtual NMC111 cathode enables evaluation of the volumetric energy and power density as optimization objectives. C-rate, electrode thickness, fiber radius and fiber volume fraction are varied to quantify their effect on energy and power. The optimization at fixed electrode thicknesses and given fiber radii identifies design guidelines for the optimal fiber volume fraction across power demands: At low power, fewer metal fibers minimize the inactive volume penalty. More metal fibers are required for high power applications to increase the specific metal fiber surface area and thus the surface transport in the electrical double layer. Compared to electrodes with current collector foils, the power density at SE=350WhL improves by up to 38% for a fixed fiber radius of rmetal=6.65μm.

publications.title: Giant Vesicle Platform for Synthetic Endoplasmic Reticulum Networks
publications.abstract: Abstract The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a membrane-bound organelle found in all eukaryotic cells. This organelle has a fascinating morphology, which involves a network of membrane nanotubes and three-way junctions connecting three nanotubes. Previous reconstitution studies were based on proteo-liposomes with a size of 100 to 200 nanometers, using electron microscopy as the main method to image the resulting membrane morphologies. These studies revealed the importance of membrane GTPases, that is, membrane proteins that hydrolyse GTP. Here, we introduce an alternative platform for the formation of synthetic ER networks starting from giant unilamellar vesicles with a typical size of 10 mirometers and containing a single membrane GTPase such as atlastin from fruit flies or Sey1 from yeast. This giant vesicle approach makes the networks accessible to optical microscopy, by which one can elucidate both their structure and their dynamics. We first demonstrate that the membranes’ propensity to form synthetic ER networks depends strongly on the lipid composition. More precisely, we show that this propensity varies non-monotonically with the mole fraction of cholesterol and that the frequency of three-way junctions has a maximum for an optimal mole fraction between 10 and 15 mol%. This optimal value is comparable to the mole fraction of cholesterol as estimated for ER membranes in vivo. We also demonstrate the formation of synthetic ER networks when the membranes contain only the membrane GTPase Sey1 but no other membrane protein, which implies that Sey1 is able on its own to generate a high membrane curvature. Based on the reconstitution approach introduced here, the synthetic ER networks can now be further investigated using the versatile toolbox that has been developed for giant vesicles.

publications.title: A Particle-Based Model for Optimization of Lithium-Ion Battery Electrodes
publications.abstract: For the optimization of electrode structures, a predictive modeling framework is desirable. So-called first-principles models address this requirement by incorporating experimentally characterized material properties. Together with a fully resolved digital representation of the electrode structure, first-principles models provide excellent prediction accuracy and remain predictive for changing geometries. However, their high computational cost makes them unsuitable for electrode optimization. To overcome this limitation, we employ a previously derived 1D particle-based model which reduces the fully resolved model across two scales: porous electrode level and particle level. The model combines effective transport properties at the porous electrode level with a time-dependent, particle-based description that accounts for single-particle morphology. We present a workflow for the full parameterization of the 1D particle-based model using a graphite half-cell. Material properties and the reconstructed electrode structure are obtained from experimental characterization, from which the effective transport properties can be derived. The particle-based properties are obtained from fully resolved first-principles simulations of single particles. Validation of the 1D particle-based model indicates prediction errors comparable to or lower than those of the P2D model. Due to its first-principles-based parameters, which incorporate real particle morphology without empirical fitting, the proposed framework is well-suited for predictive optimization of electrode structures.

publications.title: Evaluation of 3D Copper Microfiber Current Collector with Chemically Prelithiated Symmetric Lithium Titanate Cells
publications.abstract: Lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery energy density can be improved with the application of novel current collector (CC) architec-tures to allow for higher capacity electrodes that minimize the relative amount of electrochemically inactive materials. In this work, an architecture consisting of three-dimensional (3D) interconnected copper microfiber (CuMF) CCs for the negative electrode were investigated to create high areal capacity lithium titanate (LTO) electrodes up to 7.3 mAh cm −2 . The effect of changing electrode parameters, such as fiber and active material loading, on rate capability and electrode impedance were studied by testing cyclable LTO symmetric cells that were prepared with a chemical prelithiation process. Through optimizing the volumetric CuMF content, a reduction in charge-transfer resistance was achieved.

publications.title: Stress granule phase separation in stress-responsive cytosolic extract-in-oil droplets
publications.abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are biomolecular condensates that form transiently in the cytosol of mammalian cells in response to stress. Dysregulation of their assembly or disassembly is implicated in human age-related diseases. While phase separation is the key process underlying SG assembly, understanding of their function, composition and regulation in response to physiological stimuli is limited. This knowledge gap reflects the challenge of gaining comprehensive and quantitative insights into the dynamic regulation of the complex composition of SGs at the single-cell level. Here we present an emulsion-based microfluidics method to overcome this limitation. "Cytosolic extracts-in-oil droplets" (CEODs) recreate a confined active cytosolic milieu that undergoes phase separation and SG formation in response to stress under physiological conditions. This approach led to the discovery of seven previously unrecognised SG components involved in signalling pathways. CEODs provide a versatile and cost-effective screening platform for future mechanistic and therapeutic studies.
