publications.title: Vermittlung von Wissenschaftskompetenz in der Aus-, Weiter- und Fortbildung von Ärztinnen und Ärzten
publications.abstract: Objectives: Curricula of medical and dental schools at German universities as well as subsequent residency programmes aim to provide science-based education and to prepare their graduates for continuing medical education throughout their professional lifetime. In contrast to many other university degrees, scientific literacy plays a minor if any role in current curricula. The Berlin Forum hosted by the Association of Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (AWMF) on 17 November 2023 aimed to evaluate, how this deficit may be amended and to what extent this process can be based on existing pilot projects. Methods: Invited experts from scientific medical societies, medical and dental faculties, the German medical association and other institutions involved in graduate and postgraduate medical and dental training discussed requirements for and examples of best practice of scientific literacy training in medicine and dentistry. Writing teams extracted the key messages for this article. Results: The Association of Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (AWMF) recommends: – To include a longitudinal scientific literacy track as a mandatory requirement in medical and dental school curricula.– To include development of methodological and practical competency in evidence-based patient care and medical research as a mandatory requirement into residency programmes.– To credit at least six months of work in clinical or health services research towards fulfilment of residency programmes.– To integrate scientific literacy as a regular part of continuing medical and dental education programmes. Conclusions: Scientific literacy is a key competency for responsible medical care. It is also a prerequisite for progress in medicine. Development and maintenance of scientific literacy therefore deserve greater attention than today in medical and dental school curricula, residency programmes and continuing medical and dental education. Results of the Berlin Forum 2023 hosted by AWMF demonstrate that this reform is possible and how it may be achieved.

publications.title: A pilot study on the impact of age on pain induced by Water Avoidance Stress in female and male Wistar Han rats
publications.abstract: Background and Objective Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS) is a condition that changes with age. Integrating age as a biological variable in preclinical models is critical for translational validity. This study investigated whether aging modulates pain and bladder activity in a rat model of pelvic pain induced by Water Avoidance Stress (WAS). Methods Thirty Wistar Han rats (females: 6-7, 15-18, 23-25 months; males: 6-7, 23-25 months) were randomized into age- and sex-specific groups. Females with 15-18 months underwent ovariectomy. Animals were exposed to WAS (1 h/day for 10 days) and assessed at baseline and post-WAS. Ongoing and evoked pain were evaluated using the Rat Grimace Scale, mechanical thresholds (Von Frey), and thermal sensitivity (Hargreaves) at the genital/thigh and hind paw. Spontaneous bladder activity was assessed using the Voiding Spot Assay. Effect size (Hedges’ g z ) and confidence interval (CI) were calculated, alongside paired comparisons. Key Findings and Limitations Younger animals exhibited pain-like behaviors and genital/thigh sensitization, whereas old animals presented heterogeneous or minimal responses. VSA findings suggested an increase in low-volume spots in younger groups. Conclusions and Clinical Implications: Genital/thigh’s mechanical hypersensitivity indicates bladder-related pain mechanisms in the WAS model. Older rats exhibited fewer signs of pain in the WAS paradigm than younger rats. Findings support the need to refine age-inclusive models and improve bladder-specific behavioral metrics.

publications.title: Invisible cost of pain management by the current International Classification of Diseases coding system, a study in a tertiary care inpatient setting: erratum
A study design for modulating two components of the risk architecture of chronic pain: adverse life events and pain catastrophising
publications.abstract: Background: Traumatic experiences and dysfunctional emotional responses to pain modulate pain processing via partly different neural circuits. Modulation of pain experience by brain mechanisms is partly conveyed via descending pathways through the midbrain and brainstem. We designed an intervention study using Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) to desensitize (a) distressing memories of adverse life events (ALE), or (b) pain-related anxiety and emotion dysregulation such as pain catastrophising (PCAT). Our primary objective is to examine the extent to which EMDR efficacy on pain severity and affective symptoms is mediated via these targeted risk factors. The secondary objective is to assess the mediational effects of brain functional and structural markers and functions of the pain modulation circuitry of the brainstem. Methods: This study is a pre-post longitudinal trial with two parallel treatment arms in individuals with chronic primary or secondary pain syndromes. Primary outcomes and mediators of interest include measures of pain severity (intensity, interference, pain-related distress) and affective symptoms (anxiety, depression, tension, irritability) assessed at baseline and post-treatment. Secondary outcomes include structural and functional brain imaging (fMRI), smartphone-based ecological momentary assessment (EMA), biosampling (blood, stool), somatosensory testing (tender point count, quantitative sensory testing, pressure cuff algometry, nociceptive predictive processing) and self-reported measures on pain and affective symptoms. EMDR treatment will consist of six sessions over the course of 2 weeks. Outcome assessors will be blinded to treatment allocation. Mediational analyses will be conducted within a parallel mediation framework using structural equation modeling. Discussion: This study aims to investigate the mechanism of how an EMDR intervention with one of two different foci influences clinical outcomes by mediation analysis. We hypothesize that (1) EMDR treatment focussing on ALE will lead to a decrease in pain severity and affective symptoms through a decrease in arousal symptoms and engagement of paraventricular thalamus and ventral striatum, and (2) that EMDR treatment focussing on pain-related anxiety and emotion dysregulation will lead to a decrease in pain severity and affective symptoms through a decrease in PCAT and strengthening of prefrontal-limbic and brainstem controls. Clinical trial registration: https://www.drks.de, identifier DRKS00039123.

publications.title: Ein Plädoyer zur Einführung der ICD-11 in Deutschland
publications.abstract: Revision of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD-11) has been set to replace ICD-10. The old revision is no longer maintained by World Health Organization (WHO). In Germany, a national advisory board (Kuratorium für Fragen der Kodiersysteme im Gesundheitswesen (KKG)) of the Ministry of Health is concerned with ICD-11 since 2013. Members of the KKG Working Group ICD-11 from the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (AWMF) describe in this paper the need for a careful, well planned and timely transition from ICD-10 to ICD-11. The transition to ICD-11 ensures a valid representation of medical progress with the coded diagnoses and seizes opportunities of digitization for health care and science. Combining a unique documentation of medical facts with their multiple use for daily health care and research as well as for reimbursement and health policy should be the ultimate goal. This goal demands a one-time coding covering different coding systems in order to bridge a transitional period with parallel support of ICD-10 and ICD-11 on the one hand and to support further policy areas, e.g. with SNOMED CT, on the other hand. In particular, the use of generative artificial intelligence offers a high potential to achieve this goal. Even though estimating the time required is always subject to a high degree of uncertainty given the nature of the German health care system, the transition from ICD-10 to ICD-11 can be carried out in the next 5 years. Then, 13 years without content maintenance through the WHO, the ICD-10 would have lost the connection to the medical State of the Art at the latest.

publications.title: Neural processing of win-contingent audiovisual cues during virtual gambling: an fMRI cross-over study
publications.abstract: RATIONALE: Over the last 30 years, the global incidence and prevalence of gambling disorder (GD) have risen, with particularly high risk associated with slot machine gambling. Win-contingent audiovisual stimuli are considered a key mechanism that may promote risky decision-making during gambling. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate whether win‑contingent audiovisual cues modulate risky decision-making and neural responses during a virtual slot-machine task in healthy volunteers. METHODS: In a randomized cross-over design, N = 20 right-handed healthy volunteers completed a virtual slot-machine paradigm with and without win-contingent audiovisual cues. We compared risky versus safe choices and expected value (EV)-consistent versus EV-inconsistent decisions and examined differential fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging) activation during decision and feedback phases using Flexible factorial models. This study was pre-registered in the German clinical trials database: DRKS00021178 on 03.04.2020. RESULTS: Win‑contingent audiovisual cues did not significantly affect the frequency of high-risk versus low-risk choices or EV-consistent versus EV-inconsistent decisions. In the feedback phase, wins (vs. losses and near wins) elicited robust activation in hippocampal, parietal, frontal and insular regions. Compared with the uncued version, the cued version was associated with reduced activation in temporal, thalamic, parietal and insular cortices during win feedback, particularly for EV-consistent decisions. CONCLUSION: Win-contingent audiovisual cues modulated neural responses to gambling outcomes in healthy individuals without detectable changes in choice behavior. These neural differences indicate altered processing of gambling-related stimuli, their cognitive and behavioral significance remains uncertain.

publications.title: The Phenomenology of Non-Ordinary Experiences during Spiritualist Séances
publications.abstract: Non-Ordinary experiences (NOEs), such as feelings of unity with God, hearing voices, and sensing the presence of deceased persons, are prevalent in the general population. They may be life-transforming but are also associated with pathological conditions such as psychosis and dissociation. However, little is known about how cultural appraisals and religious practices shape the phenomenology and psychological impact of these experiences in non-clinical populations. For the most part, their socio-cognitive and emotional features remain unexplored. The purpose of this study was threefold. Firstly, to investigate the phenomenological characteristics and types of NOEs reported by self-defined spirit mediums from a spiritualist home circle in the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Secondly, to explore the role of social context in interpreting and shaping NOEs. Finally, to gain a better understanding of the phenomenological similarities and distinctions of experiences reported in spiritualist contexts with psychopathological constructs such as dissociative and psychotic symptoms. The study used a mixed-methods approach, combining field/ethnographic observations of spiritualist séances, thematic content analysis of reports of séance-related NOEs, and standardized scales assessing dissociation, absorption, psychotic symptoms, symptoms of common mental disorders, and satisfaction with life. We analyzed a total of 151 independent reports of NOEs provided by a group of mediumship practitioners participating in regular séances over a period of one year and five months. The reports tapped a variety of experiences including intense emotional states (e.g., happiness, gratitude), alterations in consciousness (e.g., feelings of spacing out), spontaneous mental imagery (e.g., visions of scenes of the spiritual world), sensory-perceptual experiences (e.g., hearing voices or other unusual sounds), somatic manifestations (e.g., body tremors), and unusual experiences involving the séance table (e.g., vibrations in the table). The experiences reported were episodic, controllable, and restricted to the spiritualist séances. Overall, they were described as pleasant or innocuous. The mediums generally reported perceiving their lives as satisfying and meaningful and scored similarly to the general population on items indicative of common mental disorders. Given their cultural impact and predominantly positive effects, these experiences bear implications for differential diagnosis, and the role of cultural and religious factors in mental health, wellbeing, and cognition. Séance phenomena provide a natural environment for observational and experimental studies of intentionally induced non-ordinary states of consciousness, the psychological and social underpinnings of religion and mysticism, and the transcultural psychiatry of spirituality.

publications.title: Exploring the meaning of places: a mixed-methods analysis of salience and spatial scale in Brazil and New Zealand
Where are the Big Five? A semantic search in ‘big’ psychometrically validated personality inventory items.
Making sense of the extraordinary – An investigation of the content and prevalence of appraisals of nonordinary experiences
publications.abstract: Individuals around the world report nonordinary experiences that stand out to them compared to their day-to-day or ordinary experiences. Yet, they can be appraised in very different ways, resulting in wellbeing and personal growth, or in marginalization and mental health problems. One challenge is that there are relatively few systematic efforts to explore possible appraisal processes and the overall contextual features of these experiences. In study 1, we report a validation and extension of a previously designed set of appraisal and contextual questions to the Inventory of Nonordinary Experiences, with a sample of Brazilian participants (N = 160). The study successfully validated all original appraisal categories with minor modifications and added nine new context and appraisal categories. In study 2, we conducted a prevalence study by administering these questions in a general population sample (N = 5,117) in which individuals reported on one of 38 nonordinary experiences. Most contextual features and appraisals followed a unimodal distribution approximating a normal distribution. This suggests that nonordinary experiences, however heterogeneous they may be, appear to be interpreted within the same set of beliefs and appraisals, in addition to sharing similar temporal characteristics. Furthermore, although 20% of participants reported an immediate negative impact and 25% reported some degree of suffering or discomfort from experiences, 51% evaluated experiences as promoting overall positive long-term life effects. These findings highlight the potential of human resilience and the complex role of nonordinary experiences vis-a-vis protective factors in promoting health. Our results provide new insights into consciousness states and their mental health and wellbeing implications.

publications.title: Beyond knowledge gains - learner experience and technology acceptance of virtual reality for anatomy education in Zambia: a randomized exploratory study
publications.abstract: Abstract Background Standalone virtual reality (VR) enables interactive exploration of three-dimensional anatomy, but comparative evidence from resource-constrained medical-education settings remains limited. This study explored immediate knowledge outcomes, learner acceptance, and experiences with VR and three other learning resources in Zambia. Methods In this four-arm randomized exploratory study, 67 first- and second-year Bachelor of Science in Clinical Sciences students were assigned using Excel-generated random group numbers (1–4; no allocation concealment) to standalone VR using 3D Organon, AMBOSS ® , curated textbook materials, or self-directed internet search for a self-paced learning session of up to 30 min. Knowledge was assessed using an unvalidated 10-item pre-post test, and immediate acceptance was measured with an adapted Technology Acceptance Model questionnaire. The primary between-group knowledge analysis used baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance with HC3-robust standard errors. Acceptance comparisons were adjusted for multiple testing. Brief open-text responses underwent qualitative content analysis. A pre-study review indicated that tested concepts could be located in the three fixed-content resources but did not establish equivalence in depth, organisation, or accessibility, and could not be applied to the self-directed internet group. Results The knowledge analysis included 59 participants (VR n = 12; AMBOSS ® n = 17; textbook n = 16; Internet n = 14). Within-group increases reached the adjusted significance threshold in the AMBOSS ® , textbook, and web-resource groups but not in the VR group (adjusted p = .053). The primary analysis did not detect an overall difference in baseline-adjusted post-test scores between modalities, F(3,54) = 1.945, p = .133; none of the six pairwise comparisons was significant after Holm adjustment. This finding does not establish equivalence. Acceptance analyses included 55–60 participants per construct. After adjustment across six domains, only Attitude differed significantly between modalities, H(3) = 11.801, ε² = 0.17, adjusted p = .049; AMBOSS ® was rated more favourably than the self-directed internet search (adjusted p = .019, Cliff’s δ = −0.60). Perceived ease of use and perceived enjoyment showed low internal consistency, limiting their interpretation. The qualitative corpus comprised 211 comments from 64 participants. Some VR participants valued visualisation, novelty, and enjoyment but reported navigation and content-access difficulties. AMBOSS ® participants frequently valued organisation and accessibility, while experiences with textbook and web resources were mixed. Conclusions This small exploratory study did not provide conclusive evidence of differences in immediate knowledge outcomes between the four modalities. Quantitative acceptance differences were also limited after adjustment for multiple comparisons. The findings identify content accessibility, curricular alignment, interface familiarization, and exposure time as priorities for larger, prospectively designed studies using validated instruments and longer-term outcomes.

publications.title: Additional file 1 of Beyond knowledge gains - learner experience and technology acceptance of virtual reality for anatomy education in Zambia: a randomized exploratory study
Use and operationalisation of wearable technologies for measuring mental health outcomes associated with climate change: A scoping review
publications.abstract: Background and rationale Climate impact-drivers (CIDs), as defined by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), can affect mental health through direct and indirect pathways. Understanding these relationships requires approaches that can capture individual-level environmental exposures alongside physiological and behavioural indicators of mental health. Wearable technologies offer opportunities to collect continuous or repeated measurements, including heart rate, sleep patterns and physical activity, which may provide insights into the relationship between climate impact-drivers and mental health. However, the technologies used, the ways in which exposures and outcomes are operationalised, and the measurement properties of wearable-derived indicators may vary across populations, settings and studies. A systematic mapping of the existing evidence is needed to understand how wearable technologies are being used to investigate mental health outcomes associated with climate impact-drivers, what indicators are measured, and how these measurements are validated. This scoping review will address this gap by mapping the available evidence and identifying methodological limitations and areas requiring further research. Aim and objectives The aim of this scoping review is to map how wearable technologies are used to measure mental health outcomes associated with climate impact-drivers. The specific objectives are to: Identify the wearable technologies used to measure individual-level exposure to IPCC-defined climate impact-drivers in relation to mental health, including the populations and settings in which they are used. Examine how climate impact-driver exposure is operationalised, including acute, chronic and gradual exposures, and how these exposures are linked to wearable-derived mental health indicators. Identify the physiological and behavioural signals captured by wearable technologies, such as heart rate, sleep and movement, and examine how these indicators are validated. Map the reported measurement properties of wearable-derived measures, including their reliability, accuracy, validity, feasibility and acceptability for investigating climate impact-drivers and mental health outcomes. Methods The review will follow a scoping review approach. A three-step search strategy will be used, beginning with initial searches in Scopus and PubMed, followed by comprehensive searches across Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Academic Search Premier, CINAHL and APA PsycINFO. Grey literature will be searched through Google Scholar, the King's College London Research Portal, OpenAIRE, the Heidelberg University Library, African Journals Online and Global Index Medicus. Reference lists of included sources will also be screened to identify additional relevant evidence. No restrictions will be applied to publication date or language. Search results will be screened independently by two reviewers against the review's inclusion criteria. Relevant data will be extracted independently by two reviewers using a structured extraction form, with discrepancies resolved through discussion and referral to a senior reviewer where necessary. Extracted data will be organised and categorised according to the review objectives. Climate impact-drivers will be classified using the IPCC framework, while wearable technologies, mental health outcomes, physiological and behavioural indicators, and measurement approaches will be grouped to facilitate comparison across sources. The findings will be synthesised using descriptive summaries and thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six phases. The synthesis will be led by the lead author (CM), with initial interpretations discussed with the second author (JC) before being presented to the wider review team. No formal critical appraisal of methodological quality will be undertaken, as the review aims to map the available evidence rather than evaluate intervention effectiveness. Expected outcomes and contribution The review is expected to provide an overview of the wearable technologies used to investigate mental health outcomes associated with climate impact-drivers, the exposures and indicators measured, and the populations and settings represented in the literature. It will also describe how wearable-derived indicators are validated and what evidence is available regarding their reliability, accuracy, validity, feasibility and acceptability. By identifying methodological gaps and under-researched areas, the review will help inform future research on wearable-based approaches to studying the relationship between climate impact-drivers and mental health. The findings may also support the development of more consistent approaches to exposure measurement and mental health assessment in climate and health research.

publications.title: From screen time to cyberdiseases: a systematic scoping review of health outcomes from digital technology exposure, 2019–2024
publications.abstract: Abstract Digital technologies are integral to daily life, with individuals spending substantial time in digital environments. Evidence increasingly links this exposure to adverse health outcomes, but research remains fragmented and relies largely on “screen time” as a crude proxy. The full spectrum of these health outcomes and the metrics needed to assess them remain poorly defined. In this systematic scoping review of 389 studies, we mapped reported associations between digital exposure and health outcomes spanning across mental, behavioural, visual, musculoskeletal, and metabolic systems, which we conceptualise as ‘cyber-diseases’. Screen time, assessed in 83% of clinical studies, was the most commonly used exposure metric but is likely an inadequate proxy. These findings highlight gaps in the conceptualisation and measurement of digital exposure. Based on these findings, we propose, as a possible direction for future work, a multi-dimensional digital biomarker framework—encompassing exposure time, device type, interaction mode, and content.

Global, Regional, and National Burden of Heart Failure, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
publications.abstract: Importance: Heart failure (HF) is a common condition with substantial geographical variation in its prevalence and underlying etiologies. Consistent and comparable data on the burden of HF within populations are needed to inform health system priorities. Objective: To estimate the global burden of HF. Design, Setting, and Participants: This cross-sectional study estimates disease burden using Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) methodologies to integrate multiple information sources. Data come from 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023 representing the global population with prevalent HF. Exposure: HF and underlying etiologies. Main Outcomes and Measures: Estimates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) for the prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) for HF by age, sex, location, year, and underlying etiology. Results: Globally, there were 56.0 million (95% UI, 49.9-62.2 million) estimated cases of HF in 2023. The estimated prevalence of HF generally increased with age for all locations. While ischemic heart disease and hypertensive heart disease were the 2 most common etiologies globally among older adults, there was substantial variation in etiological pattern by location and age. Congenital heart anomalies and rheumatic heart disease (RHD) were common etiologies in children and young adults, while the proportion of HF due to alcohol use peaked in middle adulthood. Location-specific estimates highlighted regions with higher burden of HF due to specific etiologies, including RHD (south Asia, east Asia, Oceania, southeast Asia, central sub-Saharan Africa, eastern sub-Saharan Africa, southern sub-Saharan Africa, and western sub-Saharan Africa), alcohol use (eastern Europe, Australasia, the Caribbean, and central Europe), and Chagas disease (southern, Andean, tropical, and central Latin America). Conclusions and Relevance: Heart failure is a significant global public health burden, and the impact is likely to increase as populations age. However, most HF etiologies can be prevented by interventions that reduce exposure to modifiable risk factors, such as elevated blood pressure, excessive alcohol consumption, and tobacco use. Etiology- and location-specific estimates can provide necessary information for public health officials to determine how best to prioritize interventions to reduce HF disease burden.

publications.title: Burden of cancer in Africa, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, with a disproportionately rising burden across Africa. Effective policy responses have been consistently hampered by fragmented and incomplete cancer surveillance data. Using the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023, we estimated the burden of 48 cancer types across all 54 African countries over the period 1990 to 2023. These age-disaggregated and sex-disaggregated findings provide a crucial empirical foundation to inform regional control strategies and monitor progress towards global health targets. METHODS: We applied GBD 2023 methodology to estimate fatal and non-fatal outcomes of cancer alongside risk-attributable burden from 88 modifiable risk factors, across all 54 African countries. The estimation of cancer burden attributable to risk factors followed the comparative risk assessment framework. Estimates of incidence, mortality, years lived with disability (YLDs), years of life lost (YLLs), and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were stratified by age, sex, location, and year (1990-2023) and reported as counts and age-standardised rates per 100 000 population. Mean estimates represent the mean across 250 draws, with 95% uncertainty intervals calculated from the 2·5th and 97·5th percentiles. FINDINGS: In 2023, cancer, including non-melanoma skin cancer, accounted for an estimated 1·54 million (95% uncertainty interval 1·37-1·75) incident cases, 923 000 (824 000-1 020 000) deaths, and 33·9 million (30·6-37·1) DALYs across all ages and both sexes in Africa, of which 98·2% (97·9-98·3) were attributable to YLLs. In Africa, 10·7 million (8·9-12·9) DALYs and 306 000 (254 000-363 000) cancer deaths in 2023 were attributable to the 88 risk factors assessed in GBD 2023, equivalent to 31·6% (26·8-35·9) of total DALYs and 33·1% (28·7-37·2) of total cancer deaths across all ages and both sexes. Between 1990 and 2023, deaths attributable to risk factors increased by 216·0% (159·3-284·5) for both sexes combined. In 2023, incident cancer cases in females numbered 960 000 (821 000-1 130 000), with breast and cervical cancers together accounting for 53·5% (44·7-62·2) of all female incident cases. In males, prostate, liver, tracheal, bronchus and lung, and colorectal cancers were the leading types, together accounting for 44·8% (36·2-54·3) of all male cancers in Africa in 2023. Childhood cancer (ages 0-19 years) in Africa accounted for 104 000 (84 600-130 000) incident cases and 54 700 (47 500-64 500) deaths, representing 27·7% (26·6-29·4) of global incidence and 38·0% (36·3-40·0) of global deaths in 2023. Cancers in adolescents and young adults (ages 15-39 years) contributed 26·6% (26·4-27·5) of total cancer DALYs in Africa, those in older adults aged 40-64 years contributed 44·8% (43·8-45·6), and those in adults aged 65 years and older contributed 18·3% (17·4-19·1). INTERPRETATION: Cancer is a growing contributor to the disease burden in Africa, with rising cases, deaths, and DALYs disproportionately affecting children, adolescents, and young adults. The increase in age-standardised mortality and DALY rates stands in sharp contrast to the ambitions of the Sustainable Development Goals for 2030 and the African Union Agenda 2063. Addressing this burden will require coordinated national and international action, with health-system strengthening and context-specific cancer-control strategies spanning prevention, early diagnosis, and treatment. FUNDING: Gates Foundation.
topics: Economic and Financial Impacts of Cancer

publications.title: Global, regional, and national prevalence of second-hand smoke and attributable disease burden in 204 countries and territories, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Second-hand smoke (SHS) exposure remains a major source of morbidity and mortality among non-smokers. This study presents the first dedicated Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) publication to systematically quantify SHS prevalence and evaluate its effect as a global risk factor across a broader range of outcomes. METHODS: Using the GBD 2023 comparative risk assessment framework, we estimated SHS exposure prevalence and attributable disease burden across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, stratified by age and sex. Exposure estimates were derived by synthesising population-based surveys and household composition data through spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression. Relative risks for nine health outcomes, now including asthma, were estimated using the Burden of Proof methodology, and applied to calculate attributable deaths and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs). FINDINGS: In 2023, an estimated 2·71 billion (95% UI 2·44-3·02) people worldwide were exposed to SHS, including 767 million (687-858) children aged 0-14 years. Age-standardised prevalence was highest in southeast Asia, east Asia, and Oceania (48·4% [44·0-53·4]), with female individuals in some countries experiencing nearly 1·8 times the exposure prevalence of male individuals. Despite a 22·2% (10·6-32·4) decline in global age-standardised prevalence since 1990, this progress has not been sufficient to reduce the absolute number of exposed individuals, which has remained stable globally and has risen sharply in sub-Saharan Africa (98·5% [62·0-144·4] increase) and North Africa and the Middle East (72·1% [47·8-101·8] increase). In 2023, SHS exposure accounted for 1·66 million (1·33-2·07) deaths and 44·8 million (35·8-54·3) DALYs globally. Ischaemic heart disease was the leading contributor to SHS-attributable DALYs (12·0 million [9·31-15·2]) overall, while lower respiratory infections predominated among children (5·16 million [3·48-7·12]). INTERPRETATION: We estimated that SHS remains a substantial driver of global health loss, particularly through cardiovascular and paediatric respiratory diseases. Persistent geographical disparities and growing absolute numbers of exposed individuals in several regions underscore the urgent need for accelerated implementation and enforcement of comprehensive tobacco control measures, particularly to protect women and children in both public and domestic environments. FUNDING: Bloomberg Philanthropies and the Gates Foundation.

publications.title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Myocarditis and Its Impairment, 1990-2023

Treatment of male patients as a subgroup of the international prospective multicenter AXSANA study evaluating different surgical methods of axillary staging in clinically node-positive breast cancer patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NCT04373655, AGO-B-053)
Impact of Neoadjuvant Carboplatin in Early-Stage Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: A Pooled Analysis of the BrighTNess, Cancer and Leukemia Group B 40603 (Alliance), and GeparSixto Clinical Trials
publications.abstract: Purpose To better characterize the therapeutic benefits of the addition of carboplatin to anthracycline- and taxane-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) in early-stage triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), we performed a pooled analysis of three randomized clinical trials: BrighTNess (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02032277 ), Cancer and Leukemia Group B 40603 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT00861705 ), and GeparSixto (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01426880 ). Methods We evaluated the impact of the addition of carboplatin to NACT on pathologic complete response (pCR) rates, event-free survival (EFS), and overall survival (OS) across a combined total of 1,084 patients. We additionally looked for associations of outcome by germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 (g BRCA ) mutation status, eight gene expression signatures, and molecular subtypes (PAM50, MD Anderson Cancer Center/Baylor College of Medicine [MDACC/BCM]). Results In the pooled data set, the addition of carboplatin to NACT was associated with a higher pCR rate (odds ratio, 1.89 [95% CI, 1.41 to 2.55]; P < .001) and improved EFS (hazard ratio, 0.71 [95% CI, 0.54 to 0.93]; P = .01), but not OS. In patients with g BRCA mutations (n = 137), we found that the addition of carboplatin conveys a significant EFS benefit but had no significant association with pCR rate or OS. We found six immune gene expression signatures that were significantly associated with a higher pCR rate and four that were significantly associated with improved EFS and OS. In addition, we found that the PAM50 luminal and MDACC/BCM luminal androgen receptor molecular subtypes were significantly associated with lower pCR rates in the combined data set. Conclusion Our findings support the recent addition of carboplatin to NACT within the standard-of-care treatment of stage II to III TNBC and emphasize the importance of the TNBC immune microenvironment to patient outcomes.

publications.title: Circulating Glypican 4 and mortality risk in patients with metastatic breast cancer–results from the DESIREE study
Efficacy and Safety of EG12014 (Biosimilar Trastuzumab) Compared to Reference Trastuzumab in HER2-Positive Early Breast Cancer: A Phase III Randomized Study
publications.abstract: INTRODUCTION: ; EirGenix/Sandoz) was approved by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in 2023. We aim to demonstrate equivalent efficacy, and to compare safety, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles, of EG12014 and reference trastuzumab (ref-TRA) in early breast cancer (EBC). METHODS: This Phase III, randomized, multicenter, double-blind study included adult patients with EBC. In the neoadjuvant phase, patients received epirubicin and cyclophosphamide for four cycles, then were randomized (1:1) to four cycles of EG12014 or ref-TRA (loading/maintenance dose: 8/6 mg/kg) with paclitaxel. Following surgery, patients continued adjuvant EG12014, or were rerandomized (1:1) from ref-TRA to ref-TRA or EG12014. Patients completed 12 months of treatment. The primary endpoint was centrally-assessed pathological complete response (pCR; defined as ypT0/is ypN0) at the time of surgery. Additional efficacy, safety, immunogenicity, and PK endpoints were evaluated. RESULTS: In the neoadjuvant phase, 405 and 402 patients were randomized to EG12014 and ref-TRA, respectively. In the adjuvant phase, 386 patients continued EG12014, 188 continued ref-TRA, and 188 switched from ref-TRA to EG12014. The primary objective, to demonstrate equivalent efficacy between EG12014 and ref-TRA, was achieved: the risk difference between treatment arms in pCR rate was - 0.004 (95% CI - 0.072 to 0.065), with the 95% CI entirely within the predefined equivalence margin of - 0.13 to 0.13 (EMA requirement). Equivalence was also demonstrated regarding the risk ratio, with a relative risk of 0.992 (90% CI 0.880-1.118) and the 90% CI completely within the predefined equivalence margin of 0.741-1.349 (US Food and Drug Administration requirement). Secondary efficacy endpoints, including overall response prior to surgery and overall survival, were also comparable between treatments. Safety, immunogenicity and PK profiles were comparable between treatments and were not impacted by switching. CONCLUSION: Trastuzumab biosimilar EG12014 and ref-TRA have equivalent efficacy, and comparable safety, immunogenicity, and PK profiles, in patients with EBC. Clinical trial registration NCT03433313; EudraCT Number 2017-003973-33.

publications.title: Atezolizumab in early triple-negative breast cancer: the randomized phase 3 NSABP B-59/GeparDouze trial
publications.abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype with an activated tumor immune microenvironment. The multicenter, multinational, double-blinded NSABP B-59/GeparDouze trial evaluated the addition of atezolizumab (atezo) (773 patients randomized) or placebo (777 patients) to sequential taxane–carboplatin–anthracycline-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy in stage II–III TNBC. The addition of atezo did not significantly improve the primary endpoint of event-free survival (EFS) (HR, 0.80 (95% CI, 0.062–1.03); stratified log-rank P = 0.083, 4-year EFS rates difference 3.3%). The HR for overall survival was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.62–1.19), with a 4-year benefit of 0.7%. Prespecified subgroup analyses suggested heterogeneity in EFS, with benefit of atezo in patients presenting with clinical lymph node involvement ( P interaction = 0.039). Treatment-emergent adverse events with grades ≥3 were reported in 75.3% (atezo) versus 73.4% (placebo), and immune-related adverse events were reported in 27.6% (atezo) versus 11.4% (placebo). A total of 196 (25.5%) patients discontinued atezo and 143 (18.8%) patients discontinued placebo in the neoadjuvant phase. In an exploratory mRNA-based subset analysis, patients with basal-like immune-activated tumors may have benefited from atezo. TNBC subtyping to identify basal-like immune-activated tumors and quantification of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes to identify tumors with high tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte counts could be a promising strategy to identify patients who benefit from the addition of immune checkpoint inhibitors to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. publications.title: The present and future of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease prevention, diagnosis, and management in China: a Lancet Respiratory Medicine Commission
A 12-month structured exercise reduces epicardial adipose volume in a frequency-dependent manner and lowers serum M-CSF in community-dwelling older adults: a randomized controlled trial
publications.abstract: Objective Exercise is a well-established strategy for promoting healthy aging and reducing cardiometabolic risk; however, its effects on epicardial adipose volume (EAV) and associated inflammatory pathways in older adults remain insufficiently understood. This randomized controlled trial examined whether a 12-month structured exercise program reduces EAV in community-dwelling older adults, and secondarily explored changes in serum pro-inflammatory cytokines. Methods This single-center pragmatic randomized controlled trial incorporated a Zelen design. A total of 156 older adults (≥60 years) were evenly allocated to a structured exercise (STE) group or a control group. The control group received health education only; the STE group performed one supervised center-based session plus at least two home-based sessions per week, with matched intensity and duration. EAV, body fat parameters, and circulating pro-inflammatory factors were measured at baseline and after 12 months. Results Among the randomized participants, 57 individuals in the control group and 61 individuals in the STE group completed the 12-month follow-up (55 men, 46.6%; mean age 69.17 ± 4.41 years). The absolute EAV change differed significantly between groups (STE vs. control: −15.15 mL, 95% CI –22.61 to −7.69, p < 0.0001). After adjusting for baseline values, only serum macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) showed a significant between-group difference (−1.75 pg/mL, 95% CI –3.34 to −0.16, p = 0.032). Univariate linear regression indicated that each additional weekly exercise session was associated with a 3.156 mL greater EAV reduction ( R 2 = 0.084). Conclusion A 12-month structured exercise intervention was associated with reduced EAV and lower circulating M-CSF levels in community-dwelling older adults, with greater reductions observed among participants engaging in more frequent weekly exercise sessions. These findings support regular supervised exercise as a non-pharmacological strategy to reduce cardiac adiposity and modulate inflammation in aging populations. Clinical trial registration https://www.chictr.org.cn/indexEN.html , ChiCTR2400081824.

publications.title: Integrative multi-omics and experimental validation identify SERINC2 as a ferroptosis-related biomarker in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
publications.abstract: Abstract Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and fatal lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death, has been implicated in various fibrotic diseases, but its role in IPF remains unclear. This study integrates spatial transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and bulk RNA-seq to explore ferroptosis in IPF. A ferroptosis scoring model and machine learning algorithms identified SERINC2 as a key gene upregulated across all datasets, with high expression in basal cells. Further analysis revealed that SERINC2⁺ basal cells are involved in key signaling pathways, such as Wnt and NT, and exhibit active intercellular communication. Animal experiments confirmed that SERINC2 protein levels are elevated in the lung tissues of BLM-induced mice, supporting its role in disease progression. Our findings suggest that SERINC2 may serve as a potential diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target, providing new insights into the pathogenesis and potential treatment of IPF.
topics: Interstitial Lung Diseases and Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis

publications.title: Branched-chain amino acid depletion and adolescent myopia progression through mechanistic target of rapamycin complex1-dependent scleral remodeling
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT The metabolomic alterations underlying adolescent myopia progression remain unclear. In this prospective school-based cohort, 186 adolescents (93 progressors and 93 non-progressors) were followed for 12 months and randomly split into a training ( n = 150) and an internal validation set ( n = 36). Baseline serum samples were profiled using untargeted UHPLC-MS/MS. LASSO, Boruta, and RFE were used to develop a metabolite panel, which was subsequently evaluated in the internal validation set. Hartley guinea pigs ( n = 15 per group) were randomized to control, form-deprivation myopia (FDM), and three branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) dose groups (412, 2060, or 4120 mg/kg per day) and received BCAAs by oral gavage for 4 weeks. Refraction, axial length, and scleral thickness were assessed. Human scleral fibroblasts were treated with TGF-β and BCAAs, with mTORC1 or LAT1 inhibition. In the human cohort, we identified 94 endogenous differential metabolites, with BCAA-related metabolism being the most prominently perturbed. A 22-metabolite panel achieved AUROCs of 0.82 and 0.86 in the training and internal validation sets, respectively. L -leucyl- L -alanine was the strongest protective marker (OR = 0.15, 95% CI 0.04‒0.40). BCAAs attenuated axial elongation and preserved scleral thickness in FDM guinea pigs. LAT1 may be involved in BCAA-associated mTORC1 activation, whereas BCAAs may suppress TGF-β/SMAD/FOXO1-associated myofibroblast transdifferentiation. Together, these findings identify a serum metabolomic signature associated with adolescent myopia progression and an internally validated 22-metabolite panel for risk stratification that requires external validation.

publications.title: Global economic burden attributable to asthma, 2025–50: a global modelling analysis of 154 countries and territories
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Asthma is a major chronic respiratory disease with substantial health and economic consequences worldwide; however, there is little evidence for the long-term macroeconomic effects of asthma across countries. We aimed to estimate the global economic burden attributable to asthma from 2025 to 2050 across 154 countries and territories. METHODS: We estimated the long-term economic burden of asthma using a health-augmented macroeconomic model covering 154 countries and territories from 2025 to 2050. Projected labour losses were captured through reductions in the workforce due to premature death and reduced labour force participation due to disability. Physical capital accumulation was affected by asthma-related medical spending, which reduces savings and investment, measured as asthma-attributable health expenditure. In the model, this spending reduced disposable income and savings, thereby lowering investment and slowing capital accumulation over time FINDINGS: Between 2025 and 2050, our model predicted that asthma would incur costs of approximately US$863 billion (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 615-1396; 2024 US$), corresponding to an annual gross domestic product (GDP) decline of 0·036% (0·026-0·058). The projected economic burden differed markedly across the 154 countries. The USA bore the largest burden (US$471 billion [371-655]), followed by the UK (US$45 billion [28-84]) and China (US$44 billion [27-81]). Across income groups, high-income countries accounted for the greatest absolute losses (US$712 billion [525-1105]) and highest proportional GDP losses (0·054% [0·039-0·083]), whereas low-income countries incurred absolute losses of US$5 billion (2-11). In low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs), labour-related losses accounted for a larger share of total costs and declines in disease burden were slower. INTERPRETATION: Our findings suggest that asthma imposes a substantial and uneven macroeconomic burden across countries, with differences by income level and region. Productivity reductions dominate in LMICs, whereas physical capital-related effects are more important in high-income settings. Improving asthma prevention and control could yield economic gain. FUNDING: Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project; Non-profit Central Research Institute Fund of Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences; European Commission Horizon Europe.

publications.title: EPCR expression marks CD150neg deeply dormant long-term hematopoietic stem cells
publications.abstract: Cell surface expression of the Slam family member CD150 is widely used for the prospective isolation of multipotent long-term hematopoietic stem cells (LT-HSCs). Here, we identify a bona fide endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR) + CD150 − HSC subset, termed LT-HSC2, that sustains serial multi-lineage reconstitution. Long-term label-retaining assays reveal that LT-HSC2s are more deeply dormant than conventional EPCR + CD150 + LT-HSC1s, exhibit reduced cell cycle activation in response to inflammatory stress, and preserve stemness for prolonged periods in vivo . Moreover, combining EPCR with established HSC and multipotent progenitor (MPP) markers resolves the earliest stages of lineage divergence toward megakaryocytic/erythroid-biased CD150 + and lymphoid-biased CD150 − trajectories. Thus, EPCR expression in HSCs and MPPs is associated with increased stemness, whereas CD150 expression does not encompass the full spectrum of long-term repopulating HSCs. Our findings establish EPCR + CD150 − LT-HSC2s as a distinct, exceptionally dormant stem-cell subset and reveal an additional layer of HSC heterogeneity governing self-renewal, decreased stress sensitvity. and earliest lineage priming.

publications.title: Control of Golgi Architecture Through Three Centrosome Cohesion Pathways
publications.abstract: Abstract Centrosome cohesion mechanisms link the two interphase centrosomes into a single microtubule-organizing center that is closely associated with the Golgi apparatus. The contribution of cohesion mechanisms to Golgi organization and function remains unclear. Here, we show that rootletin-CEP68 filaments, the C-Nap1-ninein linker, and microtubules derived from subdistal appendages, all of which promote centrosome cohesion, regulate the Golgi through distinct mechanisms while acting synergistically to maintain its organization and function. Centrosome-anchored rootletin-CEP68 filaments associate with AKAP450 through periodic binding of its PACT domain to CEP68 and extend into the Golgi, thereby establishing a physical connection between both organelles. The rootletin-CEP68-AKAP450 linkage even functions in cell types in which rootletin and AKAP450 do not mediate centrosome cohesion, suggesting that Golgi organization is the basic function of these filaments. Knockout analyses demonstrate that the three centrosome cohesion mechanisms collectively regulate Golgi morphology, positioning, and reassembly as well as cell migration. Each mechanism contributes distinctly to the overall process, indicating that they operate as a multifaceted system.

publications.title: Joint recording of past and present transcriptomes reconstructs single-cell trajectories
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT Tracing molecular cell state transitions through development, homeostasis and disease is still beyond reach at single-cell resolution. We present scReMeMber-Seq, a methylation-based cell-memory recorder connecting past transcriptional states with present transcriptome and DNA methylome in individual cells. scReMeMber-Seq leverages pulse induction of DCM-Polr2b (TimeMachine) and single-cell methylome-transcriptome (scMT) sequencing for endpoint readout. In mouse neural stem cells (NSCs) and pancreatic organoids, single-cell DCM methylation profiles (scDCMome) accurately discriminate cell types. Over time, scDCMome also record NSC quiescence-activation state changes across multiple cell divisions. In zebrafish embryos, scDCMome resolve individual transcriptional trajectories from progenitor to neuron. Together, scReMeMber-Seq enables real time reconstruction of cellular trajectories, connecting past and present molecular states in single cells, at genome scale, across experimental systems, in vitro and in vivo .

publications.title: Haemodynamic control of zonated liver function via instructive vascular Wnt signalling
publications.abstract: The vascular endothelium forms a systemically disseminated organ that translates micromilieu factors into instructive cues, designated as angiocrine signalling. While vascular control of organ function mechanisms have been discovered in essentially all major organs, the mechanisms of translating milieu factors into angiocrine signalling mechanisms remain largely elusive. Here, focussing on the well-established angiocrine Wnt signalling-regulated liver metabolic zonation paradigm, we identified blood flow-induced haemodynamic stress as a biophysical sensor that governs the angiocrine expression profile of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSEC). Combining single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial proteomics, we generated a high-resolution crosstalk map of LSEC and hepatocytes from LSEC Wnt-deficient mutant mice and littermate controls. Intriguingly, vascular Wnt receptors, in parallel with angiocrine Wnt ligands, were specifically enriched in pericentral LSEC, enforcing the spatially coordinated vascular Wnt functions. Consequently, vascular Wnt further modulated angiocrine gene signatures, LSEC morphology, and the expression of gap junctional molecules in an autocrine manner. Taken together, the data define LSEC as a dynamic cellular decoder that translates biophysical forces into instructive angiocrine signals via activating promiscuous vascular Wnt factors.
topics: Wnt/β-catenin signaling in development and cancer

publications.title: Opportunities, challenges and responsible innovation using generative artificial intelligence for biological sequence design
publications.abstract: Abstract The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and biotechnology is creating unprecedented capabilities for designing biological sequences, ranging from proteins and nucleic acids to entire genomes. However, significant barriers hinder the translation of generative AI models into real-world biological applications, including biased and fragmented training data, opaque model architectures that resist interpretation, and the increasing disparity between the speed of computational sequence generation and the throughput of experimental validation. As these barriers are overcome, the dual-use potential of these technologies is simultaneously expanded: the same advances that enable therapeutic design also lower the threshold for misuse, ranging from the generation of new pathogens to circumventing existing biosecurity screening. In order to address this issue, the Wübben Sandpit on Generative AI for Biological Sequences was convened, bringing together researchers from the fields of molecular biology, AI, biosecurity, ethics and policy. This white paper presents the resulting consensus recommendations, structured as a defence-in-depth framework spanning three domains. Firstly, the governance of sensitive training data should be achieved through risk-stratified access and funding-stage review. Secondly, the governance of models is addressed through lifecycle risk assessment, safety benchmarking and tiered deployment. Thirdly, the governance of nucleic acid synthesis is strengthened through screening, supply chain accountability and dedicated funding for countermeasure research. Rather than treating security as an impediment to innovation, the framework positions responsible governance as a prerequisite for realising the transformative potential of AI-driven biological design.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

publications.title: Myopic patchy atrophy differs from geographic atrophy in retinal pigment epithelium appearance and intraretinal hyperreflective foci
publications.abstract: To assess clinical-histological characteristics of myopic patchy atrophy (PA) and geographic atrophy of age-related macular degeneration (GA). Participants of population-based studies (Ural Eye and Medical Study (n = 5899; age: 40 + years), Ural Very Old Study (n = 1526; age: 85 + years), Beijing Eye Study (n = 3468; age: 40 + years) were clinically examined. We additionally assessed histologically human globes (n = 446) enucleated due to clinical reasons or enucleated post mortem. In the population-based studies, GA and PA were detected in 79 eyes (age: 81.9 ± 12.0 years;axial length: 23.0 ± 0.9 mm) and 59 eyes (age:70.1 ± 12.3 years;axial length: 28.2 ± 2.2 mm), respectively. The GA group versus PA group had a higher degree of intraretinal hyperreflective foci (iHRFs) (3.6 ± 1.1 versus 0.2 ± 0.7; p < 0.001) and para-lesional retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) irregularities (3.9 ± 1.0 versus 0.1 ± 0.6; p < 0.001), higher prevalence of outer nuclear layer thinning (72/79 (91.1%; 95% CI 79,100) versus 36/59 (61.0%; 95% CI 41,82); p < 0.001),and lower prevalence of Bruch´s membrane (BM) defects (0% versus 35/59 (59.3%; 95% CI 40,78)). PAs showed BM defects with absence of choriocapillaris, while in GAs, BM and choriocapillaris were intact. In all eyes with GAs and PAs, the ellipsoid zone and external limiting membrane were defect or absent. Similar findings were obtained upon histology, with intraretinally located RPE cells in GAs in contrast to PAs as additional finding. PA and GA have in common the presence of an RPE-layer opening, and they differ in continuity of BM and adjacent choroidal structures, RPE appearance and prevalence of iHRFs. PAs may be due to an axial elongation-related expansion opening in the RPE layer without marked RPE reaction, while GAs may be associated with a primary RPE reaction including intraretinal RPE cell migration.

publications.title: Global and Regional Risk Factors for Vision Impairment in 2020 and Multi-decadal Trends 1990–2020: A Meta-Analysis and Visual Display Based on Prevalence Data From the Global Burden of Disease study and Vision Loss Expert Group
publications.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate global and regional risk factors for blindness and vision impairment pertaining to all geographical locations between 1990 and 2020. METHODS: (1) Twenty-four covariates were selected with a potential link to vision impairment from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) Covariates database as predictive factors. (2) From these, the linear association was investigated, with crude and age-standardised prevalence estimates of blindness and distance and near vision impairment in 2020 by using data for the whole population, sex and 5-year age groups, and by stratifying severity through mild, moderate, severe and total impairment. (3) Analysis investigated whether percentage rates of change in risk factors were associated with rates of change in prevalence in 1990-2020. RESULTS: For adults (50+ years), for crude and age-standardised vision loss prevalence estimates for the year 2020, a significant negative association of smoking prevalence was found initially for all persons and for each sex, which appears to be due to ecological confounding and became a positive association using more granular regional and age group data. Maternal care and immunisation, sanitation proportion, Health Access and Quality Index and Socio-demographic Index were other significant age-standardised negative associations. Ophthalmologists/million population had a weak but significant protective effect, and positive associations were found for pollution (outdoor and indoor), stronger for greater vision impairment severities. Years in education per capita were weakly, negatively associated with vision loss prevalence, yet zero education proportion had a stronger but positive association for both sexes. CONCLUSIONS: This study confirmed associations at population level globally, which appear to be stable over decades. In addition, the study quantified the contribution of epidemiologically-based risk factors to vision loss at a GBD super-regional level, which is novel. This opens useful avenues for targeted intervention by policymakers. For example, reduction in sex inequity in blindness rates over 30 years has been positively associated with reducing overall prevalence of blindness.

publications.title: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Ophthalmic Foundation Models with Point-Based Classification and Retrieval
publications.abstract: Abstract General-purpose vision foundation models have been evaluated across a wide range of tasks to demonstrate the versatility of their learned representations. By contrast, ophthalmic foundation models have largely been assessed using a narrow set of downstream tasks, primarily disease classification and segmentation, providing only a limited view of their representational capabilities. Considering how clinicians interpret ophthalmic images, where disease-relevant clinical signs are identified before diagnosis, we introduced an ophthalmic foundation model evaluation framework comprising two tasks: 1) point-supervised disease classification and 2) point-guided clinical sign-based image retrieval. Each task incorporates sparse point annotations indicating disease-relevant evidence locations. We applied this approach to diabetic retinopathy using colour fundus photography (CFP) and age-related macular degeneration using both CFP and optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans. Our evaluation spanned 11 foundation models across four newly curated and six established datasets. The results reveal that existing ophthalmic foundation models, despite their strong performance on disease classification, still struggle with the clinical sign retrieval task, although they outperform general-purpose foundation models. Our findings highlight the need to improve these models' capabilities at the fine-grained sign-level. We publicly release our benchmark to facilitate further research on ophthalmic foundation models.

publications.title: Safety of intravitreally applied epidermal growth factor receptor antibody panitumumab
publications.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine the safety of the epidermal growth factor (EGF) receptor antibody panitumumab intravitreally applied in patients with myopic macular degeneration (MMD) or neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD). METHODS: Patients with MMD stage 4 underwent repeated intravitreal panitumumab injections in escalating doses, and patients with neovascular AMD received combined intravitreal ranibizumab/panitumumab injections, with single ranibizumab injections applied in between. RESULTS: The study included 28 patients. In the first cohort, 11 highly myopic patients with MMD stage 4 (age: 66.8 ± 6.3 years) received intravitreal panitumumab injections in doses of 0.6 mg (4 eyes; 1 × 1 injection, 3 × 2 Injections), 1.2 mg (4 eyes; 1 × 1 injection; 2 × 2 injections; 1 × 3 injections) and 1.8 mg (3 eyes; 1 × 1 injection, 2 × 2 injections), respectively, in intervals of 3.6 ± 1.8 months (first to second injection), and 4.7 months (second to third injection). At 3.7 ± 0.4 years (median: 3.6 years; range: 3.5-4.7 years) after the first injection, ten patients were re-examined, with no change in axial length (30.6 ± 1.0 vs. 30.7 ± 1.3; p = 0.66). A second cohort included 17 eyes with neovascular AMD and receiving bimonthly combined panitumumab/ranibizumab (1.2 mg/0.5 mg) injections (mean: 2.4 ± 0.5 injections). The mean follow-up period was 11.0 ± 1.0 months (median: 11 months; range: 6-14 months). In none of the eyes of the first and second cohort, treatment-related systemic or intraocular adverse events were noted. Ocular side effects were hyposphagmata at the injection sites. Signs of intraocular inflammation were not detected in any eye. The morphology of the optic nerve head did not change significantly, nor did the IOP (14.5 ± 4.3 mmHg vs. 13.5 ± 1.5 mmHg; p = 0.30). CONCLUSIONS: Repeated intravitreal panitumumab applications in various doses, single or combined with ranibizumab, were not associated with severe ocular or systemic side effects.

publications.title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: The rapid rise in the burden of non-communicable disease (NCDs) in African communities has resulted in a considerable mortality, disability, and economic burden. A comprehensive evaluation of incidence, deaths, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and attributable risk factors related to NCDs by sex, and geographical location is essential for informing policy decisions aimed at controlling these diseases. METHODS: This study used a comprehensive analysis based on the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 methodology to estimate the incidence, mortality, DALYs (estimated as the sum of years of life lost and years lived with disability [YLDs]), and attributable risk factors of NCDs in Africa. Data were systematically searched for and extracted from various sources, including vital registration, verbal autopsy, surveillance systems, police reports, censuses, surveys, minimally invasive tissue sampling, and sibling history. The analysis employed the Cause of Death Ensemble model, DisMod-MR 2.1, and spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression to estimate both fatal and non-fatal health metrics associated with NCDs in Africa overall, and by region and country. FINDINGS: In 2023, NCDs in Africa accounted for an estimated 2·33 billion (95% uncertainty interval 2·22-2·50) incident cases, 4·70 million (4·47-4·93) deaths, and 263 million (234-293) DALYs. Although absolute numbers increased between 1990 and 2023, age-standardised rates (per 100 000 population) decreased modestly: incidence rate by 2·7% (0·2-5·0), mortality rate by 9·0% (2·5-15·5), and DALY rate by 6·4% (1·2-12·0). The five leading Level 3 causes of death in Africa in 2023 were ischaemic heart disease (801 000 [653 000-965 000]), stroke (700 000 [544 000-863 000]), chronic kidney disease (293 000 [224 000-359 000], hypertensive heart disease (246 000 [170 000-337 000]), and diabetes (245 000 [190 000-314 000]) for all sexes and ages. Leading Level 2 causes of YLDs were mental disorders (30·9 million [22·0-42·2]) and musculoskeletal disorders (17·1 million [12·5-22·7]). Overall, 35·1% (32·4-38·2) of DALYs and 57·4% (54·2-60·4) of deaths due to NCDs were attributable to the 88 GBD 2023 risk factors. High systolic blood pressure contributed the largest proportion at 26·2% (21·6-30·9) of all NCD deaths in Africa, followed by dietary risks (14·7% [5·1-21·6]) and air pollution (14·2% [11·6-16·9]). INTERPRETATION: Our findings underscore the complex and evolving nature of the NCD burden in Africa, where modest declines in age-standardised mortality and DALY rates since 1990 have been substantially offset by rising absolute counts of deaths and DALYs-a paradox driven predominantly by rapid population growth and demographic changes. That more than half of all NCD deaths and over a third of DALYs remain attributable to modifiable risk factors-principally high systolic blood pressure, dietary risks, and air pollution-suggests that a substantial and actionable proportion of this burden is preventable through available and effective interventions, carrying urgent implications for African governments, ministries of health, and global health partners, who must take decisive action to meet health commitments. FUNDING: Gates Foundation.

publications.title: Tropomyosin Cable Formation and Its Influence on the Structural Dynamics of Tropomyosin
Spontaneous transitions of actin-bound tropomyosin toward blocked and closed states
publications.abstract: After muscle contraction, myosin cross-bridge heads detach from thin actin filaments during relaxation. Structural and kinetic data of cross-bridge–thin filament interactions have shown that tropomyosin’s position on F-actin is biased toward the blocked or closed states when myosin detaches. It is not clear if structural linkages between tropomyosin and myosin cross-bridge heads, or tropomyosin and Ca2+-free troponin, drive the process or whether tropomyosin movement is energetically independent of myosin and troponin influence. Here we provide in silico data about tropomyosin dynamics on troponin/myosin-free F-actin indicating that tropomyosin moves from the open state toward blocked- or closed-state positions on actin. To follow transitions inherent to tropomyosin itself on F-actin, we performed MD simulations initiated from the blocked-, open-, and intermediate-state models and followed tropomyosin over the surface of F-actin in the absence of myosin and troponin. These MD simulations maintain tropomyosin in a cable-like conformation, including the tropomyosin overlap domain, while allowing tropomyosin to retain most of its motional freedom. Tropomyosin shows considerable azimuthal movement away from the open state toward the surrounds of a more energetically favorable blocked B-state position over F-actin. In contrast, little movement away from the B-state location is observed. Our results are consistent with previous predictions based on electrostatic interaction energy landscapes determined by rigid-body translocation of tropomyosin. They support the view that in the absence of myosin, i.e., when myosin cross-bridges detach from actin, the blocked- or closed-state positions of tropomyosin are energetically favored, while the open state is not.

publications.title: Customer service in dentistry: Analysing online reviews of oral care using topic modelling and semantic annotation
publications.abstract: This paper investigates a collection of patient reviews of oral care in England as a form of online feedback, uncovering ‘marketised’ discourses in how reviewers position themselves in relation to dental services. Dentistry has historically navigated tensions between its treatment objectives and commercialised drives and increased privatisation in oral care has also facilitated the growth of discourses of ‘marketisation’, positing patients as ‘customers’ and health professionals as ‘service providers’, working in clinics subject to price-based competition. The vast collection of reviews available online provides insights into patient perspectives on what is important in oral care as well as these growing market practices. We apply a combined topic modelling and semantic annotation approach to investigate a corpus of 48,917 online patient reviews of oral care in England. While topic modelling is an effective approach for providing an initial overview of large collections of language data, further analysis is required to provide meaningful interpretations of latent topics. We combine the outputs of the topic modelling process with semantic annotation, which has similarly been shown to facilitate analyses on the basis of frequently occurring ‘themes’. We highlight the prevalence of aspects of ‘customer service’ in the data and discuss the extent to which reviewers engage with the commercialised aspects of oral care in their reviews. We contextualise these views within the increasing marketisation of dentistry in the UK and the broader expansion of neoliberal models of healthcare.

publications.title: How to Develop Trustworthy Evidence‐Informed Clinical and Public Health Guidelines in Oral Health: Methodological Strategies
publications.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To identify barriers for the development of evidence-informed guidelines and propose potential methodological strategies addressing key barriers to producing trustworthy evidence-informed guidelines in oral health (OH). METHODS: Findings from a qualitative study exploring barriers in OH guideline development were used, and an international working group of experts in guideline methodology and individuals with experience in clinical and public health guidelines in OH was recruited. Through an iterative consensus approach, the following steps were followed: (1) identification of barriers related to the guideline development process itself and could be addressed through implementing or enhancing methodological strategies; (2) determination of the relevance of these challenges for guideline developers and research methodologists; and (3) agreement on the content and structure of each methodological strategy to address a particular barrier. Current methodological handbooks and publications on evidence-informed guideline development informed this process. The nominal group technique was used to reach consensus, concluding when no further comments were raised and the participants confirmed that no additional modifications were needed. RESULTS: Twelve experts from nine countries participated. The working group consolidated current methodology into nine strategies addressing 13 identified barriers. The document covers: defining when a document qualifies as an 'evidence-informed guideline'; practical approaches for defining guideline topics, scope, and questions; using pre-existing systematic reviews; formulating recommendations with limited or indirect evidence; developing recommendations on dental products; integrating economic considerations and people values and preferences; and involving non-dental healthcare professionals in OH guideline development. DISCUSSION: These strategies support guideline methodologists and lead developers in producing trustworthy clinical and public health guidelines in OH at global, regional, national, and subnational levels. They aim to improve the quality, consistency, and applicability of OH guidelines, facilitating integration of reliable evidence into oral healthcare decision-making to achieve better health outcomes and more effective health systems.

Covariate-adjusted 2-way fixed effects linear and Poisson models estimated risk differences and risk ratios for contemporaneous and cumulative (10-y average) exposures, complemented by heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences estimators; the parallel trends assumption was assessed empirically and with causal diagrams. A $1.00 increase in the combined cigarette tax reduced current smoking by 0.35 percentage points (95% CI: -0.56, -0.13) and increased quitting by 0.51 percentage points (95% CI: 0.19, 0.82); the smoking reduction persisted under sustained exposure (10-y average tax: -0.47 percentage points; 95% CI: -0.95, 0.01), and retail prices showed similar effects. In contrast, taxes and prices showed no robust effect on tooth loss. Complete edentulism was unrelated to taxes in every covariate-adjusted specification (current-year tax: 0.08 percentage points; 95% CI: -0.14, 0.31), and loss of ≥6 teeth showed only a weak, statistically nonsignificant protective association that was strongest for cumulative exposure (10-y average tax: -0.44 percentage points; 95% CI: -1.17, 0.30). Indoor smoking bans (restaurant and mall/grocery) were not associated with lower smoking or less tooth loss; point estimates were small and several were positive (e.g., restaurant ban and current smoking: +0.11 percentage points; 95% CI: -0.34, 0.55), and the mall/grocery ban failed a negative control test. Cigarette taxation and pricing remain powerful levers for reducing smoking, but a population-level benefit for tooth loss could not be demonstrated within this 18-y window, and indoor smoking bans showed no robust effect on either outcome; the suggestive association between sustained tax exposure and severe tooth loss warrants evaluation over longer horizons.
