publications.title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma
publications.abstract: Mature, germinal centre-bearing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and mature lymph node follicles (secondary lymphoid structures, SLS) sustain the plasma cell response that shapes outcome and immunotherapy benefit in lung cancer. How this loco-regional axis differs between neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive tumors is poorly defined. We analyzed H&E whole-slide images of resected tumors and paired proximal and distal lymph nodes from matched neoadjuvant-treated (neoLUSC, n=20) and therapy-naive (naivLUSC, n=20) lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) patients. Aignostics Atlas H&E Tissue Analysis (HETA) models quantified cell densities per tissue compartment and cell-cell co-localization; a dedicated deep-learning model validated against pathologist annotations detected TLS and SLS and graded their maturity. Prognostic value was tested in an independent cohort (n=458; 46 treated). In neoLUSC tumors, stromal plasma cell density was 72% (p=0.004) and stromal lymphocyte density 48% (p=0.015) lower than in naivLUSC; macrophages and granulocytes did not differ significantly. Total and immature TLS did not differ, whereas mature TLS in the tumor (p=0.034) and mature SLS in the tumor-distal lymph node (p=0.003) were lower in neoLUSC patients. Peri-TLS plasma cell density correlated with tumor lymphocyte density in naivLUSC (rho=0.54, p=0.017) but not in neoLUSC tumors (rho=0.07). In the validation cohort, stromal plasma cell density (HR 0.69, p=0.011) and lymphocyte-plasma cell co-localization (HR 0.66, p=0.004) were associated with longer survival, and neoadjuvant status with shorter survival (HR 1.50, p=0.026). Neoadjuvant therapy is thus associated with fewer mature lymphoid structures and weaker coupling of the humoral compartment to the tumor rather than uniformly lower immune readouts. The stromal plasma cell/co-localization axis is a candidate prognostic biomarker.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

publications.title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
publications.abstract: Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

publications.title: Pathology foundation models for training-free case retrieval in salivary gland tumors
publications.abstract: In pathology, pattern recognition relies on a frame of reference built through extensive training and experience, which may still fall short when encountering rare cancer subtypes. Archives of previously diagnosed tumors often contain relevant precedents, yet identifying the most relevant cases remains challenging. Here we explore whether content-based retrieval with current pathology foundation models facilitates rare cancer diagnostics without any task-specific training. Pathologists can query a digitized archive using a region of interest (ROI) from a whole slide image (WSI) and retrieve morphologically similar cases, along with their ICD-O codes and corresponding WSIs. The ROI can be selected manually or automatically using a gated attention-based multiple instance learning model. We evaluate our approach by leave-one-case-out on an imbalanced dataset of 137 salivary gland tumor cases spanning 12 ICD-O morphology categories, comparing four pathology foundation models (Atlas2, Atlas2-B, Atlas2-S, and UNI2h). Top-1/3/5 retrieval was 62.5%/76.7%/81.3% for Atlas2, 50.2/66.6/72.9% for UNI2h, 52.3%/71.5%/77.6% for Atlas2-B and 54.4/65.2/73.7% for Atlas2-S. Macro-averaged F1 ranged from 69.0% for the smallest model Atlas2-S to 76.6% for the largest model Atlas2 across the five classes with at least ten cases. Our modified Chamfer similarity separated correct from incorrect matches among the Top-5 more reliably for Atlas2 (AUC 0.754) than for Atlas2-B (0.679, p = 0.020) and Atlas2-S (0.653, p = 0.003), but not UNI2h (0.697, p = 0.196). Requiring no additional training or manual annotation, this approach makes departmental archives searchable with pathology foundation models, providing a low-barrier route to case-based differential diagnosis and extending the individual frame of reference to the collective experience of the department.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

publications.title: Comparative Immunohistochemical Analysis of FAP and c-MET Expression Across Renal Cell Carcinoma Subtypes: Preliminary Results and Potential Theranostic Implications
publications.abstract: Background: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) comprises multiple histopathological subtypes with distinct biological characteristics and clinical behavior. Despite advances in conventional imaging, the detection of small RCC lesions or distant metastases remains challenging and the prognosis of advanced RCC is still poor. Theranostic approaches are promising tools combining diagnostic imaging and targeted radionuclide-based cancer therapy. The identification of suitable molecular targets in tumor tissue is a major focus of current research. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) and hepatocyte growth factor receptor (c-MET) have been proposed as theranostic targets in several solid cancers, including RCC. However, available data are limited and inconsistent, particularly regarding expression patterns across different RCC subtypes. Methods: In this study, we evaluated the expression patterns of FAP and c-MET immunohistochemically across major RCC subtypes (clear cell RCC [ccRCC], papillary RCC [pRCC], and chromophobe RCC [cpRCC]). Staining intensity was assessed semi-quantitatively and correlated with histological RCC subtypes. Results: FAP expression differed substantially among RCC subtypes, being highest in ccRCC, significantly lower in pRCC, and largely absent in cpRCC. In contrast, c-MET was ubiquitously expressed across all three RCC subtypes but showed a lower specificity for tumor cells. Conclusions: Our results provide a rationale for further evaluating FAP and c-MET as potential theranostic targets across RCC subtypes and establishing a foundation for future RCC-subtype-specific imaging-pathology correlation studies. Validation in larger multicenter cohorts including paired molecular imaging data is required before their clinical translation can be considered.

publications.title: Matched primary-metastasis single-nucleus and spatial profiling of leiomyosarcoma identifies antigen-presenting fibroblasts at the tumor-organ interface
publications.abstract: Abstract Leiomyosarcoma is an aggressive soft tissue sarcoma that metastasizes preferentially to lung and liver. Because matched primary and metastatic specimens are rarely available, the cellular changes that accompany metastatic progression remain poorly defined. Here we combined single-nucleus RNA sequencing of archival FFPE tissue from four matched primary-metastasis pairs (two lung, two liver metastases; 48,941 nuclei) with imaging-based spatial transcriptomics of an extended tissue microarray cohort of 21 patients (69 cores, 313,218 cells). Malignant cells, not assignable from transcriptomic references alone, were defined by inferred copy number profiles that were concordant with matched DNA methylation arrays and confirmed the clonal origin of each metastasis. Malignant metaprograms were organ-associated, with a stress- and hypoxia-associated program enriched in lung metastases and a proliferative, matrix-remodeling program enriched in liver metastases. Antigen-presenting cancer-associated fibroblasts (apCAFs) were enriched in metastases relative to matched primaries. This shift was reproduced in the spatial cohort (p = 0.001), where apCAFs formed a discrete band at the tumor-organ interface between malignant cells and adjacent parenchyma, whereas they were sparse and randomly distributed in primary tumors. Spatial transcriptomics further resolved the malignant compartment into three histomolecular phenotypes: (i) smooth-muscle-like with myxoid features, (ii) GPNMB⁺ with anaplastic features, and (iii) PDGFRB⁺ with vessel-rich stroma, each with a concordant immunohistochemical (α-SMA, GPNMB, PDGFRB) and morphological correlate. Together, our data provide a matched primary-metastasis reference for leiomyosarcoma, identify apCAFs as a spatially organized, metastasis-associated stromal population, and delineate histomolecular phenotypes recognizable by routine immunohistochemistry, including a GPNMB⁺ phenotype potentially amenable to GPNMB-directed therapies.

publications.title: Variance of human cortical synaptic transmission inferred from non-invasive magnetoencephalography of somatosensory evoked population spikes
publications.abstract: Non-invasive recordings of somatosensory evoked brain responses (SERs) contain high-frequency (∼600 Hz) evoked responses (hfSERs) which can be recorded at the single-trial level using ultralow-noise magnetoencephalography (MEG). hfSERs were shown to represent cortical population spikes and consist of an early (pre-synaptic) and a late (post-synaptic) component. Here, a statistical model of cortical population spiking reproduced single-trial hfSERs evoked by median-nerve stimulation in 5 healthy subjects. hfSERs were best replicated when variability was added only to the late (post-synaptic) model component, explaining 85% of inter-trial variability across subjects. Adding variability also to the early (pre-synaptic) component caused overfitting in most subjects, yet still indicated larger amplitude and latency variability post-synaptically. This proof-of-concept establishes model-based inference from non-invasively recorded population spikes as a means to estimate synaptic transmission variability in human neocortex. The approach opens a route to studying synaptic function in health and disease where invasive recordings are unavailable.

publications.title: Somatosensory evoked potentials in the human spinal cord to mixed nerve stimulation
publications.abstract: This dataset contains simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG), electrospinography (ESG), electroneurography (ENG), and electromyography (EMG) recordings from 40 participants, together with electrocardiographic and respiratory signals. Four conditions were recorded: resting state with eyes open, mixed median nerve stimulation, mixed tibial nerve stimulation, and alternating median/tibial stimulation. ESG electrode positions are provided for each participant. The study was pre-registered on OSF.

publications.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG), electrospinography (ESG), electroneurography (ENG) and electromyography (EMG) recordings from 26 participants, together with electrocardiographic and respiratory signals. Somatosensory evoked potentials were elicited by mixed nerve stimulation (median and tibial nerves) and sensory nerve stimulation of fingers and toes, alongside a resting-state condition with eyes open. publications.title: Laser-evoked potentials in the human spinal cord and cortex

publications.abstract: This dataset comprises simultaneous multimodal neurophysiological recordings (EEG, electrospinography, electroneurography, and EMG) from 26 participants during resting state and various somatosensory stimulation conditions targeting mixed nerves (median and tibial) and individual digits. The dataset enables investigation of somatosensory evoked potentials and their propagation through the central and peripheral nervous system across multiple recording modalities.

publications.title: Atrial fibrillation begets atrial fibrillation – serum-driven amplification of atrial electrical instability
publications.abstract: Rationale Atrial fibrillation (AF) is sustained by electrical triggers and atrial substrate, but whether AF itself generates circulating factors that acutely reinforce arrhythmogenesis is unknown. Objective To determine whether rhythm-dependent serum bioactivity directly destabilizes atrial electrophysiology and to identify associated cellular mechanisms and circulating mediators. Methods and Results Cardiac samples were obtained from patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) during AF and after restoration of sinus rhythm (SR) using electrical cardioversion. In isolated Langendorff-perfused mouse hearts, AF serum increased the duration, frequency, and cumulative burden of spontaneous atrial depolarizations compared with paired control perfusate. In human induced pluripotent stem cell derived atrial cardiomyocytes, AF patient serum decreased Ca²⁺-transient amplitudes without significant effect on kinetics or Ca²⁺ spark activity. Moreover, AF serum reduced peak sodium current without materially altering voltage-dependent gating or paced action-potential properties. Data-independent acquisition proteomics identified rhythm-associated changes in extracellular-matrix, proteolytic, inflammatory, and signaling proteins, including MMP9, Ccathepsin G, and 14-3-3 family members. Targeted pathway perturbation differentially modified serum-induced Ca²⁺ phenotypes, indicating context-dependent, multifactorial bioactivity. Serum-induced Ca²⁺ responses were not associated with indices of atrial disease severity, including low-voltage substrate burden and left atrial pressure. Conclusions Persistent AF is accompanied by rhythm-dependent circulating bioactivity that acutely promotes atrial electrical instability and Ca²⁺-dependent trigger formation. These findings extend the concept that “AF begets AF” beyond tissue-intrinsic remodeling and identify a potentially reversible serum-mediated feed-forward mechanism linking rhythm status and circulating proteomic signals in an atrial substrate severity independent fashion.

publications.title: Non-linear association between body mass index and sudden cardiac death after myocardial infarction: a PROFID pooled cohort sub-analysis
publications.abstract: Abstract Background The relationship between body mass index (BMI) and sudden cardiac death (SCD) after myocardial infarction (MI) remains incompletely characterised. While BMI demonstrates a J-shaped association with SCD in the general population, data specific to post-MI patients remain limited. Purpose We examined whether BMI is non-linearly associated with long-term SCD risk in a large international pooled cohort of post-MI patients. Methods This analysis included 121,481 post-MI patients from the PROFID pooled dataset with available BMI, survival time, and SCD data. BMI was modelled as a continuous variable using restricted cubic splines to assess potential non-linear associations with SCD risk. A BMI of 25 kg/m² was used as the reference value for hazard ratio estimation. In non-ICD patients, the primary outcome was SCD within 90 months following index MI. In ICD carriers, the outcome was appropriate ICD-therapy as the best available surrogate for SCD. Multivariable cause-specific Cox models were adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates. Model robustness was evaluated using alternative spline specifications, fractional polynomial modelling, proportional hazards diagnostics, competing risk analyses (Fine–Gray), and complete-case comparisons. Results During follow-up, 2,865 SCD events (2.4%) occurred. In multivariable cause-specific Cox models, BMI demonstrated a significant non-linear association with 90-month SCD risk (global spline p<0.001). The lowest estimated hazard occurred at BMI 22.8 kg/m². Relative to BMI 25 kg/m², SCD risk increased progressively with higher BMI, reaching approximately a hazard ratio of 1.45 at BMI 35 kg/m². Lower BMI values were associated with only a modest excess hazard. The extended model demonstrated good discrimination (C-index 0.815) and excellent calibration. The non-linear association remained consistent across alternative spline specifications, fractional polynomial modelling, proportional hazards sensitivity analyses, and competing risk analysis using Fine–Gray models. Conclusions In this large multinational post-MI cohort, BMI demonstrated a non-linear association with long-term SCD risk, with the lowest risk observed at BMI 22.8 kg/m² and progressively increasing risk at higher BMI values. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the association between BMI and SCD in post-MI populations.

publications.title: All-cause mortality in post–myocardial infarction patients with reduced LVEF with and without ICD therapy: insights from the PROFID study
publications.abstract: Abstract Background Previous randomized trials have demonstrated a survival benefit of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) therapy in patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). However, advances in heart failure therapy and post–myocardial infarction (MI) management over the past decade may have modified contemporary outcome patterns. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the association between ICD implantation and all-cause mortality (ACM) in post-MI patients with LVEF ≤35%, and to assess whether this association differs according to era of inclusion Methods We analyzed 140,204 post-MI patients in the PROFID study cohort, including 7,543 ICD patients and 25,058 non-ICD patients. The primary endpoint was ACM. Kaplan–Meier methods were used to estimate mortality. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation. Baseline differences between ICD and non-ICD patients with LVEF ≤35% were adjusted using propensity score overlap weighting. Weighted Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between ICD therapy and mortality, including an interaction term between ICD status and era (pre-2016 vs ≥2016). Eras were defined by the year of inclusion or ICD implantation, with 2016 as the cut-off to reflect broader temporal changes in management patterns in this population. Results During a median follow-up of 54.5±38.3 months, 33,699 deaths occurred in the overall cohort. Crude mortality proportions were 17.8% in ICD patients, 43.5% in non-ICD patients with LVEF ≤35%. In the propensity score–weighted cohort, before 2016, ACM was lower in ICD patients than in non-ICD patients with LVEF ≤35%, whereas in the post-2016 era (2016 and later), no survival advantage in ICD patients was observed (Figure). Before 2016, ICD implantation was associated with a substantially lower risk of mortality compared with no ICD (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.54-0.62, P < 0.01). In contrast, in the post-2016 era, the association was attenuated and not statistically significant (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.93-1.64, P = 0.14). The association between ICD implantation and mortality differed significantly between eras (multiplicative interaction HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.59-2.85, P < 0.01), indicating a marked attenuation of the previously observed association in the contemporary era. Conclusion In the contemporary era (2016 and later), ACM in ICD patients did not differ significantly from that in matched non-ICD patients with LVEF ≤35%. These findings suggest evolving outcome patterns in the modern therapeutic era and warrant further investigation.Figure

publications.title: Temporal trends and determinants of heart failure therapy after myocardial infarction: a PROFID subanalysis
publications.abstract: Abstract Background Patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) after myocardial infarction (MI) remain at high risk of adverse outcomes. Guideline-directed medical therapy reduces morbidity and mortality; however, long-term implementation patterns across heterogeneous healthcare settings are not well characterised. Purpose We evaluated temporal trends and determinants of baseline receipt of standard HFrEF therapy in post-MI patients with LVEF <40% over two decades. Methods We conducted a retrospective pooled analysis of harmonised individual-level data from multiple post-MI databases (2000–2020). The primary endpoint was baseline receipt of triple therapy consisting of an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB), beta-blocker, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA). Angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitors and sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors were excluded due to absence in historical datasets. Temporal trends and determinants were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression (complete-case primary analysis; multiple imputation sensitivity analysis). Prespecified interaction tests assessed heterogeneity by age group and database, with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate adjustment. Results Among 30,830 eligible post-MI patients with HFrEF (median age 72 years; 71.5% male), baseline use of ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker was high (82.1% and 86.7%, respectively), whereas MRA use was low (10.4%). In the complete-case multivariable analysis (n=19,324; 1,914 received triple therapy), receipt of triple therapy increased over calendar time (adjusted OR per 1-year increase 1.50; 95% CI 1.47–1.53; p<0.001), yet fewer than 10% of patients received triple therapy at baseline. Age >75 years was independently associated with lower odds of triple therapy (aOR 0.72; 95% CI 0.62–0.84), whereas diabetes (aOR 1.32; 95% CI 1.17–1.48) and hypertension (aOR 1.23; 95% CI 1.10–1.37) were associated with higher odds. There was no significant heterogeneity of temporal trends by age (interaction p=0.094; FDR-adjusted p=0.187) or by database (p=0.673). Findings were consistent in sensitivity analyses. Conclusion In this large multi-database cohort of post-MI patients with HFrEF from 2000–2020, uptake of foundational triple therapy increased substantially over time but remained low overall, particularly among older patients. These findings underscore persistent gaps in the implementation of evidence-based HFrEF therapy in routine post-MI care.

publications.title: Cluster-Based Phenotyping in an HFpEF Population Identifies a Biomarker-High, Atrial-Dysfunction Phenotype with Impaired Quality of Life, Reduced Exercise Capacity and Higher Healthcare Utilization
publications.abstract: Background/Objectives: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome. Atrial remodeling represents an important dimension of HFpEF beyond the presence of atrial fibrillation (AF). We aimed to identify clinically meaningful atrial phenotypes using unsupervised clustering. Methods: Overall, 153 patients were analyzed from a prospective HFpEF registry who underwent clinical assessment, laboratory testing, electrocardiography, resting and stress echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Consensus k-means clustering across multiply imputed datasets integrated markers of atrial structure and function, biomarkers, and hemodynamic burden. Clinical characteristics, functional capacity, quality of life and 12-month healthcare utilization were compared between clusters. Sensitivity analyses assessed cluster robustness. Results: Two phenotypes were identified. Cluster 1 (n = 66) was characterized by higher biomarker and hemodynamic burden, impaired renal function, larger left atrial volume index, and reduced left atrial reservoir strain. Variables not included in cluster generation also differed between phenotypes: Cluster 1 showed poorer exercise capacity, shorter six-minute walking distance, worse quality of life, and a higher observed all-cause hospitalization burden. The hospitalization finding was considered exploratory. The principal cluster structure was preserved in sensitivity analyses, including complete-case analysis. Conclusions: The clustering approach identified an HFpEF phenotype characterized by biomarker elevation and advanced atrial remodeling. The phenotype was associated with greater functional impairment and adverse patient-reported characteristics. These clinical associations support the potential relevance of multidimensional atrial phenotyping, although the findings remain hypothesis-generating and require validation in independent cohorts.

publications.title: Exchange Rate Insulation Revisited
publications.abstract: We confront the notion that flexible exchange rates insulate countries from external disturbances with new evidence for the euro area (EA) and 20 of its neighbors. Using high-frequency data, we first establish that countries with flexible exchange rates ("floats") let their currencies depreciate in response to EA monetary policy shocks, while "pegs" raise interest rates. Yet at business cycle frequency, these depreciations do not translate into insulation: floats contract just as much as pegs—not only in response to monetary policy shocks but also to other shocks originating in the EA. This result appears puzzling in light of received wisdom, but we show that it can be rationalized within a state-of-the-art HANK model and flesh out the underlying transmission channels.

publications.title: A strong clean industrial deal to reconcile Europe's decarbonization, competitiveness and security objectives
publications.abstract: In 2025 the US implemented unilateral import tariffs and passed tax legislation to reduce income and corporate tax rates (‘Big Beautifull Bill’). We regard import tariffs as a new fiscal policy. Tariff revenues are used to finance income and corporate tax cuts to increase investment. We expect this to be a permanent policy change and address two questions. What does this mean for the EU? What are suitable fiscal options for the EU? Economic models and econometric studies suggested that unilateral tariffs lead to a real appreciation. However, this prediction did not materialize. We therefore consider two scenarios: standard response with a dollar appreciation (standard scenario); tariff without appreciation (risk scenario). We show that a permanent unilateral US tariff has negative potential growth effects in the EU, irrespective of the exchange rate. Policies to foster EU competitiveness via reducing taxes on labour, capital, and increasing public investment, VAT financed, can partially offset the tariff spillovers.

publications.title: Odds-Structured Distributional Regression for Interpretable Time-to-Event Prediction
publications.abstract: Time-to-event prediction is fundamentally challenged by partial observability and aleatoric uncertainty. In clinical medicine, for instance, the timing of disease progression or acute readmission is contingent on highly dynamic and largely latent health trajectories. Rather than forcing a deterministic point forecast, distributional regression offers a principled means to address this complexity by predicting a probability distribution over time. However, explaining these distributional predictions presents a key obstacle: raw distribution parameters output by the model are abstract mathematical quantities that do not align well with domain concepts. To gain interpretability, we propose a novel paradigm where output parameters are designed to be additive in log-odds---a widely established measure in clinical risk modeling. Our approach, called ODDS-DR, moves beyond technical convenience to deliver clear domain alignment as well as the layer-wise computational structure required for robust, time-dependent feature attribution. Validated across two real-world clinical cohorts, our framework matches state-of-the-art predictive performance while resolving distributional outputs into interpretable risk markers across flexible prognostic horizons.

publications.title: Revisiting Explainable AI through Model-Independent Concept Dictionaries
publications.abstract: Modern applications of AI rely on increasingly complex models. Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a set of techniques aimed at improving model transparency. However, existing XAI methods typically assume input features to be inherently interpretable, or they rely on intermediate internal abstractions that are difficult to characterize and highly architecture-specific, hindering consistent use across models. To address these limitations, we propose DictXAI, a method that defines concepts directly in the input domain via a dictionary---a large, potentially overcomplete set of predefined elements, each carrying an interpretable meaning. Technically, DictXAI first computes a sparse code of the input and then attributes the model's prediction to the associated dictionary elements. We demonstrate the actionable nature of DictXAI explanations, showing that they can attribute AI malfunctions (e.g., Clever Hans effects) directly to identifiable artifact patterns in the data, while fostering human-AI alignment on intricate biomedical signals. We further demonstrate our method's ability to operate across a wide variety of dictionaries, including learned image bases, analytically defined waveforms for electrocardiography, and experimentally acquired dictionary elements. Overall, our results show that DictXAI provides more interpretable, actionable, and architecture-agnostic insights than classical XAI or existing concept-based approaches.

publications.title: An explainable transformer model learning from entire treatment timelines for pan-cancer risk profiling across healthcare systems
publications.abstract: Abstract Cancer outcomes vary widely between individual patients, each accumulating an irregular record of treatments, diagnoses, measurements, and complications. Current prognostic models reduce this complexity into a single snapshot, focus on narrow clinical settings, and rarely generalize across hospitals. Here we introduce Chronicle , an explainable transformer that learns from entire patient trajectories to predict diverse clinical outcomes throughout the disease course while capturing both short- and long-term temporal dependencies. Trained on 53.7 million longitudinal data points from 51,711 patients spanning 67 cancer types, Chronicle operates natively on irregular data without imputation and jointly predicts eight endpoints within a flexible framework adaptable to additional outcomes. Chronicle outperformed cross-sectional models for overall survival prediction (C-index 0.84 vs 0.76-0.79), stratified patients more accurately than established prognostic systems, including TNM stage, and predicted seven adverse event and transfusion endpoints (AUC 0.80-0.92). Applied without retraining to 69,341 patients in Germany, Switzerland, and the United States, Chronicle generalized across healthcare systems and improved further with local fine-tuning. Integrated explainability traced each risk update to patient-specific clinical factors, revealing distinct temporal persistence of prognostic information, with relevance half-lives ranging from weeks for therapies to nearly one year for baseline characteristics. These findings demonstrate that learning from hospital-wide patient trajectories enables interpretable and continuously updated predictions, providing a scalable framework to support individualized treatment decisions.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

publications.title: Large language models enable prognostic stratification of cancer patients using real-world clinical notes
publications.abstract: In medical documentation, vast amounts of unstructured text are generated that are still underutilized in current prognostic models. We investigate the potential of self-hosted large language models (LLM) to extract clinically meaningful, patient-specific information from routine clinical notes for personalized risk stratification in cancer care. We collected real-world medical notes from 2,708 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients and 814 colon cancer patients documented before treatment at a large comprehensive cancer center. LLMs extracted key prognostic indicators, including comorbidities, metastatic sites, and qualitative descriptors of patient condition, in a zero-shot manner without prior task-specific training. Integrating these LLM-derived features into machine learning models significantly improved the prediction of overall survival compared to TNM staging alone (C-Index: NSCLC, 0.72 vs 0.64; colon cancer, 0.70 vs 0.59), and surpassed models using text embeddings. Based on the LLM-informed risk scores, patients were stratified into four distinct risk groups, enabling reclassification of 61.4% of NSCLC and 68.3% of colon cancer patients. Analysis of model drivers revealed that LLM-derived factors, such as the physical condition, substantially modulated the prognostic impact of TNM stage. These findings highlight the potential of self-hosted LLM to derive prognostically relevant information from unstructured clinical documentation and support clinical decision-making.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging
Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

publications.title: Prediction of hypertension and restenosis under guideline-directed management in aortic coarctation: development and validation of machine-learning models
publications.abstract: Background: Aortic coarctation (CoA) is a major cause of arterial hypertension in young individuals, with recurrence occurring in up to one-third of patients throughout life despite guideline-directed management. Methods: We conducted a development and validation study at a single centre in Berlin, Germany, utilising routinely collected electronic health records, cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), and mid-/long-term follow-up data from 218 visits (160 individuals with CoA receiving standard of care, guideline-based management) collected between January 2014 and April 2022. Machine learning (ML) models (CatBoost, XGBoost, random forest, support vector classifiers, neural networks, logistic regression, and K-nearest neighbours) were developed to predict three endpoints: re-coarctation requiring intervention (CoA-I), aortic surgery (CoA-S) as a subset of CoA-I, and persistent arterial hypertension. The dataset was divided by random stratified split into a training set (n = 159; for model development with five-fold cross-validation), and a hold-out test set (n = 59; for out-of-sample validation). Stratification was based on sex, age, and CoA-I status. We included a final set of 38 clinically relevant features, encompassing baseline characteristics, medication intake, echocardiography, CMR, electrocardiography (ECG), and treatment decisions. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02591940. Findings: Tree-based and support vector classifier models performed best after Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, yielding high performance in a stratified validation cohort: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC) 0.90 ± 0.01 for CoA-I, 0.90 ± 0.01 for CoA-S, and 0.84 ± 0.01 for hypertension. Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) highlighted peak Doppler gradient, time since index visit, and ventricular size indices as key predictors for CoA-I. In inverse-probability-weighted analyses, antihypertensive medication was associated with a lower CoA-I probability (-17.3%; 95% confidence interval [CI], -28.2 to -6.4; p = 0.002), with concordant propensity-score-matched findings. An open-access research interface (https://icm.dhzc.charite.de/calc_coa) incorporates treatment thresholds and personalised risk estimates from an updatable ML framework. Interpretation: These findings suggest that patient-specific multimodal ML-based risk estimates may complement guideline-based care by identifying patients at increased risk of CoA-I or persistent hypertension, with the potential to support more tailored follow-up and reduce lifetime exposure to brachiocephalic hypertension. In adjusted cohort-level analyses, antihypertensive medication was associated with a lower probability of CoA-I. Funding: This study was supported by the European Commission's Seventh Framework Programme (FP7, project ID 611232). M.K. acknowledges support within the Charité Digital Clinician Scientist Programme funded by DFG. M.K. and T.K. have received funding within the CHAIN project (Project ID: 101314833), supported by the European Union's EU4Health Programme. T.K. and M.K. acknowledge support within the Collaborative Research Centre SFB 1470, funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation), project ID 437531118. M.K. has received funding from the Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR, Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space), VADYS-ME, grant number 01EJ2406A.

name: H. Lacker

publications.title: Measurement of isolated photon plus two-jet correlations in Pb+Pb and pp collisions at 5.02 TeV with ATLAS
publications.abstract: This paper presents a measurement of photon plus two-jet events in pp and Pb+Pb collisions, i.e. events in which the transverse momentum of a single photon is balanced by two distinct jets. The measurement was performed using pp data taken in 2017 with an integrated luminosity 260 pb − 1 , and Pb+Pb data taken in 2018 with an integrated luminosity 1.72 nb − 1 , both at s NN =5.02 TeV, as recorded by the ATLAS detector. Events with photons in the transverse momentum range 90–180 GeV and at least two anti- k t R = 0.2 jets with a p T > 30 GeV are selected, and three observables are measured: x JJ γ , A JJ γ , and Δ R JJ . These observables characterise the overall energy loss of the multiparton system from medium interactions (x JJ γ ), the relative energy loss between the two colour-charge carriers (A JJ γ ), and medium-induced modifications to their opening angle (Δ R JJ ). The observables are corrected for uncorrelated combinatoric background contributions using a novel multijet mixing technique, for photon purity, and for detector resolution effects via iterative unfolding. Final results are presented per photon, and the ratio ( I AA ) is taken between measurements in Pb+Pb and pp collisions, for Pb+Pb centrality intervals of 30–80%, 10–30%, and 0–10%. Significant suppression of per photon two-jet yields in all three observables, I AA < 1, is observed as a result of parton-medium interactions. The experimental measurements are compared to three different jet quenching models: Jewel , Jetscape , and Lbt .
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for $$ t\overline{t} $$ resonances in final states with exactly one or two leptons using 140 fb−1 of pp collision data at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV with the ATLAS experiment
publications.abstract: A bstract A search for heavy spin-1 and spin-2 resonances decaying into a top-antitop-quark pair has been performed with 140 fb − 1 of proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider at a centre-of-mass energy of $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ s = 13 TeV. Final states with either exactly one electron or muon, or exactly two leptons ( ee , μμ or eμ ), large missing transverse momentum, and two jets, at least one of which must be identified as likely containing a b -hadron decay, are considered. The search targets resonances with both narrow and broad widths relative to the detector resolution, and with masses in the range of 0.4–5.0 TeV. No significant deviation from the Standard Model prediction is observed. Exclusion limits are set on the production cross-section times branching ratio for hypothetical Z′ bosons, Kaluza-Klein gravitons, and Kaluza-Klein gluons that decay into top-quark pairs.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for soft unclustered energy patterns containing muons in the final state in pp collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A bstract Soft unclustered energy patterns (SUEPs) refer to high-multiplicity, isotropic distributions of low-momentum particles that could arise in strongly-coupled hidden sector theories. A search for SUEPs whose decay products contain muons in the final state is presented using 140 fb − 1 of proton–proton collision data at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ s = 13 TeV collected by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during 2015–2018. The analysis targets SUEP signatures via gluon–gluon fusion production of a scalar mediator in Hidden Valley scenarios. No significant excess over the Standard Model expectation is observed. Exclusion limits are set on the product of the mediator production cross section and the branching fraction for its decay into a SUEP, down to 0.05 fb for a mediator mass of m S = 750 GeV, 0.4 fb for m S = 400 GeV, and 70 fb for m S = 125 GeV; the last value, when identifying the mediator with the Standard Model Higgs boson, translates to an upper limit on the branching fraction of around 0.2%.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for a leptoquark in events with a hadronically decaying τ-lepton and missing transverse momentum using pp collisions at s=13TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A search for leptoquark signals is performed in final states with a hadronically decaying τ -lepton and missing transverse momentum, using data from proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of s = 13 TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during Run 2 (2015–18), corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb − 1 . The analysis is designed to probe both resonant production and non-resonant t -channel exchange of the leptoquark, covering a wide range of coupling scenarios. No excess above the Standard Model background prediction is observed. Limits are set on the couplings in the benchmark U 1 vector-leptoquark model at 95% confidence level for masses between 1.5 TeV and 3.0 TeV.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for compressed electroweak SUSY production in final states with two $τ$-leptons in $\sqrt{s} = 13$ and $13.6$ TeV $pp$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: Searches for the production of $τ$-sleptons ($\tildeτ$), charginos ($\tildeχ^{\pm}_1$), and neutralinos ($\tildeχ^0_2$) in events with at least one hadronically decaying $τ$-lepton are presented, targeting compressed mass spectra scenarios. For charginos and neutralinos, the cascade decays producing either a $τ$-slepton or a $τ$-sneutrino are considered. Two final selections are studied, requiring either one hadronically decaying $τ$-lepton and one other charged lepton, or two or more hadronically decaying $τ$-leptons. To enhance sensitivity to the compressed mass spectra, production modes with initial-state radiation (ISR) jets are considered. The searches use 140 $\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ and 53 $\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during 2015-2018 at a centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV and 2022-2023 at a centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 13.6$ TeV, respectively. The searches provide sensitivity to the compressed mass spectra scenarios with light $τ$-sleptons. The results are generally consistent with the Standard Model, although several deviations with local significances of $2.1-2.4 σ$ are observed. These deviations weaken the observed exclusion limits. For direct $τ$-slepton production, in the ISR channel alone the limits are set for $Δm(\tildeτ, \tildeχ^0_1) = 30$ GeV for $τ$-slepton masses up to $115$ GeV at 95% confidence level. Given the observed data, no exclusion limits are set for direct $τ$-sleptons production when statistically combining all considered channels. For electroweakino production, limits are set for $Δm(\tildeχ^0_2, \tildeχ^0_1) = 30$ GeV for $\tildeχ^0_2$ masses up to $200$ GeV. For pure chargino pair-production, limits are set for chargino masses up to $175$ GeV for the same mass splitting.

Primal and dual representation results as well as several examples are discussed. Principal ways to construct risk measures are given and extensions to more general situations indicated.
