name: Misha Ivanov
subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
topics: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

publications.title: Photonic architectures for synthetic chiral light-driven chiral sensing
publications.abstract: Molecular chirality gives rise to left- and right-handed enantiomers whose balance underpins biochemical function. Deviations from this enantiomeric excess are promising biomarkers of disease. Despite its importance, rapid and sensitive detection of enantiomeric excess in trace amounts of small chiral molecules remains an outstanding challenge. Synthetic chiral light introduces new opportunities for chiroptical spectroscopy, with the potential to enhance light-matter interactions by several orders of magnitude. Here we propose a new class of photonic architectures for synthetic chiral light, in which photonic structures generate, guide and optimize chiral light-matter interactions. As a first realization, we show that hollow dielectric waveguides support phase-matched propagation of multicolor fields enabling coherent accumulation of the enantio-sensitive nonlinear response over centimeter-scale distances. By combining microscopic quantum-response simulations with Maxwell's equations, we predict that incident pulse energies of around 1 uJ produce hundreds of picojoules of third-harmonic emission from only picomole quantities of carvone gas at 50 mbar over just 2 cm of propagation, with enantio-sensitive contrast approaching 5%. Phase-resolved Fourier analysis isolates a background-free chiral signal exhibiting the maximum possible dichroism of 200%. Beyond efficient chiral sensing, photonic architectures for synthetic chiral light establish a scalable platform for integrated nonlinear chiral spectroscopy, molecular fingerprinting based on ultrafast electron dynamics, and topologically robust chiroptical observables.

publications.title: Phase-sensitive avalanche quantum sensing of sub-shot-noise fields
publications.abstract: Avalanche-based detection of small perturbations is commonplace in precision measurement devices from Geiger counters to single-photon avalanche detectors. Here, we expand this principle to sensing of light waves below the quantum shot noise limit, demonstrating numerically how atomic clouds trapped in photonic cavities can exhibit non-perturbative sensitivity to changes in the cavity field when the cavity mode is tuned to a parity-prohibited transition. We find that, when pumped by a continuous-wave laser, the atomic cloud creates emissions which amplify the initially sub-shot-noise fluctuation by two orders of magnitude. Crucially, this amplification is broadly tunable with respect to frequency and independent of atomic energy structure. Even more strikingly, our amplification mechanism preserves the phase imparted on the atoms by the original ultra-weak light wave, marking a qualitative improvement over conventional protocols. Our finding has implications for both quantum state characterization and detection of weak classical signals.
topics: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

publications.title: Reconstructing Molecular-Ion Quantum States with Two-Color Strong-Field Scattering
publications.abstract: Strong-field ionization of molecules can prepare coherent superpositions of ionic states whose amplitudes and relative phases govern the ensuing ultrafast dynamics, but accessing this information experimentally remains a challenge. Here we introduce two-color strong-field scattering, in which a strong mid-infrared field ionizes the molecule and launches an electron, while a weak second harmonic field resonantly couples vibronic states of the parent ion during the electron's continuum excursion, thereby introducing structural changes on the sub-laser-cycle timescale. Scanning the relative phase between the two colors controls the ionic evolution and maps it onto phase-dependent sub-angstrom bond-length changes retrieved from the rescattering signal. Using the example of N$_2$, we apply the two-color setup to probe the coherence between different ionization channels and to reconstruct the initial ionic superposition. Our results establish two-color strong-field scattering as a powerful structural approach to characterize the complex amplitudes of ion quantum wavepackets.

publications.title: Generation of Stable Peak-Power Similaritons through Gain-Managed Nonlinearity
publications.abstract: Fiber lasers and amplifiers offer attractive alternatives to conventional solid-state systems. However, generation of high-energy ultrashort laser pulses in fibers faces challenges due to the complex interplay of multiple nonlinear effects arising due to pulse confinement within a small fiber core and also limitations imposed by the gain bandwidth of the available active fibers. The discovery of self-similar amplification and gain-managed nonlinear amplification (GMNA) pulse propagation regimes in fibers with normal dispersion suggests that these challenges can be turned into an advantage. Here we show that pulses generated in the GMNA regime are, in fact, the realization of the idealized similariton-type pulses in realistic fibers with limited gain bandwidth. Our analytical and numerical results show how one should shape the fiber gain as a function of propagation length to achieve constant peak power similariton-like pulses with steadily increasing energy, the pulse bandwidth exceeding the gain bandwidth, and the nearly linear frequency chirp allowing for efficient pulse compression to its Fourier limit. Absent Raman nonlinearities, these pulses can reach $μ$J level energies in standard single-mode fibers, representing a tenfold increase in pulse energy compared to the best currently available nonlinear amplifiers. Our results have significant implications for the fundamental understanding of nonlinear wave dynamics and for the advancement of fiber laser technology, supporting the reliable generation of high-energy pulses for practical use in areas such as micromachining, metrology, and bioimaging.

publications.title: Data and analysis code supporting "On-Chip Ultrafast Electron Pulses Reveal Electronic Dynamics in Individual Dark Nanocrystal
publications.abstract: This repository contains the experimental data, processed data, and analysis and modelling code supporting the figures and conclusions presented in the manuscript “On-Chip Ultrafast Electron Pulses Reveal Electronic Dynamics in Individual Dark Nanocrystals”. The study investigates photosensitive asymmetric nanogap (PAN) devices for ultrafast tunnelling-current measurements, including broadband optical-pulse characterisation and ultrafast spectroscopy of CsPbBr3 quantum dots, ZnO nanocrystal films, and individual optically dark AgBiS2 nanocrystals.

name: Nicola Pinna
topics: Chemical and Physical Properties of Materials

publications.title: Universal Covalent Functionalization of Two-Dimensional Transition Metal Dichalcogenides for Sarin Simulant Detection
publications.abstract: The detection of chemical warfare agents such as sarin is essential for public security, yet conventional sensors lack sufficient sensitivity for trace-level vapor detection. To address this, we developed a universal covalent functionalization approach for two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (including MoS2, MoSe2, WS2, WSe2, and In2Se3), enabling highly sensitive detection of dimethyl methylphosphonate (DMMP), a sarin simulant. Using a custom-synthesized diazonium salt (4-HFBD) with KI assistance, we rapidly graft acidic groups onto inert TMD surfaces while enhancing their n-type semiconductor characteristics. This design leverages directional hydrogen bonding between the functionalized surface and DMMP, resulting in exceptional room-temperature sensitivity. The optimized MoS2 sensor achieves selective and reversible DMMP detection with a low detection limit of 42 ppb and a fast response time of 4.6 s, surpassing most reported analogues. This work provides a versatile and tunable platform for trace chemical threat detection, representing a major advance in sensing technology.

publications.title: Scalable Room-Temperature Synthesis of Glass-like MOF Thin Films on Arbitrary Substrates with Versatile Functionality
publications.abstract: Metal-organic framework (MOF) glasses and glass-like materials offer unique advantages including improved flexibility, processability and mechanical stability, yet the rational, mild and scalable synthesis of uniform, large-area glassy MOF thin films remains largely unexplored and highly challenging. Herein, we pioneer the fabrication of homogeneous, ultra-smooth glass-like MOF thin films, which can be readily scaled into large-area coatings via a facile room-temperature immersion strategy. By simply placing diverse substrates into the precursor solution for 0.5 to 3 hours, continuous amorphous MOF films with nanometer-scale flatness and centimeter-to-0.3-meter scale uniformity can be readily prepared, with exceptional mechanical properties including Young’s modulus among the highest reported for typical ZIF glasses. Importantly, this unprecedented glass-like MOF film serves as a versatile guiding layer that enables the nucleation and growth of 15 different types of crystalline MOFs on various substrates, overcoming long-standing limitations of substrate dependence and lattice mismatch. This work not only establishes a facile and scalable synthetic platform for high-performance glass-like MOF thin films, but also extends its capability toward the universal growth of crystalline MOF films, unlocking promising new opportunities for device-oriented MOF thin-film materials for gas and isotope separation, electronic devices, sensing and electrocatalytic applications.

publications.title: Debunking top-down borophene: a multimodal reassessment of boron sonication and milling
Cavity engineering of amorphous zeolitic imidazolate framework colloids and their core-shell architectures
publications.abstract: Metal-Organic-Frameworks (MOFs), as a class of typical crystalline porous solids, have been extensively studied and applied in various fields, including gas adsorption and separation, catalysis, and chemical sensing. Recently, compared to their crystalline counterparts, the amorphous states of MOFs have attracted growing interest because they possess unique properties such as mechanical robustness, stability, molecular selectivity, and processability. However, the direct synthesis of amorphous MOF colloids remains a significant challenge, particularly for fabricating complex micro-and nanostructures such as hollow or yolk-shell architectures. Herein, we develop a simple strategy to construct hollow structures in amorphous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) colloids through controlled post-synthetic etching. Tannic acid, functioning as a proton etching agent, was utilized to achieve selective dissolution of the inner region in pre-formed monodisperse amorphous ZIF colloids, forming uniform hollow structure. This etching process has been successfully demonstrated across various ZIFs, providing strong evidence of the method's universality for ZIF systems.

name: Nikolaus Rajewsky
topics: Spectroscopy Techniques in Biomedical and Chemical Research

publications.title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
publications.abstract: Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

publications.title: Integrating UHPLC-MS and MALDI-MSI for Spatial Nucleoside Profiling in FFPE Breast Cancer: A Multimodal Molecular Pathology Framework
publications.abstract: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues constitute the primary material for diagnostic pathology and retrospective clinical research, yet their use in metabolomics remains limited due to molecular cross-linking and analyte degradation. Here, we establish a cost-efficient molecular pathology workflow that integrates ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS) with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) to quantify and spatially map nucleosides in FFPE breast cancer tissues. Optimized extraction using methanol yielded nucleoside profiles comparable to fresh-frozen tissues, while MALDI-MSI enabled the spatial visualization of nine nucleosides across distinct histological regions. Several nucleosides including deoxyadenosine and 5-formylcytosine showed strong discriminatory power between tumor stages, revealing progressive metabolic rewiring during breast cancer progression. Finally, spatial nucleoside patterns observed in a murine model were recapitulated in patient-derived FFPE tissues, underscoring the translational potential of nucleoside-based spatial metabolomics for clinical research and biomarker discovery. Together, this workflow establishes MALDI-MSI as a powerful and scalable spatial molecular pathology tool for interrogating nucleoside biology in archival breast cancer samples. Following MALDI-MSI, the same FFPE tissue sections can undergo laser capture microdissection, enabling genomic, proteomic, or targeted metabolomic profiling of MSI-defined tumor niches and microenvironmental regions. This integration directly links spatial nucleoside signatures to molecular alterations relevant to precision oncology in future.
topics: Spectroscopy Techniques in Biomedical and Chemical Research

publications.title: Ultrafast and reference-free sequence discovery in single-cell data
publications.abstract: Abstract Knowledge of RNA sequences, expression, splicing, isoforms, structure and modifications is central for understanding and targeting cellular processes. Revolutionary single-cell and spatial transcriptomics technologies—for example, as deployed by consortia such as the Human Cell Atlas—partially capture this diversity and generate cellular profiles that expand at petabyte scale each year 1–5 . Yet researchers cannot search sequences across these datasets: standard pipelines do not scale or rely on references, retaining only gene or isoform counts, whereas accessing raw sequences requires collecting, downloading and processing millions of large files. Here we present Malva, a computational platform that enables ultrafast, species-agnostic and reference-free interrogation of the raw sequence space, enabling searching for any sequence, mutation, splice junction or pathogen, or spatial location of arbitrary transcripts. The continuously expanding Malva Index currently comprises around 74 million cells from thousands of experiments in health and disease. Malva enables reference-free discovery—researchers can, for example, identify cell types and predict cell–cell similarity directly from sequence composition. Building on Malva’s speed and accuracy, we demonstrate how Malva can be flexibly connected to state-of-the-art neural networks and how to execute complex searches and enable automated analyses. Malva transforms single-cell atlases from static gene count tables into dynamic, sequence-resolved resources that may help to bridge human–machine reasoning about biology.

publications.title: Tau spreading coordinates intercellular lipid flux enhancing neuronal resilience to lipid toxicity
publications.abstract: Abstract The presence of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) in the extracellular environment of the brain suggests that protein disorder may serve functions beyond those confined to the intracellular space. Tau, a prototypical IDP linked to tauopathies, a class of neurodegenerative diseases, is continuously released and spreads between cells in the brain, yet the biological significance of this extracellular phase remains unresolved. Here, we show that spreading tau coordinates neutral lipid homeostasis by promoting neuronal lipid efflux and enhancing resilience to lipid toxicity. Integrating transcriptomics and lipidomics, we demonstrate that tau spreading reprograms lipid transport pathways and triggers redistribution of triacylglycerol pools, remodeling neutral lipid metabolism. Mechanistically, cellular uptake of spreading tau drives its accumulation within neutral lipid-rich compartments and promotes neuronal lipid efflux. The exported lipids are enriched in peroxidized species that are subsequently transferred to astrocytes, reducing neuronal lipid stress and revealing a pathway through which tau regulates lipid homeostasis. Our findings reframe spreading tau as a regulator of intercellular lipid flux and position protein disorder as an active mediator of cell-to-cell communication in coordinating tissue metabolism. Loss of this homeostatic function is likely to contribute to the early metabolic dysfunction associated with tauopathy.

name: Norbert Koch
topics: Advancements in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells

publications.title: Enhancing the Stability of Pt/Carbon with Ti3C2 MXene-Derived TiO2 for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction in Acidic Media
publications.abstract: Platinum on carbon remains the proton-exchange membrane fuel cell cathode state-of-the-art catalyst; however, durability losses tied to support corrosion and Pt coarsening hinder this catalyst. This study investigates utilizing different variations of Vulcan XC-72 and Ti3C2 MXene to improve the oxygen-reduction ORR activity and stability. Material characterization results provide in-depth knowledge of the Pt, carbon, and MXene composites. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy of the synthesized samples shows that the Ti3C2 has been oxidized, and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy further reveals that the Pt(111) fringes are present with local anatase TiO2 derived from Ti3C2 MXene, which is also confirmed by X-ray microscopy, indicating that the active support is a Ti3C2-derived TiO2/carbon support. After a U.S. Department of Energy-derived accelerated stress test (AST), the Pt/75%C+25%Ti3C2 catalyst outperforms an in-house-made Pt/C prepared by the same method. This improvement is accompanied by reduced Pt particle growth after the AST for the Pt/75%C+25%Ti3C2 when compared to the Pt/C, which is attributed to stabilization of Pt at the MXene-derived anatase surface through Pt-O-Ti bonds, consistent with interfacial anchoring, together with the greater corrosion resistance of the oxide, in a composition that retains sufficient carbon for electronic percolation and gas transport. This study is the first coupled cathode half-cell performance and potential-cycling durability testing for MXene-derived composites benchmarked against Pt/C and provides vital information on material discovery utilizing MXenes for the ORR.

publications.title: Enhanced Operational Stability in Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells via a Natural Antioxidant
publications.abstract: Abstract In tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs), Sn(II) oxidation and illumination-induced lattice instability are primary drivers of device degradation. In this study, we introduce ellagic acid (EA), a natural antioxidant, into DMSO-free fabricated tin perovskites. Computational simulations show that EA stabilizes formamidinium sites within the perovskite lattice and effectively inhibits Sn(II) oxidation. Besides, this incorporation greatly improves film homogeneity and passivates defect traps, increasing the champion power conversion efficiency from 9.3 to 10.2%. Consequently, unencapsulated EA-incorporated devices exhibit a sixfold increase in T80 lifetime (in a nitrogen atmosphere) and a threefold increase in T60 lifetime (in dry air) at the maximum power point tracking under continuous illumination. Moreover, an EA-incorporated device achieves a 16% increment over 1000 h of day/night cycling, significantly outperforming the 7% rise of the control. These results demonstrate that natural antioxidants are a highly effective and sustainable strategy for enhancing the operational stability of lead-free TPSCs.

publications.title: Supplementary information files for "Test procedures for the evaluation of the performance and stability of direct ammonia fuel cells"
publications.abstract: The first comprehensive electrochemical test protocol for probing both steady-state and transient operations of low-temperature direct ammonia fuel cells (DAFCs) is introduced. It combines galvanostatic holds, cyclic staircase loads mimicking start-up/shut-down, long dynamic current loading representative of automotive application, and extended open-circuit periods. A hydro-gen reference electrode at the anode inlet enables three-electrode operation, so anode and cathode overpotentials, impedance spectra, and polarization curves can be recorded simultaneously and de-convoluted in real time. DAFCs (25 cm2 ) with ultralow catalyst loading (0.3 mgPt /cm2) electrodeposited on nickel foam were operated on 1.0 M NH3 + 1.0 M KOH at 60°C. Durability measurements indicate that voltage decay is dominated by reversible anode deactivation driven by fuel depletion; full recovery upon fuel replacement confirms minimal permanent catalyst damage. Impedance analysis indicates that the cathodic double-layer capacitance increases, consistent with flooding. Mass spectrometry identifies N2 as the sole gaseous product at 0.2 V with no detectable NOx . The protocol’s ability to identify these phenomena over a single campaign provides an essential tool for future DAFC development. Together, the results establish links between operating regime, fuel utilization, and degradation pathway. They furnish a benchmark for emerging membranes, catalysts, and cell architectures to be compared. © The Author(s), CC Y 4.0
topics: Advancements in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells

publications.title: Test Procedures for the Evaluation of the Performance and Stability of Direct Ammonia Fuel Cells
publications.abstract: The first comprehensive electrochemical test protocol for probing both steady‐state and transient operations of low‐temperature direct ammonia fuel cells (DAFCs) is introduced. It combines galvanostatic holds, cyclic staircase loads mimicking start‐up/shut‐down, long dynamic current loading representative of automotive application, and extended open‐circuit periods. A hydrogen reference electrode at the anode inlet enables three‐electrode operation, so anode and cathode overpotentials, impedance spectra, and polarization curves can be recorded simultaneously and de‐convoluted in real time. DAFCs (25 cm 2 ) with ultralow catalyst loading (0.3 mg Pt /cm 2 ) electrodeposited on nickel foam were operated on 1.0 M NH 3 + 1.0 M KOH at 60°C. Durability measurements indicate that voltage decay is dominated by reversible anode deactivation driven by fuel depletion; full recovery upon fuel replacement confirms minimal permanent catalyst damage. Impedance analysis indicates that the cathodic double‐layer capacitance increases, consistent with flooding. Mass spectrometry identifies N 2 as the sole gaseous product at 0.2 V with no detectable NO x . The protocol's ability to identify these phenomena over a single campaign provides an essential tool for future DAFC development. Together, the results establish links between operating regime, fuel utilization, and degradation pathway. They furnish a benchmark for emerging membranes, catalysts, and cell architectures to be compared.

publications.title: Supplementary information files for "Electrodeposited MnCo and MnNiCo spinels for anion exchange membrane direct ammonia fuel cell cathodes: an alternative to platinum"
publications.abstract: Supplementary files for article ""Electrodeposited MnCo and MnNiCo spinels for anion exchange membrane direct ammonia fuel cell cathodes: an alternative to platinum" Direct ammonia fuel cells (DAFCs) hold great promise as clean energy conversion devices due to their carbon-free exhaust, the high energy density and liquid-phase storability of ammonia, and use of an existing production and distribution infrastructure. When using the state-of-the-art anion exchange membranes, ammonia crossover from the cathode to the anode can cause rapid decay in DAFC performance as the current density increases. Mixed-metal oxides containing manganese–nickel–cobalt have emerged as NH3-tolerant cathode catalysts, but their systematic testing under variable loading conditions in DAFC is rarely reported. Here, we examine low-temperature DAFCs with electrodeposited platinum (Pt), manganese–cobalt oxide (MnCoOX), and manganese–nickel–cobalt oxide (MnNiCoOX) cathodes on Ni foam. To isolate cathodic effects, all cells use identical Pt on Ni Foam anodes with alkaline ammonia feeds. Structural characterization confirms defect-rich spinel coatings. MnCoOX achieves oxygen reduction reaction performance comparable to Pt, sustaining higher load voltage with lower interfacial resistance and larger capacitance, while MnNiCoOX shows restricted performance and rapid voltage loss, indicating sluggish charge transfer and fewer active sites. These results identify electrodeposited MnCoOX on Ni foam as a promising, scalable platinum group metal-free cathode for DAFCs and highlight compositional and mesostructural tuning as key levers to improve catalytic activity and device performance. © The Author(s), CC BY 4.0
topics: Advancements in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells

name: Olaf Hohm
topics: Homotopy and Cohomology in Algebraic Topology
Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: A local action for Kodaira--Spencer gravity
publications.abstract: A local action is given for Kodaira--Spencer gravity by solving a constraint on the complex structure deformation of a Calabi--Yau threefold in terms of a $(1,1)$ form as the new gravity field. The gauge algebra becomes a genuine $L_{\infty}$ algebra based on a Courant algebroid, while the gravity field and its linearized gauge transformations coincide with those of double field theory. On a real three-dimensional slice, the free action reduces to the Fierz--Pauli action for massless spin-2 plus the Kalb--Ramond action for a B-field. Non-linearly, the theory carries parity-odd interactions with three derivatives, and it is gauge invariant without a level-matching constraint, in this sense defining an unconstrained double field theory. The full theory is encoded in a cyclic $L_{\infty}$ algebra, for which a double copy interpretation is given.

publications.title: Of-shell quantum mechanics as factorization algebras on intervals
publications.abstract: We present, for the harmonic oscillator and the spin-12 system, an alternative formulation of quantum mechanics that is “off-shell”: it is based on classical off-shell configurations and thus similar to the path integral. The core elements are Batalin–Vilkovisky (BV) algebras and factorization algebras, following a program by Costello and Gwilliam [Factorization Algebras in Quantum Field Theory, New Mathematical Monographs (Cambridge University Press, 2016), Vol. 1, Factorization Algebras in Quantum Field Theory, New Mathematical Monographs (Cambridge University Press, 2021), Vol. 2, and M. Markl, Commun. Math. Phys. 221, 367–384 (2001)]. The BV algebras are the spaces of quantum observables Obsq(I) given by the symmetric algebra of polynomials in compactly supported functions on some interval I⊂R, which can be viewed as functionals on the dynamical variables. Generalizing associative algebras, factorization algebras include in their data a topological space, which here is R, and an assignment of a vector space to each open set, which here is the assignment of Obsq(I) to each open interval I. The central structure maps are bilinear Obsq(I1) ⊗ Obsq(I2) → Obsq(J) for disjoint intervals I1 and I2 contained in an interval J, which here is the wedge product of the symmetric algebra. We prove, as the central result of this paper, that this factorization algebra is quasi-isomorphic to the factorization algebra of “on-shell” quantum mechanics. In this we extend previous work by including half-open and closed intervals, and by generalizing to the spin-12 system.
topics: Homotopy and Cohomology in Algebraic Topology

publications.title: Kaluza-Klein Perturbation Theory from Exceptional Field Theory
publications.abstract: We develop the perturbation theory of ten and eleven-dimensional supergravities on a large class of Kaluza-Klein backgrounds including familiar AdS examples such as AdS$_5\times S^5$, but also more general manifolds such as black hole geometries. Employing ${\rm E}_{6(6)}$ exceptional field theory with the backgrounds characterized by a generalized Scherk-Schwarz ansatz, we determine the first order field equations for the fluctuations that are gauge invariant under linearized generalized diffeomorphisms. We then present the details of the Higgs mechanism for all fields including spin-2 for the subset of backgrounds in which higher-form gauge fields vanish. We use a recently established machinery based on homotopy transfer that allows one to separate the fields into gauge invariant physical modes and pure gauge unphysical modes to all orders in perturbation theory. Finally, as a first application for backgrounds with higher-form gauge fields switched on, we analyze part of the spectrum of ten-dimensional Kaluza-Klein modes of type IIB supergravity around a Kerr-Newman AdS$_5$ black hole that in the near horizon limit becomes a fibered product of AdS$_2$ and a squashed three-sphere.

publications.title: Color-kinematics duality from an algebra of superforms
publications.abstract: Color-kinematics duality states that the kinematic numerators of the cubic tree-level Yang-Mills scattering amplitudes obey the same symmetry properties that the color factors obey due to the Jacobi identity. We present a novel strategy for deriving this duality, based on the differential forms on a superspace. This space of superforms carries a generalization of a Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) algebra ( BV □ algebra). We show that the homotopy algebra of color-stripped Yang-Mills theory is obtained as a quotient of this space in which a subspace, which is an ideal “up to homotopy,” is modded out. This algebra is a subsector of a BV ∞ □ algebra. Deriving the latter would provide a first-principle proof of color-kinematics duality from field theory.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Homotopy transfer for massive Kaluza-Klein modes
publications.abstract: A bstract We develop techniques to treat massive Kaluza-Klein modes to arbitrary order in perturbation theory. The Higgs mechanism that renders the higher Kaluza-Klein modes massive is displayed. To this end we give an algorithm in perturbation theory that yields new fields with the following characteristics: they are gauge invariant under all higher-mode gauge transformations, which are broken, but they transform covariantly under the zero-mode gauge transformations, which are unbroken. We employ the formulation of field theory in terms of L ∞ algebras together with their homotopy transfer , which here maps the gauge redundant fields of gravity to gauge invariant fields. We illustrate these results, as a proof of concept, for Kaluza-Klein theory on a torus. In an accompanying paper these results will be applied to a large class of generalized Scherk-Schwarz backgrounds in exceptional field theory.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

name: Patrick Hostert
topics: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Applications and Techniques

publications.title: Landscape heterogeneity is structured by multidimensional components and land-cover proportion interactions
publications.abstract: Abstract Landscape heterogeneity is a key driver of biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, and resilience. However, its multiple components—compositional, configurational, vertical, and temporal— are rarely analysed together at broad spatial scales. Compositional heterogeneity refers to the number and proportions of different elements, configurational heterogeneity to their spatial arrangement and shape, vertical heterogeneity to variation in vegetation height, and temporal heterogeneity to interannual variation in land cover and management. Here we examine relationships among these components across forests, croplands, and grasslands using nationwide geospatial data from Germany. We show that compositional and configurational heterogeneity (Shannon diversity vs. edge density) are positively correlated, although their relationship varied with land-cover proportions. Contrary to common assumptions, configurational heterogeneity does not enhance habitat connectivity. Vertical and temporal heterogeneity are largely independent from horizontal heterogeneity. Forests are the main contributors to landscape heterogeneity across land-cover types, whereas croplands contribute little or even negatively. These findings highlight the importance of considering land-cover proportions and multi-dimensional heterogeneity when assessing landscape structure. Our results have broad implications for environmental monitoring and planning for biodiversity and ecosystem assessments, offering a framework to avoid hidden collinearity and consider multi-dimensional perspective and socio-ecological context.

publications.title: Precipitable Water Vapor database derived from ERA-5 data for atmospheric correction in FORCE
publications.abstract: Precipitable Water Vapor database derived from ERA-5 data for atmospheric correction in FORCE The database comprises daily Precipitable Water Vapour (WV) 1982-01-01 - 2026-09-30 datasets derived from ERA-5 hourly Total column water vapour data (DOI: 10.24381/cds.adbb2d47) using haze. The WV database has been designed to be primarily used with FORCE and consequently adhere to the respective FORCE-specific processing parametrization in haze. Please review haze documentation for details on the processing steps. ❗The WV database features only land WRS-2 tiles, defined in the `WRS2_descending_LAND.gpkg` dataset. ❗Unlike the ERA-5 Total Column water vapour distributed as kg*m^-2, the WV is measured in centimeters. The dataset in question aims to seamlessly replace Frantz D., Stellmes M., 2018, Water vapor database for atmospheric correction of Landsat imagery [dataset]. PANGAEA, https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.893109 The WV data are distributed in annual `tar.gz` bundles with `WVP_YYYY.tar.gz` naming convention, where `YYYY` identifies a target year. The daily datasets included in the bundles are distributed as `txt` files named as `WVP_YYYY_MM_DD.txt` where `YYYY` represents a year, `MM` month, and `DD` day of the year. The internal structure of each file comprises four columns: longitude, latitude, WV value, and 'ERA' code. The data are in the EPSG:4326 projection. For the year 2026 data are distributed in the `WVP_2026_js.tar.gz` archive, which comprises daily datasets from January through September (to be updated in early January 2027). Compilation command We used the following command to download the ERA-5 hourly Total column water vapour data: haze download --global --daily --year 1982:2026 --month 1:12 --day 1:31 --hour 0:23 /path/to/logfile /path/to/data and the following command to compile the daily WV datasets: haze process --wrap-on-edge /path/to/WRS2_descending_LAND.gpkg path/to/logfile path/to/final/wvdb/ To speed up the processing, we used the looming script, which allows for parallel processing with haze. The input parameters were adopted accordingly to the processing example above. The processing was executed on the HPC@HU cluster. Use For details on use with FORCE, please see FORCE documentation. publications.title: Pre-Built Global VRT Collections of GLO-30 DEM VRTs for WRS-2 and MGRT tiles
publications.abstract: Pre-Built Global VRT Collections of GLO-30 DEM VRTs for WRS-2 and MGRT tiles Background This dataset support functionality of FORCE and comprises a collection of vrt files that group Copernicus GLO-30 DEM data for each WRS-2 and MGRT tile. The GLO-30 DEM dataset is distributed in six latitude bands Figure 5 in the Product Handbook where each zone has its own specific longitude reduction factor. This means that the x-resolution (pixel width) of the DEM data depends on latitude, with changes occurring above 50° N and S. [Figure1.png] Figure1: The x-resolution (in degrees) in relation to latitude. In black - longitude grid spacing in six latitude bands of GLO-30 data. In blue line represents the effective resolution (i.e. the average) of the European VRT mosaic. The red line represents the effective resolution of the global VRT. Image credit: David Frantz Consequently, when multiple DEM tiles are aggregated to a single mosaic or a VRT, its x-resolution will depend on the latitudinal extent of the DEM tiles used to create the said mosaic or a VRT. ❗This translates into several issues: DEM VRTs created based on different collections of tiles will likely have different resolutions. Datasets processed with different DEMs or DEM VRTs will have i) shifts between pixels, and ii) different BOA values. This, in turn, prohibits the reproducibility of FORCE results. For VRTs spanning regions with low and high latitudes (e.g., continental and global VRTs) the resolution decreases towards the Equator. [Figure2.png]Figure 2: Hypothetical effective resolution (in meters) of European (blue) and Global (red) DEM VRT mosaics in relation to latitude. In black - resolution of GLO-30 data distributed in six latitude bands. Image credit: David Frantz Solution In FORCE, the best way to address these critical issues, is to process each Landsat and Sentinel-2 tile using only these DEM tiles that overlap with the footprint of the processed tile. This functionality has been enabled in FORCE v3.8.01dev through a new parameter in the LEVEL2 parameter file called `USE_DEM_DATABASE` that allows for tile-specific processing. `USE_DEM_DATABASE` is meant to be used in conjunction with the `FILE_DEM` parameter. Whenever `USE_DEM_DATABASE = TRUE` the `FILE_DEM` needs to point not to a global, or regional VRT but to a folder with a collection of VRTs generated for each Landsat of Sentinel-2 tile. Pre-Built Global VRT Collections To facilitate the use and adoption of this new way of using GLO-30 data, we provide a ready-to-use global collection of WRS-2- and MGRS-specific VRTs. The dataset in question comprises: - MGRT_VRT.tar - global collections of Sentinel-2/MGRT specific VRTs - WRS_VRT.tar - global collections of Landsat/WRS-2 specific VRTs The list of GLO-30 tiles essential to process each WRS-2 and MGRT tile was identified based on openly available WRS-2 and MGRT footprints. > [!IMPORTANT] > Furthermore, we used 20 km buffer to account for potential deviation from the expected footprint's location. Use ⚠️ The distributed archives include only the VRT files. The Copernicus GLO-30 DEM tiles must already be present in the user's computational environment. VRTs are built with relative paths and must be placed in a directory located at the same level as the copernicus directory containing the DEM tiles. Landsat and Sentinel-2 specific VRTs can be deposited in the same parent directory. # higher-level-dir ├── DEM_VRT │ ├── MGRS_T01CDH.vrt │ ├── MGRS_T01CDJ.vrt │ ... │ ├── WRS-2_013001.vrt │ ├── WRS-2_013002.vrt │ ... │ ├── MGRS_T60XWF.vrt │ ... │ └── WRS-2_221015.vrt ├── copernicus │ ├── Copernicus_DSM_10_N00_00_E006_00_DEM.tif │ ├── Copernicus_DSM_10_N00_00_E009_00_DEM.tif │ ... │ └── Copernicus_DSM_10_S90_00_W180_00_DEM.tif ... Special Case: Caucasus Region Since the GLO-30 tiles from the Caucasus area are under embargo, under the aforementioned link, we provide SRTM tiles from this region (`SRTM_Caucasus.tar`), and respective WRS-2 (`WRS-2_VRT_Caucasus.tar`) and MGRS (`MGRS_VRT_Caucasus.tar`) collections of VRTs. ⚠️To allow for a seamless incorporation of the SRTM DEM data, the SRTM tiles from the SRTM_Caucasus.tar need to be placed in a srtm_aster directory located at the same level as copernicus and DEM_VRT directories. # higher-level-dir ├── DEM_VRT │ ├── MGRS_T01CDH.vrt │ ├── MGRS_T01CDJ.vrt │ ... │ ├── WRS-2_013001.vrt │ ├── WRS-2_013002.vrt │ ... │ ├── MGRS_T60XWF.vrt │ ... │ └── WRS-2_221015.vrt ├── copernicus │ ├── Copernicus_DSM_10_N00_00_E006_00_DEM.tif │ ├── Copernicus_DSM_10_N00_00_E009_00_DEM.tif │ ... │ ├── Copernicus_DSM_10_S90_00_W180_00_DEM.tif ├── srtm_aster │ ├── n38_e045_1arc_v3 │ ├── n38_e046_1arc_v3 │ ... │ └── n41_e049_1arc_v3 ... ⚠️Furthermore, the respective VRT files available in the global VRT distribution need to be overwritten with VRTs available in the `WRS-2_VRT_Caucasus.tar` and `MGRS-2_VRT_Caucasus.tar` archives Documentation The distributed data collection comes with readme.md comprising general information on the dataset. Furthermore, each *.tar* archive available under the abovementioned link comprises a README.MD file with setup guidelines, as well as a *log*.csv file listing all DEM tiles used to create a VRT for a specific WRS-2 or MGRS tile. publications.title: Dominant Tree Species for Germany (2017/2018)
publications.abstract: Updated version v2 This is an update of Blickensdörfer et al. (2022). We performed a postprocessing to the original data set in order to enforce plausable area changes in relation to the Dominant Tree Species Map fo 2022/23 (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22689196). We implement a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) solved via the Forward-Backward-Algorithm (Abercrombie et al., 2016). The HMM improves the temporal consistency between the maps and reduces spurious tree species change due to classification errors within each random forest classification. The random forest classifier votes are used as initial probabilities of class membership for each pixel and time step. A transition probability matrix defined the likelihood of pixels changing between different tree species classes from 2017/18 to 2022/23. The transition matrix was derived from tree species changes at plot level between the Carbon Inventory 2017 and NFI 2022 observations. All trees with a diameter at breast height greater 7 cm and that fall into the angle count sample with basal area factor of 4 (Riedel et al., 2021) were recorded by species. The dominant tree species per plot and year was derived, and then the transition probability was estimated by comparing the plots dominant species between inventory intervals. The species maps for 2017/18 and 2022/23 was generated by assigning the class with the maximum posterior probability at each pixel for that interval after the HMM was applied. Please note that the map errors within the two processed maps (2017/18 and 2022/23) remain in the same magnitude as expected tree species changes over the 5-year time span. While the HMM improved consistency between the two maps, they remain a best estimate of the tree species composition within each year. The data was not designed nor validated for the purpose of performing analysis of tree species change between the 2017/18 and 2022/23 maps. The map accuracies were estimated based on a stratified estimator according to Stehman et al. (2014, doi.org/10.1080/01431161.2014.930207). The HMM postprocessing improved map accuracies for 2017/2018, by about 5 percentage points to 92.07 ± 0.3 % for pure-species stands and by about 2 percentage points to 77.63 ± 0.2 % including mixed-species stands. ############################################################################################### Original dataset description: Spatially explicit and detailed information on tree species composition is critical for forest management, nature conservation and the assessment of forest ecosystem services. In many countries, forest attributes are monitored regularly through sample-based forest inventories. In combination with satellite imagery, data from such forest inventories have a great potential for developing large area tree species maps. Here, the high temporal and spatial resolution of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 has been useful for extracting vegetation phenology, information that may also be useful for improving forest tree species mapping. Thus, we generate cloud free time series with 5-day intervals from Sentinel-2 imagery and combine those with monthly Sentinel-1 backscatter composites to map the dominant tree species throughout Germany. Further, we incorporate information on topography, meteorology, and climate to account for environmental gradients in Germany. We use the German National Forest Inventory (NFI) as source for training data for a random forest classifier and for validation data to assess map accuracy. The optical Sentinel-2 data were downloaded, processes and structured in an analysis-ready data cube with the open-source software FORCE (Framework for operational radiometric correction for environmental monitoring; Frantz, D., 2019, doi.org/10.3390/rs11091124 ; https://force-eo.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ last accessed: 02. Nov. 2022). The preprocessed Sentinel-1 SAR data was obtained through the CODE-DE platform (https://code-de.org/en/portfolio/?q=Sentinel-1 last accessed: 02. Nov. 2022) and included in the ARD cube along with the environmental data. We used Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1 and environmental data from the two years 2017 and 2018 to generate the map with 11 tree species groups, including two broader deciduous tree classes (ODH: other deciduous trees with high life expectancy, ODL: other deciduous trees with low life expectancy), within the wooded forest area using a previously produced forest mask: Langner et al. (2022, doi.org/10.3220/DATA20221205151218 ) . The reference data for model training and map validation is based on the third German National Forest Inventory which was recorded in 2011/2012 (https://www.bundeswaldinventur.de/en/third-national-forest-inventory, last accessed: 02. Nov. 2022). To exclude inventory plots where tree species composition might have changed in between 2012 and 2018, we used the forest disturbance maps by Senf et al. (2020, doi.org/10.1038/s41893-020-00609-y ) . The map accuracies were estimated based on a stratified estimator according to Stehman et al. (2014, doi.org/10.1080/01431161.2014.930207 ) . Map accuracies were estimated for pure species stands in a first step and for the entire map, including mixed species stands, in a second step. The overall accuracy of pure-species stands is 87.07 ± 0.3 % and 75.53 ± 0.07 % for the entire map, including mixed-species stands. For further details please see the scientific publication: Blickensdörfer, L., Oehmichen, K., Pflugmacher, D., Kleinschmit, B., Hostert, P., 2024. National tree species mapping using Sentinel-1/2 time series and German National Forest Inventory data. Remote Sensing of Environment. 304, 114069. DOI: 10.1016/j.rse.2024.114069. publications.title: Benefits of the Sentinel-2 mission triplet constellation – one year on
publications.abstract: After over one complete year of Copernicus Sentinel-2A satellite extended operations and with the mission prolonged until the end of 2026, we provide the first quantitative and globally consistent assessment of its added value to the Sentinel-2 mission. Using a pixel-level overview of cloud-, shade-, and snow-free (herein usable ) observations, we show that despite reduced spatio-temporal coverage, the additional March 2025-2026 Sentinel-2A acquisitions enhanced the average number of usable Sentinel-2 observations at the global scale by 6.6 (20.81% increase with respect to the Sentinel-2B and -2C baseline). At the continental level, Sentinel-2A enhanced the mission’s data pool most in Africa, where, on average, it added over 13 new acquisitions (>34% increase) and reduced average data-gap length by three days. In Europe, Sentinel-2A added, on average, 8.54 usable observations (>33% increase) and reduced average data-gap length from 19.51 to 16.87 days. Importantly, Sentinel-2A observations had the highest relative importance in regions with systematically lower temporal fidelity in the Sentinel-2B and -2C baseline, specifically the areas outside the orbit overlaps. At the global scale, Sentinel-2A boosted data availability for regions depicted from only a single orbit by over 31% (51% in Europe alone). Overall, our results demonstrate that the triplet Sentinel-2 constellation provides measurable improvements in temporal fidelity of the Sentinel-2 mission, thus likely enhancing the quality of Copernicus downstream products and operational services aimed at monitoring and managing terrestrial ecosystems and backing the EU’s climate, agricultural policy, and sustainability goals.

publications.title: Intracrystalline Void‐Mediated Toughening of Brittle Crystals in Quail Eggshells
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT Pores and cracks act as stress concentrators during loading, making them a primary source of mechanical failure in brittle crystals. Remarkably, eggshells—composed of calcite, a material known for its brittleness—contain a high density of submicron closed voids, yet still act as an effective mechanical barrier that protects the embryo. By analyzing the void geometry and deformation behavior, we demonstrate that voids physically and geometrically serve as an essential structural motif with critical mechanical functions. The high density of intracrystalline voids, together with their disordered arrangement, inhibits lattice cleavage, hinders long‐range crack propagation, and promotes deformation twinning and quasi‐plasticity. The voids remain within a narrow subcritical size range, such that they predominantly do not act as crack initiators. Instead, through their size and spacing, they function as crack stoppers, thereby toughening the shell structure. Together, these voids play a crucial role in the mechanical integrity of ultrathin eggshells, which are primarily subjected to bending deformation. Our findings highlight the critical role of the size, density, and spatial distribution of isolated voids in thin‐walled avian eggshells and open new directions for designing flaw‐tolerant architectured single crystals and void‐mediated toughening strategies for thin‐film ceramics.

publications.title: Predicting wear in orthotropic biological nanocomposites
publications.abstract: Wear prediction remains a major challenge in tribology, particularly for anisotropic fibre-reinforced materials where contact-induced stresses, frictional interactions, and failure mechanisms depend strongly on structural orientation. Conventional wear models are largely developed for isotropic systems and therefore fail to capture the directional dependence of wear resistance observed in many biological and engineered composites. In this study, we present an analytical framework for predicting wear behaviour in orthotropic materials by coupling Hertzian contact mechanics with an orientation-dependent failure criterion based on the Tsai-Wu formulation. The model extends the framework proposed by Ning et al. by incorporating friction-induced shear stresses into the failure analysis, enabling the evaluation of direction-dependent wear behaviour. As a biological model system, locust tendons were selected due to their highly aligned chitinous fibre architecture, allowing systematic investigation of anisotropic mechanical and tribological properties as a function of fibre orientation. Nanowear experiments revealed pronounced orientation-dependent wear behaviour, with substantially higher wear resistance when sliding occurred parallel to the fibres or on the transverse fibre section, compared to perpendicular sliding across the fibres. The analytical model successfully captured the experimentally observed wear trends across the tested orientations. To further demonstrate the model’s applicability to isotropic materials, epoxy resins with varying polymer-to-hardener ratios were also tested, and the model successfully captured the experimentally observed wear-resistance trends. Unlike conventional isotropic wear indices such as H 3 / E 2 , our framework explicitly incorporates fibre orientation, friction-induced shear stress, and anisotropic failure strength. This proposed modelling approach can effectively capture wear resistance trends in both orthotropic and isotropic systems, providing a mechanistic framework for the analysis of biological materials and for the design of materials with improved wear resistance.

publications.title: Defining Osseointegration for Biodegradable Scaffolds based on Histological, Immunohistochemical and Ultrastructural Analysis
publications.abstract: Osseointegration of metal implants refers to the formation of a direct, intimate, and stable interface between bone and the implant surface under physiological loads, without intervening fibrous tissue. This concept is largely based on the long-term fixation of non-degradable implants, where bone remodeling occurs around a permanent material. However, there is no equivalent framework defining de biological integration of biodegradable scaffolds used for scaffold-guided bone regeneration (SGBR), whose architecture, mechanical properties, and surface chemistry are intentionally desined to change over time. Consequently, definitions developed for permanent mettalic are frequently applied to biodegradable scaffolds, leading to uncertainty regarding whether these scaffolds truly "osseointegrate". We argue that the biological processes at biodegradable scaffold-bone interfaces fundamentally differs from that of metallic implants, and should be distinguished. Rather than classical "bone anchorage", biodegradable scaffolds support a dynamic, immunologically active, and mechanically evolving bone-scaffold interface in which fibrous encapsulation and bone formation compete. This paper aims to clarify these issues not by redefining osseointegration in general, but by adapting it specifically to osteoconductive biodegradable scaffolds in SGBR. Using evidence from a series of studies in well-characterised large-animal models of segmental bone defects, we propose a new framework that captures the temporal, cellular, and structural complexities of osseointegration of biodegradable scaffolds in living organisms. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Biodegradable scaffolds are intended to facilitate bone regeneration and gradually degrade as new tissue develops. Nevertheless, there is limited knowledge about how these materials interact with bone over extended periods. This research examines the bone-scaffold interface over 36-months using histology, immunohistochemistry, scanning electron microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy. Results indicate that biodegradable scaffolds do not form the permanent bonds commonly defined as osseointegration in metallic implants. Instead, they establish a dynamic interface that evolves as the organ bone, composed of mineralised tissue, blood vessels, and extracellular matrix, remodels around the degrading scaffold. These insights improve our understanding of scaffold-guided bone regeneration and will guide the development of next-generation biodegradable scaffolds that shorten the timeframe and better support long-term bone growth.

publications.title: Biophysical Properties of Material‑Colonizing Fungal Biofilms: Multiscale Structural and Mechanical Characterization
publications.abstract: Black extremotolerant fungi form persistent biofilms on a wide range of natural and engineered substrates. Able to weather minerals, affect stone monument surfaces, and colonize solar panels, they demonstrate a strong capacity to interact with and modify material surfaces, even under most extreme conditions. In this study, we establish a methodological workflow for the structural and mechanical characterization of melanized biofilms formed by the black fungus Knufia petricola. This species represents a broader group of resilient surface colonizers and provides a model for in‑depth investigation. When grown on the solid agar/air interface, this species predominantly forms a compact biofilm, composed of spherical cells, while retaining the capacity for filamentous growth, providing a suitable framework to explore morphology-dependent biomechanical responses. The proposed toolbox combines complementary analytical techniques spanning multiple spatial scales, including shear rheology to quantify bulk viscoelastic behavior, microindentation to resolve local stiffness of the biofilm surface, microcomputed tomography for nondestructive three-dimensional visualization of biofilm architecture, and cryogenic preparation methods and electron microscopy for high-resolution ultrastructural analysis. As a methodological case study, we applied this workflow to compare biofilms grown on two different nitrogen sources (NO3- vs NH4+). Our results reveal nitrogen-associated differences in biofilm organization across multiple hierarchical levels, ranging from biofilm morphology and bulk mechanical behavior to cellular morphology and EPS distribution. NO3--grown biofilms presented more filaments with cells exhibiting budding-like morphologies and higher bulk viscoelastic moduli, whereas NH4+-grown biofilms were thicker with meristematic-like morphologies and a softer, more shear-tolerant mechanical response. The successful application and combination of complementary methods originally developed for bacterial biofilm research demonstrates that quantitative multiscale characterization can be extended to melanized fungal biofilms. Ultimately, this multiscale toolbox will help in advancing the mechanistic understanding of fungal biofilms and biofilm-material interactions, with implications for geomicrobiology, material biodeterioration, and the design of bioinspired functional materials.

publications.title: Rethinking osteocyte models in vitro: the need for mineralised extracellular matrix and network architecture
publications.abstract: Osteocytes inhabit one of the most extreme cellular microenvironments in the human body: a hydrated, hierarchically structured mineralised extracellular matrix where lacunar confinement, canalicular connectivity, fluid transport and mechanics are inseparable from cell function. In vitro osteocyte models have rapidly advanced through 3D culture, bioprinting, patterning, microfluidics, multicellular systems and controlled loading. Yet physiological interpretation often remains limited when marker expression, dendrite formation or bulk mineral deposition are assessed without defining the matrix and network architecture that deliver local cues. Here, we review engineered osteocyte microenvironment models through a matrix-centred and network architecture lens. We highlight advances in biomimetic mineralisation, viscoelastic and patterned hydrogels, dynamic microphysiological platforms and ECM-cell characterisation. We propose that progress will depend on modular, cross-correlative and computationally usable models that connect mineralised ECM, osteocyte network topology, transport and mechanics. Such models could move the field from descriptive osteocyte-like cultures toward interpretable niches that explain osteocyte behaviour.

publications.title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
publications.abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. Two mid-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red-sensitive animal rhodopsins. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

publications.title: Structural Basis for Near Infrared Absorption and Noncanonical Photoisomerization in Neorhodopsin
publications.abstract: Abstract In retinal proteins, light absorption leads to a double bond isomerization of the chromophore, followed by conformational relaxations that drive functional protein rearrangements. The balance between photoisomerization and radiative or non-radiative decays of the excited state is adjusted to the demands of the respective photoreceptor function. The molecular determinants controlling the excited state processes remain poorly understood and are the focus of this combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and theoretical work on the recently discovered neorhodopsin (NeoR). NeoR exhibits a highly red-shifted and fluorescent dark state and selectively photoisomerizes from all- trans to 7- cis . We show that the local electrostatic environment reduces the negative charge density near the Schiff base and suppresses torsional motion around the canonical C13=C14 isomerization site of microbial rhodopsins. Instead, the chromophore-binding pocket permits only low-efficiency C7=C8 isomerization, accompanied by polyene inversion, β-ionone ring displacement, and Schiff base deprotonation. Consequently, unlike other retinal photoreceptors, NeoR undergoes structural changes localized near the β-ionone ring.

publications.title: Effectiveness of GLP ‐1 RAs and SGLT ‐2is for Weight Loss and Glycaemic Control: An Observational Emulation of a Target Trial
publications.abstract: AIMS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is) are both recommended as second-line treatments for individuals with Type 2 diabetes and obesity, but long-term head-to-head randomized trials in this population are lacking, necessitating a real-world evaluation of their relative benefits in weight loss and glycaemic control. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using observational data from Clalit's medical records, separate target trials were emulated comparing three GLP-1 RAs (liraglutide, dulaglutide and semaglutide) with SGLT-2is in individuals with Type 2 diabetes and obesity. The main outcomes were absolute changes in body weight and HbA1c during follow-up (up to 5 years for liraglutide/dulaglutide and 3 years for semaglutide). We used inverse-probability weighting to adjust for potential confounders. RESULTS: We identified 4296, 11 159 and 5041 eligible individuals initiating liraglutide, dulaglutide and semaglutide, respectively. Long-term weight loss was similar (6.4-7.3 kg at 5 years) for liraglutide and dulaglutide compared with SGLT-2is; weight loss for semaglutide was 2.6 kg (95% CI: 1.2-4.0) greater than for SGLT-2is at 18 months. At 18 months, HbA1c reductions were 0.4% (95% CI: 0.3-0.5), 0.7% (95% CI: 0.6-0.8) and 0.6% (95% CI: 0.5-0.8) greater for liraglutide, dulaglutide and semaglutide than SGLT-2is, respectively; this advantage was maintained throughout follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: We estimated that, compared with SGLT-2is, liraglutide and dulaglutide provided superior glycaemic control and similar weight reduction over 5 years, and that semaglutide produced greater short-term reductions in both outcomes. Our analyses benchmark the results of short-term randomized trials and extend the evidence to longer periods.

publications.title: Prompting alone is insufficient for large language model-based clinical variant classification
publications.abstract: Accurate clinical genetic variant classification is becoming increasingly challenging as data volume and knowledge complexity increase. Large Language Models (LLMs) could potentially automate evidence retrieval and assist variant interpretation. To systematically evaluate the capacity of general-purpose LLMs (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity) to support clinical genetic variant classification. We analyzed 475 variants across 185 genes, with reference classifications established by expert variant scientists. Classification was performed by the four LLMs using a detailed structured prompting strategy and compared with a commercial non-LLM specialized platform. Performance was evaluated at the classification and criteria levels and stratified by various variant characteristics. Detailed prompting generally improved performance. Mean LLM classification concordance was 69.0% (70.2% precision and 68.2% recall), which was substantially lower than the 81.1% concordance (80.2% precision and 84.5% recall) achieved by the specialized commercial non-LLM platform tested. Concordance varied across variant types, with unadjusted mean concordance ranging from 87.2% for intronic variants to 56.0% for splice-region variants; adjusted associations were model-specific. At the criteria level, performance was highly criterion-specific: sensitivity exceeded 80% for BP7, PP3, PVS1, and PM2, but criterion-call precision and exact-strength agreement were substantially lower for several criteria. General-purpose LLMs used through direct or structured prompting demonstrated substantial limitations in clinical genetic variant classification compared with a specialized interpretation platform. These findings indicate that the common conversational approach of asking an LLM to classify a variant, even with detailed instructions, is insufficient for autonomous clinical use.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

publications.title: Introducing Infrastructure as Code for deployment and governance of medical AI: A case study
publications.abstract: Abstract Clinical AI deployment rarely reaches the bedside because both workstation integration and governed backend provisioning are challenging. We introduce a workflow that allows rapid and governed access to AI functionalities through a browser interface or API, enabling privacy-compliant data analysis. The complex setup for compliant healthcare applications such as a secure backend, private AI model endpoint, and managed identity configuration is encoded by itself, a concept known as Infrastructure as Code (IaC) . IaC is a concept in which networks, access rights, and service endpoints are written down as machine-readable files that can be reviewed once and executed identically in any institution. Here, we apply this concept to a clinical use case. The process of deploying a governed, private clinical AI solution using this approach in a tertiary care center took, on average, 310.3 ± 196.6 seconds (n=25, mean ± SD) . To further demonstrate the clinical value of this approach, we developed and deployed an LLM-based inconsistency checker, which identifies textual inconsistency in medical documents. When evaluating the tool on a set of 1,347 physician-approved clinical documents, the tool flagged a clinically severe inconsistency in 105 clinical documents (7 . 8%, approximately 1 in 13) . In a severity-stratified physician audit, 149 of 150 sampled findings were confirmed (population-weighted PPV 98 . 2%; CI 94 . 8 - 100 . 0) . In summary, we present the application of IaC frameworks to a healthcare use case and demonstrate that clinically useful AI applications can be deployed to physician workstations in hospital-governed cloud environments within a few minutes. Description To overcome the implementation barriers for use of AI in healthcare, we adapted Infrastructure as Code to a clinical use case and deployed a hospital-governed large language model service that clinicians reach from a browser without workstation software. Provisioned by Infrastructure as Code the service became available in 310 seconds on average, and its first clinical application, an inconsistency checker, detected inconsistencies in clinical documents with high positive predictive value.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

publications.title: Pan-ethnic preconception screening: evidence from a large-scale programme in a genetically diverse population
publications.abstract: Background Preconception genetic screening is a key preventive strategy for identifying at-risk couples (ARCs) of inherited disorders and supporting informed reproductive decision-making. However, increasing population admixture and the widespread adoption of next-generation sequencing challenge the validity of ancestry-driven risk stratification. Methods A total of 107 739 individuals participated in the national screening programme, including 51 722 couples and 4295 individuals tested independently, representing 33 ethnic groups. Under the sequential testing strategy, all women underwent initial screening, whereas male partners were tested only when a pathogenic variant (PV) was identified in the female partner. Consequently, carrier-status results were available for 76 317 individuals. Results Among 76 317 individuals tested, 30 475 (39.9%) carried at least one PV. ARCs were identified in 1.15% of couples, reaching up to 10% in certain ethnic groups. Risk increased with shared ancestry, rising to 5.72% among same-ancestry couples versus 1.28% among mixed-ancestry couples (OR 4.69; 95% CI 3.70 to 6.01). Compared with ethnicity-based screening, the pan-ethnic targeted common variant (TCV) screening approach identified 11.9% more ARCs, with 26.8% of variants detected outside their historically associated populations. Postimplementation analyses also identified variants with limited yield, supporting periodic panel refinement. Conclusion The TCV approach improves carrier and ARC detection compared with ethnicity-based approaches and represents a practical screening model for genetically diverse populations. These findings support consideration of the TCV approach as a practical screening strategy in genetically diverse populations, with continuous panel refinement, inclusive reference datasets and targeted outreach to high-risk communities essential to maximising its population impact.

publications.title: Development of an LLM pipeline exceeding physician-documented cardiovascular risk scores under routine clinical conditions
publications.abstract: Abstract Aims Risk scores are essential to evidence-based cardiovascular care, but manual calculation is labour intensive and error prone. Large language models (LLMs) could automate this process, yet LLMs are limited by their propensity for calculation errors and factual hallucinations. Pipelines separating LLM-based data extraction from deterministic score computation may improve reliability and transparency. Methods and results We conducted a retrospective diagnostic study at a quaternary heart centre in Germany (January 2020 to July 2023). Patients with atrial fibrillation (n = 179) from an ablation registry and patients with severe aortic stenosis (n = 76) evaluated by a heart team were included. Six LLMs (GPT-5.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3, GPT-OSS 120B, and Kimi K2.5) were tested in standalone, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and pipeline configurations to compute HAS-BLED, CHA2DS2-VASc, and EuroSCORE II scores from routine clinical reports. Accuracy was assessed against expert-adjudicated ground truth using root mean squared error (RMSE) and Krippendorff’s α to evaluate numerical deviation and categorical agreement, respectively. Pipeline-generated scores showed substantially higher agreement with expert adjudication than standalone LLMs, LLMs with RAG, and treating physicians (mean Krippendorff’s α: 0.78 vs. 0.32 vs. 0.39 vs. 0.31) and lower deviation from ground truth (mean RMSE: 0.89 vs. 5.81 vs. 1.85 vs. 1.34). Conclusion Pipelines combining expert-curated knowledge injection, LLM-based clinical data extraction, and deterministic score calculation enable accurate and scalable cardiovascular risk score computation from unstructured real-world clinical data, outperforming physician-documented scores. Such pipelines could form the basis for clinical decision-support systems that automate routine risk assessment, reduce clinician workload, and promote more consistent evidence-based care.

publications.title: Within-day temporal dynamics of exhaled breath features during prolonged fasting monitored by SESI-HRMS: a pilot study
publications.abstract: Fasting is widely used to standardize breath sampling and reduce short-term dietary interference, yet fasting itself is a dynamic physiological state. We investigated the temporal stability of exhaled breath m/z features during prolonged daytime fasting using secondary electrospray ionization coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (SESI-HRMS). Three healthy volunteers consumed a standardized evening meal and fasted thereafter; exhaled breath was analyzed the next day from 08:00 to 18:00 (approximately 12.5-22.5 h of fasting) at 15-min intervals in positive and negative ion modes. Targeted analysis showed pronounced increases in the features putatively annotated as protonated acetone and pentanal, with the former consistent with established fasting physiology. Untargeted analysis identified 151 m/z features with significant concordant temporal trends in at least two of the three subjects; 60 remained after applying an ambient-background criterion, and 51 of these retained a consistent trend direction under all four data-processing approaches tested in a normalization sensitivity analysis. Dense longitudinal sampling also revealed abrupt signal changes coinciding with mouthpiece replacement in one participant; this exploratory observation points to a possible, as yet unconfirmed, additional pre-analytical source of variability. Because fasting duration, time of day, and instrument run time progressed together in this design, the observed changes cannot be attributed to fasting alone. These findings suggest that a ‘fasted’ breath sample may not be temporally invariant. We suggest that fasting duration, sampling time, ambient background, and handling of the sampling interface should all be standardized and reported in future breath metabolomics studies.

publications.title: Mode-Selective Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Reveals Asymmetric Chemical and Carrier-Sensitive Raman Grading in Photovoltaic III–V Tandem Nanowire Junctions
publications.abstract: Performance of tandem junction nanowire (NW) solar cells relies on the electronic quality of the tunnel diodes which serve as the separating junctions between subcells. Yet, the relevant interfacial physics occurs below the optical diffraction limit. Here we use hyperspectral tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) to map, with nanoscale precision, axially defined heterojunctions in InP/InGaP tandem junction photovoltaic NWs. By resolving mode-specific phonon and phonon-plasmon responses, we show that the nominally abrupt p/p++ and p++/n++ junctions are compositionally graded. The TOM mode, used as the primary compositional marker, yields transition widths of ∼90-120 nm, whereas other lattice- and carrier-sensitive modes exhibit broader central widths up to ∼190 nm, reflecting their additional sensitivity to alloying, structural disorder, and electronic coupling. In a first-order approximation, rescaling these TERS-derived widths to shorter, device-relevant NWs yields narrower junctions, consistent with independent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements that qualitatively capture the same trend despite surface and tip convolution effects. Complementary equilibrium band-edge model combined with a simplified one-dimensional Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) calculation, as an illustrative trend, further indicates that such grading is expected to widen the effective tunnel barrier. These findings establish mode-selective hyperspectral TERS as a validated, noninvasive method for quantitative nanoscale mapping of compositional grading in III-V NW junctions, with the carrier-sensitive L1 phonon-plasmon response providing complementary, model-assisted insight into the electronic evolution of the junctions.

publications.title: Rapid Simultaneous Quantification of Four Typical Phthalate Esters in Complex Food Matrices via Thermal Desorption–Dielectric Barrier Discharge Ionization Mass Spectrometry
publications.abstract: Conventional analytical methods for detecting and quantifying phthalate esters (PAEs) in foods generally require lengthy sample pretreatment procedures and suffer from severe matrix interferences. To address these shortcomings, a fast analytical platform based on a thermal desorption unit that is directly interfaced with dielectric barrier discharge ionization mass spectrometry (TD-DBDI-MS) was developed. The integration of a heated nitrogen purge system effectively suppressed atmospheric background interference and improved signal stability. Moreover, a simplified liquid-liquid extraction pretreatment protocol was established that eliminates the need for centrifugation and solid-phase extraction (SPE) cleanup steps. The complete analysis cycle time per sample was reduced by approximately 55% compared to conventional GC-MS/LC-MS workflows, and each analysis by TD-DBDI-MS was completed in only 10 seconds. The method exhibited excellent linearity for four typical PAEs in the range of 0.5-200.0 μg/L with correlation coefficients (R2) > 0.998. The limits of detection (LOD) ranged from 0.11 to 0.52 μg/kg, spike recoveries were between 82% and 106%, and relative standard deviations (RSDs) were <10%. Application to 19 commercially available food samples revealed widespread PAE contamination, with butyl benzyl phthalate (BBP) being detected in every sample. Contamination levels followed the order premade dishes > milk > sugary beverages. PAE migration levels from plastic bag packaging were significantly higher than those from plastic bottle and carton packaging. Fortunately, the measured PAE concentrations were all well below the specific migration limits (SMLs) specified in China's GB 5009.271-2016 regulation and EU Regulation 10/2011. This rapid, efficient, and robust method provides a novel approach for large-scale screening of PAEs in complex food matrices.
