topics: Heart Rate Variability and Autonomic Control

publications.title: Physiological Sleep Features Associated With Dimensions of Daily Dysfunction in Insomnia
publications.abstract: Daily dysfunction is a key criterion of insomnia, but its underlying structure and relationship with objective sleep physiology remain unclear. This study aimed to identify the dimensions of subjective daily dysfunction using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) in individuals with insomnia and to examine its association with polysomnography (PSG) macroarchitecture, electroencephalographic (EEG) spectral power and odds ratio product (ORP)-based sleep depth in individuals with and without insomnia. We hypothesized that more severe daily dysfunction would be associated with poorer sleep continuity, higher high-frequency EEG activity and lighter sleep depth. The final sample included 859 adults (50.1% female; mean age 44.2 ± 14.1 years) in the Sleep Apnea Global Interdisciplinary Consortium (SAGIC) without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) or shift work, including 368 with insomnia. EFA supported a single factor underlying the nine daily dysfunction items, which were combined into a total score. In univariate linear regression analyses adjusted for age, sex and site, higher beta-1 power and several ORP measures were nominally associated with more severe daily dysfunction, but none of them survived correction for multiple comparisons. No significant predictor-by-group interactions were observed. Across three levels of sleep physiology-PSG macroarchitecture, spectral power, and continuous sleep depth-no sleep measure was associated with daily dysfunction after correction for multiple comparisons. PSG macroarchitecture and sleep EEG-derived measures may not fully capture daily dysfunction. Future studies could examine whether within-night sleep dynamics are more informative than whole-night averages.

publications.title: Impact of total hip arthroplasty on multidimensional functioning and sleep in patients with hip osteoarthritis: A prospective cohort study
publications.abstract: BackgroundTotal hip arthroplasty (THA) is an established intervention for managing advanced osteoarthritis, offering substantial improvements in pain relief. However, relationship between sleep quality and functional outcomes after THA remains underexplored.ObjectiveThis longitudinal study aimed to evaluate changes in nocturnal sleep quality and daytime sleepiness and their association with functional recovery in 55 patients undergoing primary THA.MethodsPatients undergoing primary THA were enrolled in this prospective cohort study. Nocturnal sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, functional outcomes, and health-related quality of life were assessed preoperatively and at one, three, and sixxs months postoperatively using the PSQI, ESS, WOMAC, HOOS, and SF-36. Statistical analyses included Friedman's test with post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Kendall's tau correlations.ResultsWOMAC, PSQI, all HOOS dimensions, and both SF-36 components significantly improved over time. PSQI scores significantly decreased from the preoperative assessment to the postoperative follow-ups, indicating improved nocturnal sleep quality. In contrast, the median ESS score was 5 at each assessment, and no statistically significant group-level change in ESS was detected (p = 0.996). WOMAC and ESS were significantly correlated at one and six months, suggesting an association between functional recovery and daytime sleepiness at these timepoints.ConclusionsTHA was associated with significant improvements in pain, function, health-related quality of life, and nocturnal sleep quality up to six months postoperatively. No statistically significant group-level change in daytime sleepiness was detected. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously, and larger prospective studies are needed to confirm them.

publications.title: Standardizing wearable sleep data for clinical, research, and public health use: A World Sleep Society specification
A contactless approach for accurate sleep stage detection using the Sleepal AI Lamp
publications.abstract: Abstract Objective. To validate the accuracy and clinical feasibility of a noncontact radar system (Sleepal AI Lamp) for assessing sleep architecture and staging. Although noncontact radar sensors can capture respiratory and motor mechanics without physical attachment, robust validation in large-scale, pathologically diverse cohorts remains scarce. Approach. Nocturnal respiratory and body movement signals were assessed in 1022 adults using simultaneous measurements from a frequency-modulated continuous-wave bedside radar and gold-standard Polysomnography. The cohort included individuals with normal sleep profiles and patients with varying severities of obstructive sleep apnea. A frequency-augmented deep learning architecture interpreted these respiratory and movement signals. Main results. In the independent validation set, binary sleep–wake classification achieved 92.7% accuracy, a Cohen’s kappa of 0.792, 96.4% sleep sensitivity, 80.8% sleep specificity, and a macro-averaged F 1 score of 0.896. Four-stage classification (Wake, Light, Deep, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep) achieved 77.2% accuracy, a Cohen’s kappa of 0.677, a macro-averaged F 1 score of 0.768, and balanced accuracy/macro-recall of 77.4%, with stage-specific F 1 scores of 0.839, 0.740, 0.691, and 0.802 for Wake, Light, Deep, and REM, respectively. Significance. The findings support the validity of the 60 GHz radar-based system for automated assessment of sleep macrostructure. By capturing stage-specific respiratory and movement phenotypes without physical attachment, this technology may provide an unobtrusive tool for home-based screening, longitudinal recovery tracking, and population-level sleep epidemiology.

publications.title: PPGNet: Deep Multiple Instance Learning for Automated Hypertension Detection in OSA Patients Using PPG Signals
publications.abstract: Abstract Systemic hypertension (HTN) is a prevalent cardiovascular comorbidity in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), yet no scalable framework exists for HTN detection using routinely collected polysomnography (PSG) signals. We present PPGNet, a deep learning framework for diagnostic detection of established HTN in OSA patients using photoplethysmography (PPG) signals extracted from standard overnight PSG recordings. The framework employs a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) approach to model long-term hemodynamic and autonomic patterns across full-night recordings, aggregating 30-second instances into 30-minute bags enriched with sleep stage and apnea context. Evaluated under Leave- One-Patient-Out (LOPO) cross-validation on a clinically annotated cohort of 33 OSA patients, PPGNet achieved AUROC of 86.72%, AUPRC of 88.01%, Accuracy of 79.03%, Sensitivity of 83.33%, and MCC of 0.5842. Attention-based interpretability analysis confirms that the model captures clinically meaningful vascular signatures, including arterial stiffness markers and differential vasomotor responses to apnea events. This work establishes a proof-of-concept for cardiovascular risk stratification as a secondary outcome of routine sleep studies, enabling earlier HTN identification in this highrisk population without additional instrumentation.
topics: Heart Rate Variability and Autonomic Control

publications.title: The molecular heterogeneity and clinical impact of genomic driver alterations in prostate cancer
publications.abstract: Prostate cancer is a common malignancy with a heterogeneous disease course. Prior studies have identified a paucity of point mutations in protein-coding genes and only a few clinically relevant driver alterations. Here, using the Pan Prostate Cancer Group whole genome sequencing dataset from 1001 men, we perform an integrative analysis of cancer driver genes by quantifying recurrent genomic alterations among small mutations, structural variants, and copy number alterations in 961 primary prostate tumour samples. We identify at least one recurrent somatic or germline alteration in 97% of tumours and identify putative driver genes and mechanisms of dysregulation including frequently altered regulatory elements. A prominent example is the activation of oncogenes by structural variation-mediated hijacking of onco-enhancers of the solute carrier gene family including SLC30A4. Other recurrent alterations including FOXA1, MDM4, COL5A1, TP53, and BRCA1 stratify with metastatic disease, with additional drivers enriched in African-ancestry tumours. One quarter of tumours have acquired genome-informed therapeutic targets. Unsupervised analysis of alterations reveals four oncotypes with distinct genetic and clinical characteristics, including two clinically unfavourable oncotypes with shorter metastasis-free survival. Our study uncovers the full spectrum and recurrence patterns of genomic driver alterations in primary prostate cancers and delivers targets for biomarker development, mechanistic studies, and potential therapeutic interventions. The identification of clinically relevant driver alterations in prostate cancer remains elusive. Here, integrative analysis of cancer driver genes using the Pan Prostate Cancer Group whole genome sequencing dataset from 1,001 men identifies four oncotypes, two of which are associated with poor clinical outcomes.

publications.title: Copy number signatures in targeted gene panels associate with patient outcomes in routine clinical data
publications.abstract: Abstract Targeted gene panels (TGPs) dominate clinical sequencing, yet most copy-number (CN) signature studies rely on genome-wide assays. Whether signatures can be recovered from TGPs and retain clinical relevance remains unclear. We analyzed two real-world TGP cohorts comprising 1,726 patients across 62 tumor types, including 825 with clinical annotations, and made the underlying data publicly available. TGP-derived signatures recapitulated established biological associations, including links to homologous recombination deficiency and TP53 alterations, concordant with published genome-wide assay-derived CN signatures. Using our detailed clinical data, we found TGP-derived CN signatures associated with overall survival under standard therapies in ovarian, pancreatic, and colorectal cancer. In ovarian cancer, CN2 was associated with CCNE1 amplification and shorter survival under paclitaxel/carboplatin, with the survival association validated in an independent SNP-array cohort. These findings demonstrate that routine TGPs yield biologically and clinically relevant CN signatures with potential as biomarkers for therapy stratification.

publications.title: Integrated signatures define mutational processes in prostate cancer
publications.abstract: . Here we dissect the mutational processes shaping the genomes of 959 donors from the Pan Prostate Cancer Group and assess their clinical relevance. By integrating de novo extracted single-base substitution, insertion-deletion and copy-number signatures with six novel complex structural variant signatures, we identify eight integrated mutational footprints (IMFs) that collectively explain the mutational processes in 85% of primary prostate cancer genomes. IMFs were strongly influenced by regional biases in the genome, most prevalently androgen receptor-mediated mutagenesis and replication stress. Four IMFs, present in 37% of primary tumours, were significantly associated with shorter time to metastasis. These included reactive oxygen-species-driven mutagenesis and both canonical and non-canonical homologous recombination deficiency, the latter being enriched in patients of African ancestry. Extending to the metastatic setting, we found that IMFs predicted sensitivity to androgen receptor pathway inhibitors. Taken together, our study delineates the aetiologies and mutational processes that drive the genomic and clinical heterogeneity of prostate cancer, introduces IMFs as a unifying framework, and highlights their potential to improve both risk stratification and biomarker-guided treatment selection.

publications.title: Recurrent mechanisms of biallelic epigenetic inactivation reveal new putative tumour suppressor genes in prostate cancer
publications.abstract: The inactivation of tumour suppressor genes is a key step in cancer development, and is usually achieved by homozygous loss. In prostate cancer, however, large genomic regions are often hemizygously lost, which complicates the identification of putative tumour suppressors in these regions. Here, we develop Epi2Hit, an integrative computational method that leverages whole genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling and gene expression to identify biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes involving DNA methylation of promoter and enhancer regions of one allele and genomic loss of the other allele. We apply Epi2Hit to a cohort of 2,021 prostate cancers to discover tumour suppressor genes. In particular, we identify epigenetic biallelic inactivation of ZFHX3 at a recurrence level similar to TP53. Biallelic inactivation of ZFHX3, a transcriptional repressor, leads to upregulation of oncogenes, including MYC and a shorter time to metastasis. Finally, we provide evidence that epigenetic silencing as 2nd hit is particularly enriched in regions with nearby essential genes, precluding homozygous loss. Epigenetic biallelic inactivation in prostate cancer remains to be explored. Here, the authors develop a computational method Epi2Hit that integrates the hemizygous genomic disruptions with patterns of hypermethylation at regulatory CpG sites to identify biallelic inactivation in tumour suppressor genes.

publications.title: Structured Feedback Tools in Surgical Training: Results of the Endo-Workshop of the German Society of Residents in Urology 2024
publications.abstract: INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the need for structured feedback in urological residency training, we compared two assessment tools - Global Rating Scale (GRS) and Global Assessment of Urological Endoscopic Skills (GAUES) - during the 2024 Endo-Workshop of the German Society of Residents in Urology (GeSRU). METHODS: The workshop included simulation training on ureterorenoscopy (URS), transurethral resection of the bladder (TURB), and transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP). Feedback was provided using GRS and GAUES. An online survey assessed the need for structured feedback. Descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation were used. RESULTS: Among 15 participants, 53% were female, and 60% were early-stage residents. All expressed a desire for feedback, though only 73% had previously received unstructured feedback. Mean scores on GRS were 26 (URS), 28 (TURB), and 25 (TURP); on GAUES: 32, 37, and 33 (max 58). GRS and GAUES scores correlated positively (URS: ρ = 0.85; TURB: 0.5; TURP: 0.54). Post-workshop, 93% rated structured feedback as helpful. Most participants found GAUES (86%) and GRS (79%) specific and useful for training. CONCLUSION: Structured assessments like GRS and GAUES show strong potential to improve endourological training. GAUES demonstrates value as a task-specific tool. Continuous evaluation of such tools is essential for high-quality surgical education and patient care.

publications.title: Multi-scale modeling of continent-wide tracking data confirms the importance of landscape mosaics for the European wildcat
publications.abstract: Abstract Context Land use change is a major threat to the persistence of wildlife in human-dominated landscapes, making the knowledge of the amount and spatial configuration of suitable habitat essential for conservation. The European wildcat ( Felis silvestris ) currently persists in fragmented populations and faces ever increasing human pressure. Objectives We modeled and mapped suitable wildcat habitats at the continental scale, to identify opportunities and constraints for its conservation. Methods We compiled a large telemetry dataset comprising 200 wildcats across Europe and developed multi-scale habitat suitability models using Maxent. Habitat selection was analyzed at two hierarchical levels: home-range placement within the wider landscape and selection within the established home ranges. Results At both levels, wildcats selected broadleaved forests, mixed forests, and grasslands, while avoiding landscapes dominated by large continuous forests. For home-range placement, they preferred lower terrain ruggedness and less intensive agriculture. Within the home ranges, wildcats selected forest edges and small woody features. Conclusions Our results highlight the importance of heterogeneous forest–grassland mosaics habitats. More than half of the predicted suitable habitat occurred outside protected areas, highlighting the need for effective conservation strategies beyond their borders. Predictions of suitable areas should, however, be interpreted cautiously in regions where environmental conditions extend beyond those represented in the calibration data. By providing the first continental-scale habitat suitability map based on a large European telemetry dataset, our study offers a spatial foundation for identifying conservation priorities and supporting the long-term connectivity and recovery of wildcat populations.

publications.title: Mapping major types of hunting across the South American Dry Chaco and Chiquitano forests
publications.abstract: Abstract Hunting is a central, culturally embedded relationship between people and nature, yet also drives wildlife declines with far‐reaching consequences for ecosystems and people. It is also a highly diverse practice, involving a wide range of actors and hunting techniques, both of which determine the social‐ecological impacts of hunting. However, the geography of different types of hunting remains unclear, constituting a barrier for conservation and sustainability planning. Here, we develop an approach to identify and map key types of hunting across the vast Dry Chaco and Chiquitano tropical dry forests (950,826 km 2 ). We use a structured literature review and expert elicitation to identify key types of hunting and link these to a typology of land systems to map the spatial footprints of hunting types and how they changed between 1985 and 2023. We identify four major hunting types– traditional, retaliatory, commercial and recreational hunting – each associated with specific actors, practices and socio‐ecological contexts. All hunting types were widespread, with large areas associated with multiple, overlapping hunting types. The spatial footprints of hunting types, as captured by our land systems, increased considerably over time, particularly for retaliatory hunting (+54.6%), recreational hunting (+46.8%), and commercial hunting (+32.7%). Traditional hunting had historically increased less (+20.6%) and declined recently. By conceptualising hunting as a diverse socio‐ecological phenomenon rather than a uniform threat, we show how different hunting types are geographically distributed, interact and vary as landscapes change due to land‐use change. Our land‐system‐based approach thus provides a useful tool for better representing the social‐ecological diversity of hunting in sustainability planning and policy at broad geographic extents. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

publications.title: Widespread tree-cover gains across Europe over two decades were strongest in regions of agricultural retreat
publications.abstract: Abstract Changes in canopy cover and spatial arrangement of trees can strongly influence ecosystem functioning and biodiversity. Yet, long-term, continent-wide assessments have largely focused on tree cover alone. Here, we develop an integrated framework quantifying tree cover, connectivity, and tree-cover heterogeneity, and assess their dynamics across Europe from 2001 to 2021. We further examine how trends in these metrics are associated with forest management regimes, agricultural retreat, natural disturbances, climate and human activities. The most widespread combination of structural trends, covering 23% of the analyzed area, combined increasing tree cover and connectivity with declining heterogeneity. At the landscape scale, 0.25° grid cells with larger fractions of former cropland tended to exhibit more positive trends in tree cover and connectivity and more negative trends in heterogeneity. These contrasting trajectories show that tree-cover gains do not necessarily coincide with increasing tree-cover heterogeneity, with potential benefits for carbon accumulation and forest-associated species but possible costs for species dependent on open or structurally heterogeneous habitats.

publications.title: Monitoring reintroduction success: a decade of restoring European bison in the southwestern Carpathians
publications.abstract: Animal reintroductions are a key conservation strategy and central to trophic rewilding efforts, yet many reintroduction projects fail, with scarce evidence on why. This knowledge gap largely stems from a lack of clear and practical guidelines for how to define reintroduction success and thus what to monitor. Here, we evaluate early outcomes of a European bison reintroduction in the southwestern Romanian Carpathians by assessing whether released individuals establish a population, whether this population increases, and what financial investment was required to monitor these indicators. Specifically, we assessed (i) establishment through survival, (ii) displacement from the release site and spatial expansion, and (iii) proxies of population increase for the period 2014–2024. Our results provide clear evidence of early reintroduction success: released animals had a higher survival rate after improved animal selection, GPS-tracked European bison individuals showed low displacement, progressively expanded their range to cover a total of 127.5 km 2 , and genetic capture-recapture and population estimates showed that the European bison population increased substantially, from 91 surviving reintroduced individuals to 211 (95% CI: 209–290) in 2024, retaining genetic diversity. However, we also show that tracking reintroduction progress required substantial and sustained monitoring investment (€800,000, field personnel making up 75% of these costs), stressing the importance of clearly defining indicators and budgeting associated costs. More broadly, we highlight that monitoring the early phases of post-release establishment and population growth is critical to enable adaptive management of reintroduced megafauna, to proactively mitigate human-megafauna conflict, and to ultimately restore the ecological roles of these species.

publications.title: Explaining the Emergence of Deforestation Frontiers
publications.abstract: Land use expansion is linked to major sustainability concerns, including climate change, food security and biodiversity loss. This expansion is largely concentrated in so-called “frontiers”, defined here as places experiencing marked transformations due to rapid resource exploitation. Understanding the mechanisms shaping these frontiers is crucial for sustainability. Previous work focused mainly on explaining how active frontiers advance, in particular into tropical forests. Comparatively, our understanding of how frontiers emerge in territories considered marginal in terms of agricultural productivity and global market integration remains weak. We synthesize conceptual tools explaining resource and land use frontiers, and propose a new theory of frontier emergence, which identifies exogenous pushes, legacies of past waves, and actors’ anticipations as key mechanisms by which frontiers emerge. Processes of differential rent creation and capture and the buildup of agglomeration economies then constitute key mechanisms sustaining active frontiers. Finally, we discuss five implications for the governance of frontiers for sustainability. Our theory focuses on agriculture and deforestation frontiers in the tropics, but can be inspirational for other frontier processes, including extractive resources such as minerals.

publications.title: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a)
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen is an antisense oligonucleotide that reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). In a randomized placebo-controlled trial in patients with established cardiovascular disease, pelacarsen did not reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared to placebo. We further investigated the association of pelacarsen treatment with cardiovascular outcomes. METHODS: We report the association of pelacarsen treatment with a primary composite end point of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. Analyses included on-treatment, uninterrupted treatment, total primary end point events (first and recurrent events), landmark analyses classified by changes in and achieved lipoprotein(a) at 3 months, and key subgroups including baseline lipoprotein(a), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (CRP), and time from qualifying event to enrollment. RESULTS: For participants on treatment, a primary end point occurred in 434 participants (10.4%) randomly assigned to placebo and 380 participants (9.1%) assigned to pelacarsen (hazard ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.12). When evaluating participants with uninterrupted treatment, a primary end point event occurred in 167 participants (11.0%) in the pelacarsen group and 204 participants (10.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.89 to 1.34). When evaluating total primary end point events, there were 644 events in the pelacarsen group and 646 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.14). In landmark analyses evaluating participants alive and free of the composite end point at 3 months, when compared to placebo there was no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point either in participants with reduction in lipoprotein(a) greater than or equal to the median (170 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.29) or in participants who achieved lipoprotein(a) lower than or equal to the median (69.5 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.29). There was also no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point in any of the evaluated key subgroups including classification by median baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, high-sensitivity CRP, or time from qualifying cardiovascular disease to enrollment. CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen was not associated with a reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events when evaluated by treatment exposure, changes in or achieved lipoprotein(a) levels at 3 months, considering total events, or within subgroups of baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, or high-sensitivity CRP levels.

publications.title: Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a)
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). However, the effect of pelacarsen on cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted an international, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease and a lipoprotein(a) level of at least 70 mg per deciliter. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous pelacarsen (80 mg) administered monthly or matching placebo. The primary end point was a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 8350 patients underwent randomization, with 8322 included in the efficacy analysis; 4157 patients were assigned to receive pelacarsen, and 4165 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 59.7 years, and 27.0% were women. The median lipoprotein(a) level at baseline was 236 nmol per liter. At 12 months, the lipoprotein(a) level was 64.4 nmol per liter in the pelacarsen group and 233.4 nmol per liter in the placebo group. The median follow-up was 4.7 years. A primary end-point event occurred in 511 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 503 (12.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.15, P = 0.76). Among patients with a baseline lipoprotein(a) level of at least 90 mg per deciliter, a primary end-point event occurred in 402 of 3266 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 403 of 3274 (12.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15; P = 0.99). Serious adverse events occurred in 1553 of 4166 patients (37.3%) who received pelacarsen and in 1709 of 4154 (41.1%) who received placebo. CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen did not result in a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events than placebo at a median follow-up of 4.7 years. (Funded by Novartis; Lp[a]HORIZON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04023552.)See also in NEJM Evidence: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

Beyond Disambiguation: Explanatory Context Broadens Emotion Perception From Ambiguous Faces
publications.abstract: Abstract Context can disambiguate facial expressions by shifting interpretations toward one of several plausible emotions. We tested whether context can also broaden emotional interpretation by making multiple affective components simultaneously plausible. In a 2026 online experiment, participants ( N = 107) viewed 12 ambiguous expressions following everyday vignettes presented either with or without explanatory situational information. Participants were additionally assigned to a brief loving-kindness meditation (LKM) or an active control exercise. Without explanation, expressions were predominantly perceived as angry. Providing an explanation reduced perceived anger only slightly but substantially increased perceived worry, eliminating the initial difference between these ratings. Importantly, explanatory context did not simply replace anger with another emotion: rather, participants perceived the face as showing both anger and worry. LKM did not produce a comparable shift. Exploratory process analyses suggested that explanatory context altered emotion perception through changes in situational construal. Context also increased empathy and interpersonal closeness. Thus, context did not merely resolve emotional ambiguity. By helping observers understand why someone reacts as they do, it can support a richer interpretation of an ambiguous expression.

publications.title: Narcissism and Popularity: The Functional Role of Nonverbal Communication
Affective polarization of space under imminent physical threat: Self-reported affect, physiology, and social responding across two experiments
publications.abstract: When humans navigate through their social and spatial surroundings, they construct affective representations of the spatial context that shape this navigation. The theory of affective judgment in spatial context specifies how people build these representations. We present two laboratory experiments (N = 121 and N = 254) that lend more ecological validity to this line of inquiry. In a modified threat-of-shock paradigm, participants experienced an actual physical threat at one location of an environment depicted on a computer screen. Like in previous online experiments, we observed that, compared to a control condition, participants reported that the threat at this location (termed hotspot, an affectively salient location in space) colored the surroundings negatively with high subjectively perceived arousal at close distance whereas it colored the surroundings positively with low subjectively perceived arousal farther away (i.e., an affective polarization of space). However, this polarization was not mirrored by physiological indices of affect, even though electrodermal and cardiac activity lent support to the idea that participants actually were more threatened closer to the hotspot. Furthermore, we could not find evidence for affective polarization elicited by the threat affecting the affective empathy in response to strangers shown at the different locations. Thus, whereas the subjective experience of affective polarization of space seems robust across different operationalizations, we did not find evidence that this subjective experience is reflected in underlying physiology or that affective empathy is moderated by distance to a threatening location.

publications.title: Integrating context and emotions: Top-down effects of intent on mimicry and contagion.
publications.abstract: = 229) shape emotion perception (accuracy/bias), interpersonal closeness, emotional contagion, and emotional mimicry. A further goal was to assess whether mimicry and contagion are tightly coupled or can dissociate depending on how the expression is interpreted in context. In Study 1, adolescent avatars expressed happiness or sadness in scenarios wherein the context suggested that the expression was either normative (norm consistent) or nonnormative (norm challenging). In Study 2, videos of adult avatars in wedding/funeral scenes were paired with benevolent versus malicious intent captions that were explicitly normative or nonnormative. Across studies, nonnormative, ill-intentioned expressions were evaluated more negatively, reduced closeness, altered emotion attributions, elicited negative emotional reactions, and reduced contagion (especially for nonnormative/malicious smiles). Mimicry was highly selective such that it robustly occurred only for well-intentioned, normative smiles. Overall, the pattern supports a dual-path account in which mimicry and contagion are partly separable rather than tightly coupled. Specifically, both mimicry and contagion varied with how observers interpret the expresser's intent. However, mimicry, which is a visible response, was additionally constrained by the social cost of public alignment. Our samples (collected in 2023 and 2024) consisted primarily of female, university-educated participants from a Western cultural context; findings should be interpreted with this limitation in mind. publications.title: Different Smiles for Different Occasions: The Influence of Facial Configuration and Gaze Direction on the Perception of Smiles
publications.abstract: Abstract Smiles are ubiquitous in everyday life and used in a wide range of contexts with different social demands and affordances. In recent years, these have been linked to morphologically distinct smile configurations that serve different social functions. Further, eye gaze has been proposed to modulate these perceived functions. The present research assessed perceptions of distinct smile-gaze combinations. We observed a clear functional differentiation between different smile configurations (i.e., positive-intense, friendly, dominant, and miserable smiles) in terms of emotion attributions, perceived smile authenticity, and social meaning. Gaze direction effects were overall more subtle. Overall, downward moving gaze was most consistently associated with self-directed social emotions and reduced dominance perceptions for all smiles except miserable smiles as well as perceived affiliation for all smiles. Upward moving gaze was associated with positive emotions, whereas straight gaze enhanced the perceived authenticity of positive-intense smiles. In sum, smiles are not monolithic signals of happiness but rather a complex set of facial configurations that communicate distinct emotional and social intents.

publications.title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation vs surgical replacement in low-risk aortic stenosis: time-dependent late mortality in a pooled analysis of trials
publications.abstract: The expansion of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to low-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) has been driven by randomized trials reporting favourable early outcomes and non-inferiority to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), through early and intermediate follow-up.1 However, longer-term assessment is essential for patients with a longer life expectancy, in whom durability, reintervention risk, and survival are central to treatment selection.2 Recently released extended follow-up data from pivotal lower-risk trials have raised concerns that the early advantages of TAVI may attenuate over time, with emerging signals related to late mortality, valve durability, and reintervention.3–5 However, these trials were underpowered to evaluate all-cause mortality as an individual endpoint. Moreover, conventional time-to-event analyses may obscure clinically important time-dependent differences between two treatment strategies exhibiting non-parallel patterns of early and late risk. We therefore conducted a pooled reconstructed time-to-event analysis of randomized low-risk trials with extended follow-up of up to 7 years.

Strukturierte Implementierung von Physician Assistants auf einer Intermediate-Care-Station im strukturellen Herzinterventionsprogramm: Kompetenzbasiertes Einarbeitungs- und Tätigkeitsmodell eines universitären Hochleistungszentrums
publications.abstract: Zusammenfassung Die zunehmende Komplexität kardiovaskulärer Therapien sowie strukturelle Herausforderungen im Gesundheitswesen erfordern innovative Versorgungsmodelle. Physician Assistants (PAs) stellen hierbei eine relevante Ergänzung im ärztlichen Team dar. Der vorliegende Beitrag beschreibt die strukturierte Implementierung von PAs auf einer Intermediate-Care-Station (IMC) am Beispiel einer strukturellen Herzinterventionseinheit. Ergänzend werden ein kompetenzbasiertes Einarbeitungsmodell sowie ein arbeitsbereichsspezifischer Tätigkeitsrahmen mit Logbuch entwickelt und exemplarisch erläutert. Ziel ist es, eine übertragbare Grundlage für die Integration von PAs in hoch spezialisierten kardiologischen Versorgungsbereichen zu schaffen.

publications.title: Non-atrial/non-ventricular functional tricuspid valve regurgitation: a case report
publications.abstract: Abstract Background Functional tricuspid regurgitation (fTR) is usually caused by annular dilation and leaflet tethering secondary to right atrial (RA) or right ventricular (RV) remodelling. Rarely, extrinsic factors may impair annular motion. Case summary We report a 83-year-old woman with constrictive pericarditis who presented with right-sided heart failure and moderate tricuspid regurgitation. Multimodality imaging revealed a thickened pericardium, preserved RA and RV size, and a non-dilated, saddle-shaped annulus with markedly reduced motion. Following pericardiectomy, tricuspid annular mobility normalized, right-sided pressures decreased, and TR improved from moderate to mild. We introduce the term non-atrial/non-ventricular functional tricuspid regurgitation to describe this rare mechanism of isolated annular dysfunction caused by pericardial tethering. Discussion This case highlights a novel, distinct, and reversible form of fTR caused by pericardial constraint rather than chamber remodelling. We propose the term non-atrial/non-ventricular fTR to describe this mechanism. Recognizing this entity may guide surgical decision-making and avoid unnecessary tricuspid valve intervention.

publications.title: Association of PROMIS Profile-29 based quality of life with heart failure in asymptomatic patients (HERZCHECK)
publications.abstract: Abstract Heart failure is often diagnosed only when symptoms become acute, but early detection could help prevent disease progression. As patient-reported quality of life is strongly associated with heart failure outcomes, it may also serve as an additional correlate with the disease before symptoms occur. This cross-sectional study investigates the associations of quality of life and asymptomatic heart failure and was conducted as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis. It was based on data of 4,509 asymptomatic patients aged 40 to 69 years with at least one cardiovascular risk factor and without known heart failure at the time of quality of life assessment, whose heart failure status was determined during the baseline evaluation. The quality of life of patients with and without asymptomatic heart failure was compared, using logistic regression. Lower Physical Function was associated with higher odds of asymptomatic heart failure in females generally. Among females with hypercholesterolemia, lower physical function and lower pain interference were associated with asymptomatic heart failure, while in females who smoke, lower physical function was associated with asymptomatic heart failure. In males generally, lower Pain Interference and higher Pain Intensity were associated with higher odds of pre-HF, with additional associations of lower Pain Interference in males with diabetes, higher Depression and higher Pain Intensity in males with hypercholesterolemia, and lower Pain Interference and higher Pain Intensity in males who smoke. This study highlights the association between patient-reported physical health domains and asymptomatic heart failure. The findings provide hypothesis-generating insights into the relationship between quality of life and asymptomatic heart failure and highlight the need for longitudinal research.

publications.title: Gouverner avec une Cour constitutionnelle dans les Länder. Le cas de Berlin
publications.abstract: La société est-allemande comme communauté d’apprentissage. L’exemple de Dresde L’auteur analyse les transformations de la société est-allemande après la réunification de 1990, à travers l’exemple de Dresde. Il insiste sur les nouvelles libertés et l’essor de l’engagement citoyen après la chute de la RDA. De nombreuses associations culturelles, sociales, écologiques et éducatives ont été créées pour défendre les intérêts des habitants et reconstruire la société civile. Les citoyens ont participé activement à la sauvegarde du patrimoine, à la création d’écoles alternatives et à l’organisation d’événements culturels. Cependant, les années 90 ont révélé des conflits politiques, des divisions sociales et une difficulté à développer une véritable culture démocratique du débat. Des controverses importantes ont marqué Dresde, notamment autour du pont Waldschlösschen, de la reconstruction urbaine et du patrimoine culturel. Le mouvement PEGIDA et les tensions liées au racisme et à l’immigration ont profondément divisé la population. Malgré cela, des mobilisations citoyennes importantes ont montré la volonté d’une partie de la société de défendre la démocratie et la solidarité. L’auteur considère cette évolution comme un long processus d’apprentissage démocratique et de redéfinition de l’identité historique allemande. La société civile repose sur l’engagement individuel, la persévérance et la capacité des citoyens à agir collectivement face aux crises contemporaines.

publications.title: Sex-specific cognitive costs and benefits in early parenthood
publications.abstract: Research on cognitive changes across the transition to parenthood has primarily focused on mothers and emphasized decline, whereas paternal cognition and its neuroendocrine correlates remain understudied. In this cross-sectional study, we compared cognitive performance in 158 mothers and fathers of infants aged 8 weeks to 6 months with 154 non-parent controls and examined associations with sex and plasma oxytocin and cortisol concentrations. Multidimensional structural equation models revealed no evidence for global cognitive impairment associated with parenthood. Instead, selective and sex-specific patterns emerged: Fathers showed enhanced object perception relative to non-fathers, whereas mothers exhibited modestly diminished working memory as compared to non-mothers. Face memory was positively associated with circulating oxytocin concentrations and with female sex, independent of parenthood status. Plasma cortisol concentrations were not significantly associated with cognitive performance across domains. Sensitivity analyses adjusting for age, sleep quality, depressive symptoms, stress, and hormone sampling time did not substantially alter the overall pattern of findings, although a subgroup-specific association between oxytocin and face memory in males was not retained after adjustment. Together, these findings suggest that early parenthood is characterized by domain- and sex-specific cognitive differences rather than uniform impairment. The results challenge deficit-oriented accounts of postpartum cognition and underscore the importance of integrating fathers and neuroendocrine perspectives into models of cognitive adaptation during early parenthood.

publications.title: State-dependent dual-site prefrontal TMS bidirectionally modulates working-memory accuracy
publications.abstract: Working memory (WM) is a core cognitive function that is both mechanistically tractable and clinically relevant, making it a prime target for noninvasive neuromodulation. However, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) studies targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) have yielded variable WM outcomes, possibly because single-site protocols fail to engage the distributed network dynamics that support WM and because effects depend on momentary brain states. Here, we tested whether dual-site sequential TMS, excitatory intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) over left DLPFC combined with inhibitory continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS) over medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), produces state-dependent modulation of WM performance compared with single-site DLPFC stimulation alone. Thirty-seven healthy adults completed a within-subjects protocol with intermixed 0-back and 2-back WM conditions. Self-reported fatigue before each task run served as a coarse indicator of the participant's cognitive state. Bayesian linear mixed models revealed a clear state-dependent pattern: in the high-load 2-back condition, dual-site stimulation improved accuracy when participants reported low fatigue but impaired accuracy when they reported high fatigue. No reliable effects were found for the 0-back condition or for reaction time. These findings demonstrate that dual-site prefrontal TMS can bidirectionally modulate WM accuracy relative to single-site stimulation depending on the participant's cognitive state, highlighting the importance of state-aware and network-sensitive stimulation approaches for cognitive enhancement.

publications.title: Shades of smiles: creating variants of smiles from neutral images of real individuals - method and validation
publications.abstract: Despite their crucial role in emotion research, facial expression databases primarily contain stimuli of basic emotions, rather than subtle, socially nuanced ones. Here, we introduce a rigorous yet easily applicable pipeline for synthesizing fine-grained emotional expressions—specifically, reward, affiliative, and dominance smiles—from neutral photographs, guided by Facial Action Coding System (FACS) principles and the perspective that expressions serve as social signals. From neutral images of 90 individuals (45 female, 45 male), we generated five expressions each (including neutral and disgust), and mirrored each image to address hemiface biases. In an online validation study, 13 participants rated each image on emotional content, arousal, and plausibility, yielding 26 ratings per expression and model. Rating results show that (1) reward smiles were most reliably recognized, while affiliative and dominance smiles tended to be confused with related expressions and that (2) arousal and plausibility ratings varied systematically across expression types and model gender. In summary, the suggested expression generation pipeline and the validated stimuli offer a robust method and a scalable dataset for research on fine-grained emotion recognition and emotional communication.

EEG decodability of facial expressions and their stereoscopic depth cues in immersive virtual reality
publications.abstract: Face perception typically occurs in three-dimensional space, where stereoscopic depth cues enrich the perception of facial features. Yet, most neurophysiological research on face processing relies on two-dimensional displays, potentially overlooking the role of stereoscopic depth information. Here, we combine immersive virtual reality (VR), electroencephalography (EEG), and eye tracking to examine the neural representation of faces under controlled manipulations of stereoscopic depth. Thirty-four participants viewed computer-generated faces with neutral, happy, angry, and surprised expressions in frontal view under monoscopic and stereoscopic viewing conditions. Using time-resolved multivariate decoding, we show that EEG signals in immersive VR conditions can reliably differentiate facial expressions. Stereoscopic depth cues elicited a distinct and decodable neural signature, confirming the sensitivity of our approach to depth-related processing. Yet, expression decoding remained robust across depth conditions, indicating that under controlled frontal viewing, the neural representation of behaviorally distinguishable facial expressions is invariant to binocular depth cues. Eye tracking showed that expression-related gaze patterns contained comparable information but did not account for neural representations, while depth information was absent in gaze patterns—consistent with dissociable representational processes. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of EEG-based neural decoding in fully immersive VR as a tool for investigating face perception in naturalistic settings and provide new evidence for the stability of expression representations across depth variations in three-dimensional viewing conditions.

publications.title: Composite quantile estimation for multivariate functional partially varying coefficient hybrid model with dependent errors
Quantile Tensor Regression for Integrative Genomic Analysis of Oesophageal Carcinoma
publications.abstract: Recent integrative genomic studies have increasingly exploited the tensor structure of multi-omics data to develop statistical methods that jointly model the relationship between clinical outcomes and multiple genomes. However, genomic measurements and clinical outcomes are frequently contaminated by outliers or heavy-tailed noise, necessitating robust tensor-based inference approaches. In this paper, we investigate the quantile tensor regression with an emphasis on the region selection problem. We introduce a novel estimator that integrates quantile regression for robustness with a nonconvex penalty to encourage sparsity in the tensor coefficient, thereby enabling the identification of localized genomic regions that significantly influence the clinical response. To solve the resulting optimization problem, we devise an effective algorithm tailored to the nonconvex objective and tensor architecture. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed nonconvex penalized estimator. Extensive simulations demonstrate the excellent finite-sample performance of the proposed estimator. We further illustrate the practical utility of the proposed estimator through an application to esophageal carcinoma data, providing empirical validation.

publications.title: Dynamic nonparametric functional graphical model
Spatially Correlated Analysis of Infectious Disease Outcomes Based on Bayesian Functional Hierarchical Models
publications.abstract: Prevalent infectious diseases, such as COVID-19, have triggered widespread social panic and placed immense strain on global healthcare systems. Understanding the complex spatio-temporal dynamics of these diseases and accurately forecasting their progression are essential for effective public health interventions. Existing forecasting paradigms struggle to simultaneously resolve three fundamental challenges: (1) temporal misalignment of epidemic curves across regions, (2) spatial dependency structures in transmission dynamics, and (3) persistent overdispersion in count data. This paper develops a novel Bayesian hierarchical model tailored to spatially correlated functional count data to analyze and predict the trajectories of case counts across different regions. Our key innovations address critical gaps in pandemic analytics. By implementing a curve preprocessing step, the proposed model aligns the epidemic curves, facilitating better comparison across regions with staggered outbreak timings. The Negative-Binomial distribution is employed to accommodate data overdispersion, while the temporal dynamics are captured using nonparametric basis functions, allowing for flexible and accurate modeling of disease trajectories. Spatial correlation among regions is modeled through a Leroux conditional autoregressive prior, which adapts to varying degrees of spatial dependency. An efficient Gibbs sampler is developed to derive posterior inferences and multi-step ahead forecasting distributions. Simulation studies demonstrate substantial improvements of the proposed model in estimation accuracy and prediction precision compared to several alternative approaches. Applied to COVID-19 case data across U.S. states, the model provides critical insights into the time-varying effects of key covariates. It also enables the early prediction of case surges in states with delayed outbreak trajectories, offering valuable tools for resource allocation and strategic planning.

publications.title: Quantlet: the code snippet knowledge platform
publications.abstract: Abstract Many researchers increasingly rely on code snippets, algorithms, and information they find online to address complex problems. While these resources can provide immediate solutions, they often come from unverified sources and lack the context necessary for correct application. This growing dependence on readily available, sometimes ill-advised, information can lead to significant missteps, including inefficient code, flawed methodologies, or incorrect conclusions. As a result, researchers may unwittingly propagate errors or overlook more robust, appropriate solutions that are crucial for scientific progress. This paper presents the integration of the Quantlet and Quantinar platforms, collectively referred to as the $$Q^2$$ ecosystem, aimed at overcoming challenges faced by applied scientists and researchers due to the vast and fragmented array of data and code available online. The focus of this integration is to enhance accessibility and usability of academic resources by effectively linking research with pertinent code and datasets. The study introduces an adaptive clustering algorithm that organizes and dynamically groups academic content from Quantinar alongside code and computational results from Quantlet, thus linking academic theory and practice. With these technical advancements, the $$Q^2$$ framework aspires to enhance transparency and reproducibility within the academic research landscape. Ultimately, it aims to provide a cohesive learning environment that meets the evolving needs of the academic community, empowering researchers in their pursuit of knowledge and facilitating deeper insights into complex data-driven methodologies.

publications.title: Unresolved: Deciphering the Biosphere’s Role in the Earth System
publications.abstract: Abstract. A central tenet of Earth system science is that Earth's macroscopic environmental conditions reflect the co-evolution of the biosphere and the geosphere. Nevertheless, a universal theory of the biosphere's role in the Earth system remains elusive. This paper reviews the state of knowledge and reflects on future directions from the perspective of scientifically understanding Earth as an integrated whole. Four biosphere dimensions need to be considered in developing a theoretical foundation for the biosphere’s role in the Earth system: physical, i.e., physics-based influences of life on planetary state, such as through albedo, roughness length, and latent energy fluxes; chemical, i.e., the material operations of the biosphere as part of the planetary biogeochemical cycles, chemically linking biotic and abiotic components of the Earth system; biological, i.e., the genetic programme (biodiversity) and its derived structures required to operate the organisms of a functional biosphere performing the Earth system functions; and ecological, i.e., the formations of organisms into ecosystems and their biotically altered larger environments as conduits of life for exerting macro-scale influence on Earth as a whole, by performing Earth system functions as a biosphere that is more than the sum of its parts. Today, it is primarily the physical and chemical dimensions that are included in Earth system models and their biogeochemical submodels, while empirical studies on the biological dimension often focus on limited geographical areas and species enumeration, and only to a lesser extent on systemic effects. For studying the biosphere’s role in the Earth system, a comprehensive approach across scales is required. Owing to its shared genes and evolutionary history, we argue that the biosphere can be regarded as a single global entity. However, biosphere-geosphere interactions and their Earth system consequences differ geographically and between the marine and terrestrial realms, with the terrestrial biosphere generally influencing Earth conditions more directly and over shorter time scales than the marine. A better understanding (working towards the development of a more universal theory) of the biosphere’s role in the Earth system is needed to advance Earth system science and, not least, for developing better capacity for prediction of Earth’s responses to anthropogenic perturbations. More systematic collaboration than currently occurring is required between biogeophysics, biogeochemistry, biodiversity science (extending to traits and functions), ecosystem science, and land systems research.

publications.title: A vegetation model based indicator measuring the risk for ecosystem destabilization (EcoRisk)
publications.abstract: A stable Earth system requires a healthy biosphere, but many ecosystems are being pushed beyond safe limits due to human activities such as land-use, resource extraction and climatic changes.We map the “risk for ecosystem destabilization” (EcoRisk) due climate and land-use pressures based on simulations with the dynamic global vegetation model LPJmL. EcoRisk quantifies ecosystem dissimilarity relative to a preindustrial reference on a scale ranging from no change (0) to very strong change (1). It captures shifts in the vegetation structure (e.g., transition from forest to savanna), as well as relative (relevant for the local scale) and absolute shifts (relevant for the global scale) in soil and vegetation carbon stocks and fluxes, nitrogen stocks and fluxes, and changes in the water cycle [Stenzel et al. 2024].Currently, almost 30% of the Earth’s global land area show severe changes (EcoRisk exceeds 0.55, a threshold derived from 10 independent indicators of biosphere integrity). These transgressions have steadily increased since 1600 and accelerated after 1925 [Stenzel et al. 2025]. A preliminary assessment of the future status according to simulations from ISIMIP3b scenarios indicates that EcoRisk continues to rise under SSP3-7.0, whereas under SSP1-2.6 it might plateau after mid-century, depending on the land-use scenario.EcoRisk however is not only useful as a biosphere integrity indicator, but can also be used for model evaluation, because it can be computed separately for vegetation structure, water, carbon or nitrogen. It thus provides a diagnostic tool for model evaluation, benchmarking, and isolating the sources of change after major code revisions.Data availability: https://biointegrity.pik-potsdam.deStenzel, F.; Braun, J.; Breier, J.; Erb, K.; Gerten, D.; Heinke, J.; Matej, S.; Ostberg, S.; Schaphoff, S. & Lucht, W.: biospheremetrics v1.0.2: an R package to calculate two complementary terrestrial biosphere integrity indicators -- human colonization of the biosphere (BioCol) and risk of ecosystem destabilization (EcoRisk), Geoscientific Model Development, 2024, 17, 3235-3258Stenzel, F.; Ben Uri, L.; Braun, J.; Breier, J.; Erb, K.; Gerten, D.; Haberl, H.; Matej, S.; Milo, R.; Ostberg, S.; Rockström, J.; Roux, N.; Schaphoff, S. & Lucht, W.: Breaching planetary boundaries: Over half of global land area suffers critical losses in functional biosphere integrity, One Earth, 2025, 8, 101393

publications.title: Mapping functional biosphere integrity via human appropriated NPP and ecosystem change
publications.abstract: A stable Earth system requires a healthy biosphere, but many ecosystems are being pushed beyond safe limits due to human activities such as land-use change, resource extraction, or climatic changes. Functional biosphere integrity is at the core of global assessments demarcating the limits to this human interference with our planet (Richardson et al. 2023, Rockström et al. 2023, te Wierik et al. 2025).Studying the biosphere can happen through field observations, remote sensing, or computer models. Modelling has the advantage of obtaining global scale data, and the opportunity to also study past and future states of the Earth System.We utilize the dynamic global vegetation model LPJmL to map the pressures of climate change and land use on ecosystems via the two indicators human appropriation of net primary productivity (HANPP) and the risk for ecosystem destabilization (EcoRisk) spatially explicitly for each year since 1600 (Stenzel et al. 2025). HANPP acts as a metric for human pressure on the environment, while EcoRisk is more of a response metric measuring changes in biogeochemical conditions and thus risk for degradation.Since such indicators ideally also require thresholds that define when local boundaries are breached, we developed a method using 10 independent indicators for biosphere integrity (e.g. human footprint index, biodiversity intactness index, forest landscape integrity index) informing where local transgressions have already occurred. This helped us to map regions with intermediate and high risk of degradation and allowed us to aggregate the local status to the area globally transgressing the local boundaries.Both metrics show strongly increasing values since 1600, and combined are current transgressed on 60% of the land area, with 38% already at high risk.A preliminary assessment of the future status according to simulations from ISIMIP3b scenarios indicates that climatic pressures will keep rising, while pressures due to land use change strongly vary with scenario, based on projected productivity changes on agricultural areas and the demand for bioenergy plantations as a negative emissions technology.

publications.title: Search for dark photons from Higgs boson decays in the gluon-gluon fusion channel in proton-proton collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13.6 $$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A bstract This paper presents a search for semi-visible Higgs boson decays in final states with a photon ( γ ) and missing transverse momentum $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}} $$ p T miss . The analysis is optimised for the gluon-gluon fusion production channel and exploits a novel trigger deployed in 2023, with reduced thresholds down to 50 GeV on the photon transverse momentum ( $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\gamma } $$ p T γ ) and 70 GeV on the $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}} $$ p T miss , in combination with a selection on the transverse mass of the $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}} $$ p T miss -γ system ( m T ) above 80 GeV. The results are interpreted in terms of Higgs boson decays into a γ and a dark photon γ d ( H → γγ d ). The analysis is performed using 135 fb − 1 of Run 3 data collected by ATLAS in 2023 and 2024. A boosted decision tree is used to identify events with misreconstructed primary vertices, which can affect the $$ {p}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}} $$ p T miss calculation. Data-driven methods are employed to estimate the backgrounds from jets and electrons misidentified as photons, while the backgrounds with genuine photons are taken from Monte Carlo simulations, normalised to data in control regions with muons. A binned maximum-likelihood fit to the m T distribution is performed to evaluate the compatibility of the observed data with the Standard Model expectation. No significant excess is observed over the Standard Model prediction, and an observed (expected) upper limit on the branching ratio of H → γγ d of 1.4% (1.2%) is obtained at 95% confidence level. Combining this result with previous Run 2 searches improves the observed (expected) upper limit to 0.9% (0.9%).

publications.title: Measurement of isolated photon plus two-jet correlations in Pb+Pb and pp collisions at 5.02 TeV with ATLAS
publications.abstract: This paper presents a measurement of photon plus two-jet events in pp and Pb+Pb collisions, i.e. events in which the transverse momentum of a single photon is balanced by two distinct jets. The measurement was performed using pp data taken in 2017 with an integrated luminosity 260 pb − 1 , and Pb+Pb data taken in 2018 with an integrated luminosity 1.72 nb − 1 , both at s NN =5.02 TeV, as recorded by the ATLAS detector. Events with photons in the transverse momentum range 90–180 GeV and at least two anti- k t R = 0.2 jets with a p T > 30 GeV are selected, and three observables are measured: x JJ γ , A JJ γ , and Δ R JJ . These observables characterise the overall energy loss of the multiparton system from medium interactions (x JJ γ ), the relative energy loss between the two colour-charge carriers (A JJ γ ), and medium-induced modifications to their opening angle (Δ R JJ ). The observables are corrected for uncorrelated combinatoric background contributions using a novel multijet mixing technique, for photon purity, and for detector resolution effects via iterative unfolding. Final results are presented per photon, and the ratio ( I AA ) is taken between measurements in Pb+Pb and pp collisions, for Pb+Pb centrality intervals of 30–80%, 10–30%, and 0–10%. Significant suppression of per photon two-jet yields in all three observables, I AA < 1, is observed as a result of parton-medium interactions. The experimental measurements are compared to three different jet quenching models: Jewel , Jetscape , and Lbt .
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: GEO-Based VLBI for Deep Space Navigation: Time-Position Error Modeling and Performance Analysis
publications.abstract: Radiometric interferometry, implemented through ground-based Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) and Delta Differential One-Way Ranging (Delta-DOR), is a powerful technique for angular spacecraft navigation. The previously proposed concept of Radiometric Interferometry Navigation using Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) Satellites (RINGS) replaces terrestrial stations with GEO satellites, so that its basic measurement unit is a single GEO-GEO interferometric baseline. This paper analyzes the two main practical error sources of this two-station sensor: residual relative clock misalignment between the satellites and uncertainty in their positions. Analytical models map both into angular error and show that the timing-induced path error is divided by the long GEO-GEO baseline. The timing chain is evaluated, including Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) synchronization, passive hydrogen maser (PHM) clocks, two-way inter-satellite time transfer, and relativistic corrections, and a Monte Carlo framework propagates clock and position errors through a dual-frequency angle-of-arrival estimator. For a GEO-GEO baseline of about 84,000km, residual timing errors of 10ps and 100ps contribute about 0.05nrad and 0.5nrad of angular scatter, whereas GEO position uncertainty contributes about 17nrad per meter per axis and is the dominant error driver; for the 120° three-GEO baseline these values are about 15% larger. A Sagnac-type term biases the uncorrected two-way clock estimate by about 1.25 μs and must be computed from the GEO states. Theoretical analysis supported by simulation shows that nanoradian-level angular precision is attainable with sub-meter GEO position knowledge and PHM-class timing. This is the statistical precision floor of the sensor, not its absolute accuracy after calibration.

publications.title: Search for $$ t\overline{t} $$ resonances in final states with exactly one or two leptons using 140 fb−1 of pp collision data at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV with the ATLAS experiment
publications.abstract: A bstract A search for heavy spin-1 and spin-2 resonances decaying into a top-antitop-quark pair has been performed with 140 fb − 1 of proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider at a centre-of-mass energy of $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ s = 13 TeV. Final states with either exactly one electron or muon, or exactly two leptons ( ee , μμ or eμ ), large missing transverse momentum, and two jets, at least one of which must be identified as likely containing a b -hadron decay, are considered. The search targets resonances with both narrow and broad widths relative to the detector resolution, and with masses in the range of 0.4–5.0 TeV. No significant deviation from the Standard Model prediction is observed. Exclusion limits are set on the production cross-section times branching ratio for hypothetical Z′ bosons, Kaluza-Klein gravitons, and Kaluza-Klein gluons that decay into top-quark pairs.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for soft unclustered energy patterns containing muons in the final state in pp collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A bstract Soft unclustered energy patterns (SUEPs) refer to high-multiplicity, isotropic distributions of low-momentum particles that could arise in strongly-coupled hidden sector theories. A search for SUEPs whose decay products contain muons in the final state is presented using 140 fb − 1 of proton–proton collision data at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ s = 13 TeV collected by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during 2015–2018. The analysis targets SUEP signatures via gluon–gluon fusion production of a scalar mediator in Hidden Valley scenarios. No significant excess over the Standard Model expectation is observed. Exclusion limits are set on the product of the mediator production cross section and the branching fraction for its decay into a SUEP, down to 0.05 fb for a mediator mass of m S = 750 GeV, 0.4 fb for m S = 400 GeV, and 70 fb for m S = 125 GeV; the last value, when identifying the mediator with the Standard Model Higgs boson, translates to an upper limit on the branching fraction of around 0.2%.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Observation of pair production of longitudinally polarized Z bosons in four-lepton final state with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: The production of two longitudinally polarized bosons is measured using proton–proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS experiment at a center-of-mass energy √ = 13.6 TeV and with an integrated luminosity of 164 fb−1. The candidate events are reconstructed using two same-flavor opposite-charge electron or muon pairs. The polarization fractions of the boson pair are measured inclusively in the fiducial phase space and also in two regions of the four-lepton invariant mass, and the results are consistent with the Standard Model predictions. After a statistical combination with a previous measurement at √ = 13 TeV, the first observation of the production of two simultaneously longitudinally polarized bosons is obtained, with observed and expected significances of 6.5 and 5.6 standard deviations, respectively.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for a leptoquark in events with a hadronically decaying τ-lepton and missing transverse momentum using pp collisions at s=13TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A search for leptoquark signals is performed in final states with a hadronically decaying τ -lepton and missing transverse momentum, using data from proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of s = 13 TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during Run 2 (2015–18), corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb − 1 . The analysis is designed to probe both resonant production and non-resonant t -channel exchange of the leptoquark, covering a wide range of coupling scenarios. No excess above the Standard Model background prediction is observed. Limits are set on the couplings in the benchmark U 1 vector-leptoquark model at 95% confidence level for masses between 1.5 TeV and 3.0 TeV.
