topics: Cognitive Radio Networks and Spectrum Sensing

publications.title: Angle Estimation for Initial Access in True-Time-Delay Systems: Communication and Sensing Tradeoff
publications.abstract: In joint communication & sensing (JCNS) the data signal is used to obtain parameter estimates. An example is the angle of arrival (AoA) which can be used to solve the initial access problem of beam selection. true-time delay (TTD) arrays are attractive for this purpose, as their frequency-dependent response encodes the angle information in the receive signal power spectrum. This work investigates the tradeoff between angle estimation accuracy and achievable data rate for uplink signals in a TTD array. The Fisher information (FI) for the angle is used to find the bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound (BCRLB) under the assumption of a raised cosine distributed angle prior. Maximization of the FI under a data rate constraint is solved by waterfilling power per frequency bin dependent on sensing weights. Compared to a frequency flat signal, the optimized power allocation increases the FI \approx 4.9 dB at 5% rate loss for prior width of \pm 10°. Numerical simulations show that the derived BCRLB can be attained by a maximum likelihood (ML) estimator above an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) threshold, confirming that the FI underlying the waveform design is attainable.

publications.title: Box-Shift: Fixed-Complexity Counter-Hypothesis Generation for Soft-Output MIMO Box Decoding
publications.abstract: Box Decoding is a sort-free tree-search multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector with a fixed per-layer cost independent of the quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) order. Its regular datapath is well suited to hardware implementation, but the detector has so far been limited to hard-output operation in uncoded systems. Its fixed four-point box spans two adjacent Gray-coded QAM levels per axis, leaving most bits without counter-hypotheses for higher-order QAM. This missing counter-hypothesis (MCH) problem prevents the direct computation of finite max-log log-likelihood ratios (LLRs). We propose the \emph{Box-Shift} algorithm, which shifts the existing box to the nearest node carrying the complementary value of each Gray-coded bit at each detection layer. Unlike Bit-Flip, Box-Shift analytically identifies the partially optimal counter-hypothesis using one inverter per bit and updates the path metric through an index-domain increment. The proposed method preserves the sort-free, QAM-order-independent structure of Box Decoding. Coded $4\times4$ MIMO simulations using 5G~NR low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding show that Box Decoding with Box-Shift achieves a $0.7$--$1.5$\,dB gain in $E_b/N_0$ over the same detector with Bit-Flip at a bit error rate of $10^{-5}$, with equal soft-candidate budgets. For the soft-candidate metrics, the incremental update of Box-Shift needs $75\%$ fewer real multiplications than the explicit evaluation of Bit-Flip at a comparable number of real additions.

publications.title: Iteration-Free Candidate Pruning and an Index-Domain VLSI Architecture for Sort-Free MIMO Box Decoding up to 1024-QAM
publications.abstract: Wi-Fi~7 and 5G NR use constellations up to $4096$-QAM and $1024$-QAM at multi-gigabit peak rates. The MIMO detector must sustain these rates at a low cost. Linear MMSE detection meets these rates at low cost but loses several dB in SNR. $K$-Best detection recovers this loss, but its per-layer sorting grows with the modulation order and needs large sorting networks or deep pipelines at these rates. Box Decoding is a sort-free tree-search detector whose complexity does not depend on the QAM order, and its deterministic pruning keeps the cost fixed as the MIMO size grows. Single-step candidate pruning (SCP) is fully parallel but less accurate, while iterative candidate pruning (ICP) is more accurate, but its selection loop costs either throughput or area. This paper proposes Max-Min-Exchange Candidate Pruning (MMECP), which replaces the selection loop of ICP with a single max-min exchange without a feedback path and keeps \mbox{near-$K$-Best} performance. The paper also presents a VLSI architecture that represents each candidate by its integer constellation index, so that candidates and their distances are obtained by bit selection instead of operations on symbol values. A $4\times4$ detector synthesized in TSMC $16$\,nm detects one vector per cycle at $1$\,GHz for $64$- to $1024$-QAM and produces up to $40$\,Gb/s, while its gate count grows by $63\%$ over this range. Its normalized hardware efficiency is $2.3\times$, $12\times$ and $14\times$ that of the best compared hard-output detector at $64$-, $256$- and $1024$-QAM.

name: Hans Pretzsch
topics: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

publications.title: 3D crown information enhances growth predictions and where the gain comes from
From early-warning signal to potential risk indicator: Using tree-growth variability to assess climate-related risk in major European tree species
publications.abstract: Variability metrics are the most frequently used early-warning signals across scientific disciplines. Applied to ecological time series, increasing variability is widely interpreted as a signal of reduced system stability. In trees, elevated growth variability has been linked to increased climate sensitivity, but its drivers and continental-scale patterns remain poorly understood. Here, we assess patterns of tree-growth variability under climate change and explore its potential to serve as an indicator of climate-related growth vulnerability. We quantified growth variability using the Gini coefficient applied to a Europe-wide tree-ring width dataset covering seven tree species from 631 sites. Generalized additive models were used to identify climatic and tree-level drivers of growth variability and to project spatio-temporal trends across biogeographical regions under three climate change scenarios from 2011 to 2100. To evaluate the applicability of growth variability as risk indicator, predicted growth variability was translated into species-specific risk classes. High growth variability was consistently associated with higher climate-related risk classes, whereas intermediate and low levels showed a less distinctive and more species-specific signal. Climate and tree variables were identified as key drivers of growth variability, whereby warming consistently increased variability, whereas precipitation reduced it. Growth variability increased in older trees but declined with higher basal area increment. Future projections showed increasing growth variability with scenario severity, particularly in continental parts of species' distribution areas, although responses differed among species and biogeographical regions. Our results suggest that increasing growth variability reflects rising climate sensitivity and may indicate heightened climate-related risk once species-specific thresholds are exceeded. This approach represents a first step towards using growth variability not only as a diagnostic signal, but also as a prospective indicator of climate-related tree risk that may complement existing modelling frameworks for assessments of tree species suitability in the future.
topics: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

publications.title: Simultaneous 3/4‐power scaling of leaf mass and 2/3‐power scaling of leaf area with stem mass in plants
publications.abstract: Background: Plant allometry theory developed last century focused on 2/3-power scaling, determined by light interception considerations. More recently 3/4-power scaling based on the properties of vascular distribution networks has been proposed. Methods: We assembled 783 observations on plant height, leaf area, leaf mass, stem mass and total mass, for eight species groups and spanning eight orders of magnitude for total mass to empirically explore which scaling theory best defines plant allometry. Results: The data confirmed that the relationship between leaf mass and stem mass follows ¾-power scaling. However, leaf area–total (leaf plus stem) mass relationships follow 2/3-power scaling. Previously reported non-1:1 scaling of leaf area:total mass and associated lower specific leaf area of larger plants emerges as a mechanism whereby 3/4-power scaling of organ mass for resource distribution and 2/3-power scaling of leaf area for light capture are reconciled in one body plan. In our data set, scaling coefficients of leaf area:total mass in smaller plants tend towards 1:1, which is intuitively logical where stems provide only leaf–root connection without leaf support for light capture. Conclusions: A unified theory of plant allometry would integrate ¾-power scaling of organ mass for resource distribution, 2/3-power scaling of leaf area for light capture, scaling near 1:1 for small plants and provision for variation reflecting species-specific body plan configuration.
topics: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

publications.title: Tree growth, physiology, and ecosystem services across a sealing gradient in Munich, Germany
publications.abstract: Urban trees provide essential ecosystem services, but impervious surface cover is associated with altered growing conditions and tree performance. We quantified mean imperviousness within a neighbourhood-scale 500 m buffer and classified 128 Acer platanoides , Robinia pseudoacacia , and Tilia cordata trees across the Munich–Freising region, Germany, into four categories: mostly unsealed (MU, <25%), partially sealed (PS, 25–49%), medium sealed (MS, 50–75%), and highly sealed (HS, >75%). Structural attributes, leaf physiology, local environmental conditions, and indicators of carbon storage, habitat provision, and surface-temperature reduction were assessed. Physiological measurements from two annual campaigns enabled interannual comparison but not assessment of intra-seasonal dynamics. Mean structural attributes did not differ significantly among sealing categories, although the explanatory strength of some allometric relationships varied descriptively across the gradient. Gas-exchange patterns differed descriptively among species, categories, and sampling campaigns; however, continuous imperviousness was not significantly associated with chlorophyll content (SPAD), transpiration, or stomatal conductance in the final models. Stomatal conductance was instead associated nonlinearly with shallow soil moisture and positively with precipitation and tree size. During physiological sampling, continuous imperviousness was positively associated with air temperature, corresponding to an estimated difference of approximately 0.20 °C per 10-percentage-point increase in imperviousness, whereas shallow soil moisture, relative humidity, and vapour pressure deficit showed no significant associations. Aboveground carbon storage was related primarily to DBH and species rather than sealing category; a 10% increase in DBH corresponded to an estimated 23.4% increase in carbon storage. Model-estimated microhabitat abundance was highest at partially sealed sites and was greatest for T. cordata . Model-adjusted surface-temperature reduction was descriptively higher over asphalt than over grass, although the surface materials were analysed separately; neither sealing category nor species was significantly associated with surface-temperature reduction over either surface material. Overall, neighbourhood-scale imperviousness was not a universally dominant predictor of urban-tree performance. Structural, physiological, and ecosystem-service patterns were associated with different combinations of species, tree size, sampling conditions, and local environmental characteristics. The findings support site- and service-specific urban-tree management while treating neighbourhood imperviousness as a contextual indicator rather than a direct measure of individual-tree growing conditions.

publications.title: Coupled decline in growth and fine‐branching signals the onset of drought‐induced European beech mortality
publications.abstract: Summary Severe and recurrent droughts have caused widespread canopy decline and mortality in European forests. Drought‐induced mortality occurs when structural damage and physiological dysfunction impair a tree's ability to recover, yet it remains unclear when trees transition from reversible stress to irreversible vitality loss at the whole‐tree level. We combined detailed information on fine‐branching architecture derived from terrestrial laser scanning with radial growth data from 174 trees to assess how structural and growth decline relate to drought‐induced mortality in European beech ( Fagus sylvatica ). We found that European beech trees cross a critical tipping point under drought stress when pronounced declines in fine‐branching and radial growth occur together. Mortality probability increased sharply once relative twig length (= fine‐branching) dropped below c. 325 m m −3 and relative growth fell below c. 7%, equaling a ≥ 75% mortality probability within 3 yr, whereas neither indicator alone reliably captured this transition. Our results demonstrate that drought‐induced vitality loss in an angiosperm follows distinct trajectories but converges on a critical zone of coupled crown and growth decline that marks an ‘area of no return.’ Linking crown deterioration with growth performance provides a mechanistic early‐warning signal of irreversible vitality loss under intensifying climate extremes.
topics: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

name: Helmut Krcmar
topics: Information Systems Education and Curriculum Development

publications.title: Unpacking Path Dependence in Low-Code/No-Code Platforms: Configurations of Technical and Cognitive Dependencies
publications.abstract: This study examines how path dependence in differently configured low-code/no-code platforms unfolds. Drawing on 30 interviews across multiple LC/NC platforms, the study reveals that technical and cognitive dependencies intensify through reinforcing mechanisms such as abstraction, opacity, and specialization, while balancing practices partially counteract them. In advanced configurations, dependencies are redistributed, with technical dependencies evolving into cognitive dependencies embedded in routines and mental models. The findings advance LC/NC research by explaining how specific platform characteristics (such as visual modeling, templates, and proprietary abstractions) generate distinct technical and cognitive dependencies. We map how these characteristics interact with organizational practices to shape how developers experience and manage dependency, extending prior LC/NC research beyond adoption and productivity concerns. Second, we reshape classic assumptions in dependency theory by shifting where dependencies occur, proposing a shift from dependency on technical artifacts to a dependency on abstraction and cognitive routines.

publications.title: Hiring the right CISO: Role design and fit in cybersecurity leadership
publications.abstract: As cybersecurity threats become more complex, the chief information security officer (CISO) position has emerged as a critical yet frequently misunderstood executive role. Many organizations struggle to define what cybersecurity leadership should look like in their specific context, resulting in misaligned expectations, costly hiring decisions, and underperforming security functions. Drawing on 41 in-depth interviews with CISOs across industries and regions, this study reframes CISO selection as an organizational-design challenge rather than a search for a universally capable individual. We explain three recurring CISO sub-roles: the technical information security officer, the strategic information security officer, and the business information security officer. Each sub-role reflects a coherent alignment of reporting structure, competency profile, and strategic focus, and each is suited to different organizational conditions. Using Big Five personality assessments, we conduct an exploratory analysis of the associations among personality traits, leadership tendencies, and perceived role fit within these sub-roles. Building on this framework, the study outlines how organizations can deliberately select and design CISO roles and manage transitions between sub-roles as priorities evolve. The findings provide boards, CEOs, and hiring managers with a structured approach to aligning cybersecurity leadership with their business strategy and needs.
topics: Information Systems Education and Curriculum Development

publications.title: From questions to insights: how domain-specific semantics boost LLM access to touristic real-time occupancy data
publications.abstract: Abstract Timely access to occupancy data, combining real‑time measurements and short‑term predictions, is critical for tourism destinations to enhance visitor experiences and manage overcrowding. While this data is increasingly collected, it remains stored in complex databases that are challenging to access flexibly, particularly for large language models (LLMs), which cannot query structured sources directly. LLMs are increasingly valuable in smart tourism, offering conversational access to digital services that support both guests and staff. This paper evaluates the potential of semantic approaches to improve LLM-based access to complex occupancy databases, proposing a zero-shot prompt approach and a semantic agent that iteratively corrects queries until they execute successfully. Both rely on a multi-level tourism occupancy ontology, driving a knowledge graph that captures multiple perspectives on occupancy data, both measured and predicted, and enriched with metadata such as provenance. Evaluated on 19 realistic tourism questions, the agent achieves 42% accuracy and the simpler pipeline 37%, outperforming the evaluated leading text-to-SQL systems while reducing database load and cost. Our findings indicate that semantic guidance improves accuracy and stability in LLM-based access to structured tourism data. Theoretically, this clarifies the role of semantic abstraction, natural-language annotations, input sensitivity, and agentic behavior in query generation. Practically, these insights inform ontology engineering, constrained agent design, and efficient system architectures for LLM-driven tourism applications, such as visitor management and occupancy prediction systems.

publications.title: From regulation to orchestration: Collective action in the emergence of digital circular ecosystems
publications.abstract: Abstract Digital ecosystems are essential for enabling circular economy practices. Yet, little is known about how they emerge in segmented markets where voluntary coordination repeatedly fails, and no single actor can impose standards. This study examines the formation of a digital ecosystem through an in-depth case of the Battery Pass consortium, which developed a digital product passport in response to the European Union’s New Batteries Regulation. Based on 14 interviews across 17 organisations and an inductive case study design, we show that market-driven coordination challenges alone did not trigger ecosystem formation. Instead, regulatory enforcement created a shared imperative, while the consortium acted as an institutional facilitator by translating regulatory ambiguity into actionable standards, aligning heterogeneous actors, and fostering trust and interoperability. We identify a third pathway of ecosystem emergence, i.e. policy-catalysed, consortium-orchestrated formation, that arises when regulatory mandates intersect with fragmented markets lacking a focal orchestrator. The findings extend ecosystem emergence theory and offer guidance for policymakers and industry stakeholders in designing regulatory and collaborative structures that support transparent, trustworthy, and interoperable data-sharing infrastructures.

publications.title: Why Industrial Internet of Things Platforms Fail: A Structuration Theory Perspective on Platform Evolution
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite their transformative potential, Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) platforms often fail to evolve into scalable ecosystems. Research on IIoT platforms attributes failure to discrete factors such as governance misalignment or technological complexity and rarely considers how failure unfolds. This article adopts a structuration theory perspective to examine IIoT platform failure as a path‐dependent process. Through a seven‐year longitudinal case study of Alpha, a global industrial manufacturer, we identify four structuration mechanisms—structural embeddedness, misalignment, reproduction, and reversion—that progressively constrain platform scalability. Our findings reveal that failure is not a singular event but an emergent outcome shaped by recursive interactions between architecture, governance, and market structures, as well as strategic actions. We contribute to platform governance research by showing that IIoT platforms inherit, rather than impose, governance structures, making it crucial for firms to actively reshape contracting dependencies rather than replicating existing structures. Based on these insights, we provide recommendations for firms to design governance frameworks that foster openness, modularity, and ecosystem scalability from the outset. These insights offer a more dynamic understanding of IIoT platform evolution, informing theory and practice on overcoming the barriers to the scalability of IIoT platforms.

name: Herbert E. Spohn
topics: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

publications.title: Stochastic dynamics of quasiparticles in the hard rod gas
publications.abstract: We consider a one-dimensional gas of hard rods, one of the simplest examples of an interacting integrable model. It is well known that the hydrodynamics of such integrable models can be understood by viewing the system as a gas of quasiparticles. Here, we explore the dynamics of individual quasiparticles for a variety of initial conditions of the background gas. The mean, variance, and two-time correlations are computed exactly and lead to a picture of quasiparticles as drifting Brownian particles. For the case of a homogeneous background, we show that the motion of two tagged quasiparticles is strongly correlated, and they move like a rigid rod at late times. Apart from a microscopic derivation based on the mapping to point particles, we provide an alternate derivation which emphasizes that quasiparticle fluctuations are related to initial phase-space fluctuations, which are carried over in time by Euler scale dynamics. For the homogeneous state, we use the Brownian motion picture to develop a Dean-Kawasaki-type fluctuating hydrodynamic theory, formally having the same structure as that derived recently by Ferrari and Olla. We discuss differences with existing proposals on the hydrodynamics of hard rods and some puzzles.

publications.title: Quasiparticle Diffusion for the Toda Fluid in Equilibrium
publications.abstract: Many-body integrable systems can be understood as a gas of quasiparticles. They propagate ballistically and drive large-scale transport. However, with the exception of the hard rods system, no tools have been available to numerically track such quasiparticles. Focusing on the Toda fluid, whose integrability relies on the availability of a Lax pair, we present a numerical scheme to track quasiparticle trajectories as determined by the time-dependent eigenvectors of the Lax matrix. Simulating the Toda fluid in thermal equilibrium, this tracking scheme is used to numerical confirm Brownian motion of a quasiparticle. Simulated is also the motion of a tagged particle. Our numerical results for the diffusion constant matches with a novel TBA prediction. We believe our numerical scheme can be extended to other classical many-particle models possessing a Lax matrix.

publications.title: On the asymptotic behavior at the kinetic time of a weakly interacting Fermi gas
publications.abstract: This paper is devoted to the dynamics of a weakly interacting Fermi gas at the kinetic time regime $t\sim λ^{-2}$ where $λ\ll 1$ is the strength of the interaction potential. We prove that if the initial state is close to equilibrium, then the two-point time correlation function of the many-body quantum dynamics can be computed effectively. In fact, we show that its leading order behavior is determined completely by the collisional frequency of the Boltzmann-Nordheim collision operator at equilibrium. This settles a prediction by Lukkarinen-Spohn, and thus gives a justification of the quantum Boltzmann equation from many-body quantum mechanics.
topics: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

publications.title: The Popkov-Schütz two-lane lattice gas: universality for general jump rates
publications.abstract: Abstract We consider the asymmetric version of the Popkov-Schütz two-lane lattice gas with general jump rates, subject to the stationary measure being of product form. This leaves still five free parameters. At density 1 2 the eigenvalues of the flux Jacobian are degenerate. We compute the second order expansion of the fluxes at density 1 2 and thereby identify the universality classes.

publications.title: A Gallavotti–Cohen-Type Symmetry in the Large Deviation Functional for Stochastic Dynamics

name: Heribert Schunkert
topics: Genetics, Aging, and Longevity in Model Organisms

publications.title: Impact of glycemic status on coronary lesion characteristics in patients with symptomatic coronary artery disease
publications.abstract: Purpose This study aims to determine if higher blood sugar, even within the prediabetes range, affects coronary lesion characteristics. Material and methods Symptomatic patients with confirmed CAD on CCTA were stratified into three different groups based on their glycated-hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels: 1) Euglycemia, HbA1c below 5.7% (HbA1c < 39 mmol/mol) 2) Prediabetes, HbA1c-levels between 5.7% and 6.4% (HbA1c = 39-46 mmol/mol) 3) Diabetes, HbA1c-levels ≥6.5% (HbA1c ≥ 48 mmol/mol). A plaque analysis of culprit lesions on CCTA using a dedicated plaque analysis software was performed and findings between the three different groups were compared. Results Overall 184 patients and 247 coronary lesions were analyzed. Coronary lesion length was significantly greater in prediabetic [(29.5 mm (12.7–50-4) versus 24.8 mm (11.4–51.1), p = 0.025)] and diabetic individuals [(30.1 mm (16.7–50.2) versus 24.8 mm (11.4–51.1), p = 0.005)] compared to those with normal HbA1c levels. In terms of plaque composition and volume, diabetic individuals demonstrated a significantly higher amount of total lipid-rich plaque volume [(62.5 mm 3 (38.1–93.7) versus 41.9 mm 3 (22.4–66.7), p < 0.001] and total fibrotic plaque volume [55.7 mm 3 (37.1–92.2) versus 29.3 mm 3 (16.9–61.2), p = 0.004] compared to euglycemic patients. In multivariable adjusted logistic regression, there was a significant association between both prediabetes and diabetes and predominantly non-calcified plaques (odds ratio [OR] 2.124 [95% CI (1.016–4.437), p = 0.045 and OR 2.505 (1.029–6.098), p = 0.043]. Conclusion Poor glycemic status is associated with a higher prevalence of predominantly noncalcified plaques in symptomatic individuals. When compared to euglycemic individuals, prediabetic individuals demonstrate an extended coronary lesion length similar to diabetics. These factors may play a role in the poorer clinical outcomes even observed in patients with borderline diabetes.

publications.title: Inherited cardiovascular risk and its impact on healthspan and lifespan
Integrative Multi-Omics Reveals Distinct Molecular Signatures of Metabolic Syndrome from KORA FF4 Study
publications.abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a heterogeneous cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors whose underlying molecular heterogeneity remains incompletely understood. Methods: Targeted metabolomics (388 metabolites) and untargeted proteomics (842 proteins) were analyzed in the KORA FF4 study (n = 1921). Multivariable regression, LASSO, and Multi-Omics Factor Analysis (MOFA) were applied to identify MetS-associated signatures. As a secondary analysis, soft-clustering archetypal analysis based on 22 clinical variables was performed within the MetS subgroup (n = 582) to identify extreme clinical subphenotypes. Results: A total of 117 metabolites and 70 proteins were associated with MetS, including five metabolites and eight proteins shared across all MetS traits. Key metabolomic features comprised diacylglycerols, triglyceride score, hexoses, and branched-chain amino acids. Prominent proteins included APOC4, APOE, APOB, APOD, APOF, adiponectin, LBP, and SHBG, reflecting alterations in lipid metabolism, inflammation, and metabolic regulation. MOFA identified a latent factor strongly linked to MetS, integrating signatures of lipid metabolism, insulin resistance, and inflammation. Archetypal analysis identified extreme MetS profiles and associated with metabolites and proteins shared across all Mets. Conclusions: Integrated multi-omics analysis revealed MetS-associated molecular signatures characterized primarily by dysregulated lipid metabolism, insulin resistance, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Secondary archetypal analysis highlighted clinical heterogeneity at the extreme boundaries of MetS while supporting a shared molecular foundation. These findings highlight the value of combining clinical, metabolomics and proteomics to improve characterization of MetS heterogeneity and inform future precision risk stratification.

publications.title: Genetic differences between fibroelastic deficiency and Barlow’s disease in mitral valve prolapse
publications.abstract: AIMS: Fibroelastic deficiency (FED) and Barlow's disease represent subtypes of degenerative mitral valve prolapse (MVP). Whether these two conditions represent opposite ends of an anatomic spectrum or rather distinct etiologies remains unclear. METHODS AND RESULTS: To study this question from a genetic perspective, we conducted the first genome-wide association study (GWAS) on anatomical subtypes of MVP, exploring the MVP-Munich and MVP-France cohorts, including 1,064 FED and 821 Barlow's disease cases, and 11,923 controls. Patients were stratified via echocardiographic and surgical reports. GWAS meta-analysis was performed separately for FED and Barlow's disease. The identified risk loci were analyzed via gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), targeted variant-phenotype association analysis, and mitral valve tissue was analyzed in single-nucleus RNA-sequencing.For FED, one risk locus achieved genome-wide significance (p<5e-8) at 5q23.3 (CHSY3). For Barlow's disease, two independent loci with genome-wide significance were identified at 5q35.2 (CPLX2) and 10q26.12 (WDR11). Further 30 additional independent signals showed a suggestive association (p<5e-5) with FED, and 30 different independent signals with Barlow's disease. Targeted variant-phenotype association analysis revealed an association of FED with atrial arrhythmias, while Barlow's disease was associated with atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. In combination with GSEA, our results linked Barlow's disease to changes in cell cycle, transcription, senescence, and ubiquitination. FED was connected to cardiac, valvular, mesoderm, and endoderm development. CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests genetic heterogeneity between FED and Barlow's disease and identifies risk loci for future investigation.

publications.title: Intraindividual longitudinal changes of the proteome reveal dynamic markers of biological aging
publications.abstract: Abstract Proteomic aging clocks have emerged as biomarkers of aging, but most rely on cross-sectional data. Here, we present a proteomic aging clock based on longitudinal measurements of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry plasma proteomics at up to three time points in the population-based KORA cohort, comprising 9,105 samples from 4,100 individuals in the final dataset aged 25–88 years. The model predicts chronological age and yields a measure of proteomic age acceleration associated with lifestyle and clinical risk factors. Risk factor–stratified analyses reveal shared proteomic signatures among cardiometabolic exposures and distinct signatures for smoking and physical activity. Within individuals, dyslipidemia and impaired kidney function track transitions to increases in age acceleration, while higher age acceleration is associated with increased all-cause mortality. Mediation analysis suggests that risk factors are linked to mortality indirectly through age acceleration. Affected proteins and pathways highlight extracellular matrix remodeling, complement and coagulation pathways, and liver-derived plasma proteins as key contributors to aging. Mendelian randomization identifies proteins with evidence consistent with a causal role in aging-related traits. Together, these findings are consistent with biological aging being dynamically responsive to changes in modifiable risk factors.
topics: Genetics, Aging, and Longevity in Model Organisms

publications.title: From entrepreneurial hustle to thriving at work: the role of prior startup experience and environmental uncertainty
The Signal to Stop: Exit, Termination, and the Art of Letting Go
publications.abstract: Strategic stopping is presented as an essential mechanism for bounding failure and redirecting resources toward fruitful opportunities. This chapter explores various exit modes, including harvest sales, liquidations, and stewardship transfers. A shock often triggers the decision to stop and is heavily influenced by the entrepreneur’s internal power structures (structural, ownership, expert, and prestige). A loss of power can lead to frustration and exit. The authors discuss the attentional filter, whereby experienced entrepreneurs are more ruthless in terminating projects that lack strategic fit. Psychological barriers like escalation of commitment, the sunk-cost effect, and the stigma of failure often delay termination, leading to “creeping death”—a slow, emotionally painful descent for project members. However, this delay can facilitate anticipatory grieving and learning. Finally, the chapter advocates for a disciplined postmortem learning cycle (searching, processing, coding, practicing) to turn failure into a vital source of new knowledge.

publications.title: The Metacognitive Engine: Thinking About Thinking in High-Velocity Environments
publications.abstract: This chapter explores the metacognitive engine, a higher-order cognitive system essential for navigating volatile entrepreneurial environments. Driven by state curiosity, this engine allows entrepreneurs to act as “motivated tacticians,” consciously selecting cognitive strategies to resolve environmental ambiguity. The authors detail a structural framework comprising metacognitive knowledge (of people, tasks, and strategies) and metacognitive experience (affective conduits such as intuition). The system maintains integrity through cognitive coherence, which triggers an urge to update mental models when they conflict with external signals. Furthermore, the chapter examines how neurodiversity, specifically ADHD, impacts this engine by fostering a natural bias toward rapid action and hyperfocus. Finally, the authors discuss grounding abstract thoughts through boundary objects such as prototypes to facilitate collective sensemaking and transform private conjectures into testable public hypotheses within a community of inquiry. Mastering this internal dialogue is the prerequisite for identifying and pursuing market opportunities.

publications.title: The Entrepreneurial Compass: How Entrepreneurs Think, Decide, and Act Under Uncertainty
publications.abstract: This open access book offers a clear guide for navigating entrepreneurial uncertainty by focusing how people think, feel, and act when the stakes are high

publications.title: Developing the Social Aspects of the Venture: Prosocial Motivation, Pathways of Compassion, and Hybridity
publications.abstract: Social impact is driven by prosocial motivation to alleviate suffering through two primary pathways: sustaining ventures (providing basic survival needs) and transforming ventures (restoring autonomy and self-reliance). These initiatives typically function as hybrid organizations, balancing social welfare and commercial logics. The authors introduce hybrid intensity and hybrid relativity as key dimensions of this balance. The chapter addresses the greed paradox, in which a founding team’s greed can lead to unethical pro-organizational behavior if not tempered by trust. Scaling requires political resourcefulness, employing practices such as protective, assertive, and dialogic resourcing to shield the mission from dominant participatory partners. However, persistent effort can lead to social-venturing fatigue, manifesting as detachment from and desensitization to beneficiaries. To sustain the mission, entrepreneurs must manage target feedback loops and maintain an authentic connection to the team, transforming temporary responses into enduring organizations that restore community self-reliance.

publications.title: Switching Roles─Exploring Concentration-Dependent Agonistic versus Antagonistic Behavior of Integrin Ligands
publications.abstract: High Resolution Image Download MS PowerPoint Slide Identification of integrins as cancer targets has stimulated the development of specific inhibitory ligands. However, following cilengitide′s unexpected clinical failure by promoting angiogenesis at low concentrations, pure ligand antagonism was soon scrutinized. We evaluated αvβ3, αvβ6, or α5β1 ligands for concentration-dependent functional switches in respective integrin subtype-overexpressing cancer cells. Cilengitide (L2) or L1 provoked minor transient changes in (p)-FAK and (p)-p44/42 (erk-1/2) predominantly at low concentrations and antagonized cell migration at high concentrations, while agonistically accelerating it at low concentrations. L5 (α5β1) showed bell-shaped FAK activation at both concentrations, blocking cell migration at high concentrations only in α5β1+ OV-MZ-6 cells, not acting agonistically. L3 (αvβ6) did not alter signaling upon long exposure but transiently and early activated FAK in αvβ6+ HN cells at both concentrations, with neither antagonistic nor agonistic consequences on cell motility. These data underscore the need for in-depth evaluation of ligand actions to ensure their most promising medical use.

publications.title: Importance of integrin transmembrane helical interactions for antagonistic versus agonistic ligand behavior: Consequences for medical applications
publications.abstract: Integrins are well-characterized receptors involved in cell adhesion and signaling. With six approved drugs, they are recognized as valuable therapeutic targets. Here, we explore potential activation mechanisms that may clarify the agonist versus antagonist behavior of integrin ligands. The reorganization of the transmembrane domain (TMD) in the integrin receptor, forming homooligomers within focal adhesions, could be key to the understanding of the agonistic properties of integrin ligands at substoichiometric concentrations. This has significant implications for medical applications. While we focus on the RGD peptide-recognizing integrin subfamily, we propose that these mechanistic insights may also apply to other integrin subtypes. For application of integrin ligands in medicine it is essential to consider this mechanism and its consequences for affinity and bioavailability.

publications.title: Hypoxia-driven heterogeneous expression of α5 integrin in glioblastoma stem cells is linked to HIF-2α
publications.abstract: Despite numerous molecular targeted therapies tested in glioblastoma (GBM), no significant progress in patient survival has been achieved in the last 20 years in the overall population of GBM patients except with TTfield setup associated with the standard of care chemoradiotherapy. Therapy resistance is associated with target expression heterogeneity and plasticity between tumors and in tumor niches. We focused on α5 integrin implicated in aggressive GBM in preclinical and clinical samples. To address the characteristics of α5 integrin heterogeneity we started with patient data indicating that elevated levels of its mRNA are related to hypoxia pathways. We turned on glioma stem cells which are considered at the apex of tumor formation and recurrence but also as they localize in hypoxic niches. We demonstrated that α5 integrin expression is stem cell line dependent and is modulated positively by hypoxia in vitro. Importantly, heterogeneity of expression is conserved in in vivo stem cell-derived mice xenografts. In hypoxic niches, HIF-2α is preferentially implicated in α5 integrin expression which confers migratory capacity to GBM stem cells. Hence combining HIF-2α and α5 integrin inhibitors resulted in proliferation and migration impairment of α5 integrin expressing cells. Stabilization of HIF-2α is however not sufficient to control integrin α5 expression. Our results show that AHR (aryl hydrocarbon receptor) expression is inversely related to HIF-2α and α5 integrin expressions suggesting a functional competition between the two transcription factors. Collectively, data confirm the high heterogeneity of a GBM therapeutic target, its induction in hypoxic niches by HIF-2α and suggest a new way to attack molecularly defined GBM stem cells.

publications.title: Paper-based electrochemical device for early detection of integrin αvβ6 expressing tumors
publications.abstract: Abstract Despite progress in the prevention and diagnosis of cancer, current technologies for tumor detection present several limitations including invasiveness, toxicity, inaccuracy, lengthy testing duration and high cost. Therefore, innovative diagnostic techniques that integrate knowledge from biology, oncology, medicinal and analytical chemistry are now quickly emerging in the attempt to address these issues. Following this approach, here we developed a paper-based electrochemical device for detecting cancer-derived Small Extracellular Vesicles (S-EVs) in fluids. S-EVs were obtained from cancer cell lines known to express, at a different level, the αvβ6 integrin receptor, a well-established hallmark of numerous epithelial cancer types. The resulting biosensor turned out to recognize αvβ6-containing S-EVs down to a limit of 0.7*10 3 S-EVs/mL with a linear range up to 10 5 S-EVs /mL, and a relative standard deviation of 11%, thus it may represent a novel opportunity for αvβ6 expressing cancers detection.

publications.title: Treatment with αvβ3-integrin-specific 29P attenuates pressure-overload induced cardiac remodelling after transverse aortic constriction in mice
publications.abstract: Heart failure remains one of the largest clinical burdens globally, with little to no improvement in the development of disease-eradicating therapeutics. Integrin targeting has been used in the treatment of ocular disease and cancer, but little is known about its utility in the treatment of heart failure. Here we sought to determine whether the second generation orally available, αvβ3-specific RGD-mimetic, 29P, was cardioprotective. Male mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC) and treated with 50 μg/kg 29P or volume-matched saline as Vehicle control. At 3 weeks post-TAC, echocardiography showed that 29P treatment significantly restored cardiac function and structure indicating the protective effect of 29P treatment in this model of heart failure. Importantly, 29P treatment improved cardiac function giving improved fractional shortening, ejection fraction, heart weight and lung weight to tibia length fractions, together with partial restoration of Ace and Mme levels, as markers of the TAC insult. At a tissue level, 29P reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis, both of which are major clinical features of heart failure. RNA sequencing identified that, mechanistically, this occurred with concomitant alterations to genes involved molecular pathways associated with these processes such as metabolism, hypertrophy and basement membrane formation. Overall, targeting αvβ3 with 29P provides a novel strategy to attenuate pressure-overload induced cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis, providing a possible new approach to heart failure treatment.

publications.title: Chemical Delithiation of Ni-Rich NCM Materials: Quantification and Minimization of the Concomitant Proton Intercalation
publications.abstract: The development of advanced lithium-ion batteries requires a detailed understanding of cathode active material (CAM) properties. Chemical delithiation of CAMs enables the ex situ preparation of delithiated powders at varying degrees of delithiation, which are more amenable to detailed structural and spectroscopic analyses than materials prepared by electrochemical delithiation of electrodes. This study addresses a major drawback of chemical delithiation, namely concomitant insertion of protons. It aims to determine its origin and to modify the NO 2 BF 4 -based method such that proton insertion is minimized. Using NCM811 as a model material, the elimination of water impurities from the ambient atmosphere and the NO 2 BF 4 strongly improves agreement between targeted and measured lithium contents and lowers proton insertion. The proton content after chemical delithiation is determined via prompt gamma activation analysis (PGAA) and a novel method based on thermogravimetric analysis coupled with mass spectrometry (TGA-MS). The structure of chemically delithiated NCM811 materials is examined with X-ray diffraction (XRD) and high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (HR-STEM), including their structural evolution upon annealing, which induces oxygen release and separation into rock-salt and fully lithiated NCM811 bulk structures. Charge/discharge cycling and differential capacity analysis of strongly delithiated NCM811 show that extensive chemical delithiation can degrade particle surfaces.

publications.title: The Springback Effect in Pre-Densified Sulfidic Solid Electrolyte/Binder-Sheets and its Implication for All-Solid-State Batteries
publications.abstract: Abstract Cell components that enable high energy density, the reduction of operation pressure, and the adaptation of established production processes are important for the breakthrough of Li-ion all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Slurry-based processing, adapted from Li-ion battery technology, represents a promising production route. Although slurry-based fabrication of separators has been reported, the influence of the operation pressure on their conductivity and the effect of the mechanical properties of the polymer binder in composite separators remains elusive. Here we report a slurry-based process to obtain free-standing solid electrolyte (SE)/binder composite sheets as ASSB separators, employing different contents and types of binder. Using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, we investigate their ionic conductivity as a function of fabrication pressure (yielding different separator porosities) and operation pressure. Using a novel cell-setup approach, we quantify the conductivity loss for fully densified composite SE/binder-sheets when measured at practically relevant, reduced operation pressures, comparing it with the maximum conductivity attained at very high operation pressures. The conductivity loss is related to a “springback” effect, whereby the pressure release after fabrication leads to a volumetric expansion of the polymer phase, resulting in decreased ionic conductivity. The extent of this effect strongly depends on both the type of binder and its content.
topics: Advancements in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells

publications.title: Impact of the OER Activity and Stability of IrO 2 Anode Co–Catalysts on the Durability of Membrane Electrode Assemblies under Transient Operation Conditions of a PEM Fuel Cell
publications.abstract: IrO 2 is widely used as an anode co–catalyst in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) to mitigate cell reversal (CR) induced damages. In this study, two types of IrO 2 anode co–catalysts with different reduction resistances in H 2 atmosphere are implemented into membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) and subjected to accelerated stress tests (ASTs), combining start–up/shut–down (SUSD) and CR cycles within two protocols. Protocol 1 starts with a segment of SUSD cycles followed by a segment of CR cycles, while Protocol 2 combines SUSD and CR cycles within the same segments. Although Protocol 1 helps to isolate the performance losses induced by SUSD and CR cycles, Protocol 2 introduces a more realistic testing scenario and captures the complex interplay of concurrent degradation mechanisms. The results of Protocol 2 show that the detrimental impact of iridium dissolution from the reducible anode co–catalyst outweighs the benefit of its higher OER activity at the early stages of the AST, while the advantage of its higher OER activity becomes apparent in the later stages of the AST. This study shows that OER activity and reduction resistance are critical for benchmarking anode OER co–catalysts, with the optimal balance dictated by system–specific operating conditions.
topics: Advancements in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells

publications.title: SAFE - Thermische Sicherheitsanalytik von sulfidischen Festkörperbatterien
publications.abstract: Das SAFE-Projekt diente der Untersuchung der thermischen Stabilität sulfidischer Festkörperbatterien (SSB), um Materialkombinationen und Betriebsparameter zu identifizieren, die einen sicheren Betrieb gewährleisten. Neben der Untersuchung der Wärmeentwicklung und des Wärmetransports wurde auch die Wärmeverteilung innerhalb der Zellen modelliert. Darüber hinaus wurden Single-Layer-Pouchzellen bei verschiedenen Temperaturen betrieben und thermisch induzierte Degradationsprozesse der Komponenten analysiert. Am Lehrstuhl für Technische Elektrochemie (TEC) der TU München lag der Fokus auf der experimentellen Untersuchung der Langzeitstabilität sulfidischer SSB-Zellen in Abhängigkeit der Betriebstemperatur.

publications.title: Platinum and Gold Complexes with Unusual Oxidation States and Their Potential Role in Anticancer and Therapeutic Modalities
publications.abstract: Transition metal complexes featuring unusual oxidation states represent an exciting frontier in inorganic chemistry. This review surveys the unusual oxidation states of two biologically important metals, platinum (Pt I and Pt III ) and gold (Au II ), examining their electronic structures, bonding characteristics, and biomedical relevance, among other features. Emphasis is placed on synthetic strategies, redox behavior, and factors influencing their stability and stabilization. Pt III complexes can potentially offer an alternative to the traditional Pt II/IV anticancer chemotherapy framework and be an intermediate in Pt II/IV redox chemistry. Indeed, the Pt III -based platinum blues have been widely investigated as anticancer agents soon after the landmark discovery of cisplatin as a cancer chemotherapeutic. Au II complexes are less explored for their biological properties but may be intermediates in Au I/III redox chemistry and offer an alternative pathway to gold-based chemotherapeutics. We outline current challenges and future directions in this evolving field, where fundamental chemistry meets therapeutic innovation.

publications.title: Chemical aspects of the preparation of Vulcanised Fibre using zinc chloride hydrates: from a brief history to a new consideration of the key reactions in ionic liquids
publications.abstract: Abstract In work of the mid-19th century, it has been shown that the physical properties of cellulose and related materials are changed drastically upon their immersion in “aqueous zinc chloride solutions”, followed by washing to remove the salt and drying the resulting fabric, whose chemical composition did not change, but had a different structure. It was soon recognized that the process worked only at very high concentrations of zinc chloride, but it was only in the last decade that the “solutions” were finally identified to be in fact ionic liquids with an optimum performance for the trihydrate ZnCl2(H2O)3 which is built up of [Zn(H2O)6]2+ cations and [ZnCl4]2− anions, both in the solid state and in the melt, and which has a melting point of 6.5 °C. The production of Vulcanised Fibre has long been an important industrial process based on the treatment of cellulose with zinc chloride following established protocols. In the present paper the consequences of the ionic liquid concept for the underlying processes are discussed on the molecular level, proposing a sequence of reversible reactions, which allow the reorganization of the cellulose structure under surprisingly mild conditions. Due to its advantageous properties as a biomaterial, the all-cellulose, self-reinforced composite is currently being rediscovered for newly considered applications within several industries such as the construction industry as one example. Its strength, lightweight and plasticity present unique opportunities for architectural as well as structural applications.

publications.title: Preface
publications.abstract: Preface In the late 1990s, already close to my retirement, I was approached by my colleague and friend John Fackler Jr. of Texas A&M University with the idea to write my autobiography. At that time, John was senior editor of a series with the title Profiles in Inorganic Chemistry and had successfully recruited a number of protagonists of inorganic chemistry for the first few books in the series. I was of course honored by the offer to join these celebrities of our field of science. I promised John to give it a try and to find out if I liked to recollect all the circumstances that had led me into a life in research and teaching at universities, and that took me into positions of academic administration and science organizations, with contacts literally all over the globe. …

publications.title: Chapter 6. Technical University of Munich (TUM): the First Decade (1973–1983)
publications.abstract: Technical University of Munich (TUM): the First Decade (1973–1983). I just had signed my contract with TUM in the summer of 1973, when great things happened there: The Stockholm Nobel Committee announced that the Prize in Chemistry of this year would go to Ernst Otto Fischer and Geoffrey Wilkinson. This news not only set the spirit of the Inorganic Chemistry Institute of TUM on fire but also of the wider scientific community at TUM and elsewhere. This top honor in science of course made a big difference in the relations of TUM with officials in the State Ministry of Culture and we all benefitted from this new status. It also affected the plans for the new campus, where now with Fischer and Rudolf Mössbauer two Nobel Laureates would be installed. As the innocent newcomers from Würzburg we considered us very lucky to become also carried away by the new wave sweeping through the natural sciences institutes of TUM. …

topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Production of $$\Xi $$ and $$\Omega $$ hyperons in high-multiplicity proton–proton collisions at $$\mathbf {\sqrt{\textit{s}}}$$ = 13 TeV
publications.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the first measurements of $$\Xi $$ Ξ and $$\Omega $$ Ω hyperon yields at the highest multiplicities reached in pp collisions at $$\sqrt{s}=13$$ s = 13 TeV. This measurement exploits the high-multiplicity pp collisions collected by ALICE with dedicated triggers. The selected collisions are characterised by about 30 charged particles per unit of rapidity, over four times more than in minimum-bias pp collisions at the same centre-of-mass energy, and about twice as many as in minimum-bias p–Pb or very peripheral Pb–Pb collisions at similar energies. The production yields and average transverse momenta of the hyperons agree with trends indicated by previous measurements in pp collisions at lower multiplicities. The difference in average transverse momenta between pp and p–Pb collisions, observed with the new high-multiplicity pp data, provides additional insight into the underlying particle production mechanisms in small collision systems. The results support a strong correlation between multi-strange hadron yields and final-state multiplicity regardless of the collision system at the LHC energies, extending this observation to the highest multiplicity reached in pp collisions. The comparison with several state-of-the-art models suggests that the description of strange-hadron production is improved by recently introduced features such as interactions between overlapping strings in Pythia 8.2 with Ropes and the collective expansion of high-density string regions in EPOS4.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Measurement of the B0-meson production cross section in proton-proton collisions at $$\sqrt{s}=13.6$$ TeV
publications.abstract: A bstract This article reports the measurement of the transverse-momentum ( p T ) differential production cross section of B 0 mesons in proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of $$\sqrt{s}=13.6$$ TeV with the ALICE detector at the CERN LHC. For the first time, the B 0 production cross section is measured at midrapidity (| y | < 0 . 5) down to p T = 1 GeV /c at LHC energies. The B 0 mesons and their charge conjugates were reconstructed via the B 0 → D − π + decay channel, followed by the D − → K + π − π − decay. The measured p T -differential production cross section is described within uncertainties by state-of-the-art models based on perturbative quantum-chromodynamics calculations. Its rapidity dependence is also studied by computing the p T -differential ratios between the ALICE measurement and the one of B + mesons performed by the LHCb Collaboration at forward rapidity. The B 0 production cross section per unit of rapidity at midrapidity is $$\mathrm{d}{\sigma }^{\mathrm{B}^{0}}/{\left.\mathrm{d}y\right|}_{\left|y\right|<0.5}=24.2\pm 1.4\left(\mathrm{stat}.\right)\pm 2.6{\left(\mathrm{syst}.\right)}_{-0.3}^{+0.2}\left(\mathrm{extrap}.\right)\upmu \mathrm{b}$$ .
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Hyperon (Λ) polarization along the beam axis in Pb-Pb collisions at $$\sqrt{{s}_{\text{N}\text{N}}}=5.36$$ TeV
publications.abstract: A bstract The measurement of hyperon (Λ and $$\overline{\Lambda }$$ ) polarization along the beam axis in Pb-Pb collisions at $$\sqrt{{s}_{\text{N}\text{N}}}=5.36$$ TeV using the ALICE detector is presented. The polarization, arising from vorticity components induced by anisotropic flow, is studied relative to the second- and third-order event planes. The measured polarization exhibits clear azimuthal sine modulations, providing the first observation of polarization along the beam direction measured relative to the third-order event plane at the Large Hadron Collider. The values of the polarization measured with respect to the second-order event plane are consistent with previous measurements at $$\sqrt{{s}_{\text{N}\text{N}}}=5.02$$ TeV and show improved statistical precision owing to the larger data sample. Comparisons with hydrodynamic calculations indicate that the measured polarization is sensitive to the bulk viscosity and the vortical structure of the quark-gluon plasma, offering new constraints on its transport properties. In particular, the polarization measured relative to the third-order event plane is expected to provide an additional and independent input to constrain both bulk and shear viscosities of the quark-gluon plasma.

publications.title: Exclusive dimuon production and coherent charmonium photoproduction at forward rapidity in ultra-peripheral Pb–Pb collisions at $$\sqrt{{s}_{\text{NN}}}=5.36$$ TeV
publications.abstract: A bstract This Paper presents rapidity-differential measurements of coherent J /ψ and ψ (2S) photoproduction, as well as rapidity- and mass-differential measurements of exclusive dimuon production, in the forward rapidity region −4 < y < −2 . 5 in ultra-peripheral Pb–Pb collisions at $$\sqrt{{s}_{\text{NN}}}=5.36$$ TeV using data recorded by the ALICE detector at the LHC in 2023, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of ℒ = 1170 ± 50 μ b − 1 . The J /ψ and ψ (2S) results reveal the significant role of nuclear shadowing effects. The square root of the ratio of the measured quarkonium cross section to the impulse approximation prediction is about 0.76 for J /ψ and 0.71 for ψ (2S), at y ≈ −3, corresponding to typical Bjorken- x values of 10 − 2 . The exclusive dimuon results highlight the sensitivity of such measurements to precise modeling of the photon flux, particularly at impact parameters near the nuclear radius.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: $$\pi $$, K, and p production in high-multiplicity pp collisions at $$\mathbf {\sqrt{ s} = 13}$$ TeV
publications.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the measurement of $$\pi ^{\pm }$$ π ± , $$\text {K}^{\pm }$$ K ± , and p( $$\bar{\text {p}}$$ p ¯ ) production in high-multiplicity proton–proton collisions at $$\sqrt{s}=13$$ s = 13 TeV at midrapidity ( $$|y| < 0.5$$ | y | < 0.5 ) using the ALICE detector at the LHC. The transverse-momentum ( $$p_\textrm{T} $$ p T ) spectra of these particles are reported for three high-multiplicity classes. The results show a mass- and multiplicity-dependent hardening of the $$p_\textrm{T} $$ p T spectra and an enhancement of the p/ $$\pi $$ π ratio at intermediate $$p_\textrm{T} $$ p T . These features are similar to those observed in heavy-ion collisions, where quark–gluon plasma formation is expected. The new measurements have extended the highest average charged-particle multiplicity density per unit of pseudorapidity achieved in pp collisions, roughly a factor five higher than that in average inelastic pp collisions, thereby reducing the multiplicity gap between small and large collision systems. In addition, the results are further compared with previously published measurements and with model calculations obtained using distinct tunes of the PYTHIA 8 Monte Carlo generator, as well as with predictions from the EPOS4. The comparison of the $$p_\textrm{T}$$ p T -integrated K/ $$\pi $$ π and p/ $$\pi $$ π ratios across different collision systems and energies suggests that particle production scales with charged-particle multiplicity, rather than with collision energy or system size. While the PYTHIA 8 tunes and the EPOS4 model are able to reproduce some of these measurements, either quantitatively or qualitatively, none of them consistently describes all observed features of the data.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Increased soil organic carbon in organically managed croplands: Evidence from on-farm monitoring in Bavaria (Germany)
publications.abstract: Organic farming is widely associated with environmental benefits and is commonly assumed to promote soil organic carbon (SOC). However, it remains unclear to what extent organic farming leads to higher SOC contents under practical farming conditions. This study compares SOC contents and their temporal changes in organically and conventionally managed arable soils across Bavaria using data from the Bavarian Soil Organic Matter Monitoring Program. The dataset comprises 198 conventionally and 65 organically managed sites, all representing practical farming conditions, with repeated soil sampling after a ten-year period (initial sampling: 2001/2008; resampling: 2011/2018). SOC at resampling tended to be higher under organic management. A higher proportion of perennial grass-clover leys and other perennial forage crops and a lower share of root crops in organic crop rotations were identified as key drivers of SOC, which are intrinsic to organic agriculture but can be applied in any management system. Across all sites, SOC showed a non-significant decline of 0.74 % (16.19 to 16.07 g kg −1 ), while total nitrogen (Nt) increased significantly by 3.13 % (1.60 to 1.65 g kg −1 ). Organically managed sites exhibited a slight mean increase in SOC (+0.73 %), whereas conventionally managed sites showed a mean decrease (−1.14 %). Temporal SOC changes were further influenced by soil texture, with clay-rich soils showing slightly stronger declines or weaker increases. The increase in Nt, combined with contrasting SOC trends, resulted in a significant narrowing of the C:N-ratio across all sites (10.16 to 9.74; −4.13 %). The decline was stronger under conventional (10.14 to 9.69; −4.44 %) than organic management (10.22 to 9.95; −2.64 %). This shift may enhance SOC mineralization and increase the risk of future SOC losses. These findings highlight that results from experimental systems may not fully translate to practical farming conditions and underline the importance of long-term monitoring to develop effective, practice-oriented management strategies for maintaining or enhancing SOC stocks.

publications.title: From sink to source: long-term soil carbon trends in cropland soils under high organic matter inputs
publications.abstract: SOC in European croplands has declined over recent decades, affecting CO 2 emissions and soil functioning. A more detailed understanding of the relative contribution of agricultural management and climate change in these losses is lacking. We analyzed SOC dynamics over 29 years (1994–2023) in a long-term field experiment in Puch, Germany, comparing organic amendments (green manure, three compost types) combined with different mineral N fertilization levels. We further examine how recent climate change may have influenced SOC trajectories during the experimental period. Organic amendments significantly increased SOC content, with fine sized compost achieving the highest levels, 33% above the non-amended control, which showed the lowest SOC. High mineral N fertilization also significantly enhanced SOC content by 7–9%, though its effect (η 2 = 9.7%) remained smaller than that of organic amendments (η 2 = 68.3%), despite substantially increasing crop yield and associated crop residue C input. SOC content increased until 2012 but substantially declined in all treatments thereafter despite high C inputs from organic amendments and rising C inputs from crop residues. This decline coincided with rising temperatures and more frequent droughts at the site. RothC model configurations that explicitly accounted for climatic controls best reproduced observed SOC trajectories, suggesting that climate-related effects may have contributed to the observed SOC decline. Although compost application mitigated SOC decline on croplands, additional measures are required to fully prevent climate-induced losses. The long–term effectiveness of organic amendments depends on amendment properties and climatic conditions. This pattern raises questions about SOC accumulation under combined influences of organic matter inputs and climatic warming.

publications.title: Quantifying soil aggregate hierarchy through energy-based dispersion modelling in contrasting soil types and land uses
publications.abstract: Aggregate hierarchy, the organization by which microaggregates form progressively larger, structurally distinct macroaggregates, is central to soil stability, governing resistance to erosion and response to disturbance. However, the mechanisms and extent of hierarchical breakdown remain poorly quantified across different soil types and land management. In this study, we addressed this gap by evaluating the stepwise breakdown of soil structure into aggregates, driven by incremental sonication energy, across a range of soils differing in mineral composition and management practices. By applying a quantitative modelling framework, we derived three key parameters: the disruption constant (k₁), reflecting the rate of aggregate breakdown; the dispersion constant (k₂), which describes particle release; and the critical energy threshold (E crit ), which denotes the transition point between aggregate disruption and full particle dispersion. These parameters were used to evaluate the degree of hierarchy in aggregate breakdown, whereby higher k₁/k₂ ratios signal a pronounced stepwise (hierarchical) disintegration, and ratios near unity indicate direct dispersion into clay-sized particles. Our results indicated that soils enriched in 2:1 phyllosilicate clay minerals, such as Luvisols, exhibited markedly higher k₁/k₂ ratios in larger aggregates, demonstrating a structured, multi-step breakdown process. In contrast, oxide-rich soils like Ferralsols and Andosols typically lacked such hierarchy, dispersing rapidly into smaller fractions, which is consistent with a stronger role of mineral-mineral binding relative to organic-mediated aggregation. In the studied Luvisols, direct seeding was associated with higher stability (higher E crit ) and a greater degree of hierarchy than conventional tillage, emphasizing the synergistic effects of organic matter input and reduced disturbance on soil structural integrity. These findings highlight the mechanistic roles of distinct pedogenic groups and management practices in controlling aggregate hierarchy and stability. Our study shows that sonication-derived indicators can differentiate not only distinct pedogenic groups but also soil management. These indices can be further developed to provide a quantitative insight into the structural organization that underpins water retention, erosion resistance, and other soil functions critical for conservation.

publications.title: Enhanced Rock Weathering Affects Formation of Mineral-Associated Organic Carbon in Soil
publications.abstract: Abstract Enhanced silicate rock weathering (ERW) is increasingly considered for climate mitigation through inorganic carbon (IC) formation, yet its effects on soil organic carbon (OC) turnover remain poorly constrained and mechanistically unresolved. We investigated how the basalt weathering state influences mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM) in a 6 month microcosm incubation of a slightly acidic Cambisol. Fresh basalt (olivine-rich) and naturally weathered basalt (olivine-depleted and phyllosilicate-enriched) were applied, and 13C-labeled straw was used to trace the incorporation of plant-derived C into MAOM. Fresh basalt caused more native MAOM-C loss (∼13%) by 0.86 ± 0.29 mg of C (g of soil)−1, likely driven by pH, whereas weathered basalt caused minimal pH change and marginal native MAOM-C loss (∼0%) compared to the control. In 13C-labeled straw-amended soils, weathered basalt, characterized by a larger specific surface area and limited pH alteration, increased straw-derived new MAOM-C formation by 20% and 8.5% compared to fresh basalt and the control, respectively. These microcosm incubation results suggest that basalt weathering within 6 months of application may strongly modulate native MAOM-C loss and new MAOM-C formation. Our findings indicate that ERW can influence soil MAOM-C beyond IC sequestration, which implies the need to include MAOM-C responses in ERW carbon accounting to improve its climate mitigation potential assessments.

name: Jan Christoph Steckel
topics: Renewable energy and sustainable power systems

publications.title: Climate-Economic Country Risk Profile: Nigeria
publications.abstract: Climate mitigation and impacts are not separate spheres – they interact. Mitigation reduces climate damages, while avoided damages preserve resources for emissions reductions. Successes and failures in this nexus also affect geopolitical, geoeconomic and security risks, not least due to their capacity to shape socioeconomic fortunes. This profile focuses on Nigeria, which faces high transition and physical climate risks simultaneously.

publications.title: Climate-Economic Country Risk Profile: Indonesia
publications.abstract: The current pace of climate change has impacts that range from rising sea levels to extreme weather patterns, forcing governments around the world to grapple with two distinct types of risk: The physical risks of climate change include the potential destruction of land and infrastructure, lost productivity in the agriculture sector and the health impacts of heat stress and natural disasters. Minimising future impacts through decarbonisation, however, creates a set of transition risks as the economy adjusts to new regulations, energy systems and consumer sentiment. Managing these risks will entail mitigation measures that tackle the root causes of climate change – chiefly by reducing carbon emissions – and adaptation measures that build resilience to the impacts that can’t be avoided, such as investments in protective infrastructure.

publications.title: Exposure to Climate Policy Costs and Public Backlash: Evidence from Germany
publications.abstract: Previous research has shown that people often punish their government for climate policy when they are directly affected. Is this electoral backlash driven by a lasting shift in political attitudes? We hypothesize that people who expect economic losses from policy change revoke their support for similar policies and lose trust in political institutions deemed responsible. We test this claim for the case of Germany using a difference-in-differences design. In 2023, the government proposed an installation ban for fossil-based heating systems, which triggered a contentious public debate. Drawing on survey panel data collected before, during, and after the debate, we find that disproportionate exposure to the predicted costs of the policy had no effect on support for other climate policies. However, it caused a significant decline in willingness to pay for further climate policy and a loss of trust in government. These effects persisted even after the ban was postponed.

publications.title: The Political Consequences of Energy Price Shocks: Evidence from Germany
publications.abstract: We study the political consequences of Germany's 2022–2023 electricity price increases using four waves of original panel data. Identification exploits the German billing system, under which suppliers raise monthly instalment payments at dates plausibly exogenous to household characteristics. In a staggered difference-in-differences design with later-treated households as controls, those facing an above-median increase become 7.5 percentage points more likely to support the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD). The shift persists, and attitudes, including support for climate policy, adjust only afterwards. This response emerges even though no climate policy caused the shock, households could not anticipate it, parties at both political extremes opposed the underlying sanctions, and compensation was generous. We interpret our reduced-form results in a spatial voting framework in which the loss raises the value of a party's promise of lower future energy costs. Our results imply that the standard welfare-economic separation of efficiency from distribution can carry a political cost even when compensation is generous and non-distortionary.

name: Johannes A. Lercher
topics: Physical Organic Chemistry and Reaction Kinetics

publications.title: Molecular Origins of Solvent Effects in Cyclohexanol Dehydration on H-BEA Zeolite
publications.abstract: Abstract Solvents can substantially alter reaction rates by modifying the thermodynamic states of substrates and the free-energy landscapes of elementary steps in acid-catalyzed reactions. Cyclohexanol dehydration within BEA-type zeolite was investigated experimentally and theoretically to elucidate solvent effects on elementary steps. Adsorbed alcohol monomers and dimers were identified in acetone, cyclohexanol, 1,4-dioxane, methanol, and decalin. Hydrated hydronium ions formed in water at Brønsted acid sites (BAS), while solvents interact with protonated cyclohexanol. Kinetic H/D isotope effects (KIE) revealed solvent-dependent rate-determining steps of C–O cleavage (KIE < 2) in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin, while C–H cleavage (KIE > 2) dominates in water and methanol. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations showed that acetone induces dissociation of protonated cyclohexanol from BAS to form solvated cyclohexanol-acetone complexes, whereas 1,4-dioxane and decalin leave the alcohol bound to the framework, providing a molecular-level rationale for higher dehydration rates in acetone. Solvation in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and methanol destabilizes the initial state (excess chemical potential) by 11–13 kJ/mol, compared to 6–7 kJ/mol in water and decalin. The excess chemical potential of the transition state correlates well with the free-energy barrier of the rate-determining step. The excess chemical potential of C–O cleavage transition states in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin shows greater stabilization (−21 to −11 kJ/mol) than C–H cleavage in water and methanol (−5 to −1 kJ/mol). The combined initial-state and transition-state (de)stabilization yields reaction rates up to 3 orders of magnitude higher in acetone compared to water and decalin.
topics: Physical Organic Chemistry and Reaction Kinetics

publications.title: Integrating Enzymatic and Chemocatalytic Transformations through Shared Reaction Environments
publications.abstract: Abstract The integration of enzymatic and chemocatalytic transformations is emerging as a powerful strategy for converting renewable carbon to fuels and chemicals. By combining biocatalytic selectivity with chemocatalytic reactivity in shared reaction environments, integrated chemoenzymatic systems enable a holistic approach to biomass conversion that considers the catalyst compatibility, solvent effects, mass transport, and separation simultaneously. Ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents exemplify tunable media that function not only as solvents but also as active reaction environments by modulating the chemical potentials, water content, and catalytic coexistence. However, catalyst compatibility, mismatched operating windows, feedstock variability, product recovery, solvent recycling, and predictive design remain as major barriers to practical implementation. This Perspective highlights environment-centered design, in which catalysts, media, intermediates, and reactor operation are developed as an integrated system as a promising framework for more selective, carbon-efficient, and scalable renewable chemical manufacturing.
