publications.title: Conventional diversity metrics underestimate gut microbiome disruption under florfenicol exposure in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
publications.abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome is an integral component of fish health and growth performance and therefore represents an important production factor in aquaculture. Antibiotics are a major stressor, not only by disturbing microbial diversity, but also by altering microbial interactions involved in digestion, colonization resistance and functional redundancy. Current risk assessments, however, rely largely on diversity-based evaluations and rarely consider changes in network topology. Here, we investigated the impact of florfenicol on the gut microbiome of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) using 16S rRNA sequencing, combining conventional diversity metrics with microbial co-occurrence network modelling. While the microbial community remained overall stable at the diversity level, with treatment explaining only a minor proportion of the observed variation, network analysis revealed substantial fragmentation and a less robust network structure. Network connectivity was significantly reduced, with a near-complete turnover of central hub taxa in the florfenicol network. Our findings demonstrate that diversity-based assessments alone may substantially underestimate the extent of antibiotic-induced microbiome disturbance, with network analysis capturing changes within the community that are highly relevant for microbiome stability and would otherwise remain undetected when evaluations are restricted to diversity metrics.

publications.title: Cities cannot go green without soil microorganisms
Differential abundance and self-organizing tree algorithm clustering nominate PDGFC and TIMP3 as candidate resection-responsive plasma extracellular vesicle proteins in head and neck cancer
publications.abstract: Abstract Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) recurs in a large proportion of patients after multimodal therapy, and no circulating molecular biomarker reliably reports whether tumor-associated signals persist once the primary tumor has been removed. Because tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) accumulate in the tumor microenvironment and enter the circulation, we asked whether the plasma EV proteome changes with tumor resection and whether such changes carry functional and prognostic weight. Using quantitative proteomics and advanced integrated statistical analysis, we profiled paired plasma EVs obtained from the same patients (n = 11) at two vascular sites, peripheral and tumor-draining venous blood, at two time points, before and shortly after resection. Nine proteins were significantly more abundant in peripheral EVs before than after surgery (PDGFB, PDGFC, PPBP, TIMP3, HPSE, COL6A1, LTBP1, PF4 and PF4V1), whereas the local tumor-draining compartment showed only ENO3. Unsupervised Self-Organizing Tree Algorithm clustering independently identified a 24-protein cluster, likewise higher before resection, that converged on platelet-, collagen- and extracellular matrix receptor-related pathways. Data were verified in external patient tissue (TCGA HNSCC) using the Kaplan-Meier Plotter database, where high expression of the pairwise signature (hazard ratio (HR) 1.40, p = 0.023), the cluster signature (HR 1.72, p = 0.0043) and the two shared proteins PDGFC and TIMP3 (HR 1.43, p = 0.018) was associated with poorer 3-year overall survival. Functionally, EV size, morphology, and number were unchanged, but post-resection peripheral EVs stimulated HNSCC cell proliferation significantly less than pre-resection EVs, with no effect on non-malignant keratinocytes. These findings indicate that tumor resection depletes circulating EVs of a platelet- and matrix-associated, growth-promoting protein cargo, and identify PDGFC and TIMP3 as candidate prognostic markers that warrant validation in independent cohorts.

publications.title: Comprehensive and bias-aware analysis of small RNA NGS data for biomarker detection with caRNAge
publications.abstract: Aim: Small RNA sequencing (small RNA-Seq) is a widely used and important method for biomarker discovery in extracellular vesicles (EVs), which carry small RNAs among their cargo and protect them from degradation in liquid biopsies. However, existing computational tools for small RNA-Seq data are not tailored to EV-RNA. Methods: We present comprehensive and bias-aware analysis of small RNA gene expression (caRNAge), a biomarker discovery pipeline for small RNA-Seq data intended for users without extensive bioinformatic expertise. Ready to use as a Snakemake pipeline, caRNAge assists users in bias-aware normalization, differential gene expression analysis, and pathway over-representation analysis. Results: Possible confounding factors can be identified and corrected to maximize data comparability between experiments and biomarker robustness. caRNAge is not limited to miRNAs; it also supports the detection of miRNA isomer (isomiRs), tRNA-derived fragments (tRFs), transfer RNA (tRNAs), and other small RNA species, thereby enhancing the specificity of biomarker signatures. Specific tissues can be selected for target prediction and pathway analysis to eliminate false-positive results. All results are provided in accessible and interactive HTML reports. We provide example data for each step of the pipeline to demonstrate caRNAge’s capabilities and advantages across three EV-miRNA biomarker discovery use cases. The pipeline is not limited to EV-miRNA data but can be used for data evaluation in any small RNA-Seq experiment. Conclusion: By assisting users at every step of the discovery workflow, caRNAge fills an important gap in the field of EV-associated transcriptomic biomarker development. The pipeline is freely available at https://gitlab.lrz.de/kirchner/carnage.

publications.title: Plasma-Derived sEVs from HNSCC Patients Differentially Regulate NF-κB Signaling in Macrophages Depending on the HPV Status
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCCs) are highly immunosuppressive, and tumor-associated macrophages constitute a major component of HNSCC tumor microenvironments. Here, we investigate the effects of circulating small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) from HNSCC patients on primary macrophages, to elucidate systemic sEV-mediated immune regulation in HNSCC patients. METHODS: sEVs were isolated from plasma by size-exclusion chromatography. Internalization of PKH26-labeled sEVs was demonstrated, and mass spectrometry analysis was performed on HNSCC sEVs and sEV-treated macrophages. NF-κB activation was investigated by Western blot and p65 translocation assay. Downstream, mRNA and protein levels of cytokines and chemotaxis of T cells were investigated. RESULTS: Proteomic analysis revealed time-dependent modulation of the macrophage proteome and NF-κB signaling pathway, which was confirmed by Western blot and p65 translocation assay. sEVs from HNSCC patients negative for human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV) differentially modulated NF-κB signaling and sEV uptake mechanisms compared with sEVs from HPV-positive patients and healthy donors. CONCLUSIONS: Circulating sEVs derived from HNSCC patient plasma modulate macrophage proteomic profiles and NF-κB signaling. HPV16 status was associated with differential sEV-mediated macrophage regulation, suggesting a potential role of sEVs in systemic immune modulation in HNSCC.

publications.title: Extracellular vesicles as prognostic biomarkers: results of a neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy clinical trial in stage IIIA (N2) non-small-cell lung cancer (SAKK 16/14)
publications.abstract: The introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitors has transformed cancer therapy. In non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), immune-checkpoint blockade targeting programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) and its ligand PD-L1 has demonstrated substantial therapeutic efficacy and survival benefit. Recent evidence indicates that small extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes, play a crucial role in modulating the tumor microenvironment and immune responses, potentially influencing immunotherapy efficacy. This study investigates longitudinal EV dynamics in patients with resectable stage IIIA (N2) NSCLC undergoing multimodal therapy, including sequential neoadjuvant chemotherapy (cisplatin and docetaxel) combined with anti-PD-L1 antibody (durvalumab) immunotherapy, followed by surgery, and adjuvant durvalumab. Serum samples from the SAKK 16/14 trial were analyzed using a galectin-based EV isolation technique. EV marker expression (PD-L1, PanEV, PanCK, EpCAM, and CD45) was assessed by flow cytometry at five predefined treatment time points. Nanoparticle tracking analysis and electron microscopy confirmed successful EV isolation. Results indicated a trend toward decreasing EV-MFI values following initial therapy. In current smokers, EV-associated markers levels correlated significantly with disease progression. Importantly, elevated post-therapeutic PanEV/PanCK double-positive EV levels were significantly associated with reduced event-free survival and overall survival (p = 0.001 and p = 0.003, respectively). This study demonstrates the feasibility of longitudinal EV biomarker assessment in NSCLC and suggests that EV-based liquid biopsies may provide complementary prognostic information in the context of cancer therapy. Such approaches may be particularly informative in heterogeneous cancer stages, supporting future efforts toward personalized treatment strategies.

publications.title: Bovine Corpus Luteum Proteomics during Different Reproductive and Physiological Stages
publications.abstract: Corpus luteum (CL) is an endocrine structure that undergoes substantial changes over short intervals during the bovine reproductive (estrous) cycle. These changes are regulated by a vast array of signaling molecules, mainly proteins, that govern reproduction. We collected a comprehensive set of CLs from non-pregnant (days 1-2, 3-4, 5-7, 8-12, 13-17, and >18) and pregnant (months 1-2, 3-4, 5-6, and >7) cows, enabling a detailed characterization of temporal changes in CL biology. While previous studies have focused on a limited number of proteins, we employed a broader approach to exploring additional proteins potentially involved in CL regulation across different stages. Using high-resolution mass spectrometry (HR-LC-MS/MS), we identified approximately 3,783 individual proteins. These proteins may be useful for research in species where access to well-characterized CL tissue is limited. Our findings indicate diverse changes in protein expression across groups, highlighting proteomic patterns that may reflect key processes of bovine reproduction, particularly during the transition toward regression, a critical period that influences whether the CL is maintained to support pregnancy or undergoes regression.

publications.title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction
publications.abstract: Dysfunctional immune responses impair remyelination and contribute to neurodegeneration. While immune and metabolic responses to acute myelin injury are well characterized, myeloid cell adaptations to chronic myelin damage remain poorly understood. Here we performed a comparative analysis of genetic and toxic mouse models of acute and chronic demyelination, which identified a distinct microglial state associated with chronic demyelination, characterized by sustained pro-inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid sequestration and reduced lipid droplet formation. Transcriptomics profiling further revealed a metabolic program marked by upregulated cholesterol synthesis and diminished sterol efflux. Treatment with a desmosterol mimetic possessing 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase inhibitor activity reversed this microglial state, attenuated pro-inflammatory signaling (including C-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 4 expression), reduced myelin damage and improved motor performance in a mouse model of leukodystrophy. Our findings uncover a pro-inflammatory microglial state characterized by lysosomal dysfunction and increased myelin reactivity, highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic demyelinating disorders.

publications.title: Author Correction: T cell-mediated microglial activation triggers myelin pathology in a mouse model of amyloidosis
publications.abstract: In the version of this article initially published, the Source Data for Fig. 1h and Extended Data Fig. 10b contained values from an internal working file used to validate tracking rather than the final analysis. In addition, the Source Data files for Extended Data Figs. 2–7 retained figure labels from an earlier version of the manuscript. The affected Source Data files have been replaced, Fig. 1h has been updated, the figure labels have been corrected, and the legend of Extended Data Fig. 10 has been revised to report the correct sample sizes. These corrections do not affect the conclusions of the study. For comparison, the original Fig. 1 is available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

publications.title: The Maintenance of Dysmyelinated Small‐Diameter Axons by 14‐3‐3s in the Central Nervous System
publications.abstract: In the central nervous system, myelin formed around nerve axons by oligodendrocyte enables efficient conduction of action potentials and maintains axonal homeostasis. Therefore, in demyelinating diseases, such as multiple sclerosis (MS), axonal degeneration and loss, particularly in small-diameter axons, are observed. Teneurin-4 deficient (Ten-4 -/-) mice exhibit severe dysmyelination of small-diameter axons, but survive for over a year. Here, we aimed to elucidate the mechanism of the survival of small-diameter axons without myelin using Ten-4 -/- mice. An immunohistochemical analysis showed abnormally diffused and intense staining of neurofilament. Further, the immunohistochemical signal of nonphosphorylated neurofilament and amyloid precursor protein was higher in Ten-4 -/- mice. An electron microscopy analysis unexpectedly revealed that small-diameter axons in Ten-4 -/- mice survived at the age of 1 year, despite the absence of compact myelin. To elucidate the molecular mechanism, we performed a proteomics analysis in the Ten-4 -/- tissue by mass spectrometry. The result indicated that four of the seven 14-3-3 isoforms were highly expressed in Ten-4 -/- small-diameter axons. Finally, when the function of 14-3-3s in Ten-4 -/- mice was inhibited by 14-3-3 inhibitors, BV02 and difopein, the progression of small-diameter axon damage was observed. Altogether, 14-3-3s are among the pro-survival factors in dysmyelinated small-diameter axons. Our findings may be useful for better understanding the pathogenesis of demyelinating diseases, such as MS, as well as for the development of new treatments.

publications.title: Endothelial cannabinoid CB1 receptor deficiency reduces shear stress-induced arterial inflammation and lipid uptake
publications.abstract: Abstract Peripheral cannabinoid CB1 receptor antagonists that lack central nervous system effects are emerging as promising therapies for metabolic disease, yet the role of endothelial CB1 signaling in atherosclerosis remains unclear. Here, we show that endothelial CB1 is expressed in human atherosclerotic plaques, is induced by oscillatory shear stress in atheroprone flow regions, and promotes vascular inflammation, permeability and lipid uptake. Endothelial-specific Cnr1 deletion or peripheral CB1 antagonism in mice attenuates atherosclerosis, reduces endothelial caveolae–dependent low-density lipoprotein uptake by downregulating caveolin-1 and ALK1 expression, and improves metabolic parameters in brown and white adipose tissue and the liver. The anti-atherogenic and metabolic effects are more pronounced in females, which is possibly linked to estrogen signaling. These findings identify endothelial CB1 as a proatherogenic, sex-biased regulator of vascular lipid transport and plaque development and associated metabolic dysfunction.

publications.title: Study protocol: double-blind, randomized, prospective, placebo controlled parallel group phase II study to investigate the effect of glycerol phenylbutyrate (GPB) on neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels in patients with corticobasal syndrome (CBS)
publications.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Corticobasal syndrome (CBS) is a rare progressive neurodegenerative disorder, with no disease-modifying treatments currently available. The most common underlying pathology is a 4-repeat tauopathy. Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is a biomarker of neuronal damage and has shown potential as a measure of disease progression. Glycerol phenylbutyrate (GPB), a prodrug of phenylbutyric acid, has demonstrated potential neuroprotective properties in preclinical studies on tauopathies. This phase II clinical trial will investigate the effects of GPB on NfL levels in CBS patients. The primary objective is to assess the efficacy of GPB in reducing NfL levels over 26 weeks compared to placebo as well as safety and tolerability of GPB. Secondary objectives include evaluating changes in clinical scales. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is an investigator-initiated double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase II clinical trial, performed in two German university hospitals. A total of 32 patients with CBS will be enrolled and randomized to receive either GPB or placebo. The primary outcome is the change in NfL levels between baseline and 26 weeks as well as safety and tolerability of GPB. Secondary outcomes are changes in clinical scores. Exploratory analyses involve pharmacokinetics, changes in the metabolomic, proteomic and lipidomic profiles and imaging outcomes, such as MRI and microglia-PET. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study protocol has been approved by the lead ethics committee at LMU Munich and conforms to the ethical principles outlined in the Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines. PERSPECTIVES: If successful, this clinical trial could identify a novel therapeutic approach for slowing disease progression in CBS, contributing to a broader understanding of GPB's therapeutic potential. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The clinical trial has been registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05983588) and due to Transition in the Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS; EUCT No. 2024-516897-31-00, date of transition: 2024-09-26).

name: Mohan Manubhai Trivedi
topics: IoT and GPS-based Vehicle Safety Systems

publications.title: Safety-Critical Learning for Long-Tail Events: The TUM Traffic Accident Dataset
publications.abstract: Even though a significant amount of work has been done to increase the safety of transportation networks, accidents still occur regularly. They must be understood as an unavoidable and sporadic outcome of traffic networks. We present the TUM Traffic Accident (TUMTraf-A) dataset, a collection of real-world highway accidents. It contains ten sequences of vehicle crashes at high-speed driving with 294,924 labeled 2D and 93,012 labeled 3D boxes and track IDs within 48,144 labeled frames recorded from four roadside cameras and LiDARs at 10 Hz. The dataset contains ten object classes and is provided in the OpenLABEL format. We propose Accid3nD, an accident detection model that combines a rule-based approach with a learning-based one. Experiments and ablation studies on our dataset show the robustness of our proposed method. The dataset, model, and code are available on our project website: https://tum-traffic-dataset.github.io/tumtraf-a.

publications.title: Towards Vision Zero: The Accid3nD Dataset
publications.abstract: Even though a significant amount of work has been done to increase the safety of transportation networks, accidents still occur regularly. They must be understood as unavoidable and sporadic outcomes of traffic networks. No public dataset contains 3D annotations of real-world accidents recorded from roadside sensors. We present the Accid3nD dataset, a collection of real-world highway accidents in different weather and lighting conditions. It contains vehicle crashes at high-speed driving with 2,634,233 labeled 2D bounding boxes, instance masks, and 3D bounding boxes with track IDs. In total, the dataset contains 111,945 labeled frames recorded from four roadside cameras and LiDARs at 25 Hz. The dataset contains six object classes and is provided in the OpenLABEL format. We propose an accident detection model that combines a rule-based approach with a learning-based one. Experiments and ablation studies on our dataset show the robustness of our proposed method. The dataset, model, and code are available on our website: https://accident-dataset.github.io.

publications.title: Implementation of Smart Traffic Light Control System with Emergency Vehicle Prioritization
publications.abstract: Time plays an important role in traffic management. Traffic conditions will get worse every day, especially in emergency situations. During periods of heavy traffic, many intersections occur, making it difficult for emergency vehicles to cross the road. When a patient or someone involved in an accident needs to be transported to the hospital quickly, it is the responsibility of emergency vehicles such as ambulances to get there. Traffic congestion can cause delays in rescue operations. Emergency vehicle management is designed and developed to control emergency vehicles, how to operate traffic lights, and how to donate to emergency vehicles. Emergency vehicles are ambulances, and more. The system uses radio frequency identification (RFID) as the main tool to implement the control system. RFID tags help verify the passage of emergency vehicles according to traffic signs. The movement of emergency vehicles around the signal indicates that the signal has changed, which helps emergency vehicles pass through each intersection without wasting time on the signal. This continued until the emergency vehicles arrived at their location. All these processes occur without human intervention. The system will provide multiple outputs showing the following parameters, such as continuous readings from four ultrasonic sensors, a timer, and an emergency lane. As they are read, the system will change the signal accordingly. The timer reading is displayed in milliseconds and the ultrasonic sensor reading (i.e. distance) is displayed in centimeters.
topics: IoT and GPS-based Vehicle Safety Systems

publications.title: Language-Driven Active Learning for Diverse Open-Set 3D Object Detection
publications.abstract: Object detection is crucial for ensuring safe autonomous driving. However, data-driven approaches face challenges when encountering minority or novel objects in the 3D driving scene. In this paper, we propose VisLED, a language-driven active learning framework for diverse open-set 3D Object Detection. Our method leverages active learning techniques to query diverse and informative data samples from an unlabeled pool, enhancing the model's ability to detect underrepresented or novel objects. Specifically, we introduce the Vision-Language Embedding Diversity Querying (VisLED-Querying) algorithm, which operates in both open-world exploring and closed-world mining settings. In open-world exploring, VisLED-Querying selects data points most novel relative to existing data, while in closed-world mining, it mines novel instances of known classes. We evaluate our approach on the nuScenes dataset and demonstrate its efficiency compared to random sampling and entropy-querying methods for training 3D object detection models. Our results show that VisLED-Querying consistently outperforms random sampling and offers competitive performance compared to entropy-querying despite the latter's model-optimality, highlighting the potential of VisLED for improving object detection in autonomous driving scenarios. We make our code publicly available at https://github.com/Bjork-crypto/VisLED-Querying.

publications.title: Enhancing Highway Safety: Accident Detection on the A9 Test Stretch Using Roadside Sensors
publications.abstract: Road traffic injuries are the leading cause of death for people aged 5-29, resulting in about 1.19 million deaths each year. To reduce these fatalities, it is essential to address human errors like speeding, drunk driving, and distractions. Additionally, faster accident detection and quicker medical response can help save lives. We propose an accident detection framework that combines a rule-based approach with a learning-based one. We introduce a dataset of real-world highway accidents featuring high-speed crash sequences. It includes 294,924 labeled 2D boxes, 93,012 labeled 3D boxes, and track IDs across 48,144 frames captured at 10 Hz using four roadside cameras and LiDAR sensors. The dataset covers ten object classes and is released in the OpenLABEL format. Our experiments and analysis demonstrate the reliability of our method.

name: N. Serra
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for CP violation in D+ → ϕπ+ decays
publications.abstract: A bstract A search for charge-parity ( CP ) violation in the Cabibbo-suppressed D + → ϕπ + decay is presented, using proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 6 fb − 1 , collected at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with the LHCb detector during Run 2. An abundant sample of $$ {D}^{+}\to {K}_{\mathrm{S}}^0{\pi}^{+} $$ D + → K S 0 π + decays is employed to correct for asymmetries arising from the production of the charmed meson and from detection effects associated with the charged pion accompanying the ϕ meson. Asymmetries induced by interference of multiple processes, such as neutral kaon mixing, regeneration of neutral kaons, and interference between the Cabibbo-favoured $$ {D}^{+}\to {\overline{K}}^0{\pi}^{+} $$ D + → K ¯ 0 π + and the doubly Cabibbo-suppressed D + → K 0 π + decay, are subtracted. The direct CP asymmetry in the D + → ϕπ + decay is measured to be $$ {a}_{CP}\left({D}^{+}\to \phi {\pi}^{+}\right)=\left(0.1\pm 4.9\left(\mathrm{stat}\right)\pm 2.4\left(\mathrm{syst}\right)\right)\times {10}^{-4}. $$ a CP D + → ϕ π + = 0.1 ± 4.9 stat ± 2.4 syst × 10 − 4 . For the first time at a hadron collider, the modulus of the ratio and the relative strong phase of the D + → K 0 π + to $$ {D}^{+}\to {\overline{K}}^0{\pi}^{+} $$ D + → K ¯ 0 π + decay amplitudes are also investigated. Two-dimensional confidence intervals are reported for these parameters.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Energy-energy correlators within $Z$-tagged jets in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
publications.abstract: Energy-energy correlators probe perturbative and nonperturbative QCD regimes of jet formation through momentum-weighted angular correlations between hadrons. First measurements in light-quark-enriched jets are presented for inclusive, like-sign, and opposite-sign charged-hadron pairs, using proton-proton collisions at LHCb. The results support universality of the confinement scale for light-quark-initiated jets across collision systems and the reported transverse momentum scale of the jet. In the charge-dependent measurements, opposite-sign correlations are enhanced as angular separation decreases down to the confinement-scale region, a behavior that is well described by simulations.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Deploying Local Large Language Models for Automated Article Screening in Scientific Literature Reviews
publications.abstract: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) show promise in scientific literature reviews, but cloud-based proprietary models like GPT-4 raise concerns around privacy, copyright, and licensed article access. Using a scoping review on AI applications for treatment effect estimation as a use case, this study evaluated local open-source LLMs for automated article screening in scientific literature reviews and developed a practical workflow for their implementation. Methods We extracted a sample dataset of 300 records from an ongoing scoping review on machine learning methods for treatment effect estimation using real-world medical data. We divided the dataset into training (n = 200) and testing (n = 100) datasets. We evaluated 11 locally deployed open-source LLMs from five model families (GPT-OSS, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, Llama) for both abstract screening and full-text screening. Full-text screening was done using text converted by two PDF-to-text conversion tools: Docling and PyMuPDF4LLM. Performance was assessed using raw accuracy with 95% Wilson’s confidence interval, relaxed accuracy, Cohen’s kappa, and runtime. During workflow development, prompt engineering, output extraction strategies, and generation settings were iteratively optimized using the training dataset. Results GPT-OSS-20B achieved the highest raw accuracy for title and abstract screening (0.890 on the training set and 0.850 on the test set), followed closely by Gemma-4-31B-it (0.875 on the training set and 0.830 on the test set) and Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (0.810 on the training set and 0.790 on the test set). In full-text screening, slightly higher raw accuracy and reduced false-positive rates were observed, with GPT-OSS-20B and Gemma-4 variants consistently demonstrating strong performance. Only minor variations were found between the two PDF-to-text conversion methods evaluated, though runtime varied substantially across models. Based on these findings, we compiled a set of practical recommendations for local LLM-assisted article screening. Conclusions Local LLMs can effectively support literature screening when integrated into a carefully designed workflow. Recent generations of open-source local models achieved performance comparable to human reviewers and proprietary LLMs. Local deployment also provides advantages in data privacy, copyright compliance, customization, and cost-efficiency. While human oversight remains essential, the proposed workflow demonstrated that local LLMs represent a practical and reproducible approach for accelerating evidence synthesis.

publications.title: Measurement of the $Ω_b^-$ baryon lifetime
publications.abstract: The lifetime ratio ${r_τ\equivτ_{Ω_b^-}/τ_{Ξ_b^-}}$ between the ${Ω_b^-}$ and ${Ξ_b^-}$ baryons is measured using a sample of $pp$ collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 6 fb$^{-1}$ and collected by the LHCb experiment during LHC Run 2 (2015$-$2018). The ratio $r_τ$ is measured in two sets of decays modes, ${ {(Ω_b^-,Ξ_b^-)\to(Ω_c^0π^-,Ξ_c^0π^-)}}$ and ${(Ω_b^-,Ξ_b^-)\to(J/ψΩ^-, J/ψΞ^-)}$, with ${(Ω_c^0,Ξ_c^0)\to pK^-K^-π^+}$, ${(Ω^-,Ξ^-)\to(Λ^0 K^-,Λ^0π^-)}$, ${Λ^0\to pπ^-}$ and $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-$. The measured $r_τ$ values are averaged and combined with Run 1 (2011$-$2012) measurements in the same decay modes to obtain ${r_τ = 1.109\pm0.055\pm0.010}$. Multiplying by the known ${Ξ_b^-}$ lifetime results in the ${Ω_b^-}$ lifetime ${τ_{Ω_b^-} = 1.751\pm0.089\pm0.022~{\rm ps}}$, where the uncertainties are statistical and systematic. This measurement improves on the precision of the $Ω_b^-$ lifetime by about a factor of two over the previous world average. The value of $r_τ$ is in agreement with the most recent theoretical predictions from the heavy quark expansion framework.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Discovery of an unexpectedly light and narrow beauty-strange state
publications.abstract: As the essential building blocks of visible matter, hadrons have traditionally been classified by the quark model as mesons composed of quark-antiquark pairs and baryons built from three valence quarks. Yet, this classical picture does not account for the intricate chiral dynamics of the strong force and the emergence of exotic multi-quark hadrons. While experimental evidence for such unconventional dynamics has surfaced in the charm sector, the open-beauty system remains the long-sought frontier for testing the universality of these mechanisms. Here the observation of a new resonance in the beauty-strange sector with a global significance exceeding seven standard deviations is reported using proton-proton collision data recorded by the Large Hadron Collider beauty (LHCb) experiment at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). It exhibits a narrow natural width and a substantial mass deficit compared to the conventional quark model predictions. This result marks the first observation of a nonconventional single-beauty hadron, providing crucial insights into the chiral dynamics of the strong interaction and heavy-quark spin symmetry in the exotic domain.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

name: Nassir Navab
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

publications.title: PhenoRoute training features
publications.abstract: Precomputed evidence-channel features used to train the structured scoring head of PhenoRoute (released checkpoint v3_noicmax_nodeg.pt). Training the head on these files with the PhenoRoute code reproduces the released checkpoint (selected epoch 36, validation MRR 0.7629). Files: features_train.pt (disease ranking, 23,874 training lists), features_train_gene.pt (causal-gene ranking, 20,679 lists), features_val.pt (4,377 validation lists), features_val_gene.pt (3,850 lists), SHA256SUMS and README.md (format and usage). All patients are simulated patients from SHEPHERD (Harvard Dataverse, doi:10.7910/DVN/TZTPFL, CC0); no real patient data are included. Training uses 7,958 simulated patients, each followed by two augmented variants, and validation uses 4,377. Candidates (up to 3,000 diseases or genes per patient) were retrieved from the Monarch knowledge graph (CC BY 4.0), and channel scores use BioLORD-2023-C embeddings of HPO term names.

publications.title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models
publications.abstract: Objective: To develop a unified vision-language model for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement that addresses the mismatch between continuous measurement targets and discrete token-based numerical prediction. Methods: This article presents HAD-VLM, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework that combines autoregressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction within a shared backbone. Visual prompt tuning adapts the vision encoder to ultrasound images. A diffusion process predicts a five-component representation comprising caliper endpoint coordinates and measurement length. A post-processing strategy combining the proposed coordinate-length consistency mechanism with ensemble prediction is introduced to refine measurement estimates. We evaluate four echocardiographic measurement tasks on EchoNet-LVH, with additional assessments of medical question answering and X-ray vertebral measurement. Results: HAD-VLM achieves mean absolute errors of 1.36, 2.77, 3.05, and 1.16 mm for IVSd, LVIDd, LVIDs, and LVPWd, respectively, reducing errors by 21.4-37.6\% relative to the Vicuna-based autoregressive baseline. It also outperforms fine-tuned Qwen3-VL and direct MLP regression across all four tasks. Medical question answering performance is preserved on the evaluated dataset. For X-ray vertebral measurement, HAD-VLM reduces mean absolute error from 11.4 to 6.7 pixels. Conclusion: Integrating autoregressive language generation with diffusion-based continuous prediction improves quantitative medical image measurement while retaining prompt-conditioned task flexibility. Significance: HAD-VLM provides a unified approach to combining language interaction with anatomically grounded numerical prediction for quantitative medical image analysis.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

publications.title: From Freehand Demonstrations to Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound: An Anatomy-Anchored Learning Framework
publications.abstract: Ultrasound imaging is highly operator-dependent, motivating robotic systems that reproduce expert scanning skills consistently. These skills involve coordinated interpretation of anatomical landmarks, ultrasound images, and probe-tissue interactions that are difficult to encode in hand-designed control strategies. Imitation learning offers an alternative, but its observation and action representations should reflect the anatomically structured nature of scanning. We propose an anatomy-anchored imitation-learning framework that combines anatomy-guided probe placement with learned ultrasound navigation. The placement module identifies a task-specific anatomical starting point from external visual observations and establishes the initial probe pose as the reference frame for scanning. A flow-based policy then generates scanning motions from anchor-relative probe poses, ultrasound images, probe-mounted camera views, and contact forces, while a termination head predicts task completion. This avoids continuous reliance on third-person vision and reduces dependence on the robot-patient configuration. A handheld acquisition platform enables multimodal demonstrations to be collected during natural freehand scanning without a robot. On 16 unseen participants, task success reaches 96%, 94%, 88%, and 94% for kidney, gallbladder, and liver standard-plane acquisition and radial artery sweeping, respectively. Compared with a fine-tuned pi_0 model, success on the abdominal tasks improves by 10-42 percentage points, with lower time-to-target, peak contact force, and trajectory jerk. Ablations support the complementary roles of anatomical anchoring, egocentric vision, and force feedback. End-to-end trials with automatic placement achieve 90-100% success, and the policies transfer without retraining to a second robot with 83-100% success.

publications.title: Towards reliable morphological subtyping and cancer detection on Barrett’s esophagus pathology through ensembling foundation models
publications.abstract: The reliability of emergent histopathology foundation models (Histo-FMs) for real-world diagnostic tasks remains unproven. Given the complexity of diagnostic tasks and the challenges inherent in real-world data, we utilized Histo-FMs to investigate their utility for morphological subtyping of Barrett's esophagus (BE) and detecting esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) across the BE progression spectrum. We benchmarked Histo-FMs on the BarrettNet cohort, spanning diagnostic categories ranging from normal to EAC (N2EAC). The dataset comprised 3528 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) from 790 patients. A multi-magnification, multi-backbone aggregation of the five most expert-consistent single-scale models yielded incremental performance gains (AUROC of 0.907, F1-score of 0.696, accuracy of 0.795, and κ of 0.651 for morphological subtyping; AUROC of 0.909, F1-score of 0.836, accuracy of 0.959, and κ of 0.673 for EAC detection), with non-uniform gains across single-model comparisons and limited benefit for dysplasia. The findings support the capability of Histo-FMs for BE morphological subtyping and EAC detection in a multicenter clinical cohort, while highlighting persistent challenges in dysplasia assessment and the need for external validation. This study provides a foundation for future clinical validation.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

publications.title: Multimodal Visual Question Answering System for Survival Prognosis in PSMA-Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapy
publications.abstract: Large language models show great promise for clinical decision support but generally lack medical imaging integration. Therefore, vision–language models have been proposed, but there is little evidence on their performance, particularly compared with conventional machine learning. Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)–targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy is a well-established treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but it is still not known which patients will be good long-term responders. Therefore, this study proposes a physician-inspired visual question answering (VQA) framework that emulates the structured integration of PSMA-directed imaging and clinical data used in routine clinical assessment for overall survival prognostication. Methods: As a proof of concept, we conducted a retrospective, multicenter study across 2 academic institutions that included 110 patients with mCRPC who were treated with either [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T or [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. Our VQA approach incorporates a 3-dimensional image encoder, the domain-specific language model RadBERT, and a cross-modal transformer to process baseline and interim (after 2 cycles) PET and SPECT images, clinical data, and clinical query. The model was trained to predict 24-mo survival, and performance was compared with state-of-the-art approaches. External validation was performed with the [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 cohort. Results: The VQA model outperformed all state-of-the-art approaches while showing accuracy comparable to the query-free attention multimodal fusion model. Specifically, it achieved 81.8% accuracy (95% CI, 0.52–0.95) when integrating SPECT or PET images with prostate-specific antigen measurements. External validation of the VQA showed 71.9% accuracy (95% CI, 0.53–0.86) after few-shot fine-tuning, with further improvement over all state-of-the-art approaches in survival stratification. The VQA approach showed the closest calibration with the ground-truth survival distribution, with no significant differences observed (log-rank test, P = 0.76). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed the highest area under the curve (0.75) among the evaluated models. Together, these findings suggest that the VQA approach demonstrated adaptability across different PSMA ligands while maintaining slightly improved yet comparable overall survival prognostic performance. Conclusion: By adopting a physician-inspired assessment workflow, the VQA framework shows advantages in integrating imaging and laboratory data for clinical decision support compared with conventional machine learning. The preliminary results indicate that VQA-based approaches warrant future evaluation for survival prognostication in patients with mCRPC who are receiving PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy.

publications.title: Measurement of isolated photon plus two-jet correlations in Pb+Pb and pp collisions at 5.02 TeV with ATLAS
publications.abstract: This paper presents a measurement of photon plus two-jet events in pp and Pb+Pb collisions, i.e. events in which the transverse momentum of a single photon is balanced by two distinct jets. The measurement was performed using pp data taken in 2017 with an integrated luminosity 260 pb − 1 , and Pb+Pb data taken in 2018 with an integrated luminosity 1.72 nb − 1 , both at s NN =5.02 TeV, as recorded by the ATLAS detector. Events with photons in the transverse momentum range 90–180 GeV and at least two anti- k t R = 0.2 jets with a p T > 30 GeV are selected, and three observables are measured: x JJ γ , A JJ γ , and Δ R JJ . These observables characterise the overall energy loss of the multiparton system from medium interactions (x JJ γ ), the relative energy loss between the two colour-charge carriers (A JJ γ ), and medium-induced modifications to their opening angle (Δ R JJ ). The observables are corrected for uncorrelated combinatoric background contributions using a novel multijet mixing technique, for photon purity, and for detector resolution effects via iterative unfolding. Final results are presented per photon, and the ratio ( I AA ) is taken between measurements in Pb+Pb and pp collisions, for Pb+Pb centrality intervals of 30–80%, 10–30%, and 0–10%. Significant suppression of per photon two-jet yields in all three observables, I AA < 1, is observed as a result of parton-medium interactions. The experimental measurements are compared to three different jet quenching models: Jewel , Jetscape , and Lbt .
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for $$ t\overline{t} $$ resonances in final states with exactly one or two leptons using 140 fb−1 of pp collision data at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV with the ATLAS experiment
publications.abstract: A bstract A search for heavy spin-1 and spin-2 resonances decaying into a top-antitop-quark pair has been performed with 140 fb − 1 of proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider at a centre-of-mass energy of $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ s = 13 TeV. Final states with either exactly one electron or muon, or exactly two leptons ( ee , μμ or eμ ), large missing transverse momentum, and two jets, at least one of which must be identified as likely containing a b -hadron decay, are considered. The search targets resonances with both narrow and broad widths relative to the detector resolution, and with masses in the range of 0.4–5.0 TeV. No significant deviation from the Standard Model prediction is observed. Exclusion limits are set on the production cross-section times branching ratio for hypothetical Z′ bosons, Kaluza-Klein gravitons, and Kaluza-Klein gluons that decay into top-quark pairs.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for soft unclustered energy patterns containing muons in the final state in pp collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A bstract Soft unclustered energy patterns (SUEPs) refer to high-multiplicity, isotropic distributions of low-momentum particles that could arise in strongly-coupled hidden sector theories. A search for SUEPs whose decay products contain muons in the final state is presented using 140 fb − 1 of proton–proton collision data at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ s = 13 TeV collected by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during 2015–2018. The analysis targets SUEP signatures via gluon–gluon fusion production of a scalar mediator in Hidden Valley scenarios. No significant excess over the Standard Model expectation is observed. Exclusion limits are set on the product of the mediator production cross section and the branching fraction for its decay into a SUEP, down to 0.05 fb for a mediator mass of m S = 750 GeV, 0.4 fb for m S = 400 GeV, and 70 fb for m S = 125 GeV; the last value, when identifying the mediator with the Standard Model Higgs boson, translates to an upper limit on the branching fraction of around 0.2%.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for a leptoquark in events with a hadronically decaying τ-lepton and missing transverse momentum using pp collisions at s=13TeV with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: A search for leptoquark signals is performed in final states with a hadronically decaying τ -lepton and missing transverse momentum, using data from proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of s = 13 TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during Run 2 (2015–18), corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb − 1 . The analysis is designed to probe both resonant production and non-resonant t -channel exchange of the leptoquark, covering a wide range of coupling scenarios. No excess above the Standard Model background prediction is observed. Limits are set on the couplings in the benchmark U 1 vector-leptoquark model at 95% confidence level for masses between 1.5 TeV and 3.0 TeV.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for compressed electroweak SUSY production in final states with two $τ$-leptons in $\sqrt{s} = 13$ and $13.6$ TeV $pp$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
publications.abstract: Searches for the production of $τ$-sleptons ($\tildeτ$), charginos ($\tildeχ^{\pm}_1$), and neutralinos ($\tildeχ^0_2$) in events with at least one hadronically decaying $τ$-lepton are presented, targeting compressed mass spectra scenarios. For charginos and neutralinos, the cascade decays producing either a $τ$-slepton or a $τ$-sneutrino are considered. Two final selections are studied, requiring either one hadronically decaying $τ$-lepton and one other charged lepton, or two or more hadronically decaying $τ$-leptons. To enhance sensitivity to the compressed mass spectra, production modes with initial-state radiation (ISR) jets are considered. The searches use 140 $\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ and 53 $\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during 2015-2018 at a centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV and 2022-2023 at a centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 13.6$ TeV, respectively. The searches provide sensitivity to the compressed mass spectra scenarios with light $τ$-sleptons. The results are generally consistent with the Standard Model, although several deviations with local significances of $2.1-2.4 σ$ are observed. These deviations weaken the observed exclusion limits. For direct $τ$-slepton production, in the ISR channel alone the limits are set for $Δm(\tildeτ, \tildeχ^0_1) = 30$ GeV for $τ$-slepton masses up to $115$ GeV at 95% confidence level. Given the observed data, no exclusion limits are set for direct $τ$-sleptons production when statistically combining all considered channels. For electroweakino production, limits are set for $Δm(\tildeχ^0_2, \tildeχ^0_1) = 30$ GeV for $\tildeχ^0_2$ masses up to $200$ GeV. For pure chargino pair-production, limits are set for chargino masses up to $175$ GeV for the same mass splitting.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: IGS BDS-3 satellite antenna calibration campaign
publications.abstract: Abstract A new antenna model for BeiDou-3 satellites in medium Earth orbit (MEO) and inclined geosynchronous orbit (IGSO) is presented. This model enables consistent processing of BeiDou-3 with other GNSSs in the IGS20 reference frame and has been adopted for use within the International GNSS Service (IGS) in February 2026. The model introduces estimated phase patterns for four different blocks of BeiDou-3 satellites and provides satellite- and frequency-specific phase center offsets (PCOs) for the B1, B2, and B3 bands. B1C/B2a phase patterns and PCOs are obtained as weighted averages of individual estimates from up to nine IGS analysis centers (ACs) to minimize the dependence on AC-specific models and processing standards. In order to support users of the B1I/B3I legacy signals, satellite-specific PCOs for this linear combination have been determined by two ACs. As part of the antenna model development, temporal variations of PCOs at the few decimeter level were observed over the 2021–2024 time frame for selected satellites built by the Shanghai Engineering Center for Microsatellites (SECM), which are handled as piece-wise constant PCOs in the new IGS antenna model for the affected satellites. The new phase center model is aligned to the IGS20 reference frame and ensures consistency between GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, and BeiDou-3 in multi-GNSS processing. A precise point positioning validation of the new antenna model with B1C/B2a observations confirms a 0.11 ppb scale consistency of BeiDou-3 with the IGS20 reference frame.

publications.title: Toward a standardized GNSS satellite attitude modeling framework
Hardware-in-the-loop verification of GNSS-based orbit determination, time synchronization, and oscillator disciplining for LEO-PNT
publications.abstract: Abstract Positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services from low Earth orbit (LEO) present an important alternative or complement to established global satellite navigation systems (GNSSs). Within a LEO-PNT system, proper knowledge of the instantaneous LEO satellite position and onboard time is essential for the generation of navigation signals. Among the currently proposed LEO-PNT systems, GNSS-based onboard orbit determination and time synchronization (ODTS) is a widely considered concept for the autonomous generation of navigation signals and satellite ephemerides. To demonstrate the feasibility of autonomous real-time ODTS and assess the achievable performance, a realistic hardware-in-the-loop simulation for a LEO environment is employed. As a device under test, a miniature satellite payload developed for the ATOMIC (Autonomous Time and Orbit Determination for Micro-satellite Constellations) experiment is utilized, which involves a multi-constellation GNSS receiver, a chip-scale atomic clock (CSAC) and a micro-processor executing the GNSS-based real-time orbit determination and clock disciplining process. For maximum realism, the simulation replicates the real-world orbital dynamics of a representative LEO satellite at 1336 km altitude along with the true GPS and Galileo orbits and clocks as well as the actual broadcast navigation messages transmitted by those constellations on the day of interest. The results for a 24 h data arc show that a 3D root mean square (RMS) position error of 9.5 cm can be achieved, while the clock phase of the onboard oscillator can be synchronized to the GNSS system time scale with a precision of 1.0 ns. While the carrier-phase-based real-time ODTS enables a significantly better clock synchronization than traditional GNSS-disciplined oscillators, the achieved performance is ultimately limited by the broadcast ephemeris accuracy and the correlation between the receiver clock offset and the float-valued carrier phase ambiguities in the real-time ODTS process.

publications.title: Precise Orbit Determination of the ISS in the frame of ACES
publications.abstract: The Atomic Clock Ensemble in Space (ACES) is a European facility on the International Space Station (ISS) and consists of two atomic clocks: PHARAO and the space hydrogen maser SHM. Its purpose is to test Einstein’s theory of relativity and to allow for time transfer between continents. In addition to the atomic clocks, the facility is equipped with a geodetic grade GNSS (global navigation satellite systems) receiver for precise orbit determination (POD) to support scientific goals. GNSS based POD using a reduced dynamic approach is a well-established method. However, the accommodation on the ISS brings several challenges in contrast to GNSS receivers on satellites. This publication provides a first evaluation – still within the Commissioning Phase – of the GNSS observation quality and the current state of POD processing. It shows how the accuracy requirements can be reached despite the aforementioned limitations. An external accuracy assessment is provided using satellite laser ranging (SLR) observations.

publications.title: Performance Assessment of Onboard Time-Synchronization for LEO Satellites
publications.abstract: Future Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) systems will require accurate real-time Orbit Determination and Time Synchronization (ODTS) to meet performance and scalability demands. This paper evaluates the achievable real-time ODTS performance using flight data from three Sentinel satellites equipped with GPS/Galileo receivers. The analysis uses a ten-day dataset and assesses synchronization accuracy when relying on broadcast navigation messages and when applying Galileo High Accuracy Service (HAS) corrections, representing realistic operational conditions for future LEO-PNT architectures. Reference solutions are derived from the Navigation Support Office of the European Space Agency (ESA) Precise Orbit Determination products, aligned to Galileo System Time (GST). The results show that sub-nanosecond synchronization to GST is achievable in orbit. These findings confirm the feasibility of autonomous onboard ODTS for large-scale LEO constellations and highlight key design drivers for next-generation LEO-PNT systems.

publications.title: Measurement of the Neutrino Spectrum along the Galactic Plane with IceCube
publications.abstract: We present the first measurement of the variation of the high-energy neutrino flux along the Galactic plane using 10 years of neutrino-induced particle-shower data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. In this Letter, we fit both the neutrino flux normalization and the spectral index, in multiple regions along the plane, independent of model expectations. The neutrino flux per solid angle in the inner Galactic region ($\vert l\vert< 30^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) is approximately five times higher than in the outer Galactic plane ($\vert l\vert>60^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) at $E_ν=5\mathrm{TeV}$. The spectral indices in the inner and outer region are $γ=2.76^{+0.18}_{-0.15}$ and $γ= 3.13^{+0.57}_{-0.37}$, respectively. publications.title: Search for High-Energy Neutrinos from Infrared Flares
publications.abstract: IceCube has detected a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. While its astrophysical origin is unknown, a significant neutrino emission has been observed from the gamma-ray blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068. This suggests accretion by supermassive black holes as one of the candidate mechanisms of the diffuse neutrino flux. Indeed, external studies that made use of IceCube data identified candidate sources, including AT2019dsg, likely a stellar tidal disruption event (TDE), and AT2019fdr, associated with an active galactic nucleus (AGN). An additional study using an optically detected sample of 63 accretion flares revealed another candidate as a potential high-energy neutrino counterpart: AT2019aalc. All of these candidate transients exhibit strong dust echoes, characterized by delayed infrared (IR) emission relative to the initial optical outburst. We look for correlations between the most comprehensive catalog of infrared flares and 10 years of IceCube archival data. We perform a time-dependent stacking analysis testing 393 sources in the Northern Sky against 10 years of through-going tracks. No significant neutrino emission is observed, and we derive upper limits to constrain neutrino emission from this catalog. These limits are subsequently extrapolated to a population-level study. We find that the contribution of IR flares to the IceCube diffuse neutrino flux at 100 TeV is below 2.7% for a spectral index of 2.5.

publications.title: Planck-Scale Constraints on Quantum Gravity-Induced Neutrino Decoherence with IceCube
publications.abstract: Many quantum gravity theories predict spacetime fluctuations at the Planck scale. Neutrinos, which interact only via the weak force and gravity, propagate over long distances without losing quantum coherence. Planck-scale fluctuations would spoil that coherence, damping the flavor oscillation probability over long baselines. This makes neutrinos sensitive interferometers for Planck-scale physics. We present a search for quantum decoherence using 368,071 atmospheric neutrinos detected by IceCube in the energy range 0.5-100 TeV, an order of magnitude higher in energy than any previous decoherence search. We find no evidence for decoherence and set the strongest constraints to date on this class of neutrino decoherence models, improving on previous limits by over an order of magnitude for decoherence rate scaling as $E^2$ and $E^3$. These results exclude natural Planck-suppressed decoherence for all energy scalings $E^n$ with $0\leq n \leq 3$, the first such exclusion at the Planck scale for $n=3$.

publications.title: Newtrinos.jl: A Julia Package for Global Analysis of Neutrino Data
publications.abstract: Newtrinos.jl is an open-source Julia package for performing global analyses of neutrino data.It provides a modular, three-layer architecture that separates physics models, experiment descriptions, and statistical inference into independent modules.This allows researchers to freely combine experiments and test them against a variety of theoretical models.New experiments and physics models can be added without modifying core code.Full statistical forward models including all relevant systematic uncertainties are implemented for each experimental dataset, defining both the likelihood and the data-generating process and enabling modern statistical inference workflows.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Multiplets of IceCube alert events
1FLAT: a Firmamento-based catalog of AGN in Fermi-LAT high Galactic latitude γ-ray sources
publications.abstract: We present a systematic reassessment of 5,062 high–Galactic latitude γ-ray sources from the Fermi-LAT 4FGL-DR4 catalog using Firmamento, a web-based platform for multi-frequency source discovery and analysis. Our approach provides an independent evaluation of LAT associations by combining alternative spectral and spatial methods that integrate both recent and legacy survey data with human validation of spectral energy distributions, morphology, variability, and template-based comparisons. Firmamento confirms approximately 89% of the 4FGL/4LAC counterparts and identifies 421 new blazar associations among previously unassociated sources, reducing the fraction of unidentified extragalactic Fermi sources from 25% to 17%. We also report 64 alternative associations and 49 cases where the original identification is not confirmed. For all confirmed blazars, we provide homogeneous estimates of synchrotron peak frequency and flux based on machine-learning and template-based methods, generally consistent with previous Fermi-LAT catalogs. The main outcome of this work is the First Firmamento Catalog (1FLAT), a catalog published in the literature and available through the Firmamento platform, providing validated associations and multi-wavelength data products. The project involved extensive manual validation and benefited from active student participation, highlighting the platform’s value for both scientific research and education.

publications.title: Impact of Spectral Coverage on Parameter Recovery in Blazar Modeling
publications.abstract: Abstract Understanding the impact of spectral coverage on parameter recovery is critical for accurate interpretation of blazar spectra. In this study, we examine how the data coverage influences the reliability of parameter estimation within the one-zone synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) framework. Using OJ 287, TXS 0506+056, and Mrk 421 as representative of the low, intermediate, and high synchrotron peak (LSP, ISP, and HSP) subclasses, respectively, we generate synthetic spectral energy distributions based on their best-fit models and perform 1000 fits for each of the 21 observational configurations per source type. Our analysis quantifies the coverage probability for all model parameters, such as the magnetic field strength and the electron luminosity, and reveals that different blazar subclasses exhibit distinct sensitivities to spectral gaps. For LSPs, a minimal dataset comprising optical/UV, X-ray, and GeV γ -ray bands is sufficient for robust parameter inference. In contrast, ISPs and HSPs require broader spectral coverage to constrain the physical parameters. For ISP, we find that reliable parameter recovery can be achieved with two different minimal band combinations: (i) X-ray, high-energy (HE) γ -ray, and very HE γ -ray data, or (ii) optical/UV, X-ray, and HE γ -ray data. For HSPs, the minimal configuration enabling reliable parameter recovery includes the optical/UV, X-ray, and very high energy γ -ray bands. We discuss the role of very high energy γ -ray observations, showing that they significantly enhance parameter recovery for HSPs. Our results provide practical guidelines for designing optimized multiwavelength observation campaigns and for assessing the robustness of SSC model inferences under incomplete spectral coverage.

publications.title: Searches for Gamma-Ray Counterparts of IceCube Neutrino Events in the AGILE Public Data Archive
publications.abstract: Parallel talk presented at the XXI International Workshop on Neutrino Telescopes - Padova 29 September - 3 October 2025 (https://agenda.infn.it/event/44606/) Abstract: The search for gamma ray counterparts of IceCube neutrino events is a key item for understanding the role of blazars as possible sources of cosmic high energy neutrinos. We have searched the counterparts of IceCube neutrinos events in the AGILE gamma-ray satellite public data archive that occurred in the interval 2018-2020.We present the candidate counterpart sources in the error regions centered on the detected neutrinos and report their light curves and Spectral Energy Distributions, together with the estimates of the gamma ray flux above 100 MeV for the AGILE detections. The possible associations with blazar systems are discussed.

publications.title: 1FLAT: A Firmamento -based Catalog of Active Galactic Nuclei in Fermi-LAT High-Galactic-latitude γ -Ray Sources
publications.abstract: Abstract We present a systematic reassessment of 5062 high-Galactic-latitude γ -ray sources from the Fermi-Large Area Telescope (LAT) 4FGL-DR4 catalog using Firmamento , a web-based platform for multifrequency source discovery and analysis. Our goal is to provide an independent evaluation of LAT γ -ray source associations using alternative spectral and spatial methods that integrate both recent and legacy survey data. The evaluation is further refined through human supervision of spectral energy distributions, source morphology, flux variability, and template-based comparisons. Firmamento confirms the 4FGL-DR4 and 4LAC-DR3 counterparts or unassociated sources in 4493 cases (88.8%), demonstrating the robustness of both approaches. Beyond this general agreement, we identify 421 new blazar counterparts among previously unassociated sources, thereby reducing the fraction of unidentified extragalactic Fermi-LAT sources from 25% to 17%. In addition, in 64 cases, we find alternative blazar associations, while in 49 instances, we do not confirm the 4FGL-DR4 association. For all confirmed blazar counterparts, we provide homogeneous estimates of synchrotron peak frequency and peak flux using machine learning and template-based methods. The results agree with 4LAC-DR3 values in most cases, though significant discrepancies appear for a few dozen sources, often due to improved X-ray coverage. The primary outcome of this work is the First Firmamento LAT AGN Table, made publicly available through the Firmamento platform ( https://firmamento.nyuad.nyu.edu ), where all related multiwavelength data and images are available. The project involved extensive manual validation and benefited from the active participation of graduate and undergraduate students, highlighting the platform’s value for both research and education.

publications.title: Counterintuitive Photoresponsiveness of Thermoresponsive Polyacrylamides: Effects of Azobenzene Content and Amino Acid Spacers
publications.abstract: Abstract Four sets of dual-responsive statistical copolymers are synthesized from N,N-dimethylacrylamide and acrylamide comonomers bearing photoresponsive 4-aminoazobenzene (AzBn) side groups linked by various amino acid spacers. In aqueous solution, the copolymers exhibit lower critical solution temperature (LCST) behavior modulated by the E-to-Z photoisomerization of AzBn. Their cloud point temperatures (TCP) decrease markedly with increasing AzBn content and, at contents of 8 mol % and above, are counterintuitively lower in the—a priori—more polar-Z-state, with photoinduced shifts reaching –16 °C. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) on three exemplary copolymers support the formation of compact, spherical single-chain nanoparticles (SCNPs), ascribed to hydrophobic association of AzBn. In most cases, photoisomerization induces only modest changes in global SCNP dimensions, but substantially alters the LCST behavior. These results indicate that the AzBn content primarily determines the overall photoresponsive trend, whereas spacer-dependent differences in local chemical and steric environment further modulate the thermoresponsive behavior.

publications.title: Multifunctional CNF-Based Composite with Photochromic and Upconversion Luminescence Properties for Advanced Anticounterfeiting Applications
publications.abstract: The development of advanced security materials with multimodal optical responses is of increasing relevance for anticounterfeiting technologies. In this study, we report the successful synthesis and comprehensive characterization of a multifunctional composite based on cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) covalently functionalized with photochromic PSPA oligomers and cross-linked with upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs). Covalent grafting of PSPA onto the CNF backbone was done via Cu0-mediated radical polymerization (SET-LRP) and confirmed by spectroscopic analyses, while microscopic and structural investigations verified the homogeneous incorporation of UCNPs within the nanofibril-based hybrid gel. The resulting material combines reversible photochromic behavior under ultraviolet irradiation with near-infrared (NIR)-to-visible upconversion luminescence, enabling dual-mode optical signaling. The nanocomposite exhibited distinct and reproducible color changes upon UV exposure and characteristic luminescent emission under NIR excitation, demonstrating its suitability for advanced anticounterfeiting applications. Furthermore, the formulation as a stable, printable gel underscores its practical processability and compatibility with scalable anticounterfeiting technologies. The integration of photochromic and upconversion optical functionalities within a renewable CNF-based platform provides a robust, versatile, and sustainable approach for secure labeling and product authentication.

publications.title: Piezoelectricity-Enhanced Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution via Switching Nanofibers to a Flat Structure and Construction of a Photoconductive Interface in Kelp-Shaped Hybrid Electrospun Membranes
publications.abstract: Inspired by the efficient light-harvesting capability of kelp with a flat structure, a piezoelectricity-enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen evolution is realized by constructing kelp-shaped hybrid electrospun membranes to improve the separation efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers. During electrospinning, the addition of LiCl to the PVDF electrospinning solution triggers an inhomogeneous distribution of charges, inducing asymmetric stretching and transforming the nanofibers into a kelp-shaped structure. After that, a photoconductive polydopamine (PDA) layer is in-situ synthesized on the nanofiber surfaces. After deposition of g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets on the kelp-shaped PVDF membranes with a PDA interlayer, a second electrospun PVDF membrane with a regular round shape is coated on top to ensure the stability of g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets. The flat cross-section of PVDF nanofibers significantly enlarges the contact area between the nanofibers and g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets. The formed hydrogen bonds strengthen the interface interaction and improve conductivity. Therefore, the piezoelectric field generated by PVDF membranes can efficiently separate the photogenerated charge carriers from g-C3N4@Pt and prolong their lifetime. The hydrogen evolution is profoundly enhanced to 17,500 μmol g-1 h-1 under water flow, 11.8 times that of g-C3N4@Pt. Thus, kelp-shaped hybrid PVDF membranes are perfect for piezoelectric-photocatalytic hydrogen evolution under water flow and solar energy.

publications.title: Balancing Crystallization Kinetics and Lattice Strain Enables Thermally Stable Slot‐Die‐Coated Narrow‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT Unbalanced crystallization kinetics in mixed Sn‐Pb perovskite cause film heterogeneity and high defect densities, thereby constraining overall performance and stability, particularly under scalable processing conditions. Here, we investigate nanocrystal‐mediated crystallization regulation in ambient‐processed, slot‐die‐coated narrow‐bandgap Sn‐Pb perovskites by combining CsPbI 3 nanocrystal‐assisted processing with time‐resolved in situ grazing‐incidence wide‐angle X‐ray scattering (GIWAXS). After nine ISOS‐T‐3 thermal cycles, the perovskite solar cells (PSCs) fabricated from seeded perovskite films retain 80% of their initial efficiency at 25°C. Operando GIWAXS reveals differences in lattice evolution, residual PbI 2 formation, and microstrain accumulation between the control and nanocrystal‐assisted films. By linking scalable processing and crystallization kinetics to the subsequent lattice response under thermal cycling, this work establishes a processing, crystallization, structure, stability relationship for narrow‐bandgap Sn‐Pb perovskites and highlights the importance of controlling early‐stage film formation for thermally robust, scalable perovskite photovoltaics.
