publications.title: NumPEx position on Agentic AI for Science
publications.abstract: The emergence of Agentic AI in scientific discovery is a research policy challenge, not merely a question of adopting new tools. As international initiatives advance rapidly, France must define how these systems can strengthen scientific excellence, autonomy and trustworthy discovery. This requires strategic choices extending beyond computing power to scientific methods, software infrastructures, skills and governance, informed by independent assessment of capabilities and risks. Acting now is essential to ensure that public investment serves scientific priorities and that researchers retain control over the direction, validation and critical assessment of their work. Drawing on its expertise in scientific computing, numerical methods, scientific software and high-performance computing, the NumPEx community offers this position paper to support dialogue with public authorities, research organizations and European partners, and to help shape a coordinated national strategy for ambitious, rigorous and reproducible science with Agentic AI.

publications.title: Technological maturation of a Gigapixels Astrometry instrument for the Habitable World Observatory
publications.abstract: This paper presents the development strategy for HWO-AGATE (Accurate Guiding and Astrometry Targeting Exoearths), a high-precision relative astrometry instrument concept designed for the future Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The instrument is based on a gigapixel-class focal plane that incorporates the new generation of large-format GigaPyx CMOS sensors developed by Pyxalis. The proposed architecture relies on four 220-megapixel sensors assembled into a focal plane array and coupled with a dedicated calibration system to achieve the astrometric precision required for exoplanet detection and characterization. Preliminary study identified three major technological challenges. First, the performance of the 220-MP detectors must be validated against HWO’s astrometric requirements. Second, the development of space-qualified packaging and integration solutions is required for a multi-sensor focal plane, while addressing the electrical and thermal constraints associated with the fast readout of large-format CMOS detectors. Third, an onboard calibration data-processing architecture must be implemented to reduce the raw data volume by approximately two orders of magnitude, enabling efficient operation within spacecraft resource limits. To address these challenges, we propose a comprehensive technology maturation program based on the construction of a representative end-to-end detection chain. The demonstration setup will include a partial focal plane equipped with 220-MP sensors, front-end electronics, a dedicated processing unit, and the calibration subsystem. The objective is to demonstrate compliance with HWO-AGATE requirements and to raise the maturity of large-format CMOS detector technology to Technology Readiness Level 5 (TRL 5). Detector validation and space-qualified packaging activities are already supported through institutional funding and the French national PEPR ORIGINS program in the RETINA (Researching Exoplanets Through Imaging for Narrow-angle Astrometry) project.

publications.title: Neoadjuvant botensilimab with or without balstilimab in pMMR and dMMR colon cancer: the phase 2 UNICORN trial
publications.abstract: Preoperative immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are active in patients with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) colon cancer (CC), whereas proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) CC has been consistently considered resistant to first-generation ICIs. In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, we evaluated short-course preoperative botensilimab (BOT; multifunctional Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 monoclonal antibody) alone or in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody balstilimab (BOT + BAL) in 56 patients with resectable, locally advanced CC. Twenty-eight patients with pMMR CC were sequentially enrolled in BOT (n = 14) and BOT + BAL (n = 14) cohorts. Twenty-eight patients with dMMR CC followed the same sequential allocation strategy. The primary endpoint of centrally assessed pathological major response (pMR) rate (≤10% of residual viable tumor) was met in all cohorts, except pMMR BOT. Specifically, the pMR rate was 0% (95% confidence interval (CI): 0-23.2%) in pMMR BOT, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in pMMR BOT + BAL, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in dMMR BOT and 100% (95% CI: 76.8-100%) in dMMR BOT + BAL. Secondary endpoints included safety, quality of life, describing treatment-induced transcriptional dynamics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell dynamics, radiomics and radiogenomics features, fecal microbiota composition and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics. Eight (29%) and 15 (54%) patients treated with BOT and BOT + BAL, respectively, experienced immune-related adverse events, most commonly flu-like syndrome and diarrhea. Single-cell spatial transcriptomic analysis of matched baseline and post-treatment samples highlighted high baseline PD-L1 stromal expression and low post-treatment regulatory T cell signatures in pMMR responders, whereas dMMR responders displayed high baseline FCGR2A and FCGR3A expression on intratumoral macrophages. Clearance of ctDNA before surgery correlated with pathological response and lack of recurrence at data cutoff. Preoperative BOT + BAL elicits pathological responses in patients with pMMR or dMMR CC, supporting the combination as a promising strategy to expand ICI benefits to the early-stage setting. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05845450 .

publications.title: Microbiome-derived TOPOSCORE is associated with response to immune checkpoint inhibitor re-induction after chemotherapy in primary resistant metastatic melanoma
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains a major challenge in metastatic melanoma. The prospective multicenter PROMIT trial showed that intermittent chemotherapy could restore sensitivity to ICI re-induction in a subset of patients. We investigated whether gut microbiome ecosystem states characterized by TOPOSCORE were associated with tumor response in this setting. METHODS: In the phase II PROMIT trial (NCT04225390), 24 patients with longitudinal stool samples were included in this exploratory microbiome analysis. ICI-resistant patients received two cycles of dacarbazine followed by ICI re-induction. Stool samples underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Microbiome ecosystem states were classified into SIG1- or SIG2-associated ecosystem states using the TOPOSCORE framework, which is based on species-interacting groups (SIGs) defined by ecological co-abundance patterns. RESULTS: Baseline TOPOSCORE distributions and s-scores were not associated with clinical outcome. In the nine patients with complete BL-CTX-ICI sampling, six retained the same TOPOSCORE category throughout treatment and three changed category. Of the two patients with PR, one remained SIG2 throughout, whereas the other changed from SIG2+ to SIG1+ after chemotherapy and returned to SIG2+ during ICI re-induction. Analyses using all available samples at each phase likewise did not show significant differences in s-score among PR, SD, and PD groups. CONCLUSIONS: Baseline TOPOSCORE classification was insufficient to predict treatment outcome in this cohort. Longitudinal TOPOSCORE patterns were heterogeneous, and the small number of complete longitudinal profiles precludes conclusions that chemotherapy induced a favorable microbiome transition. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of microbiome ecosystem dynamics in larger prospective cohorts.

publications.title: Antibiotics and outcomes of cancer immunotherapy: An updated meta-analysis and clinical applications
publications.abstract: The gut microbiome is a modifiable determinant of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), positioning antibiotic exposure as a critical yet under-recognized risk factor for worse survival outcomes in immuno-oncology. As nearly 30% of ICI-treated patients receive antibiotics and indications of cancer immunotherapy are expanding, this issue represents a global challenge in oncology. Here, we paint an updated and comprehensive landscape of antibiotic exposure in immuno-oncology, provide actionable clinical recommendations, and envision future avenues for improvement. First, we describe the biological mechanisms by which antibiotic-induced dysbiosis contributes to ICI resistance. Next, through an updated meta-analysis of 116 cohorts and 97,850 cancer patients treated with ICI, we found a significant association between antibiotic exposure and survival outcomes (overall survival, hazard ratio [HR]: 1.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.34-1.65; progression-free survival, HR: 1.44, 95% CI: 1.31-1.58). Finally, we discuss antibiotics stewardship and microbiome-centered strategies to prevent, diagnose, and/or repair dysbiosis.

publications.title: Biomarkers of subclinical cholestasis predict cancer immunotherapy outcomes
publications.abstract: In a recent paper published in Cancer Cell, we identified subclinical cholestasis as an accessible imprint of gut dysbiosis predicting resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. Our work connects γ-glutamyl transferase, bile-acid remodeling, and MAdCAM-1 loss to compromised antitumor immunity, opening avenues for novel biomarker-guided microbiota interventions.

publications.title: Opposing functions of gut immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T therapy
publications.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed hematological cancer treatment, yet nearly half of patients still relapse or progress. Increasing evidence implicates the gut microbiome and antibiotic exposure as key modulators of clinical outcomes. In a cohort of 129 patients across three German centers, shotgun metagenomics and targeted mass spectrometry revealed that reduced short-chain fatty acids, particularly valeric acid, prior to CAR-T cell therapy correlated with increased risk of disease progression. Conversely, high levels of indole metabolites, including indole-3-carboxaldehyde and indole-3-acetic acid as well as the branched-chain fatty acid isovaleric acid, were linked to adverse outcomes. Functional validation in human and murine CAR-T cell models demonstrated that valeric acid supplementation enhanced, while indole-3-carboxaldehyde and isovaleric acid impaired, CAR-T cell efficacy. These findings reveal the opposing roles of immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T cell therapy, carrying significant implications for the design of metabolite-guided, microbiome-based therapeutics.

publications.title: Search for light scalar particles produced in Higgs boson decays in exclusive final states with two muons and two hadrons in proton-proton collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13 $$ TeV
publications.abstract: A bstract A search for new scalar particles of 𝒪(GeV) mass in exclusive final states with muons and light hadrons is presented. The analysis uses proton-proton collision data produced at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC in 2016–2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb − 1 . The search targets exotic decays of the Higgs boson to a pair of prompt or long-lived identical scalar particles with proper decay lengths cτ up to 100 mm and masses within the range of 0.4–2.0 GeV. This mass window corresponds to a unique parameter space where hadronic decays of these particles mostly result in a pair of light hadrons. The considered experimental signature is a collimated pair of muons and another pair of charged kaons or pions, each of which may be prompt or displaced. The analysis improves the sensitivity to very light scalar boson masses and demonstrates a novel approach to probe hadronic decays of light scalar bosons. Upper limits on the branching fraction of the Higgs boson to scalar bosons at the level of 𝒪(10 − 4 ) are obtained for several scalar boson masses between 0.4 and 2.0 GeV, with proper decay lengths of up to ∼ 1 mm.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Search for long-lived particles decaying into muons in proton-proton collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13.6 $$ TeV using data scouting
publications.abstract: A bstract A search for long-lived particles decaying into muons is performed using proton-proton collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13.6 $$ s = 13.6 TeV, collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC in 2022 and 2023, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb − 1 . The data were collected using dedicated dimuon triggers with low transverse momentum thresholds, recorded with a high-rate data scouting trigger stream. This data stream retains a reduced amount of information at the high-level trigger, to explore otherwise inaccessible phase space at low multimuon invariant mass and nonzero displacement from the primary interaction vertex. No significant excess of events above the standard model prediction is found. Upper limits on branching fractions at 95% confidence level are set for a wide range of mass and lifetime hypotheses in several beyond the standard model frameworks, where the Higgs boson decays into long-lived dark photons or into dark partons that produce showers containing long-lived particles, or where a long-lived scalar resonance is produced from the decay of a b hadron. The resulting constraints improve and extend existing ones in large regions of the parameter space.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
publications.abstract: Abstract Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at √ s = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb -1 . Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high p T . The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

publications.title: Precision luminosity measurement in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with the CMS detector at the Large Hadron Collider
publications.abstract: Discovering new fundamental physics requires spotting subtle deviations between theoretical predictions and experimental data. This delicate comparison hinges on the precise knowledge of the integrated luminosity, the measure of how many particle interactions were actually delivered by the collider. Here, we report a landmark measurement of the integrated luminosity by the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment for proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV at the CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC). By calibrating multiple independent monitors through specialized beam-separation techniques and rigorously validating their long-term stability against well-understood Z boson production rates, we comprehensively map and minimize systematic uncertainties. Combining the findings yields a total integrated luminosity precision of 0.73% for the entire data set. This marks the most precise luminosity measurement ever achieved at a bunched-beam hadron collider. Crossing the sub-percent precision threshold per data taking year fundamentally sharpens our ability to test the standard model and establishes a vital baseline for the upcoming High-Luminosity LHC era.

publications.title: Search for pair production of additional neutral scalars within the Inert Doublet Model in a final state with two electrons or two muons in proton-proton collisions at $$\sqrt{s}=13$$ TeV and 13.6 TeV
publications.abstract: A bstract A first dedicated search for pair production of new scalars predicted by the Inert Doublet Model is performed using proton-proton collisions. Data were collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC at $$\sqrt{s}=13$$ TeV and 13.6 TeV, corresponding to integrated luminosities of 138 fb − 1 and 35 fb − 1 , respectively. Within this model, four additional scalar bosons (H, A, H + , and H − ) are predicted. Through an additional discrete symmetry, the lightest new scalar, H, is stable, rendering it a viable dark matter candidate. These candidates can originate from quark-antiquark annihilation producing an offshell Z boson that decays to a pair of the new scalars. The target final state consists of exactly two opposite-charge same-flavour leptons (electrons or muons), with missing transverse momentum due to the stable neutral scalars, and very little hadronic activity. A parameterised neural network is used to separate the signal from the standard model background. No significant excess of events is observed. Exclusion limits at 95% confidence level are set on the production cross section of the two new neutral scalars, H and A, expressed in terms of their masses, m H and m A , in the m H vs. m A − m H plane. The observed (expected) exclusion region reaches m H = 108 (106) GeV for m A − m H = 78 (76) GeV and at m H = 70 GeV, covers the range of m A − m H = 40–90 (35–90) GeV.

publications.title: First measurements of vector boson scattering in W±W± and WZ production in all-leptonic final states at $$ \sqrt{s}=13.6 $$ TeV
publications.abstract: A bstract The production cross sections of W ± W ± and WZ boson pairs in association with two jets in proton-proton collisions are measured at $$ \sqrt{s}=13.6 $$ s = 13.6 TeV. The data sample corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 171 fb − 1 , collected with the CMS detector during 2022–2024. The measurements are performed in the leptonic decay modes: W ± Z → ℓ ± νℓ′ ± ℓ′ ∓ and W ± W ± → ℓ ± νℓ′ ± ν , where ℓ , ℓ′ = e or μ . The electroweak productions of W ± W ± and WZ bosons are each observed with a significance greater than five standard deviations from the background-only hypothesis. Differential fiducial cross sections as functions of several observables are also measured.

publications.title: Non-volatile Orbital magnetoelectric effect in a two-dimensional electron gas
publications.abstract: Electrical control of orbital magnetism is a central goal of orbitronics. While current-induced orbital polarization has recently been demonstrated in inversion-asymmetric systems, nonvolatile electrical control of an equilibrium orbital moment has remained elusive. Here, using x-ray absorption spectroscopy with \textit{in situ} electric-field control of the FE polarization, we demonstrate non-volatile switching of the equilibrium orbital magnetization of the oxide q2DEGs formed at the LaAlO$_3$/EuTiO$_3$/Ca-STO (001) interface. X-ray linear dichroism reveals a reversible modulation, driven by the FE-polarization direction, of the Ti-3$d$ crystal-field splitting and orbital occupancy, establishing a ferroelectric-like metallic state. X-ray magnetic circular dichroism shows a polarization-controlled switching of the Eu$^{2+}$ orbital magnetic moment induced by the orbital magnetization of the q2DEG projected onto Eu-5$d$ states and detected at the Eu-$M_{4,5}$ edge through Eu-5$d$/Eu-4$f$ hybridization in the inversion-symmetry-broken interface. These results provide spectroscopic evidence of ferroelectric control of orbital magnetism in an oxide q2DEG.

publications.title: Site-Selective Electronic Structure and Dynamical Softness in the Metallic Antiferromagnet Mn3CuN
publications.abstract: Electronic structure, local bonding, and magnetic order are intimately coupled in correlated antiperovskites, making it challenging to distinguish the contributions of individual crystallographic sites to their collective properties. Here, we combine element-specific X-ray spectroscopy, temperature-dependent X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, electrical transport measurements, and first-principles calculations to investigate the site-selective electronic structure of epitaxial metallic antiferromagnetic Mn3CuN thin films. We reveal an anomalous charge distribution characterized by effective low-valent Mn and subvalent Cu states stabilized by covalent Mn-N-Cu interactions. While the Mn sublattice forms a robust noncollinear antiferromagnetic framework below ∼120 K, the electronically distinct Cu sites remain magnetically inactive yet exhibit pronounced temperature-dependent local structural evolution. Despite the onset of magnetic ordering, Mn3CuN retains metallic transport with a near-zero temperature coefficient of resistivity (NZ-TCR), indicating minimal coupling between magnetic ordering and charge transport. These findings demonstrate that site-selective electronic structure enables chemically differentiated lattice dynamics while preserving a robust magnetic framework, establishing Mn3CuN antiperovskite in which electronic, structural, and magnetic responses can be selectively decoupled. This work provides a materials design principle for engineering multifunctional metallic antiperovskites through site-selective electronic structure and local chemical bonding.

publications.title: Applied spintronics: From spin transport to spin-charge interconversion and emerging devices
publications.abstract: Spintronics exploits the electron's spin degree of freedom to go beyond the capabilities of conventional charge-based electronics. Since the discovery of giant magnetoresistance, the field has evolved from the study of spin-polarized transport in ferromagnets to a broader framework encompassing spin-orbit coupling, collective spin dynamics, and electric-field control of magnetic states. In this Review, we discuss the physical mechanisms that underpin modern applied spintronics, with particular emphasis on spin-charge interconversion, magnetoresistive effects, and the electrical detection and manipulation of collective spin phenomena. We examine how spin currents, spin-orbit torques, and voltage-controlled magnetic properties enable efficient control of magnetization and magnetic excitations in nanoscale devices. These mechanisms form the basis of key technologies such as magnetic sensors and magnetic random-access memory (MRAM) while also opening pathways toward emerging architectures including racetrack memories, spin-based logic, and unconventional computing. By highlighting common principles across materials platforms and device concepts, we provide a perspective on the current state of spintronics and outline promising directions for future spin-based electronics.

publications.title: Slow structures, fast degrees of freedom, and the morphology of chess openings
publications.abstract: Chess openings naturally separate into slow and fast degrees of freedom: pawns evolve through irreversible moves, whereas pieces can be rapidly reorganized within the resulting structure. We exploit this separation to construct a quantitative morphology of opening space. From a catalogue of 3810 named variations, 1749 reach a common depth of $N=10$ plies, corresponding to 619 distinct positions and only 435 joint pawn structures. We characterize these positions through observables measuring pawn commitment and spatial organization, blockade and tension, and piece activity and centralization. Their partial independence reveals a multidimensional opening space and in order to explore its structural organization, we construct a network whose nodes are distinct White pawn structures, connected when a single pawn move or capture transforms one into another. Remarkably, 139 of the 149 observed structures belong to a single connected component containing $98\%$ of all positions. This network exhibits a statistically significant modular organization, with eight communities whose representative structures correspond to familiar pawn formations. Rather than forming isolated categories, these formations emerge as distinct regions of a connected structural landscape. Our approach thus complements the traditional opening taxonomy by revealing similarities between differently named openings and providing a quantitative basis for comparing the positions they produce.

publications.title: Urban scaling and the dynamics of individual cities
Social Physics: A manifesto
publications.abstract: Social Physics seeks quantitative, empirically testable explanations of collective human behavior. Its name has a long and contested history, but its contemporary program is neither the claim that society is literally a physical system nor an attempt to replace the social sciences with physics. It is an interdisciplinary practice: observation and experimentation, model construction, mathematical and computational analysis, and repeated confrontation with data. The field has been transformed by analyzing digital traces, network science, agent-based modeling, large-scale experiments, and the capacity to study coupled dynamics across economic, social, technological, biological, and physical layers. We review advances in financial analysis and modeling; economic complexity; the structure and evolution of social networks; spreading, opinion, and information dynamics; inequality, cooperation, conflict, mobility, cities, culture, science, and collective behavior; and the emerging study of human-AI ecosystems. Across these domains, common features recur - heterogeneity, interaction, feedback, adaptation, non-equilibrium dynamics, multiscale organization, and emergent collective outcomes. We also confront the limitations that have arisen in this field: convenience samples, platform dependence, weak causal identification, over-universal claims, insufficient engagement with meaning and institutions, privacy risks, and the danger that predictive models become instruments of manipulation. We propose a future Social Physics organized around theory - data reciprocity; causal and generative explanation; measurement validity and cross-context generalization; responsible, participatory data governance; genuinely interdisciplinary collaboration; and reflexive study of interventions and algorithms that alter the systems being observed.
topics: Complex Systems and Time Series Analysis

publications.title: Bearings communities algorithm
publications.abstract: This notebook splits a street network into bearings communities — connected sets of intersections sharing the same local street orientation — and measures how ordered the resulting mosaic is. The language is borrowed from condensed matter: a bearings community is a grain, the streets separating two grains form a grain boundary, and a city sits somewhere between a single crystal (one grid) and a polycrystal (many mutually rotated grids). For more details please see the companion paper: Geometry of Urban Order Marc Barthelemy & Geoff Boeing https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13029

publications.title: Geometry of Urban Order
publications.abstract: Urban street networks are modeled as spatial graphs whose geometry reflects planning, history, and physical constraints. Global orientation measures describe the overall order of a city but do not reveal how street directions form coherent neighborhoods. Here we introduce bearings communities---spatially connected domains whose streets share a common orientation---and analyze them using concepts from the physics of polycrystalline materials. Across $1025$ large cities worldwide, these domains are almost perfectly ordered: their mean coherence is $0.964$ and varies by only $1.4\%$ from one city to the next, far above the value expected for randomly oriented streets. Every city is therefore a mosaic of well-ordered orientational grains, differing only in their number, size, and mutual alignment. Because the grains are equally regular everywhere, a city's global order is set mainly by how many of them it averages over: a city appears ordered because it is built from a few large grains, not because its fabric is locally more regular. A null model in which grain orientations are randomized confirms this grain-counting mechanism. Finally, the interface fraction $γ$ measures how strongly domains interlock, yielding a morphology diagram that organizes cities continuously between grid-like, polycrystalline, and fragmented limits.

publications.title: From two pressures to three: reconstructing mean, systolic, and diastolic pulmonary arterial pressures in pulmonary hypertension
publications.abstract: Background Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) defines pulmonary hypertension (PH) and underpins hemodynamic classification. mPAP is time averaged during right heart catheterization. In echocardiographic studies, systolic and diastolic pressures (sPAP and dPAP) are frequently reported, and the conventional formula mPAP ≈ dPAP+0.33×pulse pressure (PP) is widely used, although its 0.33 form factor was not specifically calibrated for PH. The geometric formula mPAP ≈ √(sPAP×dPAP) has also been proposed. Whether these formulas and their rearrangements can accurately reconstruct a pressure component missing from a hemodynamic dataset when the other two are available remains uncertain. Methods This analysis included invasive hemodynamic data from 336 patients with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension, post-capillary PH, and chronic thromboembolic PH. mPAP, sPAP, and dPAP were compared with values estimated using the conventional 0.33 formula, a cohort-derived recalibrated 0.37 formula based on the observed form factor, and the geometric formula. Results Measured mPAP was 41.2±10.3 mmHg. The 0.33 formula underestimated mPAP (mean bias −1.6±2.6 mmHg) and, when rearranged, overestimated sPAP (+4.8±7.8 mmHg) and dPAP (+2.4±3.9 mmHg). The 0.37 formula reduced all three mean biases to <1 mmHg while preserving precision. The geometric formula closely estimated measured mPAP (mean bias +0.1±3.0 mmHg). For both the 0.37 and geometric formulas, mPAP estimation performance was not materially altered by PH phenotype, age, sex, PP, heart rate, stroke volume, PA stiffness, or resistance. Conclusions In PH, form factor recalibration to 0.37 improved mPAP estimation and pressure-set consistency and may support missing-value estimation. The geometric relationship was confirmed and provides a parameter-free framework for physiological interpretation.

publications.title: Circulating Activin A, FSTL3 and BMP9 in asymptomatic BMPR2 pathogenic-variant carriers
publications.abstract: Extract Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by distal pulmonary arteriolar remodelling with a progressive rise in pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction, and, in the absence of effective therapy, premature death [1]. Pathogenic variants in the BMPR2 gene, which encodes bone morphogenetic protein receptor type II (BMPR-II) represent the most common genetic predisposition to heritable PAH [2]. Beyond BMPR2, overactivation of the pro-proliferative TGF-#x03B2;–activin–nodal axis plays a pivotal role in driving obstructive vascular remodelling in PAH pathogenesis.

publications.title: Characteristics of patients with isolated anti-Ku antibodies
Anti-annexin A5 Autoantibodies in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Related to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection (HIV-PAH): A Case-Control Study
publications.abstract: Autoantibody profiles in HIV-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (HIV-PAH) remain poorly characterized. Using a validated proteomic pipeline (two-dimensional immunoblot, mass spectrometry, ELISA), we compared 20 HIV-PAH patients with 20 HIV controls without PAH. Anti-annexin A5 (AnxA5) autoantibodies were present in 55% of HIV-PAH patients versus 0% of controls (P < .001) and anti-14-3-3ε in 35% versus 5% (P = .04), despite comparable HIV duration, CD4 counts, and virological control. Both remained associated with PAH after adjustment for coinfections. These autoantibodies mirror those described in connective-tissue-disease-PAH, suggesting a possible overlap in autoimmune features and a research biomarker warranting prospective validation.

publications.title: Estimating mean pulmonary arterial pressure in the machine learning era
publications.abstract: Extract We read with great interest the article by Shams et al. [1] describing an artificial intelligence-based workflow to extract pulmonary haemodynamic variables from right heart catheterisation reports and reconstruct missing mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) values. This issue is of major interest because accurate assessment of mPAP is central to the diagnosis, haemodynamic classification and follow-up of pulmonary hypertension.

publications.title: Electromagnetic Information Theory for Programmable Metasurfaces
publications.abstract: Programmable metasurfaces enable fine-grained control of electromagnetic waves and are creating new opportunities for information extraction, information transfer and information processing. Yet, despite exciting experimental demonstrations, their fundamental capabilities remain poorly understood. In this Perspective, we argue that programmable metasurfaces, and programmable wave systems more generally, call for an electromagnetic information theory that addresses limits at two levels, in a unified manner across applications like communications, sensing and computing. First, for a given physical platform, such a theory should bound achievable information manipulations, such as sensing precision, information-transfer rates, and computational performance. Second, at a more fundamental level, it should determine what non-programmable and programmable physical resources bound these system-specific limits, and what minimum resources are required to attain a prescribed level of performance. We discuss emerging theoretical approaches to these questions, and their connection to experimentally realizable systems. We examine how device thickness, programmable degrees of freedom, nonlocality, coupling and multiple scattering constrain these limits. Establishing the envisioned framework could clarify the ultimate capabilities of programmable metasurfaces and guide the design of future wave-based information systems.

publications.title: TRP-UE Bistatic Sensing for 6G Performance Analysis and Insights
publications.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) equips cellular networks with the dual capability of data transmission and environmental sensing by sharing spectrum, waveforms, and radio hardware. While network-side sensing via transmission-reception points (TRPs) has been widely investigated, the use of user equipment (UEs) as sensing receivers introduces additional bistatic viewpoints and can improve target observability. UE-assisted operation is nevertheless constrained by small UE apertures and by waveform processing, especially when data-bearing communication signals are reused for sensing. The present paper investigates theoretical limits and operating conditions for UE-assisted passive target positioning, with emphasis on hybrid operation that fuses TRP--TRP and TRP--UE measurements. A unified OFDM-based signal-and-noise model is developed to cover both positioning reference signals (PRS) and communication waveform reuse with modulation-dependent noise enhancement. Based on this model, closed-form Fisher-information expressions and Cramer-Rao lower bounds are derived for delay and angular parameters and are mapped to positioning error bounds (PEBs) for two estimator classes: time-angle positioning based on TDOA + DoA and delay-only 3D ellipsoid positioning based on excess-delay/TDOA measurements. Monte-Carlo simulations across reference SNR, subcarrier spacing and occupied bandwidth, modulation order, radar cross section (RCS), sensing mode, and positioning algorithm identify regimes where UE participation and hybrid sensing provide significant gains and quantify the associated estimator-to-bound trade-offs.

publications.title: Performance Evaluation of Mobile Target Sensing and Tracking Across Multiple Sensing Modes
publications.abstract: Moving extended-target sensing and tracking are studied in a beamformed PRS/OFDM ISAC framework. The target is modeled as a rigid cluster of scatterers whose Tx--target--Rx echoes coherently combine in a MIMO scattering channel. Delay, azimuth/elevation, and Doppler are estimated using PRS matched filtering with delay centroiding, single-cluster 2D-MUSIC, and FFT-based Doppler estimation, then used for independent localization and EKF-based tracking. The framework is evaluated in monostatic and bistatic modes under target-directed, receiver-directed, and omnidirectional beamforming. Simulation results show that EKF tracking reduces the aggregate 3D RMSE from 1.61 m to 1.38 m relative to independent localization. Target-directed beamforming substantially improves tracking accuracy, achieving 1.38 m RMSE compared with 5.91 m and 8.38 m for omnidirectional and receiver-directed beamforming, respectively. The results highlight the importance of target-aware beam management, delay-angle-Doppler fusion, and sensing geometry for mobile-target tracking in ISAC networks.
topics: Target Tracking and Data Fusion in Sensor Networks

publications.title: Efficient Alternating Optimization for Hybrid Digital-Wave Beamforming in SIM-Assisted Cell-Free Massive MIMO
publications.abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) have recently emerged as a promising architecture for large-scale beamforming systems, including cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO), due to their cost-effective wave-domain signal processing capabilities. However, existing algorithms for the joint optimization of digital and SIM-enabled wave-domain beamforming typically incur prohibitive computational complexity. In this work, we propose an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm for weighted sum-rate maximization in SIM-assisted CF-mMIMO systems employing hybrid digital-wave beamforming. Unlike prior approaches that rely on general-purpose optimization solvers or per-element gradient ascent methods, the proposed algorithm updates the digital and wave-domain beamforming variables on a per-access point (AP) or per-SIM-layer basis, enabling closed-form updates at each step. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm reduces the computational complexity by more than 99\% compared to existing algorithms while achieving nearly identical sum-rate performance.

publications.title: Impact of Phase Noise and Power Amplifier Nonlinearity on Realistic ISAC Networks from 3.5 GHz to 60 GHz
publications.abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems impose more stringent requirements than communication only systems. They require absolute phase coherence across the OFDM frame for reliable Doppler and angle estimation. They further rely on sub-sample timing precision to achieve fine range resolution. Additionally, ISAC systems demand a high dynamic range to detect weak targets in the presence of strong reflections. In this study, we evaluate and characterise the impact of two of the most prominent hardware limitations, Local Oscillator (LO) Phase Noise and Power Amplifier (PA) nonlinearity on ISAC performance across five significant frequency bands (FR1 3.5 GHz New Radio (NR), outdoor 6 GHz WiFi 7, future 15 GHz cellular, FR2 26 GHz NR, and outdoor 60 GHz Wireless Gigabit (WiGig)). The simulation results quantify the extent impairment severity increases with operating frequency and illustrate the resulting trade-offs between communication reliability and sensing accuracy. Furthermore, the results identify, for each frequency band, the operational conditions under which both communication and sensing can successfully coexist and simultaneously satisfy their respective Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

publications.title: CONSTANCES, the French nationwide population cohort: major accomplishments
publications.abstract: The CONSTANCES cohort is an epidemiological research infrastructure accessible to the international epidemiologic research community (doi.org/ https://doi.org/10.13143/inserm_constances ). CONSTANCES also provides public health authorities with data regarding prevalence of numerous health conditions and determinants among the French population. CONSTANCES comprises a representative sample of about 220,000 French adults aged 18-69 at enrolment (7.6% participation rate). Follow-up begins at enrolment and is intended to last for the lifetimes of study participants. At inclusion, the selected subjects completed questionnaires and underwent a comprehensive health examination. A biobank was established. The follow-up includes a yearly self-administered questionnaire, and a health examination every four years. Social and health data are collected continually from French national administrative databases. The data collected cover a wide spectrum of somatic and mental health disorders, social and demographic characteristics, socioeconomic status, life events, behaviors, environmental and occupational factors. In order to estimate prevalences that are unbiased by non-participation, weighting methods based on data from national administrative databases were developed. The CONSTANCES research infrastructure is open to legitimate researchers from any country, on any topic for which a sound research project is proposed, and for which certain ethical conditions are met. Up to 2025, over 200 projects have been conducted and more than 250 papers have been published; the numbers are expected to grow as the participants age. Highlighting the broad scope of CONSTANCES data collection, already published papers pertain to many health research fields, such as chronic diseases, aging, women's health, environmental and occupational risks or research methods.

publications.title: Global and regional reference curves for pain across the lifespan in 6.1 million individuals in 118 countries
publications.abstract: Pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide, yet no harmonized self-reported reference framework exists to characterize how its burden is distributed across the lifespan and world regions. In this study, we harmonized individual-level self-reported pain data from 6,125,459 participants across 902 population-based data sources in 118 countries to establish global reference trajectories of pain. We implemented these trajectories in an open-access benchmarking platform for positioning external datasets against global pain norms. Pain prevalence ranged from roughly 2% for facial pain to 40% for back pain, was consistently higher in women across all 11 anatomical sites (risk ratio range: 1.08-1.83) and increased most steeply before age 55 years. Contrary to existing estimates that generally project higher prevalence of pain conditions in higher Human Development Index (HDI) regions, we found that individuals in the lowest HDI countries experienced a substantially higher late-life prevalence of any bodily pain than those in the highest (risk difference: 30.6 percentage points (95% confidence interval: 26.9-34.3)), with low back pain approaching twice the prevalence at the oldest ages. Globally, 18.3% of pain burden across anatomical sites was attributable to three modifiable risk factors (smoking, obesity and low income), but this varied from 12.6% in sub-Saharan Africa to 27.1% in eastern Europe, indicating that the factors underlying pain in lower-HDI settings remain poorly characterized. Together, these reference trajectories provide a common framework for defining and comparing pain burden and informing more equitable global surveillance and prevention.

publications.title: Lifetime exposure to atypical working hours among healthcare professionals compared with the workforce in other sectors: Nationwide cohort study
publications.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite well-documented health risks, cumulative exposure to atypical working hours (AWH) over a career remains poorly quantified, especially among healthcare workers. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare career-long AWH exposure among healthcare professionals and other occupational groups in France. METHODS: We analysed 2013-2017 data from the French nationwide CONSTANCES cohort, including participants aged 18-69 with job histories. The longest-held occupation was identified using cumulative job duration. Weighted prevalence estimates of six AWH were calculated, accounting for sampling design and non-response. RESULTS: A total of 95,827 participants were included. Overall, 63.9% [95% CI, 63.5-64.4] of the workforce experienced at least one AWH, including weekend (37.3% [36.8-37.7]), long working hours (31.3% [30.8-31.7]), extreme shift (29.8% [29.4-30.3]), alternating or irregular schedules (21.5% [21.1-21.9]), night work (11.7% [11.4-12.0]) and insufficient weekly rest (26.4% [25.9-26.8]). Healthcare professionals represented 5.7% [5.4-6.1] of the sample: among them, nurses showed the highest prevalence of exposure to at least one AWH (94.1% [92.9-95.1]) and were mostly exposed to alternating, irregular or extreme shift schedules, weekend and night work, while physicians (85.1% [81.9-87.8]) were particularly exposed to long working hours and insufficient rest. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first nationwide estimates of career-long exposure to multiple AWH across the French workforce. Healthcare professionals experienced the highest burden of AWH structurally. By leveraging occupational histories and calibrated survey weights, our approach reduces the underestimation inherent in "current job" assessments and supports prevention policies targeting structural scheduling constraints in healthcare.

publications.title: Author Correction: Obesity rise plateaus in developed nations and accelerates in developing nations
publications.abstract: In the version of the article initially published, María Elena Díaz-Sánchez, Patricia Varona-Pérez and Ramón Suárez-Medina (all affiliated with the National Institute of Hygiene, Epidemiology and Microbiology, Havana, Cuba) were inadvertently omitted from the list of NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC) members and have now been added in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

publications.title: POPGEN: building a reference panel of local ancestry to study genetic variability across metropolitan France
publications.abstract: Abstract Understanding the fine-scale genetic structure of human populations is essential for both demographical history and genomic medicine. The POPGEN project was initiated as part of the France Genomic Medicine Initiative to construct a whole-genome reference panel representative of the ancestral genetic diversity that existed across metropolitan France at the beginning of the 20th century. Building on previous studies that reported significant fine-scale population structure within France, POPGEN aimed to improve geographic coverage and generate regional allele frequency data to support medical and population genetics applications. We recruited 15,000 participants from the largest French population-based cohort, CONSTANCES, based on the birthplace proximity of their four grandparents and sent saliva kits at their homes. The high return rate (68.3%) demonstrates feasibility of large-scale self-sampling in the general population. Genotyping data from the 9,772 samples that could be processed confirm the presence of widespread fine-scale structure across France, and extend this finding to previously underrepresented regions. These results highlight the value of recruitment strategies based on grandparents’ origin for capturing subtle genetic structure. The development of sampling strategies that best capture genetic diversity at the finest scales will indeed be essential to characterize population structure across Europe and to enable more accurate analyses in medical genetics, especially when addressing rare variant interpretation and fine-scale ancestry adjustment for association tests and polygenic scores calibration. The thorough description of our recruitment strategy would provide useful insights for other initiatives like the Genome of Europe (GoE) project, which aims to generate whole-genome references encompassing European diversity.

publications.title: Human iPSC-derived liver organoid model multicellular tissue responses and therapeutic rescue in Wolman disease
publications.abstract: Abstract Wolman disease (WD), the severe infantile form of lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) deficiency, is a rare metabolic disorder caused by inactivating mutations in the LIPA gene. Although WD is characterized by profound hepatic dysfunction, experimental human systems capable of modeling multicellular liver pathology and supporting therapeutic testing remain limited. Here, we generated an isogenic human model of WD by introducing LIPA loss-of-function mutations into induced pluripotent stem cells and differentiating them into multicellular human liver organoids (HLOs). LIPA-deficient HLOs preserved hepatic lineage specification while recapitulating key biochemical and cellular features of WD, including loss of LAL activity, lysosomal expansion, lipid accumulation, and activation of inflammatory and fibrogenic programs. Single-cell RNA sequencing resolved cell-type-specific disease states across hepatocyte-, stromal-, and biliary-like populations, revealing the emergence of a reactive biliary program consistent with ductular reaction (DR), a complex tissue response associated with chronic liver injury. Importantly, this reactive biliary phenotype was supported by targeted gene-expression analysis in WD liver organoids and independently validated in liver tissue from mouse models and WD patients. Isolated LIPA-deficient cholangiocyte organoids failed to reproduce the DR-associated program, indicating that this response depends on multicellular interactions within the hepatic microenvironment rather than on biliary cell-autonomous dysfunction alone. Consistently, hepatocyte-directed AAV-mediated restoration of LIPA expression attenuated metabolic stress, inflammatory and fibrogenic programs and suppressed ductular reaction both in organoids and in vivo. Together, these findings establish multicellular human liver organoids as a physiologically relevant platform for modeling emergent tissue-level responses in WD and for evaluating therapeutic rescue strategies in a human context.

2.65eP CRISPR activation of utrophin as a mutation-independent approach for Duchenne muscular dystrophy therapy
SP10 Mutation-independent upregulation of utrophin through CRISPR-based strategies for Duchenne muscular dystrophy

RADIOCARBON DATING ON ECHOMICADAS, LSCE, GIF-SUR-YVETTE, FRANCE: NEW AND UPDATED CHEMICAL PROCEDURES
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT The Laboratoire des Sciences du Climat et de l’Environnement (LSCE) has operated a radiocarbon dating laboratory for almost 70 years. It has evolved from a traditional ß-decay counting to an accelerator mass spectrometry facility. In 2015, the LSCE received a major upgrade with the installation of a MICADAS. This evolution required adjustments in sample preparation to match the new capability to date samples as small as a few tens of µgC. We summarize here the sample cleaning procedures and the chemical purification or extraction treatment that we apply to the samples. We also report values of blank and reference materials of different matrices that match the large diversity of samples handled at LSCE.

publications.title: Late Quaternary deglaciation of Prince William Sound, Alaska
publications.abstract: Abstract To understand the timing of deglaciation of the northernmost marine-terminating glaciers of the Cordilleran Ice Sheet (CIS), we obtained 2610Be surface-exposure ages from glacially scoured bedrock surfaces in Prince William Sound (PWS), Alaska. We sampled six elevation transects between sea level and 620 m and spanning a distance of 14 to 70 km along ice flow paths. Most transect age–elevation patterns could not be explained by a simple model of thinning ice; the patterns provide evidence for lingering ice cover and possible inheritance. A reliable set of 20 ages ranges between 17.4 ± 2.0 and 11.6 ± 2.8 ka and indicates ice receded from northwestern PWS around 14.3 ± 1.6 ka, thinned at a rate of ~120–160 m/ka, and retreated from sea-level sites at 12.9 ± 1.1 ka at a rate of 20 m/yr. The retreat rate likely slowed as glaciers retreated into northern PWS. These results are consistent with the growing body of reported deglacial constraints on collapse of ice sheets along the Alaska margin indicating collapse of the CIS soon after 17 ka. These data are consistent with paleotemperature data indicating that a warming North Pacific Ocean caused catastrophic collapse of this part of the CIS.

publications.title: Near-Field Channel Estimation via Deep Unfolding for Extremely Large-Scale Antenna Arrays
publications.abstract: The Extremely Large-scale Antenna Array (ELAA) has been envisioned as a promising candidate to meet the ambitious demands of 6G. However, this evolution also brings about two primary limitations: high computational complexity caused by large-scale arrays and inherent operation in the near-field region. To address these issues, this work exploits the sparsity of near-field channels in the polar domain and formulates channel estimation as a compressed sensing (CS) problem, thereby enabling estimation with reduced pilot overhead. In particular, we propose a guideline to design a sparsifying codebook for the near-field channel, which is strictly based on a target coherence value. Building on this, we develop a deep unfolding architecture, derived from the iterative solver ISTA, with a hybrid loss, namely Hybrid LISTA. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed codebook, with comparable complexity, still exhibits improved estimation performance and greater coverage in the near-field region. Moreover, our unfolded model with the hybrid loss consistently delivers better recovery performance over existing estimation schemes.

publications.title: Leveraging Quantum Measurement Randomness for Shot-Efficient Diffusion Models
publications.abstract: In quantum computing, the readout always carries finite-shot sampling noise. Suppressing this noise through repeated measurements raises the cost of a quantum neural network (QNN). Meanwhile, a stochastic diffusion sampler deliberately adds randomness at each reverse (generation) step. This paper turns the measurement noise from a liability into a resource. Specifically, we use the noise quantum measurement produces anyway to replace part of the noise the sampler would otherwise inject. We characterize the measurement error as multinomial sampling noise propagated through a trainable linear readout. To connect the circuit's Born probabilities to the denoising task, we further formulate the diffusion process on a bounded zero-sum hyperplane mapped to the probability simplex. Therefore, we can employ a compensation noise to match the mean and covariance of the shot-noise-free linear update under some minimum shot conditions. Solving this condition for the shot count gives a state-dependent adaptive budget. For the denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM), this budget increases as the sampler becomes more deterministic. On an eight-dimensional Gaussian mixture, the schedule achieves comparable generation quality with $303$ shots per sample against a high-shot reference of $1.6\times10^{6}$, about $5300\times$ fewer. Latent diffusion experiments on MNIST further validate the proposed mechanism for generation in a learned latent space.
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

publications.title: Fluid Antenna Systems for ISAC Design: A Survey
publications.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) introduce dynamic positional degrees of freedom (DoFs), extending the spatial domain from a static and discrete resource to a quasi-continuous and reconfigurable design space. This spatial flexibility provides an effective means of alleviating the geometric rigidity and functional conflicts that constrain integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Against this backdrop, we provide a comprehensive overview of FAS-enabled ISAC, tracing the evolution from theoretical performance limits to practical transceiver architectures. To illustrate the surveyed design evolution, we further propose the fluid antenna multi-mode modulation (FA-MM) framework as a representative case study of multidimensional physical-layer design for FAS-ISAC. Finally, several open challenges are discussed, with emphasis on predictive sensing, adaptive coordination, and secure spatial-state management in future FAS-ISAC systems.

publications.title: An Efficient SIM Beamforming Scheme Based on Physical-Empowered Projected Gradient
publications.abstract: Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) have emerged as a promising technology for next-generation wireless systems. Especially in multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems, it has the potential to realize complicated wave-domain transformations with low hardware costs and energy consumption. However, SIM-assisted MIMO systems face two major challenges in channel estimation and beamforming. As the SIM elements do not have the signal processing capability, channel estimation can only be conducted in an indirect manner, which makes it challenging. Moreover, the precoding optimization after channel estimation is non-convex and also difficult. Targeting these issues, we exploit the time-division duplex (TDD) channel reciprocity to calculate the gradient backpropagation in an over-the-air manner. Based on this structure, we propose a gradient-based optimization framework that optimizes beamforming without explicitly estimating the SIM--UE channel. The proposed method, namely the physical projected gradient descent (P2GD) method, optimizes the achievable sum rate while incorporating zero-forcing (ZF) constraints. Based on the method of incorporating the ZF restriction, we propose two variations of P2GD, namely user equipment (UE)-P2GD and base station (BS)-P2GD. We also provide a theoretical convergence analysis and projected gradient techniques to ensure physical feasibility. Simulation results show that the proposed approach can achieve suboptimal beamforming in the multi-user system within a small number of over-the-air iterations, using a per-direction signaling budget below the pilot cost of explicit SIM--UE channel estimation. The proposed method provides a low-overhead beamforming scheme for SIM systems without explicit SIM--UE channel estimation.

publications.title: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction
publications.abstract: Accurate acquisition of full channel state information (CSI) is essential for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) wireless systems, while dense pilot-based estimation incurs substantial overhead. Directly minimizing the prediction error over raw CSI coefficients is fragile in realistic propagation environments, since small-scale fading, mobility, local scattering, and small spatial perturbations can induce large phase-sensitive variations. Nevertheless, wireless channels contain strong spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain correlations that can be more predictably represented in a latent propagation-field domain. Motivated by this observation, we propose a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA)-inspired field world model, defined as a latent predictive model of the wireless propagation field, for sparse-pilot channel reconstruction. The model maps CSI observations into latent time-frequency tokens, predicts masked or future latent field states from historical multi-band context, and fuses the predicted latent prior with sparse noisy current pilots to reconstruct the full MIMO-OFDM channel. Ray-tracing experiments show that the proposed method improves normalized mean square error (NMSE) over pilot-only and direct reconstruction baselines, supporting latent field prediction as an effective prior for sparse-pilot channel acquisition.

publications.title: Du bon usage des données 14C, publication et archivage : règles, métadonnées et erreurs à éviter pour une publication rigoureuse
publications.abstract: Introduite en 1949, la datation au carbone 14 (14C) s’est imposée comme un outil incontournable dans de nombreuses disciplines, notamment l’archéologie. Aujourd’hui, elle est au cœur des publications scientifiques – qu’il s’agisse de rapports, de monographies ou d’articles. Cependant, cette omniprésence s’accompagne d’un usage parfois imprécis, voire erroné, des données et des métadonnées associées, compromettant la fiabilité et la lisibilité des résultats. Dès ses débuts, la géochronologie 14C a établi des standards rigoureux pour garantir l’uniformité et la pertinence des interprétations (Olsson, 1970 ; Stuiver & Polach, 1977). Pourtant, la pratique actuelle révèle une grande hétérogénéité dans la présentation et l’archivage des résultats. On rencontre tout autant des excès de détails inutiles et déroutants que des formulations lacunaires, souvent dépourvues des métadonnées essentielles. Ces incohérences entraînent non seulement des confusions, mais aussi des interprétations erronées, voire trompeuses. Cette communication vise à rappeler les règles fondamentales d’un bon usage des données 14C, tant pour la publication que pour l’archivage. En mettant l’accent sur les métadonnées indispensables et leur justification, nous offrirons une approche pédagogique qui permettra une appropriation durable de ces bonnes pratiques. L’objectif est de remédier aux dérives actuelles et de garantir la qualité scientifique des travaux.

publications.title: VARIABILITY OF RADIOCARBON RESERVOIR AGE EFFECTS IN LAKES AND RIVERS IN ANATOLIA AND LESSER CAUCASUS
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT Multiproxy sedimentary sequence analysis constitutes the basis for reconstructions of past paleoenvironments and climate evolution. These sequences are, for the most part, obtained by coring in lakes, maars or crater lakes whose waters can record volcanic activity or karstic contributions, especially in Eastern Anatolia and the Lesser Caucasus. The reservoir age effect in these geological contexts leads to an apparent aging of the radiocarbon ages which also affects the plants and animals developing in or near these waters and consequently the population consuming them. We present here some results obtained from modern samples taken from Mediterranean, central and eastern Anatolian lakes, from the Van and Sevan lakes and along the Kura River and its tributaries from the Lesser Caucasus. The effect of volcanic CO2 outgassing in the vicinity of maar crater lakes is also discussed.

publications.title: Nussloch: 30 years of multidisciplinary research to establish a European reference loess sequence for the last glacial period
Early presence of Homo Sapiens in South America -a review of about 40 years of geochronological research in the Serra da Capivara National Park, Piauí, Brazil
publications.abstract: The settlement of the Americas, particularly the question of how early Homo Sapiens arrived in South America, is a central topic of scientific interest within the archaeological community. Growing evidence suggests an early human presence in the southern part of the American continent, and some previously overlooked findings are now being brought to light and acknowledged. The dating associated with evidence of human presence, regardless of the method used, suggests that humans might have been present 30, 40 or even 50 kyr BP. Among various archeological sites, significant efforts have been dedicated to the region of Serra da Capivara in Piauí, Brazil, for both archaeology and dating, for several decades, since the initial investigations conducted by Niède Guidon and Georgette Delibrias in 1980s.In this communication, we present a comprehensive analysis of the dating results obtained over the past twenty years, within the framework of systematic characterization of all stratigraphical and/or archeological units. Geochronological modeling is carried out with the ChronoModel software , in particular by using its specific option that allows for the correlation of multiple constraints among datings, events, and units. This feature enables us to link geochronological events by their significance, stratigraphic succession, and their association to the same technical facies, as defined by meticulous and objective analysis of lithic assemblages. With the help of these multiple constraints, we can objectively determine the techno-cultural phases by their boundaries (both start and end) and duration, each associated with a probability distribution.The meta-analysis of over a hundred 14C and OSL datings, which characterize more than 50 archeological layers across eight sites in and around the Serra da Capivara National Park, indicates a nearly continuous human presence over the last 40,000 years. Furthermore, it shows varying occupation of these sites depending on the period and their geographical location.

publications.title: RADIOCARBON DATING ON ECHOMICADAS, LSCE, GIF-SUR-YVETTE, FRANCE: NEW AND UPDATED CHEMICAL PROCEDURES
publications.abstract: ABSTRACT The Laboratoire des Sciences du Climat et de l’Environnement (LSCE) has operated a radiocarbon dating laboratory for almost 70 years. It has evolved from a traditional ß-decay counting to an accelerator mass spectrometry facility. In 2015, the LSCE received a major upgrade with the installation of a MICADAS. This evolution required adjustments in sample preparation to match the new capability to date samples as small as a few tens of µgC. We summarize here the sample cleaning procedures and the chemical purification or extraction treatment that we apply to the samples. We also report values of blank and reference materials of different matrices that match the large diversity of samples handled at LSCE.

publications.title: Ten years of measurements (2012-2022) of the atmospheric composition at Saclay/SIRTA observatory in the Ile de France region as part of ICOS and ACTRIS
publications.abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO 2 )is the main contributor to global warming, and cities now account for more than two-thirds of emissions of this gas. Atmospheric observatories located on the outskirts of cities are therefore important facilities for measuring the impact on atmospheric composition of the emission reductions planned by cities. The Saclay observatory, part of the ICOS and ACTRIS research infrastructures and located 20 km southwest of Paris, has been monitoring greenhouse gases (CO 2 , methane – CH 4 ), reactive gases (Nitrogen oxides – NO x , Ozone – O 3 , Carbon monoxide – CO), and carbonaceous aerosols (eBC) since 2012 (https://doi.org/10.57932/5c399263-a317-41b7-8900-184b177c4216, Bouillon and Ramonet, 2025). This study presents 10 years of monitoring of these compounds, characterizing diurnal, seasonal cycles and decadal trends. In order to best characterize the impact of Parisian emissions, we defined two sets of data depending on whether the station is downwind of Paris or, conversely, in background conditions with westerly winds. This strategy allows us to characterize the urban offset in the Saclay measurement series. The results show a significant decrease in the urban offset of compounds mainly linked to traffic emissions: −35.6 %, −52.3 %, and −56.7 % for CO, NO x , and eBC lf (equivalent black carbon from liquid fuel). There was also a 15 % decrease in urban offset of CO 2 between the 2012–2017 and 2019–2022 periods, a figure consistent with the Airparif inventories' estimate of the decrease in emissions in Paris over the same period.

publications.title: Assessing greenhouse gas measurement consistency and traceability in the UK and Ireland atmospheric monitoring network using whole and synthetic air reference materials
publications.abstract: Atmospheric measurements of greenhouse gases (GHG), including carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), methane (CH 4 ) and nitrous oxide (N 2 O) are essential for assessing climate change and verifying national emission inventories. As global networks rely on high-precision observations of GHGs, ensuring accuracy between observation stations is essential. Maintaining accuracy within a network requires the use of whole air reference materials (RMs) with well-defined calibration scales, such as those maintained by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) for the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO). With the global expansion of atmospheric monitoring networks there is a growing need for readily available RMs, stimulating the development of complementary alternatives such as synthetic air RMs traceable to the International System of Units (SI). In the United Kingdom (UK) and Ireland, the atmospheric GHG monitoring network, comprising long-term atmospheric monitoring stations, is equipped with high precision in situ GHG analysers. These observations are used to verify bottom-up assessments of national emissions. Here, a case study is presented which provides the first direct, network-wide evaluation of whole air versus synthetic air RMs under routine field conditions, allowing an assessment of the implications of SI-traceable RMs within an active national atmospheric monitoring system. We assess the UK and Ireland's network consistency and performance using WMO-NOAA scale-traceable whole air RMs and SI-traceable synthetic air RMs, through a blind multi-site round-robin intercomparison. Between 2021 and 2022, measurements were made of CO 2 , CH 4 and N 2 O in whole and synthetic air RMs at six sites using a range of instruments and the results were used to assess consistency between sites. The measured mole fractions for each cylinder, at each site were then compared with the assigned value on the WMO-NOAA scale and the SI-traceable values for the whole air and synthetic air RMs, respectively. Weighted residual analysis reveals that whole air RMs generally meet the WMO/Global Atmosphere Watch (GAW) compatibility goals for CO 2 and CH 4 , while N 2 O remains more difficult as its relatively small atmospheric variability requires measurement biases to be minimised to resolve meaningful atmospheric differences. Synthetic SI-traceable RMs have associated absolute uncertainties on their assigned values for CH 4 that are comparable to the extended WMO compatibility goals. However, absolute uncertainties for CO 2 and N 2 O remain significantly larger than both the compatibility and extended compatibility goals, which is consistent with previous studies. Overall, these results indicate that while scale-traceable whole air RMs remain essential for achieving the highest level of network compatibility required for atmospheric monitoring, SI-traceable synthetic RMs could play a valuable complementary role, particularly for CH 4 . However, it is first critical that improved characterisation and compensation of matrix effects arising from instrument-specific responses to differences in RM composition, non-linear instrument response across the relevant mole fraction range, and long-term stability, are achieved for them to become suitable for use in high-precision atmospheric monitoring.

publications.title: Review of the Radon Tracer Method for GHG emission estimates: development, application guidelines, improvements, and caveats
publications.abstract: The Radon Tracer Method (RTM) is an established, independent top-down method that can be used to cross-check bottom-up greenhouse gas (GHG) emission estimates. Furthermore, as uncertainties of Atmospheric Transport Models are reduced, the RTM can provide a convenient means of quantifying continual improvement of inversion-based top-down GHG emission estimates. While the accessibility and perceived simplicity of the RTM drive its popularity, the technique is better suited to assessing long-term relative changes in GHG emissions than absolute changes, due to short-term soil moisture influences on simulated radon flux uncertainty. Considerations for applying the RTM, based on fundamental assumptions of the technique's development, are application and season specific, making the development of a “standard protocol” for its use challenging. After proposing a novel alternative means of applying the nocturnal accumulation RTM, which improves interpretation of findings, we use measurements from a range of contrasting sites to discuss the significance of the technique's eight key considerations: (i) nocturnal window definition, (ii) radon and target gas accumulation thresholds, (iii) radon-to-target gas regression linearity thresholds, (iv) measurement height, (v) the contributing fetch, (vi) spatial and temporal radon flux variability, (vii) RTM temporal resolution, and (viii) application specific selection of a suitable radon monitor. The insight provided by these examples to the flexibility (or otherwise) of the technique's considerations will clarify the implications if users choose to relax or ignore them, potentially making future RTM studies more directly comparable.

publications.title: Projections in Enlargements of Filtrations under Jacod’s Absolute Continuity Hypothesis for Marked Point Processes
publications.abstract: Abstract We consider the initial enlargement $${{\mathbb {F}}}^{(\zeta )}$$ F ( ζ ) of a filtration $${{\mathbb {F}}}$$ F (called the reference filtration) generated by a marked point process with a random variable $$\zeta $$ ζ . We assume Jacod’s absolute continuity hypothesis, that is, the existence of a nonnegative conditional density for this random variable with respect to $${{\mathbb {F}}}$$ F . Then, we derive explicit expressions for the coefficients that appear in the integral representation for the optional projection of an $${{\mathbb {F}}}^{(\zeta )}$$ F ( ζ ) -(square integrable) martingale on $${{\mathbb {F}}}$$ F . In the case in which $$\zeta $$ ζ is strictly positive (called a random time in that case), we also derive explicit expressions for the coefficients, that appear in the related representation for the optional projection of an $${{\mathbb {F}}}^{(\zeta )}$$ F ( ζ ) -martingale on $${{\mathbb {G}}}$$ G , the reference filtration progressively enlarged by $$\zeta $$ ζ . We also provide similar results for the $${{\mathbb {F}}}$$ F -optional projection of any martingale in $${{\mathbb {G}}}$$ G . The arguments of the proof are built on the methodology that was developed in our paper (Gapeev et al. in Electron J Probab 26:1–24 2021) in the Brownian motion setting under the more restrictive Jacod’s equivalence hypothesis.

publications.title: On the Construction of Conditional Probability Densities in the Brownian and Compound Poisson Filtrations
publications.abstract: In this paper, we construct supermartingales valued in [0,1] as solutions of an appropriate stochastic differential equation on a given reference filtration generated by either a Brownian motion or a compound Poisson process. Then, by means of the results contained in [M. Jeanblanc and S. Song, Stochastic Processes Appl. 121 (2011) 1389–1410], it is possible to construct an associated random time on some extended probability space admitting such a given supermartingale as conditional survival process and we shall check that this construction (with a particular choice of supermartingale) implies that Jacod’s equivalence hypothesis, that is, the existence of a family of strictly positive conditional probability densities for the random times with respect to the reference filtration, is satisfied. We use the components of the multiplicative decomposition of the constructed supermartingales to provide explicit expressions for the conditional probability densities of the random times on the Brownian and compound Poisson filtrations.

publications.title: Projections of martingales in enlargements of filtrations under Jacod's equivalence hypothesis for marked point processes *
publications.abstract: We consider the initial and progressive enlargements of a filtration generated by a marked point process (called the reference filtration) with a strictly positive random time. We assume Jacod's equivalence hypothesis, that is, the existence of a strictly positive conditional density for the random time with respect to the reference filtration. Then, starting with the predictable integral representation of a martingale in the initially enlarged reference filtration, we derive explicit expressions for the coefficients which appear in the predictable integral representations for the optional projections of the martingale on the progressively enlarged filtration and on the reference filtration. We also provide similar results for the optional projection of a martingale in the progressively enlarged filtration on the reference filtration. This paper represents the continuation of research contained in our previous paper in EJP [11].

publications.title: Generalized Cox model for default times
publications.abstract: In this paper, we present a model in which the default time may coincide with a strictly positive probability with stopping times in the reference filtration. One of the advantages of our construction is that one can choose the sequence of these stopping times.

publications.title: Localizing Momentum Waves on Mazes
publications.abstract: We examine the proposal and analysis of arXiv:2404.14477 for putting momentum waves on mazes of intersecting M2 and M5 branes by computing a family of simple examples of momentum waves on pure M5 branes. We re-analyze the BPS equations for the near-brane M5-P system with the prescribed supersymmetry structure of the full M2-M5-P system and show that the general linear system obtained in arXiv:2404.14477 captures all of the null momentum waves on the simpler M5-P system. Despite the absence of explicit M2 branes in our examples, we find that the momentum waves still localize on an AdS$_3$ factor of the AdS$_7$ associated with M5 branes, showing that the supersymmetry prescription still reflects the M2-M5-P structure. This momentum localization takes two forms: explicit singular sources and smooth, localized bump functions reflecting ''momentum migration'' that is a feature of other microstate geometries. The simple, physical form of the momentum localization in our examples supports the broader proposal in arXiv:2404.14477 that independent momentum waves can localize at each brane intersection. We suggest further generalizations of momentum waves at brane intersections that could have important implications in holography.
